author: ctaylortt
body:
### PR Category
Feature + Performance

### Summary

#54993 provides host bridge support for fabric. The host bridge support implementation uses OpenMPI single-sided operations (MCA OSC aka: One-Sided-Communications). This requires retooling the existing OpenMPI build for tt-metal.

The PR includes docker container scripts that compile UCX with verbs support and then OpenMPI with UCX support. OpenMPI has a plugin system called MCA (Modular Component Architecture). MCA allows for different aspects of MPI to operate over different communication backends.

The PR sustains existing tt-metal use of ULFM over ethernet (MCA PML aka: Point-to-Point Management Layer) since ULFM will not work over RDMA.  The PR adds in the MCA OSC so host bridge one sided communications will benefit from rdma.

### Notes for reviewers

Decision needs to be made to split the dockerfile for this PR or merge it into the existing Dockerfile.

author: alfredo1996
body:
## Drill

**Scope.** Stop tracking three generated/dead artefact trees — `docs/.astro/` (Astro content-collection cache, rewritten by every docs build; the only dirty thing in a fresh checkout, swept into #1604), `design-shots/baseline/` (`scripts/shoot-stories.mjs` and the design-reviewer only *write* into `design-shots/`; nothing reads `baseline/`), and `screenshots/v1.1-redesign/` (30 before/after PNGs from #832–834, referenced nowhere — the issue says 29). Replace the stale Fumadocs-era `docs/.source` / `docs/.next` ignore rules with Astro-era ones. Delete `connection/.gitignore` (all four rules already covered by the root file) and the `docs/NEODASH_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` tombstone (grep: zero references; the canonical `migration-from-neodash.mdx` it points at exists). Add a ratchet so the cache cannot come back.

**Non-goals.** The six top-level README screenshots (`screenshots/0*.png`) stay tracked — the new rule is anchored to `screenshots/v1.1-redesign/`. `docs/src/env.d.ts` keeps its `../.astro/types.d.ts` reference: that is the standard Astro layout and `astro build` regenerates it. The two other Fumadocs-era CodeRabbit filters (`!docs/content/**/*.mdx`, `!docs/next-env.d.ts`) are not paths this issue names and are left alone.

**Edge cases.** `docs-ci` builds on a checkout with no `.astro/` — proven locally by wiping `docs/.astro` + `docs/dist` and building (71 pages, gate ≥10, cache regenerated, `git status -- docs/` silent). `git add -f` bypasses `.gitignore` — the ratchet catches it (proven by mutation). `git ls-files` on a now-absent path exits 0 with empty output, so the ratchet stays green after the files are gone; it asserts exit 0 so it cannot pass vacuously.

**Security.** None — no runtime code.

**Acceptance.** `git ls-files docs/.astro design-shots screenshots/v1.1-redesign` empty; `git check-ignore` matches the three paths and not `screenshots/01-login.png`; docs build green from zero cache; `npm run verify` green.

## What changed

- `git rm -r --cached docs/.astro design-shots/baseline screenshots/v1.1-redesign` — 39 files leave the index, stay on disk.
- `.gitignore`: the `# Fumadocs generated` block (`docs/.source`, `docs/.next`) becomes `docs/.astro/`, `design-shots/`, `screenshots/v1.1-redesign/`, each with a one-line reason.
- `.coderabbit.yaml`: dropped the dead `!docs/.source/**` path filter (same Fumadocs-era path).
- Deleted `connection/.gitignore` (redundant with root) and `docs/NEODASH_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` (unreferenced tombstone).
- New `scripts/__tests__/tracked-generated.test.mjs` — the ratchet.

## Tests

**Unit (`npm run test:scripts`, also run by CI):**
- `scripts/__tests__/tracked-generated.test.mjs` — three cases, one per path: `git ls-files -- <path>` exits 0 and prints nothing. Written red first (3/3 failing against the tracked cache), green after the untrack, then proven by mutation: `git add -f docs/.astro/settings.json` → 1 failed, restore → 3 passed.

**Docs build (mirrors `docs-ci`):** `rm -rf docs/.astro docs/dist && npm run build --prefix docs` → 71 HTML pages (gate ≥10), `.astro/` regenerated, nothing dirty under `docs/`.

**`npm run verify`:** exit 0 — app 278 files / 3831 tests, component 143 / 1996, connection 33 / 435 (1 file + 10 tests skipped, pre-existing Docker gate), scripts 11 / 124 (ratchet collected), node --test 50/50.

**E2E:** none apply — no UI or app code changed (`touchedUi: false`); no existing spec covers repo hygiene and none was added.

## Verification

Unit suites (`npm run verify`, exit 0):
- `app` — 278 files / 3831 tests passed
- `component` — 143 files / 1996 tests passed
- `connection` — 33 files / 435 tests passed (1 file + 10 tests skipped — pre-existing Docker gate)
- `scripts` (vitest) — 11 files / 124 tests passed, including the new `tracked-generated.test.mjs` ratchet (re-run standalone at ship time: 3/3 passed)
- `scripts` (`node --test`) — 50/50 passed

Ship-time checks: `git check-ignore` matches `docs/.astro/`, `design-shots/`, `screenshots/v1.1-redesign/` and rejects `screenshots/01-login.png`; `git ls-files` on the three paths is empty.

Playwright: no specs run — chore, no UI or app code touched.

Closes #1689

author: alseif0x
body:
Fourth semantic vertical, and the first that moves *behaviour* rather than state.

47 associated functions inside `impl WorldSession` never mentioned `self` at all and never awaited: opcode DOS limits, admission arithmetic, item modifier maths, equipment-slot tables, speed conversions, directory formatting, transfer-completion predicates. A function that cannot touch session state is not session behaviour, so they now live in `crates/wow-world/src/session_rules/`, together with five session-level helper rules that only they used.

## The largest reduction the track has produced

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| session hotspot production lines | 84,178 | 83,160 |
| session hotspot total lines | 192,823 | 191,801 |
| `WorldSession` associated items | 3,745 | 3,698 |
| `WorldSession` fields | 648 | 648 |
| registry / bridge accesses | 594 / 65 | 594 / 65 |

Fields, registry accesses and bridge accesses are unchanged because no state moved - only rules. Nothing was added to the inventory.

Unlike the state extractions in #668, #670 and #674, this one shrinks *both* sides: `Self::f(a)` becomes `f(a)` through one import, so no other hotspot grows and no physical ceiling moves. The 1,223 lines of rules now sit outside the session in two modules, both inside the review budget.

## Two details worth recording

The detector first matched any indented `fn` in the session tree and swept up `impl Default for X` bodies, which cannot move; it now requires an inherent `impl WorldSession` block. And the moved functions needed the session root's import environment - rather than copy 200 lines of imports, each module imports exactly the 88 names its rules use, which documents what a rule actually depends on.

## Evidence

- 3,822 `wow-world` lib tests pass unchanged.
- Workspace build clean; architecture check, self-test, physical ratchet, hotspot ratchet and `session-ownership-check check --syntax-only` pass, the last reporting 3,698 items.
- `./tools/validation-v2 final --base origin/3.4.3` passed at 9984be5d (clean tree, aarch64 host).
- The hotspot ledger baseline is tightened to the validated figures.

No rule body, signature or call order changes; no state moves; no new crate edge. This closes neither #133 nor #584.

Closes #676

author: c00ldudenoonan
body:
Closes #454
Theme: ALE-55

## The issue's code already shipped; its first ask never happened

`storage_read_compression: none | lz4 | zstd` landed in #509, `_table_read_options`
wires the Arrow-native mechanism, and the docs already say "**measure before
setting it**" and point at `seconds_read_transfer` vs `seconds_read_decode`.

What was missing is the measurement. The guidance told an operator to compare
two numbers without giving them a scale to compare against.

## Measured

120,000 rows of `sec_chunk_embeddings` — the 768-float vector plus chunk text
the issue describes — from BigQuery US to a developer machine, three runs per
codec, means:

| codec | wall | transfer | decode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `none` | 20.7 | **13.2** | **1.0** |
| `lz4` | 14.4 | 8.0 | 1.5 |
| `zstd` | 15.0 | 7.3 | 2.5 |

**Transfer runs ~13x decode uncompressed.** This read is decisively
transfer-bound, has room to trade, and either codec takes roughly **30% off
the wall clock**.

## Which codec is not decidable from this, and the issue guessed the wrong way

The wall-clock gap between `lz4` and `zstd` is inside run-to-run variance —
`lz4` won runs 1 and 3, `zstd` won run 2. I am not reporting a winner.

What *is* consistent across all three runs is the structural trade: `zstd`
always moves fewer bytes (7.3s vs 8.0s transfer) and always costs more CPU to
unpack (2.5s vs 1.5s decode). So `zstd` pulls ahead as the network slows and
falls behind as it speeds up.

The issue quotes Google recommending `zstd`, and offers `lz4` as the pick "when
the client is CPU-bound rather than network-bound". On this path the shape is
the opposite: `lz4` is at least as fast in wall clock while being the *less*
network-efficient codec. Worth writing down so the next reader does not
re-derive it from the vendor default.

## No default changes

Still `none`. The right answer depends on the network between client and
BigQuery and on the client's CPU headroom, neither of which stel can know — and
a client colocated with the data is a different regime that may not be
transfer-bound at all. The docs now carry the worked numbers so an operator has
something to calibrate their own reading against.

## The issue's other two asks, for the record

- *Expose the codec on the profile rather than hardcoding one* — done in #509.
- *Note the mutual exclusion with `response_compression_codec`* — cannot be hit:
  stel only ever sets `arrow_serialization_options`, and the code says so at
  `bigquery.py:357`.

## Validation

- `uv run ruff check` — clean ✅
- `uv run ty check` — one diagnostic, the pre-existing Windows-only `os.mkfifo` ✅
- Docs-only; no behavioural surface.

author: pragun-agent
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves premature context truncation and replaces rigid numbered note templates with a content-adaptive note architecture that preserves 100% technical fidelity across technical deep dives (Linear: **[BAC-30](https://linear.app/pragun-a/issue/BAC-30/support-content-adaptive-note-generation-without-context-truncation)**).

### Key Architectural Improvements:
1. **Context Truncation Elimination (Zero Information Loss)**:
   - Escalated `MAX_TOPIC_CONTEXT_CHARS` from 14,000 to **120,000 characters** in `extractTopicRelevantContext`.
   - Removed brittle heuristic regex header-splitting and keyword-filtering that previously dropped deep technical subsystems (e.g. WAL, SSTable, Compaction, Bloom filters) if subheadings did not repeat the top-level topic keyword.
   - Expanded Note Critic source context evaluation window from 6,000 to **30,000 characters**.
2. **Content-Adaptive, Topic-Driven Heading Architecture**:
   - Eliminated artificial, generic numbered section templates (`## 1. Problem Context`, `## 2. Conceptual Core`, `## 4. Algorithmic Logic & Pseudocode`).
   - Instructed LLM to use descriptive Markdown section headings (H2 `##` and H3 `###`) that directly name the specific mechanisms, state machines, and protocols of the topic (e.g. `## The Write Path: Memtable & Write-Ahead Log (WAL)`, `## Immutable SSTable On-Disk Format`, `## Compaction: Size-Tiered vs Leveled Compaction`).
   - Retained universal pedagogical anchors: Prerequisites, Key Operational Guarantees, Mermaid diagrams (`flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`), real-world trade-off matrices, failure modes, and clear summary checklists.
3. **Note Critic Rubric Upgrade**:
   - Refocused the evaluation rubric on **Technical Completeness & Omission Detection** across the entire source context, auditing for missing storage internals, formulas, or system guarantees.
4. **Walkthrough Generator & UI Enhancements**:
   - Inline expandable note and quiz previews inside the AI Walkthrough modal (`IngestionWalkthroughModal.tsx`).
   - High-readability typography hierarchy in `MarkdownContent.tsx` and interactive Cyberdeck cards in `QuizViewer.tsx`.

---

## Verification & Test Results
- [x] Playwright E2E verification passed locally (`npx playwright test`: 21 / 21 passed)
- **Backend Test Suite (`vitest run`)**: 215 / 215 passed (100% green)
- **Frontend Test Suite (`vitest run`)**: 162 / 162 passed (100% green)
- **TypeScript Production Build (`tsc && vite build`)**: Clean compilation with 0 errors
- **Live Ingestion Verification**: Verified against `https://www.hellointerview.com/learn/system-design/deep-dives/time-series-databases`, successfully generating 6 in-depth, adaptive study notes (~47,000 chars total) with zero technical omissions.

body:
## Summary Repair partial workflow reruns and reduce repeated CI work while preserving supported-platform runtime and package checks. Recheck changed recovery-directory identities before treating a resolved-path mismatch as an unsafe stable directory. ## Problem Merged-main run 34419485608 exposed a noisy one-record timing comparison and a separate aggregation bug: rerunning one failed shard omitted successful evidence from the previous attempt. CI also repeated costly benchmark and release-checker fixtures across platforms. The revised Windows cache job then exposed an existing stale-lock recovery failure at the realpath-mismatch check. ## Design - Keep native Node testing. Context7 research and an eight-file controlled comparison found Node fastest locally: 1.152s median versus 1.269s for Vitest threads and 1.305s for forks, using four workers on macOS/Node 26.5. This is not a universal framework benchmark. - Separate runtime tests from benchmark and release-tool fixtures. Run runtime/filesystem/process checks on all supported platforms; run expensive tooling fixtures once on Linux. Build explicitly rather than implicitly through the test command. - Run the Windows cache file separately. Its union with Windows core is the complete runtime suite, with no duplicate files or omitted assertions. - Measure all fifteen representative operations at 1,000 records across six Linux shards. Retain twenty samples, two warmups, fresh workers, adjacent same-runner base/candidate pairs and every numerical threshold. Smaller corpora retain behavioural and smoke coverage. - Let `large-reads` alone own package sizes and packed startup evidence. Aggregate the newest available pair for each shard within the same workflow run, recording its attempt. Never mix sides across attempts or fall back from incomplete newer evidence; failed prerequisite jobs still block aggregation. - Pass the package producer's actual retained artifact name to dependent jobs, so downstream-only reruns use the correct candidate. - Move the recovery-directory realpath mismatch check after the existing final type and identity checks. Missing or replaced identity returns `changed` for existing bounded reobservation. Stable wrong realpaths, symlinks and non-directories remain rejected. Add one deterministic regression covering movement, replacement and a stable wrong-path control; retain the genuine two-process stale-lock test. ## Scope CI scheduling, test selection, benchmark scope, rerun evidence selection, performance documentation and the explicitly owner-approved three-line recovery-directory correctness exception. The owner approved this runtime exception on 10 September 2026. ## Deliberately excluded Framework migration, broader runtime optimisation, threshold increases, sample filtering, automatic retries and downstream ticket work. The five-sample/diagnostic-p95 proposal remains unapplied. ## Compatibility Preserve Linux/macOS/Windows on Node 24.15 and Linux on Node 26. Build and check the exact package on Linux 24.15, then check the same bytes on macOS, Windows and Linux Node 26. Published-oracle compatibility and publish dry-run checks remain on Linux. Required contexts, read-only permissions, pinned actions, public bounds and synchronous APIs remain intact. Recovery-directory error precedence now recognises observed identity changes before classifying a path mismatch; stable unsafe layouts still fail closed. ## Performance | Work | Previous workflow | This branch | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Workflow jobs | 35 | 23 | | Comparison shards | 12 | 6 | | Raw operation reports | 2,720 | 600 | | Expensive tooling fixtures | Repeated across OS lanes | Once on Linux | Final-head [CI 34455295615](https://github.com/isaachinman/encephalon/actions/runs/34455295615) passed all 23 jobs in **6m55s**, with **51.65 summed runner-minutes** versus 100.05 previously. Windows core/cache passed in 157s/280s. The independent artifact audit passed all **600 raw reports and 58 comparisons**, using base `4e1111be7a7b291f6e4f26aee218761e0a82695e`, candidate `5bee06abcf5e2e1be96cbd0a87d87932f8a7ad0a`, and common harness `7143ad061631aba5380340cebdd622c3c1052dd2ea5a861180b94dbb530531a2`. Each operation uses matched Linux ARM64/Node 24.15 measurements within its own shard; different runners are not pooled. Reports retain raw samples, ranges, variances, preparation/query phases and package/startup metrics. The table shows base → candidate; required limits remain 15% median, 25% p95, 20% RSS and 10% bytes. Values are rounded only for display; gates use unrounded observations. | Operation (1,000 records) | Median ms | p95 ms | Peak RSS MiB | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | gather | 8015.00 → 8012.77 | 8039.97 → 8031.65 | 169.32 → 169.51 | | maximumPayloadSearch | 7956.97 → 7956.89 | 7969.45 → 7981.60 | 187.09 → 187.75 | | largePayloadSearch | 8013.90 → 8019.98 | 8043.86 → 8051.94 | 168.83 → 168.84 | | coldHydrate | 743.13 → 740.13 | 770.26 → 772.67 | 144.97 → 146.45 | | unchangedPrepare | 485.73 → 481.54 | 501.18 → 497.71 | 166.12 → 167.87 | | stalePrepare | 966.28 → 961.02 | 1002.08 → 973.55 | 174.93 → 176.32 | | list | 469.30 → 470.09 | 489.95 → 483.18 | 168.07 → 168.08 | | show | 468.21 → 468.47 | 491.22 → 491.94 | 167.71 → 167.59 | | compactSearch | 486.98 → 486.81 | 505.90 → 501.56 | 166.46 → 167.68 | | fullSearch | 469.82 → 472.71 | 478.05 → 491.84 | 168.99 → 168.73 | | payloadOnlySearch | 480.56 → 483.90 | 500.01 → 502.99 | 188.00 → 187.30 | | missingSearch | 463.11 → 465.45 | 482.60 → 485.28 | 168.17 → 167.77 | | listMaximum | 489.52 → 488.40 | 507.28 → 504.59 | 174.36 → 174.43 | | validateArtifacts | 252.86 → 254.91 | 258.38 → 267.42 | 123.40 → 123.00 | | strictCacheValidation | 468.68 → 465.25 | 494.57 → 478.84 | 167.93 → 168.34 | Narrowing the timed corpus reduces coverage; it does not eliminate hosted-runner noise. ## Verification - The new deterministic regression failed against the original production function and passed after the correction; the existing two-process stale-lock test passed locally. - `bun run lint`, all four typecheck projects, build and generated-version checks passed. Runtime: 811 passed plus three platform skips in 50.4s; tooling: 90 passed in 154.5s. Repository validation passed for all 43 records. Benchmark smoke passed in 46.3s. The exact original Windows interleaving was not captured; the regression establishes the corrected conditional behaviour and Windows CI must verify integration. Reverting restores the previous scheduling and error precedence, including the known partial-rerun defect and excess repeated work. ## Linear [MAR-2784](https://linear.app/marcoappio/issue/MAR-2784) — follow-up to #86. author: valpr
body:
## Summary

Fixes two related multi-cloud sync bugs:
1. **Cloud sources appeared disconnected after every reload** - startup only restored the primary target's session (or triggered the re-auth banner). Sessions are now restored silently for all stored cloud sources, and the banner surfaces whichever source expired.
2. **With multiple connected clouds, only the primary target synced** - now **book-scoped data** (reading progress, bookmarks, library) syncs to **every connected cloud**, while **stats/reading goals/profiles** remain scoped to the primary **"Statistics Sync Target"**.

## Changes

- `fix(sync)`: silently restore cloud sessions (`restoreCloudSessions`) for all stored sources on app load and retry on `online`; multi-source header/manage banner surfaces any `NEEDS_RECONNECT` source or pending sync.
- `feat(sync)`: `BOOK_SCOPED_DATA_TYPES` vs `PRIMARY_ONLY_DATA_TYPES` split in `cloud-sync.ts`; `syncDownData`/`executeReplication` fan out to all connected clouds; down-apply order is non-primary-first so the primary target wins for scoped data.
- `feat(settings)`: per-source connection status chips + last-sync time in the storage list; dropdown relabeled to *Statistics Sync Target*; manual sync now marks per-source freshness (`lastSyncBySource$`).

## Testing

- `pnpm -F web check` - 0 errors, 0 warnings. `lint` and `build` pass.
- New `apps/web/tests/cloud-sync-scope.spec.ts` (4 tests): statistics-scope label + helper text; custom sources render per-source status chips; chips and per-source last-sync time survive reload.
- Full suite: 70/76 pass. The 10 failures (settings-tabs-url, tooltips, reader-profiles, reader-settings-layout, navigation-performance) reproduce identically on `origin/main` and are unrelated to this PR.

body:
aifactory sandbox（VM 内の agent）による自動作業。workflow: **bug**。ゲート緑・レビュー PASS・CI 緑なら aifactory が自動で `develop` へマージする（条件を満たさなければ開いたまま人間に渡す）。

## コミット
```
e7e00c7 fix: windows-pull / linux-pull にも鍵の用途の記録と系統別の鍵の選び分けを届ける（391）
9d5baac docs: pull backend の鍵の出どころ（鍵プールが正本）と keys pick を書く（391）
c886de3 fix: pull backend の Claude の鍵を鍵プールから取り、ジョブ環境から古い鍵を落とす（391）
ea039ce feat: sandbox keys pick を足し、pull backend の鍵の再現テストを置く（391）
3c28da6 fix: sandbox が無い環境で鍵の起動報告が runner を落とすのを止める（391）
```

## plan.md

# 計画: pull backend の Claude 鍵を鍵プールから取り、console/MCP のジョブ環境から古い鍵を落とす（391）

添付なし（`/home/dev/work/391/attachments/` は無い）。以下はコードを読んで確かめた事実と、そこからの判断。

## 問題の理解

無効化したはずの鍵 `keiyukai_partner-n5` が使われ続けた。経路は 3 段で、どれも「プロセス環境に残った鍵に落ちる」ことが原因。

1. `console/lib/core.py:109 child_env()` が `dict(os.environ)` をそのまま子に渡す。`bin/mcp` は起動時に 1 回だけ
   `load_ctl_env()`（`core.py:121`）を呼ぶので、長生きした MCP サーバーは起動時点の `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` を持ち続ける。
   `load_ctl_env` は「既に非空の環境変数は上書きしない」規則なので、呼び直しても古い値は消えない。
2. その環境が `kb run` → `workflow/bin/run` → pull backend まで素通りする。
3. `workflow/lib/macos.py credentials()` が `~/.config/sandbox/env` と `pj/<pj>.env` を `source` したうえで
   `printf "${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN:-}"` するので、**ファイルに鍵が無いと `source` 前の（＝プロセス環境の）値がそのまま残って**採用される。
   さらに系統別の変数（`_FABLE` / `_OPUS` / …）を書かないので、`workflow/bin/run:715 token_env_prefix()` の
   `${CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_<系統>:-$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN}` が全系統でその 1 本に落ちる。

対比: Proxmox 側は `sandbox/bin/sandbox:58` が起動直後に `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN*` を `unset` してから env ファイルを
`source` し、`pool_apply_keys`（ADR-0044 / ADR-0046）で系統別に選ぶので、環境の鍵は届かない。**この不変条件を pull backend にも広げるのが本件**。

`workflow/lib/linux.py` は `credentials()` / `refresh_token()` / `command()` を macos からそのまま継承しているので同じ穴（推測ではなく継承関係で確認）。
`workflow/lib/windows.py:55` は `refresh_token()` を上書きするが値は `credentials()` から取るので同じ穴。

## 再現条件（確定。実機も VM も要らない）

R1（console / MCP）: `os.environ` に `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=**** があり、ctl.env の同じ key が**別の値**に変わっている。
  → `core.child_env()` は古い値を返す。再現テストの置き場: **`console/tests/test_console.py`**（新クラス `ChildEnvKeysTest`。`LoadCtlEnvTest` の隣）

R2（pull backend）: `~/.config/sandbox/env` と `pj/<pj>.env` に `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` が**無く**（プール運用で消してある）、
  プロセス環境に鍵がある。→ `credentials()` がその環境の鍵を返し、`refresh_token()` が guest の `runtime.env` に書く。
  再現テストの置き場: **`workflow/tests/test_macos.py`**（新クラス `PullBackendKeyTest`。偽 worker の `sb` で
  `runtime.env` に渡る stdin を捕まえる。`sandbox` は PATH に置く偽スクリプト）

R3（無効化が伝わらない）: プールで鍵を `--disable` にしても、R2 の経路は `keys.json` を一度も読まないので何も変わらない。
  再現テストの置き場: **`workflow/tests/test_sandbox_keys.py`**（bash 切り出し。`keys pick --current=…`）と
  `workflow/tests/test_macos.py`（工程 2 回ぶんで名前が変わること）

## 原因の仮説（確度つき）

- A（確度: 確実）: `credentials()` が env ファイルに鍵が無いときプロセス環境の鍵に落ちる。コードで確認（`macos.py` の `script` に `unset` が無い）。
- B（確度: 確実）: `child_env()` が親の `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN*` をそのまま渡す。コードで確認。
- C（確度: 確実）: pull backend の `runtime.env` に系統別変数が無いので全モデルが同じ鍵になる。`credentials()` の戻り値が 2 key だけ。
- D（確度: 高）: pull backend の起動は `sandbox keys used` に届いていない。`run_agent` の `report_key_launch` は
  guest の `CLAUDE_KEY_NAME_<系統>` を見るが、pull backend は誰もその変数を書いていない → `LAUNCHES` が増えない。

## 変更範囲（ファイル）

- `sandbox/bin/sandbox` … `sandbox keys pick` を新設（選び方の正本を bash に残す）
- `console/lib/core.py` … `child_env()` と ctl.env 読み込みの分離
- `workflow/lib/macos.py` … `credentials()` / `take()` / `run_agent()`
- `workflow/lib/windows.py` … `command()`（runtime.env の全 key を env に入れる）
- `workflow/bin/run` … `Run.NoKey`（backend から使えるようにクラス属性で公開。`PoolBusy` と同じ流儀。1〜2 行）と
  `report_key_launch()` の `sandbox` 不在ガード（下の「基準が赤」参照）
- テスト: `workflow/tests/test_sandbox_keys.py` / `workflow/tests/test_macos.py` / `workflow/tests/test_windows.py` / `console/tests/test_console.py`
- 文書: `docs/macos-worker.md`・`docs/windows-worker.md`・`docs/linux-worker.md`・`workers/README.md`・
  `website/content/ja/reference/cli-sandbox.md`・`website/content/ja/guides/{macos,windows,linux}-worker.md` と対応する `en/`
- `changelog.d/391-pull-backend-key-pool.md`

### 触らない範囲

- `workflow/lib/linux.py`（macos の継承で直る。差分を入れない）
- `glue/bin/intake`（ctl.env の鍵を使う設計のまま。ADR-0044 の対象外）
- Proxmox 側の `cmd_take` / `cmd_reset` / `cmd_reinject` / `inject_env` の既存の振る舞い
- `keys_pick` / `_pool_assign` の**選び方そのもの**（規則を増やさない。呼べるようにするだけ）
- 既存の `docs/adr/*.md`、`CHANGELOG.md`、`LICENSE`、`workspace/`

## 手順（implementer 向け）

0. **基準の赤を先に片付ける**（下の「基準が赤」。`workflow/bin/run:728 report_key_launch()` が
   `sandbox` の無い環境（CI・この VM）で `FileNotFoundError` を投げて 13 件を落としている。
   `sh()` は `check=False` でも `OSError` は投げるので、`report_key_launch` 側で握って `self.log` に落とす。
   docstring の「失敗しても run は止めない」を満たすだけの数行）。
   これを直さないと自分の変更の赤と見分けられず、完了条件の「CI が緑」も満たせない。

1. **再現テストを 2 本書いて赤を見る**（本件の起点）。
   - `console/tests/test_console.py` に `ChildEnvKeysTest`（`LoadCtlEnvTest` の隣）:
     `os.environ["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"]="old-n5"` を置き、`core.CTL_ENV` に新しい値の ctl.env を向けて
     `core.child_env()["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"]` が **新しい値** であることを要求 → 現状は `old-n5` で赤。
   - `workflow/tests/test_macos.py` に `PullBackendKeyTest`:
     偽 `sandbox`（PATH に置く shell script）が `gh-app token` に `ghs_…` を返し、`~/.config/sandbox/env` 相当に鍵が無い状態で
     `os.environ["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"]="leaked-env-key"` → `refresh_token()` が書く `runtime.env` に `leaked` が出ないことを要求 → 現状は赤。
2. **`sandbox keys pick` を足す**（`sandbox/bin/sandbox` の `cmd_keys`）。
   `sandbox keys pick --pj <pj> --task <id> [--need=fable,other] [--current=fable=<名前>,other=<名前>] --json`
   - `load_pj "$pj"` → `pool_apply_keys "$task"` → `pool_require_keys` の順（`cmd_take` と同じ並び。ロック・`uses`/`last_used` の更新は既存のまま）
   - `--current` は `_pool_apply_locked` が `$STATE` から引いている `cur` の**上書き**として渡す。
     いま `jq … '.[$id].keys[$g]'` を書いている 2 か所を `_pool_cur_of <task> <group>` に抜き、上書きがあればそれを返す
     （pull backend は Proxmox の貸出台帳に載らないので、前回の名前は run の `state.json` が持つ）
   - 出力は **stdout に JSON 1 行だけ**。`[key] 鍵: …` のような人向けの行は出さない（stdout をそのまま Python が読む）
     形: `{"keys":{"fable":"<名前>","other":"<名前>"},"env":{"CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN":"…","CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_OPUS":"…","CLAUDE_KEY_NAME_OPUS":"…", …}}`
     中身は `claude_family_lines` / `claude_key_name_lines` と同じ集合を `jq -n` で組む（値はコマンド行に置かず環境変数経由。`_keys_add_locked` と同じ流儀）
   - 鍵が足りなければ `pool_require_keys` が `鍵なし:` で `die`（stderr・rc≠0、stdout は空、`uses` は動かさない）。プールが空なら env ファイルの鍵に落ちる（既存の互換規則そのまま）
   - `_keys_usage` の文言に `pick` を足す
3. **`console/lib/core.py`**
   - `read_ctl_env(path=None) -> dict` を切り出す（ファイルを parse して dict を返すだけ。`os.environ` を触らない）。
     `load_ctl_env()` はこれを使って今までどおり「未設定の key だけ環境に補う」に整理する（振る舞いは変えない）
   - `child_env()`: `dict(os.environ)` から `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_*` / `CLAUDE_KEY_NAME_*` を落とし、
     `read_ctl_env()` にある同名の key **だけ**入れ直す。`CTL_ENV` はモジュール変数を呼び出し時に読む（テストが差し替えられるように）
   - ここを通るのは `kb`（`core.py:189`）・JobStore（`:892`）・`sandbox_cli`（`:1506`）。intake は JobStore 経由なので ctl.env の最新の鍵を受け取る（今までと同じ結果）
4. **`workflow/lib/macos.py`**
   - `credentials()`: GH_TOKEN は今のまま。Claude 側は env ファイルの `source` をやめて
     `sandbox keys pick --pj <pj> --task <task> --need=<…> --current=… --json` を呼び、`env` をそのまま戻り値に混ぜる。
     `state["keys"]` に選ばれた名前を残して `save()`（次回の `--current`、および人が読む記録）
   - 失敗の扱い: stderr に `鍵なし:`（`workflow/bin/run:127 NO_KEY`）があれば `NoKey` を上げる。それ以外は今までどおり `RuntimeError`。
     **`sandbox` の stdout を例外文・ログに入れない**（鍵の値が入っている）
   - `NoKey` の取り方は `pool_busy()` と同じ流儀で `getattr(self, "NoKey", None)`（`workflow/bin/run` の `Run` に `NoKey = NoKey` を足す）
   - `take()`: `self.state["needed_keys"] = self.needed_keys()` を保存してから prepare に入る
     （ADR-0046 の再開判定。`kanban/bin/kb:354` が読む。無いと「両方の鍵待ち」に丸められる）
   - `run_agent()`: 先頭の `self.refresh_token()` が `NoKey` になったら、工程の中断として扱う。
     `commit_tracked(WIP_KEY_MESSAGE)` 相当 → `self.last_fail = {"failure": "key", …}` を立てて `(False, 理由)` を返す
     （`workflow/bin/run:1058` の `PAUSE_KINDS` に載って human 行き・戻し回数を消費しない。文言は既存の「鍵が使えず」に合わせる）
5. **`workflow/lib/windows.py`** `command()`: `runtime.env`（JSON）の **全プロパティ**を `$env:` に入れる形へ。
   いまは `GH_TOKEN` と `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` の 2 つ決め打ちなので、系統別の鍵と `CLAUDE_KEY_NAME_*` が guest に届かない。

author: alainmenag
body:
## Per-client provisioning tokens

Adds a per-client token to the provisioner and enforces it on the provisioning
endpoint via HTTP Basic auth. A client with a token set is no longer served on
MAC address alone.

Bumps the module to **1.0.12** / dbversion **1.0.7**.

### Storage

- New `token` column on `oryk_provisioner_clients` (`VARCHAR(255) NULL`, after
  `profile_id`). Added to the `CREATE TABLE` and to a new
  `addClientTokenColumn()` migration, guarded by `schemaHas()` in the same
  additive style as `addResourceFileColumns()` — an existing site upgrades
  with every client tokenless, which is the same as it was before.
- The column holds a `password_hash()`, not the secret. It is deliberately
  **not indexed**: it is verified against, never looked up by, since the MAC in
  the request path already says who is asking.

### Admin UI

- A **Token** field on the client editor, typed as `username:password`.
- The field round-trips the stored hash. Leaving it alone rewrites what was
  already there; typing a new `user:password` over it replaces the token;
  emptying the box removes it. **A colon is what distinguishes the two** — a
  `password_hash()` never contains one, so a value with a colon is a new token
  to hash.
- `clientRow()` now selects `token` so the editor can show it. The hash is only
  exposed on the admin page; `clientTokenHash()` is private and deliberately
  kept out of `clientRow()` so nothing else in the module gets handed it.

### Endpoint

- `engine/provisioner.php` reads `PHP_AUTH_USER` / `PHP_AUTH_PW` and composes
  them into `user:pass`, replacing the commented-out Basic-auth stub.
- `serve()` and `resolveRequest()` take a third `$token` argument (both public —
  signature change).
- `resolveRequest()` returns a `code` on the result; `serve()` honours it, and
  on `401` sends `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Provisioning"` and exits.
  401s are still written to the provisioning log before the exit.
- Behaviour: client with no token → unchanged. Client with a token and no
  credentials → 401 challenge. Client with a token and wrong credentials →
  401. Correct credentials → served as before.

### Also added

- `hashToken()` (public) — `password_hash(PASSWORD_DEFAULT)`; algorithm, cost
  and salt travel inside the hash, so nothing else has to be kept in step.
  Returns `null` on failure, and `saveClient()` refuses the save rather than
  storing something that could never verify.
- `verifyToken($mac, $token)` (public) — `password_verify()` against the stored
  hash. A client with no token returns **false**, not true: whether an
  unauthenticated request should be let through is policy for the caller.

### Notes for review

- **`resolveRequest()` dereferences `$client` before the null check.**
  `$client['token']` is read while `$client` may be `null` (unknown MAC), which
  is a PHP 8 warning; it evaluates falsy so the request still falls through to
  the existing 404, but the check wants to be `$client && $client['token']`.
- **`verifyToken()` is not what enforces the token.** `resolveRequest()` calls
  `password_verify()` against `$client['token']` directly, so there are now two
  paths to the same comparison. Worth collapsing onto one.
- **A token typed without a colon is stored verbatim** and can never verify,
  since the endpoint hashes nothing on the way in. Whatever eventually issues
  tokens must issue ones containing a colon; a validation error on save would
  be cheaper than the silent failure.
- **Failures are still not uniform** — a 401 now distinguishes "this client has
  a token" from "this MAC is unknown" (404), which gives a prober one more bit
  than before. Called out in the README's security notes as still-outstanding.

body:
## 背景

issue#168 第二阶段 PR-2 编码落地。依据：

- N4 §4（PR-2 详细设计：registerTool 契约 + 删除/保留项）
- N4 §4.5（4 个 registerTool 接口契约）
- N4 §4.6（LLM 决策流）
- 方案 A 保留 substringMatch 后备（你已确认）

PR-2 目标：**鉴权判定（业务描述 → 群组匹配）由 PI Agent LLM 决策**，lark-bot 仅保留成员资格校验。

## 核心变更

### 1. 4 个新 registerTool（PR-2）

| registerTool | 用途 |
|--------------|------|
| `larkbot_list_candidate_groups` | 返回 description 非空的群组列表 |
| `larkbot_authorize_user` | 校验 openId 是否在 chatId 群组成员中（4 种 status） |
| `larkbot_resolve_operator` | 把 open_id 解析为稳定 user_id（包装 identity-resolver） |
| `larkbot_get_chat_auth_state` | 查询 chatId 的鉴权状态 |

registerTool 总数：PR-1 7 个 → PR-2 后 11 个（7 feishu_* + 4 larkbot_*）。

### 2. auth.ts 改造

**删除**：
- `substringMatch` 内部调用（函数保留作回滚后备）
- `AgentMatcher` 类型与 factory 调用
- `normalizeForMatch` 内部调用

**改造**：
- `AuthInput` 移除 `businessDescription`，新增 `chatId`（LLM 决策的）
- `authorize()` 改为仅做成员资格校验（含缓存缺失重试逻辑）

### 3. extension 单例（自治）

新增 module-level 单例，与回滚路径（main.ts + ingress.ts）隔离：

- `extensionAuthModule`（createAuthModule 工厂）
- `extensionBroadcastModule`（createBroadcastModule 工厂）
- `extensionIdentityResolver`（createIdentityResolver 工厂）
- `chatAuthStates: Map<chatId, ChatAuthState>`

author: jlfassio-vibecoder
body:
## The experiment settled it, and I was wrong

Posting the PNG and WebP pair to X: **both rendered.** WebP was never the problem, so the PNG-first change in #144 was based on a wrong hypothesis. It is harmless and stays — PNG is the more compatible default — but it was not the fix.

What X actually does is crop `og:image` to roughly **1.9:1 out of the vertical middle**. Measured against the posted card, the band it kept ran about y=690–1258 of 1920:

| | |
|---|---|
| header | **cropped off** |
| hero "27 rounds" | **cropped off** |
| name "Justin" | **cropped off** |
| 540 reps · score 459 | visible |
| THE WORKOUT + movements | visible |
| ROUND SPLITS | partial |
| url + watermark | **cropped off** |

Everything that says *whose* result it is, gone. The movement list survived.

## Fix

`og:image` and `twitter:image` are separate tags precisely because platforms crop differently — that is the whole answer. Facebook and Apple's Messages letterbox the 9:16 card and show all of it, both verified, so they keep it. X gets the **landscape** render (1.78:1, survives its crop) in `twitter:image`.

This is the per-destination split you suggested, done in metadata instead of UI — the athlete still composes one card and presses one button.

It also means #141, the landscape layout fix, was load-bearing after all.

## Schema

- `mission_shares.wide_image_path`
- storage policy admits `{id}-wide.png|webp` and nothing else new — the suffix is in the policy, not free-form
- `set_mission_share_image` takes and validates the wide path the same way it validates the portrait one, and first-write-wins is now per column so a late wide upload can still land
- `get_share_summary` carries it — body copied verbatim from `20260909570000` plus one key, because rewriting it from memory is how the participant/segment scoping on the score would have quietly gone missing

Shares made before this fall back to the portrait card, which is exactly what they show on X today.

**The wide card never blocks the portrait one.** If it will not encode under the bucket limit or will not upload, X falls back — the link never loses its card over a bonus.

## Verified against production

Migration applied, then:

```
get_share_summary       → "wideImagePath": null        ✓ column reaches the edge
foreign wide path       → {"ok":false,"reason":"invalid_wide_path"}
arbitrary storage key   → HTTP 400 (anon)
```

## Tests

Two new panel tests: both layouts get rendered and uploaded, and the portrait card still uploads when the wide one is too large (`wideBlob` null). Plus a `shareShell` test asserting `twitter:image` and `og:image` differ.

lint / typecheck / 2758 tests pass.

**Not verified end to end** — needs a post to X after deploy.

author: tk-ap
body:
Six superseded tasks produced **66 "Decision required" cards in one session — eleven each.** Two independent defects combined.

## 1. Revoked work was carded at all

`collect_reviews` selected `phase IN ('review','blocked','revoked')`. Revoked is terminal — the mandate expired or was withdrawn — so there is nothing to decide. Asking anyway is worse than silence: it presents dead work as pending a decision. What stopped is reported by the digest instead.

Fixed in both the base collector and the human-first one that replaces it. Only the second is live, but a divergence between them is how the next storm starts.

## 2. The card key carried a workspace fingerprint

`fingerprint()` spans git HEAD, the full diff against it, **and every untracked file**. When the workspace is this repository, an unrelated commit changes it — and mints a brand new card for the same task at the same attempt. Every commit, merge and rebase during a working session produced another round.

The refresh itself is deliberate and worth keeping: a verdict belongs to the files it was formed against, and `decide()` refuses acceptance when the card's snapshot no longer matches (`"Files changed since this card; review the refreshed card"`). So this **bounds** the behaviour rather than removing it.

After `MAX_CARD_REFRESHES` rounds for one task/phase/attempt, the standing card is left alone. It still cannot be accepted while stale, and the digest still lists the task under "Needs you" — nothing is lost except the repetition.

## The pattern

This is the same defect class as the duplicate blocker alerts in #74: **an `event_key` that describes the state of the world rather than the event it announces.** I noted that and didn't chase it. This is the second instance, so it's worth naming as a rule rather than fixing case by case.

## Verification

Three cases: revoked work produces no card; a changed workspace still refreshes *below* the cap; refreshes stop *at* the cap. Full suite **224 tests, all passing**.

The live database was also repaired by hand — the seven superseded orders had been swept back to `revoked` and their orphaned cards marked decided, which stopped the storm before this fix landed.

body:
## What

Adds an AI layer to the customer-support system, plus the dev tooling to work on it.

### Product agent — `POST /agent/chat`
A stateless customer-facing self-service assistant (`backend/app/agent/`). Runs an LLM tool loop over the **existing service layer** (no MCP subprocess per request). Security properties:
- identity (`actor_customer_id` / `actor_role`) always comes from the verified JWT — the model never supplies it;
- admin-only tools are not offered to non-admin callers;
- `max_steps` cap bounds each turn (and does **not** execute tools on the final step).

### Pluggable LLM provider
`LLM_PROVIDER` selects `gemini` (default) or `openrouter` (free models). Provider-neutral message/tool types (`backend/app/agent/types.py`) mean a third provider is one file. `chatbot.py` is refactored onto the shared `AgentRunner` and keeps demonstrating the MCP client path.

### Frontend
Angular **Assistant** page (`/chat`): chat UI, suggestion chips, tool badges, stateless history round-trip. Environment split so `npm start` → localhost and `npm run build` → Azure.

### Claude Code dev tooling
`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/agentic-ai.md` concept primer, `.claude/` skills (`add-backend-capability`, `run-backend`, `db-schema`), a `test-verifier` subagent, and permission settings.

## Tests
`tests/test_agent.py` is the first **hermetic** suite (fake LLM + fake tool executor). Live provider smoke tests are marked `integration` (skip on missing key / rate limit).

```
uv run pytest tests/ -m "not integration"   # 29 passed
```

Verified end-to-end in the browser: login → `/chat` → tool calls → multi-turn history, on both Gemini and OpenRouter.

## Review

Ran `/code-review` (high). 10 findings; 9 fixed in this branch, 1 skipped as a follow-up:
- **Follow-up:** admin `list_tickets` via the agent returns *all* tickets with a description that says "the authenticated customer's" — needs pagination/scoping on the agent-facing tool.

## Notes
- New env vars documented in `.env.example`: `LLM_PROVIDER`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_MODEL`, `GEMINI_MODEL`, `AGENT_MAX_STEPS`.
- No per-user rate limiting on `/agent/chat` yet (noted for a fast follow).

author: jf10r
body:
## Summary

Port the ValheimPlus patches affected by Valheim 1.0 to **Valheim 1.0.7 (network version 39)**.

This PR intentionally keeps the compatibility diff narrow: signature changes,
overload selection, transpiler operand updates, map-data type adaptation, and a
rebuild of the bundled ServerSync dependency against the 1.0.7 ABI.

No new ValheimPlus feature or configuration option is introduced.

## Compatibility changes

### Attack / Eitr

`Attack.GetAttackEitr` is overloaded in Valheim 1.0.7.

The V+ patch now targets the shared `GetAttackEitr(Character, ItemDrop.ItemData)`
overload so the configured Blood Magic / Elemental Magic Eitr modifier is not
applied twice when the parameterless overload delegates to it.

### Crafting / Craft From Chest

Valheim 1.0.7 changed the local layout of the affected `Player` methods.

The transpiler operands were updated for
`Player.HaveRequirementItems(Recipe, bool, int, int)` and
`Player.ConsumeResources(Piece.Requirement[], int, int, int)`.

The 1.0.7 IL was inspected to identify the semantic values at the actual
`Inventory.CountItems` / resource-consumption call sites rather than deriving
the changes from local indices alone.

### Repair

Adapt the affected repair transpilers to the current Valheim signatures,
including `EffectList.Create(..., ZDOID)` and
`Character.Message(..., bool, ...)`.

### Guardian Power

`SEMan.AddStatusEffect` now receives a status-effect hash and variant instead of
a `StatusEffect` instance.

The V+ patch now targets `AddStatusEffect(int, bool, int, float, short)` and
resolves the resulting status effect through `SEMan.GetStatusEffect`.

### Map Sync

`Minimap.m_explored` is now a `BitArray`.

A small adapter converts the current `BitArray` input to the existing V+
`bool[]` range encoder. The server-side representation, persistence format and
historical `MapRange` behavior are intentionally left unchanged by this
compatibility PR.

### ServerSync

The bundled `ServerSync.dll` was rebuilt against the Valheim 1.0.7 assemblies.

The previous binary referenced `ZRoutedRpc.Everybody` as a field. In Valheim
1.0.7 that ABI no longer exists in that form and caused a
`MissingFieldException`.

The replacement DLL was rebuilt **without ServerSync source changes** from
`blaxxun-boop/ServerSync` commit
`9aa6f89d360f898cfcd4628cc66b64c9b248f605`.

The rebuilt dependency contains no remaining `ZRoutedRpc.Everybody`
`FieldReference`.

## Validation

Test target: `Valheim 1.0.7`, network version `39`, BepInEx `5.4.23.5`.

### Static compatibility audit

A Mono.Cecil/Harmony compatibility census was run against the deployed
ValheimPlus DLL and the Valheim 1.0.7 game assembly.

Results: `0` missing Valheim Harmony targets, Workbench targets resolved
exactly, `39` explicit transpilers, `7` convention-based transpilers, and `46`
effective transpilers in total.

The affected `Player` transpiler locals and instance argument slots were also
checked against the 1.0.7 IL.

### Runtime / manual validation

Validated in a clean Valheim 1.0.7 QA world:

- ValheimPlus loads and patches without the original startup Harmony failures.
- Crafting from nearby chests.
- Mixed player/chest crafting resource consumption.
- Building requirements using resources in nearby chests.
- Repair.
- Inventory row / stack behavior.
- Workbench behavior.
- Advanced Building Mode.
- Game time/day display.

### Dedicated-server ConfigSync

Validated with an official Valheim 1.0.7 dedicated server and client:

- ServerSync configuration transfer completes.
- `415` V+ configuration entries received.
- A synchronized server value overrides the local client value while connected.
- A local-only value remains local.
- The client's original synchronized value is restored after disconnect.
- No `ZRoutedRpc.Everybody` `MissingFieldException` occurs with the rebuilt
  ServerSync assembly.

## Related work

Related: #153.

Both PRs address Valheim 1.0 compatibility. This PR keeps the change set limited
to compatibility failures reproduced or statically/runtime-attested against
1.0.7, and additionally includes the repair signature updates and ServerSync ABI
relink.

Broader inventory/UI behavior changes from #153 are intentionally not included
unless they are required by a reproduced 1.0.7 regression.

## Remaining validation

This remains a **Draft** while the remaining compatibility checks are completed,
including:

- Eitr behavior with an actual Blood Magic / Elemental Magic attack.
- Guardian Power duration.
- multiplayer MapSync.
- remaining production-system / string-RPC compatibility checks.

Once those checks are complete, the draft can be marked ready for review.

## Scope

This PR intentionally does **not**:

- change configuration defaults;
- add new features;
- alter the historical MapRange encoding behavior;
- perform unrelated refactors;
- change ValheimPlus release/version metadata.

author: zyrtnin
body:
Phase 1 of #598 form 2. **Stacked on #663 (fold decision) and #662 (Phase 0)** — review those first.

## What it does

`pyrxd.glyph.walk_mutable_chain` follows a mutable glyph along its **own spend chain**, one mutable
output at a time, and reports `complete` only when every link verified **and** the final output is
proved unspent. Anything else returns the walked prefix with a reason.

That distinction is the feature. A truncated history is how a superseded value becomes
authoritative: stop one transaction early and a naive walker reports the previous target with no
sign anything is missing — which is what an index was observed doing to a live WAVE name.

## The plan's model was wrong, and measuring corrected it

The plan assumed the chain was the index's history list ordered by spend links, with `transfer` as a
member kind. Measured on `custodian-gate-x7f3.rxd`:

```
458585  f644794b  MINT    mut out 1     <- chain
458591  315b4630  UPDATE  mut out 1     <- chain   (spends f644794b:1)
458591  2cee4847  -       no mut out             (spends 315b4630:0 and :2 - siblings)
458601  3c7b43df  UPDATE  mut out 1     <- chain   (spends 315b4630:1)
```

`2cee4847` is in the index's history, shares a block with a real update, and is spent *from* by the
next real update — **and never touches the token.** It isn't a transfer member of the chain; it
isn't in the chain. It is reported as `excluded`.

**Height cannot order it**, confirmed twice: two of those transactions share height 458591, and
`ars.rxd` has two update envelopes at one height.

**The ref is the identity** — constant across every mutable output from mint to tip. A step carrying
a different one **raises** rather than degrades; following it would splice two tokens' histories
together. Absence degrades, contradiction raises — the split `dmint/chain.py`'s S2 verifier already
draws.

## The repo's reachability guard caught this, and was right

`walk_mutable_chain` had no shipped caller, and `test_no_public_symbol_is_unreachable_from_shipped_code`
said so: *"a capability only tests invoke is not finished."*

Its in-repo caller arrives with Phase 4. Until then it is genuine consumer surface — an indexer or
wallet integrating a mutable glyph needs "what did this token say, and am I looking at its current
state" — so it is exported deliberately through the glyph facade (the same shape as
`verify_creator_signature`), and a test reaches it that way rather than importing the module.

## Verification

| plant | result |
|---|---|
| `complete=True` without a tip proof | 4 tests fail |
| take the candidate list as the chain (no spend-link check) | 5 fail, incl. sibling exclusion |
| drop the ref-continuity check | the contradiction test fails |

The contradiction fixture splices a **real** foreign mutable output onto the **real** spending
transaction, leaving its inputs untouched — serving some other transaction instead would never be
selected as the spender, and the test would pass without exercising the check at all.

Full suite **12,219 passed**, 0 failed.

- Runtime/Prisma persistence edges and incoming Uber root-module composition seams.

## Safety / behavior
- No Uber wire/provider behavior change.
- No module responsibility change or new public contract expansion.
- No Prisma schema or migration change.
- Production Web Clover untouched.

## Validation
Per the requested workflow, no local lint/build/test/scanner was run. Remote CI is the validation gate for this slice.

author: rafaelaraujo004
body:
# Parte 1 — Landing page

Auditoria completa do `index.html` e da sua cadeia de CSS/JS, com a página rodando localmente. **26 achados**, todos medidos no navegador ou localizados no arquivo — nada por impressão. Todos resolvidos, mais o redesenho da metade inferior.

Relatório navegável com o detalhe e a verificação de cada item: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/588ac726-c87a-4cdf-8d09-b32e98c5d56a

## Números

| | antes | depois |
|---|---|---|
| Peso do primeiro load | 5.607 KB | **447 KB** (−92%) |
| Requisições | 126 | **35** |
| Imagens no primeiro paint | 17 (5,2 MB) | **3** |
| JSONs de tema na home | 20 | **4** |
| Cache no navegador | desligado em tudo | 1 ano nas imagens |
| Indicadores do carrossel | 10 para 17 slides | **17** |
| Fontes carregadas e em uso | nenhuma | Sora + Manrope + JetBrains Mono |
| Console numa visita anônima | 4 logs + 2 erros | **zero** |
| `!important` em theme-system.css | 396 | **59** |

## As três coisas que anulavam o design antes de chegar à tela

1. **Nenhuma fonte carregada era usada.** O `<head>` baixava Sora e Manrope (bloqueando o render), mas o sistema de tema apontava para Inter — que não era carregada em lugar nenhum. Todo o texto renderizava na fonte padrão do sistema. Corrigido no CSS, no JS e nos 19 arquivos de tema, que também declaravam Inter.
2. **Overlay do hero fixo sobre 17 fotos de luminância muito diferente.** Nos slides de código e de setup RGB o parágrafo ficava ilegível. Agora são duas camadas mais uma placa de vidro atrás do texto.
3. **Todo conteúdo abaixo da dobra nascia em `opacity: 0`** esperando o IntersectionObserver, com `threshold: 0.18` — que nunca dispara em elemento mais alto que a viewport (a seção de agendamento tem ~1.900px). A página agora nasce visível e o estado inicial da animação só é aplicado quando há JS.

## Bugs corrigidos

- **Carrossel**: 17 slides para 10 indicadores fixos no HTML — nenhum acendia nos 7 últimos, silenciosamente. Agora são gerados a partir de `slides.length`.
- **Badge sazonal**: estava `hidden` e o único script que a revelaria (`index-app.js`) não era carregado por nenhum HTML. Extraída para `seasonal-badge.js`, junto com a correção de ano bissexto no cálculo de dia-do-ano.
- **`vercel.json`** aplicava `Cache-Control: no-store` a `/(.*)`, inclusive às imagens: cada visita repetida rebaixava os 5,2 MB do zero.
- **`<section class="cta-duo">`** ficou aberta e vazia de uma edição anterior, com a seção "Sobre" aninhada dentro dela.
- **Seção "Sobre" invisível em desktop** por uma regra deliberada no `styles2.css`, o que deixava o link "Sobre" do menu sem destino no computador. Reexibida a pedido do autor.
- Console limpo: saíram 5 `console.log` de depuração, o `"Formulário encontrado: null"` de toda carga e o `permission-denied` do Firestore (a gravação remota do tema agora só acontece no admin).

## Metade inferior redesenhada

O formulário de agendamento era **uma coluna só**, com rótulos centralizados sobre inputs de 1065px e campos de 36px de altura. Agora: duas colunas, rótulos à esquerda, campos de 48px, selects com seta própria, total em destaque e coluna de apoio sticky que acompanha a rolagem. No mobile empilha com o contexto (horário, local, como funciona) antes do formulário.

No rodapé os cards eram brancos sobre o fundo escuro — "Instagram", "WhatsApp" e a cidade davam **1,19:1** de contraste. Agora são vidro sobre o próprio fundo, com zero elementos abaixo de 4,5:1.

## Fonte única de preços e contato

Cada preço vivia em 4 lugares e o número de WhatsApp em 14. `site-config.js` passa a ser a fonte; `npm run sync:config` escreve os valores no HTML (para quem chega sem JS) e `npm run check:config` falha se os dois divergirem.

> Nota: o "Configuração de preços" do admin grava em `localStorage`, que é por navegador — ligar a landing page a ele não alcançaria visitante nenhum. Por isso a configuração vive no código. Levar para o Firestore continua possível, agora a partir de um ponto só.

## Como as mudanças de CSS foram provadas

Não por inspeção visual. Para cada passo comparei o **estilo computado de 918 elementos × 37 propriedades**, em desktop e 375px, nos temas claro e escuro — **zero diferenças**. Foi assim que removi 124 declarações e propriedades mortas e 337 dos 396 `!important`.

A fusão das folhas de estilo **não** foi feita, e isso é deliberado: `scripts/css-conflict.js` mostrou 19 conflitos reais em media queries entre `mobile-desktop.css` e `styles2.css`. Juntá-las quebraria o mobile. As ferramentas de análise ficaram em `scripts/css-*.js`.

## Um erro meu, e a rede que criei por causa dele

Ao excluir `*.secure.js` do deploy, levei junto `auth-system.secure.js` e `firebase-config.secure.js`, que o `admin.html` carrega. **O painel teria quebrado em produção sem nenhum sinal em desenvolvimento**, porque localmente os arquivos estão lá. Corrigido, e `npm run check:deploy` agora confere se alguma página publicada depende de arquivo ausente ou excluído. Ele já pegou um segundo caso, este pré-existente: o botão "Documentação Completa" do `guia-orcamentos.html` apontava para um `.md` que o `*.md` excluía — 404 em produção desde sempre.

## Pontos de atenção para a revisão

- **`images/hero/optimized/` (102 arquivos, 5,2 MB) precisa ir para o repositório.** O deploy é estático, sem etapa de build no Vercel, e o `<picture>` aponta para esses arquivos. Sem eles o hero quebra em produção. Regeração: `npm run build:images`.
- **Os `.jpg` originais foram mantidos** como fallback do `<picture>` para navegadores sem AVIF/WebP.
- **`X-XSS-Protection` foi removido** do `vercel.json` (obsoleto e desaconselhado); entraram `Referrer-Policy` e `Permissions-Policy`.
- **Conflito de números não resolvido**: a seção "Sobre" diz "500+ Clientes" e "5+ Anos", enquanto a prova social mais acima diz "+100 PCs otimizados". Os dois aparecem na mesma página. Não mexi — é decisão de conteúdo.
- **13 arquivos JS órfãos** (`main.secure.js`, `index-app.js`, etc.) já não vão para produção, mas continuam no repositório. Apagar é decisão sua.
- **O service worker nunca é registrado**: existe `manifest.json` no HTML, mas o site não é instalável nem funciona offline. É recurso novo, não conserto.

## Verificação

```
npm run check        # check:config + check:deploy — ambos passam
```

Sintaxe validada em todos os JS alterados e balanceamento de chaves conferido nos 6 arquivos CSS. Testado em desktop e 375px, nos temas claro e escuro, sem rolagem horizontal e sem nenhum elemento estourando a viewport.

---

# Parte 2 — Painel administrativo

Mesma abordagem: UI inspecionada no navegador, cada bug reproduzido antes de corrigir.

## Seis bugs de lógica

**1. Clicar no ícone de uma aba não destacava aba nenhuma.**
`switchTab` usava o `event` global e `event.target.classList.add('active')`. Como o alvo do clique costuma ser o `<i>` do ícone e não o `<button>`, a classe ia para o ícone e o operador perdia a referência de onde estava. Chamar a função por código também quebrava (`event` undefined). Reproduzido com `botao.querySelector('i').click()` → `botoesAtivos: 0`.

**2. Taxa de conversão mostrava 233%.**
Dividia serviços concluídos por total de orçamentos — duas populações sem relação. `orcFechados` já era calculado na linha de cima e nunca usado: era o numerador certo.

**3. A projeção do gráfico nunca era desenhada.**
`buildMerged` montava 19 pontos para 13 rótulos: `real` já vinha com 13 posições (7 reais + 6 nulls futuros) e recebia mais 6 da projeção. O Chart.js descarta o excedente em silêncio, e o descartado era justamente a projeção — o botão "Ocultar Projeção" não tinha efeito visível. Confirmado com `serie.data.slice(labels.length)` → 6 pontos com valor, fora do gráfico.

**4. O Gerenciador de Temas não funcionava fora de datas comemorativas.**
Com a automação sazonal ligada (o padrão), `resolveTheme` devolvia `'classico-neutro'` direto sempre que ele existisse — e ele existe sempre. Escolher qualquer tema salvava a configuração e **não mudava nada no s

author: kstrat2001
body:
Closes #2587.

The tool bench read a manifest key into a timeout that reaches only the tool-less single-call paths, while the field that bounds the container path — which every tool-bench task actually uses — was hardcoded absent at the call site. So the key bounded nothing. Like the crawl config key #2586 fixed, and unlike a command-line flag, it lives in a checked-in manifest reused across every run: written once, trusted indefinitely.

## The sweep found three more keys with the same shape

Every key this provider reads was checked, not just the named one:

| key | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the timeout | dropped silently on a string, unbounded on garbage | parsed or refused loudly |
| trial count | same silent drop | fixed |
| seed | same silent drop | fixed |
| the depth ladder | an **all-string** array collapsed to the default with no error; a mixed array silently dropped its string entries | fixed |

That last one is the worst of the four: an author writing the whole ladder as quoted numbers got the built-in default and no indication their configuration was ignored, and one quoted entry among numbers silently disappeared. An explicitly empty array still falls back to the default, which was deliberate and is preserved.

## Zero is refused

A zero bound resolves to an already-expired deadline, meaning an instant kill. Refusing matches both #2586 and the command-line flag for the same knob, whose parser already rejects it.

## The end-to-end pin is parity with #2586, plus breadth

This provider had no dispatch seam at all, so one was added, mirroring the pattern #2586 established.

**A correction to an earlier version of this description**, which claimed to go one hop further: #2586 already has the identical seam and its tests already read the field off the constructed options. This is parity at the same hop. The real addition is breadth — asserting across all six dispatches in the run loop rather than one.

**What this does not cover**, stated rather than implied: the hop from that field into the container's real inactivity budget. That hop is unpinned and is #2596, tracked separately and not claimed here.

## Red-proven four times

Forcing the field absent fails both present-key tests. Forcing it always-populated fails the omitted-key test. Weakening the floor fails both zero-refusal tests. Removing the string fallback fails the string-form tests. Each mutation built clean first, so each is a real mutation rather than a compile error.

629 lab tests green, clippy clean, workspace builds.

## Fix pass: the shipped manifest would have overridden the operator

Review found the built-in manifest set this key, so every run of that workload passed an override — and the resolver gives an override unconditional precedence. An operator whose environment or configuration named a longer bound **used to get their value and would now get darkmux's**, silently, from a value they never typed, with the container told the source was direct operator input. That is a false provenance claim, and the field's own documentation draws exactly that line: it is for input typed at dispatch, explicitly contrasted with a caller-derived fallback that only fills a gap.

The value is deleted from the shipped manifest — it merely restated the built-in default — so that workload now takes the absent-key path and falls through to the standing chain like every other. Pinned by a test that parses the **actual shipped file** and drives it through the real loop.

**Out-of-range now refuses loudly rather than clamping silently**, naming the range. Same reasoning: a field that outranks the operator's own configuration must not quietly substitute a bound they never typed and then attribute it to them.

**Three more from the same review.** A depth above the integer range silently saturated to the maximum, which the task generator turns into a loop of billions of iterations — a hang, from a shape that used to be inert; there is now a named ceiling. An integral float, which is what a script or a format conversion produces, hard-failed; it is now accepted. And the shared error message called a seed a positive integer, which is wrong for a key that accepts zero and misleading for an arbitrary value. The knob's own description called it a per-dispatch cap in two places when it is an **inactivity** cap, and the run fixture now records the effective bound, since it is live and outranks configuration.

643 tests green, up fourteen.

author: dementatech
body:
## What

A school-examination concept (Mid-Term, End of Term, Mock, …), distinct from
`prior_exam_result` (national exams a student sat *before* joining). Same
reference-vs-instance split as `curriculum` / `school_curriculum`.

### `exam_session` — global catalog (super admin)

`{ exam_name, exam_code, description, is_active }`. Full CRUD under
`/api/v1/exams/sessions`; `exam_code` is uppercased and globally unique;
`DELETE` returns **409** while any school still references the session
(deactivate instead). Managed from a new **System → Exam Sessions** page.

### `school_exam` — a school's activated instance (school admin)

A school admin picks an active `exam_session` and **creates + activates** an exam:

- **Academic year and term are auto-attached** from the school's current year /
  current term. `POST /api/v1/exams` returns **400** with a clear message if
  either isn't set.
- **Compulsory dates**: `starts_on`, `ends_on`, `marks_due_on`. A DB check
  constraint *and* the repo enforce `start ≤ end ≤ marks due`. All editable
  later. `marksEntryOpen` is derived (`status = active AND today ∈ [starts_on,
  marks_due_on]`) and returned to the client — the mark-entry module itself is
  out of scope here.
- **Several exams can be active in one term** at once. `POST /:id/close` and
  `POST /:id/reopen` toggle `status` (`active` / `closed`).
- **`name`** defaults to the `exam_session` name and is editable. The **same
  session may be run twice in a term** as long as the names differ — unique on
  `(school_id, academic_year_id, term_id, name)`, so a same-name second pick
  returns **409**.

Managed from a new school-admin **Exams** page (year/term filter, create / edit /
close / reopen / delete).

## Changes

- **Migration** `1700000048000_exams.cjs` — `exam_session` + `school_exam`.
- **New module** `backend/src/modules/exams/` (`exam-sessions` + `school-exams`
  repositories, routes, schemas), registered in `server.ts`.
- `getCurrentAcademicYear` / `getCurrentTerm` added to the academic-structure
  repos and re-exported from `modules/academic-structure/index.ts` (new barrel).
- Frontend: `admin/system/exams` + `school-admin/exams` pages, two form modals
  (`components/admin/exams/`), and a nav entry in each layout.

## Out of scope

Per-subject mark entry, grading schemes, report cards. The date fields are the
hook for a later marks module — nothing writes marks yet.

## Verification

- Backend `typecheck` / `lint` / `build` pass; migration `up` → `down` → `up` clean.
- DB integration script against a real schema: exam_code uppercased + dup → 409;
  `createSchoolExam` with no current term → 400; name defaults to the session
  name, year+term auto-attached; same session same name → 409, different name →
  ok; inactive session → 400; dates out of order → 400; close/reopen flips
  `marksEntryOpen`; delete session in use → 409.
- Server boots; `GET /api/v1/exams/sessions` and `/api/v1/exams` → 401 (registered, guarded).
- Frontend `tsc` / `eslint` / `vitest` / `next build` pass; both new routes compile.

## Note

Branches off `main`; independent of PR #14 (payment code). Migration numbered
`1700000048000` to avoid colliding with #14's `1700000047000`.

author: mpsddd-commits
body:
Closes #488

## Intent (의도)

화면 주인이 청한 것은 하나다.

> 마스터 관련 프롬프트 창이 너무 작고 화면을 크기 조절 가능하게 설정하고 싶다

`MasterDock` 에 너비 `820px` 과 높이 `min(58vh, 520px)` 이 박혀 있어서 넓게 볼 방법이 없었다.
여기에 시연 기준일을 데이터가 있는 날로 옮기는 일을 함께 실었다.

### 설계 결정과 이유

**크기를 정하는 수는 `lib/dock_size.ts` 가 혼자 쥔다.**
화면이 쓰는 CSS 식(`DEFAULT_HEIGHT_CSS` · `MAX_HEIGHT_CSS`)도 같은 상수로 만들어 내보낸다.
`58` 과 `520` 과 `88` 이 두 파일에 각자 적히면 다음 사람이 한쪽만 고친다.

**범위 밖 값은 자르지 않고 기본값으로 되돌린다.**
큰 화면에서 잡아 둔 높이가 작은 기기에서 뒤 화면을 덮는 것을 막아야 한다.
자르면 "왜 하필 이 높이인가" 를 아무도 설명할 수 없어서, 되돌리는 쪽을 택했다.

**상한을 CSS 에도 한 번 더 건다** — `min(617px, 88vh)`.
창을 줄이는 동안에는 JS 가 안 돌기 때문에, 그 사이 프레임을 CSS 가 막는다.

**저장소는 서랍을 열 때 처음 읽는다.**
첫 렌더에서 `localStorage` 를 보면 서버 렌더와 값이 갈려 하이드레이션이 어긋난다.
서랍은 접힌 채로 뜨고 접혀 있는 동안 높이는 0 이라, 열 때 읽으면 충분하다.

**끄는 동안은 `window` 가 듣는다.**
`setPointerCapture` 로도 되지만, 창에 거는 쪽이 마우스·손가락·펜을 가리지 않고 똑같이 돈다.
실측에서 손잡이에만 건 첫 판은 손이 손잡이 밖으로 나가는 순간 추적을 놓쳤다.

**`넓게` 는 너비만 쥔다.**
켤 때 높이를 상한까지 올려 주지만, 그 뒤 손잡이를 끌면 높이만 바뀌고 너비는 그대로다.
미세 조정하다 판이 갑자기 좁아지지 않게 했다.

**대화 화면을 `useMemo` 로 한 번만 만든다.**
끄는 동안 서랍은 프레임마다 다시 그려지는데, 그때마다 대화까지 그리면 끌리는 것이 끊긴다.

### 일부러 하지 않은 것

- `backend/` 는 한 줄도 건드리지 않았다. 다른 판이 `envelope.py` · `sales_flow.py` 를 만지고 있다.
- `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AS_OF` 갈래는 그대로 뒀다. 환경으로 덮을 수 있는 것이 맞다.
- 접힘 구조(`hidden` 이 아니라 높이 0)를 바꾸지 않았다. 되묻던 확인이 사라지면 안 된다.
- 프론트에 검사 관례가 없어서(테스트 러너·테스트 파일 0건) 이 판에서 새로 만들지 않았다. 화면 확인으로 대신했다.

### 수용 기준

- 손잡이를 끌면 높이가 바뀐다.
- 새로고침해도 그 높이다.
- 넓게 보기가 켜지고 꺼진다.
- 접었다 펴도 대화가 남는다.
- 저장된 값이 범위 밖이면 기본값으로 돌아간다.
- `localStorage` 가 터져도 정상 동작한다.
- 좁은 화면에서 안 깨진다.
- 콘솔 오류 0건.

## What Changed (변경 내용)

**`frontend/src/lib/dock_size.ts` (새 파일)**
서랍 크기의 수를 정하는 곳이다.
하한 `200px`, 상한 `88vh`, 기본값 `min(58vh, 520px)`, 화살표 한 번에 `24px`.
`readDockSize` · `writeDockSize` 는 `session.ts` · `demo_as_of.ts` 와 같은 모양으로 `localStorage` 를 try/catch 로 감싼다.
`sanitizeHeight` 가 범위 밖 값을 기본값으로 되돌린다.
저장 키는 `haetdeul.dock_size`, 모양은 `{ height: number, wide: boolean }`.

**`frontend/src/components/console/MasterDock.tsx`**
펼쳤을 때만 위 모서리에 손잡이 줄이 붙는다.
`role="separator"` · `tabIndex={0}` · `aria-valuenow` 로 화살표 위아래 조절과 포커스 표시(초록 손잡이)를 받는다.
오른쪽에 `넓게` / `원래대로` 토글이 있다.
끄는 동안에는 `transition-[height]` 를 떼서 따라오는 것이 늦지 않게 했다.
저장은 손을 뗄 때 한 번이다 — 끄는 동안 매 프레임 쓰면 저장소가 쉴 새 없이 돈다.
접힘 구조는 그대로다: 높이 0 + `display:none`, 대화는 언마운트되지 않는다.

**`frontend/src/lib/demo_as_of.ts`**
`DEFAULT_AS_OF` 를 `2026-01-20` 에서 `2026-01-30` 으로 옮기고 실측 근거를 주석에 적었다.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_AS_OF` 갈래는 그대로다. `frontend/` 에 `.env` 가 하나도 없어서(실측 2026-09-10) 지금 쓰이는 것은 코드값이다.

**`.gitignore`**
`.claude/` 를 넣어 **저장소에서 뺀다.** 에이전트 작업 설정이라 사람마다 환경이 다르고, 남의 것이 들어오면 그 자리에서 안 돈다 — `launch.json` 의 포트·실행기가 특히 그렇다.

앞 이름 없이 적어 뿌리와 하위 폴더가 다 걸린다.

```text
git check-ignore -v frontend/.claude/launch.json  →  .gitignore:55
git check-ignore -v .claude/settings.json         →  .gitignore:55
```

⚠️ 화면 확인에 쓴 `frontend/.claude/launch.json` 은 **이 판에서 다시 뺐다.** 확인은 그것으로 했지만 저장소에 남길 것이 아니다.

### 기본값과 끄는 방법

- 아무것도 저장돼 있지 않으면 예전과 같은 `min(58vh, 520px)` 이다. 이 변경 전과 첫 화면이 같다.
- 정한 크기를 지우려면 브라우저 저장소에서 `haetdeul.dock_size` 를 지우면 된다.
- 기준일은 `NEXT_PUBLIC_AS_OF` 로 덮을 수 있다.

### 미결

- `npm run build` 가 `/_global-error` 프리렌더에서 깨진다. **이 변경 이전부터 그렇다** (아래 Testing 참고).
  Next.js 16.3.0 내부 문제이고 이 판의 범위 밖이라 손대지 않았다.

## Risk Assessment (위험도)

⚠️ Medium

동작은 브라우저에서 전부 확인했지만, 저장소 상태와 뷰포트 크기에 따라 갈리는 경로가 여럿이라 상태 관리 복잡도가 있다.

## Testing (검증)

프론트에 테스트 러너가 없다 — `package.json` 에 test 스크립트가 없고, `vitest`/`jest` 도, 테스트 파일도 0건이다.
없는 관례를 이 판에서 만들지 않고 **실제로 띄워서 화면으로 확인**했다.

워크트리에서 `next dev -p 3100` 을 띄우고 `/console` 을 열어 DOM 을 직접 읽었다.
백엔드는 안 띄웠다 — 화면 뼈대만 보면 되는 일이라 표 자리에 `[500]` 이 뜨지만 서랍 동작에는 상관이 없다.

| 확인한 것 | 결과 |
|---|---|
| 손잡이를 끌어 높이가 바뀌는가 | `499` → `617` · 저장소에 `{"height":617,"wide":false}` |
| 끄는 동안 글자가 딸려 잡히는가 | 안 잡힌다 (`getSelection()` 빈 문자열) |
| 새로고침해도 그 높이인가 | 다시 열었을 때 `min(617px, 88vh)` |
| 화살표 위아래로 되는가 | `617` → `689` (↑×3) → `569` (↓×5), 한 번에 24px |
| 위 상한에서 멈추는가 | ↑×30 → `757` (`round(860 × 0.88)` = 757) |
| 아래 하한에서 멈추는가 | ↓×40 → `200` |
| 포커스가 보이는가 | `:focus-visible` 참 · 손잡이가 초록으로 |
| 넓게 토글이 도는가 | 너비 `820` → `1042`, 높이 `757`, `aria-pressed="true"` |
| 원래대로가 도는가 | 너비 `1042` → `820`, 높이 `499` |
| 접었다 펴도 대화가 남는가 | 입력칸에 넣은 `fold-test-12345` 가 접힘·펼침 뒤에도 그대로 |
| 접힘에서 언마운트되지 않는가 | 접힌 상태에서 판 높이 `0px` · `aria-hidden="true"` · 입력칸은 DOM 에 살아 있고 값도 그대로 |
| 저장된 값이 범위 밖이면 | `5000` 을 심고 새로고침 → `499` (기본값) |
| localStorage 가 터져도 도는가 | `Storage.prototype.getItem`/`setItem` 이 던지게 바꾼 뒤 → 저장값 `300` 대신 기본값 `499` 로 열리고, 화살표 조절도 그대로 돈다. 잡히지 않은 오류 0건 |
| 좁은 화면에서 안 깨지는가 | 뷰포트 `577px` (md 아래) · 사이드바 대신 상단 탭 · aside 왼쪽 0 · 손잡이 483px · 넓게 버튼이 오른쪽 안에 들어옴 · `document.scrollWidth == innerWidth` (가로 넘침 없음) |
| 콘솔 오류 0건인가 | React·하이드레이션 오류 0건. 남은 것은 백엔드를 안 띄운 데서 오는 `/api/screen` 500 뿐 |

### 파이프라인

```text
npm run lint    ✅ 통과 (exit 0, 경고 0건)
npm run build   ⚠️ TypeScript ✅ 통과 · 정적 내보내기에서 실패
```

빌드 실패는 **이 변경 이전부터 있던 것**이다. 같은 워크트리에서 변경을 `git stash` 로 치우고
깨끗한 `origin/dev`(`328c620`)로 돌린 뒤 같은 자리에서 같은 오류가 났다.

```text
Error occurred prerendering page "/_global-error".
Error [InvariantError]: Invariant: Expected workStore to be initialized. This is a bug in Next.js.
Export encountered an error on /_global-error/page: /_global-error, exiting the build.
```

Next.js 16.3.0 이 스스로 만드는 페이지라 이 판이 건드릴 자리가 아니다.
이 변경이 책임지는 구간(컴파일 + TypeScript)은 둘 다 통과한다.

## Evidence (증거)

- Evidence: `npm run lint` exit 0, 출력 없음 (경고 0건).
- Evidence: `npm run build` 에서 `Compiled successfully` + `Finished TypeScript` 뒤 `/_global-error` 에서 중단.
- Evidence: 같은 워크트리에서 `git stash` 후 `origin/dev` 로 빌드해도 같은 `/_global-error` 오류 — 기존 문제임을 확인.
- Evidence: 끌기 전후 DOM 측정 — `aria-valuenow` `499` → `617`, `localStorage["haetdeul.dock_size"]` = `{"height":617,"wide":false}`.
- Evidence: 새로고침 뒤 판의 인라인 스타일 `height: min(617px, 88vh)`.
- Evidence: 화살표 눌림 뒤 `aria-valuenow` `689` / `569` / 상한 `757` / 하한 `200`.
- Evidence: 넓게 켠 뒤 컨테이너 너비 `1042`, 끈 뒤 `820`.
- Evidence: 접힌 상태 DOM — 판 `style.height = "0px"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, 입력칸 값 `fold-test-12345` 유지.
- Evidence: 저장값 `5000` 을 심고 새로고침 → `aria-valuenow="499"`.
- Evidence: `Storage.prototype` 을 던지게 바꾼 뒤 열기 → `aria-valuenow="499"`, 화살표 4번 → `595`, `window.onerror` 수집 0건.
- Evidence: 뷰포트 `577px` 측정 — `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` 577 == `innerWidth` 577.
- Evidence: 콘솔 로그 전체에서 오류는 `/api/screen` 500 두 줄뿐 (백엔드 미기동).
- Evidence: 스크린샷 — 기본 높이로 열린 콘솔 · 끌어서 키운 콘솔 · 넓게 켠 콘솔 · 하한에서 초록 포커스 손잡이 · 접힌 상태. 세션 기록에 남아 있다.

author: luiscantupagos-bit
body:
Normaliza la **presentación documental** y reorganiza el módulo como una **biblioteca por áreas**, con branding visible **C3 Sentinel**. No toca el motor de datos DOC-001 ni las referencias DOC-002; sin rename técnico masivo.

## Branding
- **C3 Sentinel** como nombre visible: favicon, marca "S", sidebar, login, título/metadata.
- **0** nuevas ocurrencias visibles de "GAPSI Sentinel" en `src/app`.
- Sin rename técnico masivo (repo, tablas, migraciones y variables internas conservan sus nombres).

## Presentación documental
- **Procedimiento simplificado**: `#` / Actividad / Descripción / Responsable. Se eliminan **Evidencia** y **Observaciones** del estándar visible.
- Datos legacy `evidencia`/`observaciones` **preservados** en `structured_content` (no destructivo) y **no renderizados**.
- `@` y `//` intactos en Descripción.
- **Header** documental con marca de la organización; **footer** de confidencialidad + atribución discreta a C3 Sentinel (`www.c3digital.com.mx`).
- **Print CSS** (`@media print`: repetición de `thead`, control de `page-break`).
- Modos `editor_preview` / `published_document`; omisión de secciones/campos opcionales vacíos en publicado.

## Tema documental
- Tabla `document_themes` por organización; colores **HEX validados** (primary/secondary/accent), sin inyección CSS.
- Aplicado **solo al render del documento**, no al tema global de la app. RLS por organización; fallback seguro al default.
- Configuración en `/dashboard/documents/settings` con vista previa en vivo.

## Biblioteca
- Dashboard documental con buscador, KPIs clickeables, **carpetas por área** y navegación **área → tipo**.
- **Listado maestro** (`/dashboard/documents/master`) con filtros (búsqueda/tipo/área/estado/sitio/origen).
- Estados en **español** (sin estados internos crudos).

## Control de cambios
- Tabla automática desde el versionado (Versión/Fecha/Modificación/Realizado por).
- v1.0 sin notas → "Documento nuevo"; `change_notes` **obligatorio** para publicar versiones > v1.0; corte histórico por versión vista.

## Compatibilidad
- Documentos estructurados DOC-001, referencias `@`/`//` DOC-002, `rich_text` y `external` intactos.
- Legacy `evidence`/`observations` preservado al re-guardar (match por nombre de actividad; no resucita eliminadas ni hereda a nuevas).

## Migración
- `20260911000000_document_presentation` — `CREATE TABLE document_themes` + FK + RLS + grants.
- **0 DROP TABLE, 0 DROP COLUMN**. No modifica migraciones previas.

## Tests / gates
- `npm test` **500/500** · `test:db` **171/171** · `build` verde · `format:check`/`typecheck` limpios · `lint` solo warning preexistente ajeno.

## FOLLOW-UP (no incluidos en este PR)
- Logo de organización aún no cableado a storage real.
- Algunas metadata históricas (fechas/área) no son versionadas.
- Definición del default "Activos" del listado maestro (effective + in_review).
- `dueSoon` = 30 días hardcoded.
- Control de cambios puede incluir borradores hasta el corte.
- Gaps menores de cobertura (ruta de área inválida, filtros combinados de master, etc.).
- "Página X de Y" pendiente de un export PDF real.

## Fuera de alcance
DOC-003 (programas ejecutables — congelado aparte), notificaciones, IA, OCR, Microsoft/Google, DOC-004, TASK-012.

author: ryanvanmass
body:
## Summary
- Adds a third Connection Manager connection family: manually-registered GL.iNet routers, each opening a management dashboard tab (Overview, Clients, WiFi, VPN status, Reboot) via the third-party `python-glinet` library.
- `python-glinet` is GPLv3+ licensed; rather than relicense it-toolbox (Apache-2.0), it's treated as an optional, not-bundled runtime dependency — never listed in `pyproject.toml`, gated behind `try: from pyglinet import GlInet; except ImportError: GlInet = None` (same pattern as FreeRDP/SpiceWidget). See `docs/glinet-dashboard-status.md`.
- Each host's password is encrypted to the user's SSH key (`core/settings.py`'s `encrypt_glinet_password`/`decrypt_glinet_password`, generalized from the existing JumpCloud API key encryption) and stored alongside the rest of the host record in `glinet_hosts.json` — never in plaintext, and never decrypted until a dashboard is actually opened.
- v1 scope: read/write WiFi SSID/password/enabled, read-only VPN tunnel status, reboot, connected-clients list, and an at-a-glance overview. VPN tunnel configuration and full WiFi parameter coverage are explicitly deferred (see docs).
- New Settings page section shows whether `python-glinet` is installed.

## Test plan
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` — 392 passed
- [x] New unit tests: `tests/modules/connection_manager/test_glinet_client.py`, `tests/widgets/test_glinet_dashboard_widget.py`, GL.iNet additions to `tests/core/test_settings.py`, `tests/modules/connection_manager/test_main_view_sessions.py`, `tests/modules/settings/test_settings_view.py`
- [ ] Manual verification against a real GL.iNet router (not done in this session — `python-glinet`'s own field-name mappings are best-effort from its README/example docs, flagged in `glinet_client.py`'s module docstring)

author: npflood
body:
## What

`SourceSynchronizer#process_row` treats a locally deleted record as a kept tombstone whether the upstream row still carries the record or lists it as deleted again. `FpiRunPredictor#classify` mirrors the change. One spec case each.

## Why

Found in the FPI staging rehearsal (fpi-connector plan M3 step 6): after accepting a `source_deletion` conflict (the record is soft-deleted), re-running the same payload opened a **new** `source_deletion` conflict on the already-deleted record instead of counting `tombstone_kept`. The old condition `record.deleted_at.present? && !deleted` only covered the case where upstream had stopped listing the record.

The connector's deletion ledger emits each disappearance once per environment, so in normal operation this only bites on a re-delivery or a repeated run, but a tombstone must win either way.

## Test plan

- [x] `spec/services/source_synchronizer*_spec.rb`, `spec/tasks/fpi_run_predictor_spec.rb`, `spec/tasks/fpi_sync_run_spec.rb`, `spec/models/sync_conflict_spec.rb`: 77 examples, 0 failures
- [x] rubocop clean on the changed files
- [ ] after deploy: rerun the staging deletion rehearsal payload; expect `tombstones kept 1` and no new conflict on the accepted record
