author: wittjeff
body:
`ChartExtractionModelGraniteVisionV4` loads `ibm-granite/granite-vision-4.1-4b` with `trust_remote_code=True` unconditionally. The `modeling.py` bundled with the pinned checkpoint calls `create_causal_mask(..., cache_position=...)`, and transformers removed that argument in huggingface/transformers#45884 (released in 5.9.0). Since #4150 (2.125.0) relaxed the transformers caps, a plain `pip install docling[granite_vision]` resolves to transformers 5.16.x and chart extraction fails with:

```
TypeError: create_causal_mask() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cache_position'
```

transformers ships `granite4_vision` natively from 5.8.0, and the model card says `trust_remote_code=True` is only needed on older versions. However, `AutoModel*.from_pretrained` prefers remote code whenever `trust_remote_code=True` and the config carries an `auto_map`, so docling was forcing the stale bundled code over the native implementation.

This PR only passes `trust_remote_code=True` when the installed transformers is older than 5.8.0. The pinned checkpoint's `config.json` already declares `model_type: granite4_vision`, and its `tokenizer_config.json` already sets `padding_side: left`, so no other loader changes are needed. The `merge_lora_adapters` guard becomes a no-op on the native class (the checkpoint ships no adapters).

Not yet done: an end-to-end run of `docs/examples/chart_extraction.py` on transformers 5.16.1 comparing native vs. remote-code output. Opening as a draft until that is confirmed.

body: ## What this adds A 35-page technical roadmap taking GardenWise/RootVio from the current GitHub Pages plus hand-provisioned AWS estate to a codified platform, delivered as a print-ready PDF with its HTML source. - `docs/GardenWise-Cloud-Platform-Roadmap.pdf` — the rendered document, A4, 35 pages - `docs/roadmap/cloud-platform-roadmap.html` — the source, self-contained (no external assets or fonts) - `scripts/build-roadmap-pdf.mjs` — regenerates the PDF with headless Chrome or Edge ## Basis The current-state assessment was verified against `main @ dc4e305` rather than assumed. It records what is present — React 19.2 / Vite 8 SPA deployed to Pages at `rootivio.app`, a 10-route Express API running both locally and as a Lambda through `@vendia/serverless-express`, RDS PostgreSQL/PostGIS, DynamoDB planner layouts, Firebase auth, and the Python ONNX weed-scan container Lambda — and what is absent: - No infrastructure as code of any kind (no Terraform, CloudFormation, SAM or CDK) - No backend deployment pipeline; API releases are manual zip uploads - No automated tests; CI runs `typecheck` and `lint` only - No metrics, alerting or tracing beyond `GET /api/health` and `console.log` - Docker and `k8s/` work added in `6be8279` and reverted in `dc4e305` - The security plan living in dangling commit `107129f`, reachable from no branch ## Structure Five phases across 22 weeks, each gated on demonstrable exit criteria: baseline and guardrails, Terraform foundation (import-first), GitHub Actions delivery with OIDC, containers and Amazon EKS, Prometheus observability, then hardening, DR and FinOps. Includes a target architecture diagram, a phase Gantt, a cost model, a ten-item risk register and eight open decisions with defaults. The document is explicit that EKS is the largest cost increase in the plan (roughly $455/month versus $185 on an ECS Fargate variant) and frames it as a decision to be made deliberately at week 9 rather than assumed. ## Notes for review - The PDF is committed because it is the deliverable; the HTML is committed so it stays editable and diffable. - Page numbers and the table of contents are generated at render time from document order, so reordering pages does not require renumbering by hand. - Every page was verified to fit within its A4 page box, with no clipped content. No application code, CI configuration or infrastructure is changed by this PR.

author: frankiedeane
body:
## 1. Topbar rotativo (descubrimiento de secciones)

La barra celeste de arriba arranca con el mensaje de marca de siempre y, a los 5 segundos, empieza a rotar **14 datos reales del sitio**, cada uno linkeado a su sección: mapa de spots, costa 3D, calculadora de equipo, glosario, comparador de marcas, cámaras en vivo, videos por nivel, riders, FAQ, encuesta, etc.

El orden se mezcla (Fisher-Yates) en cada carga, así dos visitas seguidas no ven lo mismo y cada visitante descubre otra parte del sitio. Detalles: pausa la rotación en hover y cuando el link tiene foco de teclado (no le sacamos el mensaje a alguien que lo está por clickear), frena si la pestaña pasa a segundo plano, y respeta `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Elegí reusar el topbar existente en vez de agregar un banner nuevo: la página ya tiene cookie banner + popup rotativo de cafecito/sponsor, y un cuarto elemento hubiera sido ruido.

## 2. Recalibración de vientos por spot

Tenías razón con Paso de la Patria. Varios rangos venían inflados: mezclaban **ráfaga máxima** con **rango navegable habitual**. El criterio que usé para corregir es coherencia interna con **San Isidro (12-25 kn)**, que es el spot que conocés de primera mano — si San Isidro, que es ventoso, está en 12-25, un spot del litoral no puede estar en 18-35.

| Spot | Antes | Ahora |
|---|---|---|
| **Paso de la Patria** | N 18-35 kn | **N/NE 12-25 kn** |
| Laguna Mar Chiquita | N/NE 15-35 kn | N/NE 15-28 kn |
| Lago Lolog | S/SO 18-35 kn | S/SO 15-30 kn |
| Nahuel Huapi — Dina Huapi | O/NO 20-40 kn | O/NO 15-35 kn |
| Puerto Madryn | S 18-35 kn | S 15-30 kn |
| Corrientes — Río Paraná | N/NE 15-28 kn | N/NE 12-22 kn |
| Mar del Plata — Waikiki | S/SE 15-30 kn | S/SE 12-25 kn |
| Embalse Río Tercero | S/SO 15-30 kn | S/SO 12-25 kn |
| Lago Lacar | SO 15-28 kn | SO 12-25 kn |
| Lago Gutiérrez | O/SO 15-30 kn | O/SO 12-28 kn |
| Rawson — Playa Unión | S 15-30 kn | S 15-28 kn |

Sin cambios (ya eran conservadores): San Isidro, Pinamar, Chascomús, Paraná Setúbal, Gualeguaychú, Playa Bonita. Dina Huapi queda como el más ventoso del listado, que sí se sostiene para la Patagonia.

También corregí lo que se volvió incoherente con los números nuevos:
- Textos de `months`/`safety` que citaban "40 kn" o "el spot con más viento garantizado del país".
- **Paso de la Patria**: el tag `Viento fuerte` pasó a `Corriente fuerte`. Lo que lo hace nivel avanzado es la corriente de la confluencia Paraná-Paraguay, no la intensidad del viento — que es lo que ya decía su propio texto de seguridad.

Y agregué la aclaración que ataca la ambigüedad de fondo, bajo el dato de viento en el panel: *"Rango habitual navegable, no ráfagas máximas. Chequeá siempre el pronóstico del día."*

⚠️ **Importante sobre esta corrección**: desde este entorno no tengo salida a internet (el proxy bloquea Windguru/Open-Meteo), así que **no pude validar contra datos de estación reales**. Los valores nuevos salen de climatología regional + coherencia con San Isidro. Son conservadores a propósito — si algún spot de tu red te dice que su rango real es otro, decímelo y lo ajusto puntual.

author: maria-rcks
body:
The client only clears a thread's pending `titleRegeneration` when the server's completion event arrives, so any lost completion leaves the row dimmed and pins the menu entry at `Regenerating…` / disabled forever — and the guard `if (isRegeneratingTitle) return;` then swallows every later click with no toast and no retry, which is what makes the action look permanently dead.

This bounds the pending state instead of trusting it indefinitely: `isTitleRegenerationPending` treats a request older than 15 minutes as lost, so the row un-dims, the menu item becomes clickable again, and the retry re-issues the request — which the decider accepts and which replaces the stale `requestId`. The window is sized for the bulk path: the server regenerates on a single serial worker and one generation runs to its provider's own limit (180s for most, unbounded for OpenCode), so `Regenerate titles (N)` legitimately leaves later threads pending for several minutes. Same shape and clock-skew handling as the existing `QUEUED_TURN_START_GRACE_MS` bound next to it, which exists for the identical "permanently unsettleable" failure. Web and mobile both route through the shared helper. Web menus read the clock when they open; the mobile row menus are memoized, so they now take the minute clock the screens already keep as a dependency and the entry re-enables on the next tick after the window. Web row dimming stays as rendered until the next thread event, like the neighbouring snooze guard.

This is a client-side mitigation: it closes the one-way door so the user can retry, it does not change why a completion fails to arrive.

Scope note: I could not reproduce the reporter's follow-up claim that the server never dispatches the completion on remote environments, and I did not change server behaviour — the underlying leak is still open, hence `Refs` rather than `Fixes`. I did confirm the client applies `thread.meta-updated` correctly (`applyThreadDetailEvent` and the shell stream both carry `titleRegeneration` end to end, with no remote-vs-local branch), so the original "the client never consumes the completion" framing is not the defect.

Verified (all from the package dir with the workspace `vp`):
- `vp test run src/state/threadSnoozed.test.ts` (client-runtime) — 33 passed.
- `vp test run src/components/Sidebar.logic.test.ts src/components/threadActionMenu.logic.test.ts` (web) — 168 passed.
- `vp test run src/features/threads/thread-title-regeneration-menu.test.ts src/features/threads/threadListV2.test.ts` (mobile) — 74 passed.
- `vp run --filter @t3tools/client-runtime|@t3tools/web|@t3tools/mobile typecheck` — all pass.
- `vp lint` on the seven changed files — pass; warning counts match origin/main file for file, no new findings.

Refs #7328

UI evidence: unverified. The browser preview host was unavailable in this session, so the changed interaction was not exercised in a real client.

author: bradbor23
body:
Started as three doc gaps in the portal UI. Finding them meant running the docs build, which turned out to be **failing on main**.

---

## The deploy has been broken for six merges

`Deploy: Documentation` has failed on every push to main since 2026-09-09 20:54. Same cause each time:

```
(!) Found dead link ./skills in file docs/user-guide/plugins.md
[vitepress] 2 dead link(s) found.
```

`user-guide/plugins.md` links to `skills.md` twice. The Skills guide is `docs/skills.md`, so both resolve to `docs/user-guide/skills.md`, which does not exist. The **in-app** guide gets away with it because the Blazor build copies `docs/skills.md` in beside the user-guide pages; the website does not.

Nobody saw it because the failure is in a deploy that runs *after* merge, not in a gate that runs on the PR — the same shape as [#84](https://github.com/bradbor23/botnexus/issues/84).

`npm run docs:build` is green on this branch, for the first time in at least six merges.

## The nav, in both places — and they are not the same place

- **`docs/.vitepress/config.mts` is what actually builds the site.** Its User Guide was missing Tools, Notifications, Plugins and the new Portal page.
- **`mkdocs.yml` builds nothing.** Nothing invokes it; it survives only in workflow path filters. It is still read as documentation, so it now lists all thirteen guide pages ordered to match `guide-index.json` rather than inventing a second reading order, and no longer lists `websocket-protocol.md`, deleted in `950b61218`.

## The original three gaps

**1. A documented feature that does not exist.** `channels/signalr.md` described **My Sections**. `c8bf7f1d` deleted it — panel, API client, state service, five test files. The same block described a sidebar holding the navigation, which `52f7ce9d` moved to a toolbar.

**2. The portal shell was undocumented.** The toolbar and its *measured* overflow menu, sub-navigation as a second row, the conversation sidebar's **allow-list** (`/`, `/chat`, `/chat/*`, `/agent`, `/agent/*`) and why the burger and splitter are hidden with it, and the loading skeletons — including that the shapes are `aria-hidden` with one polite live region.

**3. Activity's filter bar.** Search matches title **or agent id**. Agent and Status stayed; Recency, Origin, Pin state and Live state went behind **More filters**, whose badge counts only the *hidden* set facets.

The structural fix is that there is now a portal page at all. The portal UI lived inside the SignalR **channel** page, which is why portal changes kept missing the docset.

## Verification

Claims read from `MainLayout.razor`, `PortalLoadingSkeleton.razor` and `ActivityDashboard.razor` at tip, not from the commit messages that introduced them. `npm run docs:build` green.

**Merge this before [#89](https://github.com/bradbor23/botnexus/pull/89)** — the dead-link fix lives here only, deliberately, so the two PRs do not both carry the same two lines.

body:
## Summary
Bundles the "Kobi"-rebranded Qwen Code Desktop (Electron GUI) into the offline
installer and adds selectable packaging flavors so the installer can be built
as a full combined bundle, GUI-only, or CLI-only.

## Changes
- **Kobi Desktop (GUI) integration** (`27dc1dd`)
  - `desktop-brand/`: tooling to fork upstream qwen-code desktop and rebrand it
    to "Kobi", vendoring the same qwen-code tarball the CLI uses.
  - `make.sh`: package `Kobi-Desktop-*.exe` when present; extract portable
    MinGit into `Kobi_Runtime\git` (qwen-code runtime needs git; the Desktop
    fails to run without it on git-less PCs).
  - `Install-Kobi.ps1` / `Uninstall-Kobi.ps1`: merge vLLM settings into
    `~/.qwen/settings.json`, silently (un)install the Desktop (per-user), and
    register bundled `git\cmd` on the User PATH.
- **Packaging flavors in make.sh** (`509469c`)
  - `windows-gui|gui`: GUI-centric package, omits CLI agent + skills (~26% smaller).
  - `linux`: portable Linux bundle (no Desktop).
  - `NO_GIT=1` / `NO_SKILLS=1` / `NO_DESKTOP=1` env vars for trimmed builds,
    e.g. `NO_DESKTOP=1 NO_SKILLS=1 ./make.sh windows` for a CLI-only package.
- **README** (`a5b702e`): document the Desktop usage, rebuild flow, and the

author: yemfan
body:
Found while testing helmsmart.ai in Simplified Chinese. Requesting a reset link for a real address put a red box under the Chinese form reading:

> Email address "michael.yes@mail.com" is invalid

## The security half

`resetPasswordForEmail` returns success for an address with no account **on purpose**, so this screen cannot be used to enumerate who has one. Supabase does not always hold that line — it answers `400 email_address_invalid` for an address on a reserved or blocked domain, and per [supabase/auth#2702](https://github.com/supabase/auth/issues/2702) that check only runs **once the user exists**.

`authErrorMessage` ended in `return message`, so we forwarded it. The screen then said one thing for a real account and another for an absent one:

| | before |
|---|---|
| account exists | red box: `Email address "…" is invalid` |
| no account | green: `请查收邮件 — 我们已发送密码重置链接。` |

One submission per guess. The upstream inconsistency is Supabase's; **publishing it was ours.**

## The i18n half

That same `return message` was the last English on an otherwise Chinese page — it failed *open* into English for every Supabase failure nobody had enumerated yet, which is the thing #1693 exists to prevent.

## Changes

- `authErrorMessage` maps the unrecognised tail to `errors.unexpected` and logs the raw text. The detail was worth keeping; it just isn't the user's.
- `requestPasswordReset` answers identically whether or not Supabase refused. **Rate limiting is still reported** — it's a fact about the caller, not the address, and swallowing it would strand someone on "check your email" for a mail that was never sent.
- `errors.unexpected` added to `en`, `zh-Hans`, `es`. Locale-parity guards pass.

Deliberate trade: an undeliverable address is now indistinguishable from a delivered one. That's what the non-disclosure requires, and it's why the log line matters — it's the only place the real reason survives.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npx vitest run` → **29 files / 215 tests green**, including the i18n parity, residual-English and missing-key guards.

Tests assert the two properties by name: a refused address and a sent one return byte-identical state, and an unmapped error never reaches the screen. Reverting either half fails **6 of the 9**, one of them on the literal string above.

Not verified in a browser — it's a server action against Supabase, so it needs a deploy. Worth one manual reset attempt on preview to confirm the red box is gone.

### Motivation

- Remove unsupported production-scale claims and prevent synthetic or missing artifacts from surfacing as real model evidence. 
- Make the demo a reproducible portfolio showcase that clearly distinguishes synthetic fixtures, offline smoke artifacts, and trusted saved artifacts. 
- Preserve substantive modeling code (including the ensemble) while ensuring serving and evaluation contracts are honest and auditable.

### Description

- UI: Rewrote and relabeled maintained Next.js pages to present an evidence-first portfolio message and visible fixture notices, removed hard-coded KPI marketing (accuracy, predictions served, uptime) from maintained pages, and marked the legacy dashboard as historical. (files under `frontend/app/*`, `frontend/components/*`, `dashboard/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`).
- Serving & API: Removed the previous in-memory fallback model behavior and introduced `ModelUnavailableError` so missing/untrusted artifacts fail explicitly; added provenance to prediction results (`provenance: {source_kind, model_version, observed_at}`) and surfaced provenance in API responses and the client. (`ml/serving/predictor_v2.py`, `api/endpoints/predictions.py`, `frontend/lib/api-client.ts`).
- Cache & safety: Partitioned Redis cache keys by `source_kind` and `model_version` and include provenance in cached payloads to avoid cross-contaminating synthetic fixtures and real-model results. (`ml/serving/predictor_v2.py`).
- Synthetic artifacts: Replaced the ad-hoc dummy generator with an isolated deterministic artifact generator that refuses to write into a serving `models/` directory, refuses non-empty outputs without `--overwrite`, and writes `provenance.json` with seed, feature contract, generator command, commit hash/dirty state, and artifact SHA-256s. (`scripts/create_dummy_model.py`).
- Validation: Added Pydantic validation to reject non-finite prediction/metric values while preserving legitimate zeroes. (`api/models.py`).
- Documentation: Rewrote `README.md` for technical reviewers and added `docs/PORTFOLIO_EVIDENCE.md` describing route maps, evidence rules, limitations, and post-merge actions. Cleared unsupported marketing claims. (`README.md`, `docs/PORTFOLIO_EVIDENCE.md`).
- Tests: Added focused regression tests exercising missing-model behavior, cache partitioning, synthetic artifact isolation, zero/non-finite checks, and UI fixture labeling. (`tests/test_provenance_contract.py`).
- Minor: Updated `scripts/deploy_check.py` to look for fixture provenance notices instead of old accuracy strings and adjusted small API metadata strings. (`scripts/deploy_check.py`, `api/main.py`).

### Testing

- Ran focused unit/integration tests: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_provenance_contract.py` — 6 tests passed (1 SQLAlchemy deprecation warning). 
- Python compile checks: `python -m py_compile` on the changed modules — succeeded for the updated modules. 
- Frontend type check: `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` — passed.
- Frontend production build: `cd frontend && npm run build` — Next.js static generation completed successfully for the maintained app (build reports that ESLint was not available in this environment). 
- Synthetic artifact smoke: `python scripts/create_dummy_model.py --output-dir /tmp/synthetic-demo --samples 40` — created isolated artifacts and produced `provenance.json` with hashes and metadata; generator refuses to write into `models/` and to overwrite without explicit `--overwrite`. 

Notes on blocked or environment-limited checks: frontend linting is interactive/blocked because ESLint dev-dependency is not installed in this environment and npm registry access returned HTTP 403 when attempting to add it; the legacy Create React App `dashboard` build is blocked because its tracked `public/index.html` is absent; no browser automation or remote deployment was performed, so desktop/mobile visual verification and public deployment checks remain to be run by the repository owner after merge.

author: gabriel7silva
body:
Codex reviewed #18 at `a0bb9f22`, two commits behind that branch's head, and raised five items. One had already been fixed by a later commit; the other four were real and are addressed here, one commit each.

## What was wrong

**Let a failed GPU wait stop the work that was waiting on it** — `waitFence` grew a time limit when the freeze was fixed, so it can now return having given up. Only `applyWorldRayEffects` read that result; everything else carried on into exactly the work the wait existed to make safe. `waitGpu` now reports whether the GPU drained, and the three callers that destroy something check it. The four copies of the guarded ray target resize became one helper.

**Sample the material only for the ray that reads it** — all five ray types share one hit group, so giving `ClosestHit` a material gave it to every ray. Only the reflection ray reads `albedo`; shadow, occlusion and contact rays read nothing past `t`, and the bounce ray takes its colour from the light loop. `ACCEPT_FIRST_HIT_AND_END_SEARCH` does not skip the closest-hit shader, so none of them were exempt. The payload now carries the caller's request, gated above the attribute fetch rather than just above the sample. Costs one dword: `MaxPayloadSizeInBytes` 32 → 36.

**Give the linear scene colour a resting state it can be found in** — `linearIn` was created as a render target and left as a shader resource, so from the second Ray Reconstruction frame on, `OMSetRenderTargets` took it in `PIXEL_SHADER_RESOURCE` with no barrier back. It now rests as a shader resource and `linearizeSceneColour` transitions it in and out in the same call.

**Claim a linear source only for a frame Ray Reconstruction accepted** — `m_rrLinearIn` was set several failure points before RR had agreed to anything. A failed tag or evaluate dropped the frame to ordinary DLSS while the flag still told the tonemap the gamma-encoded output was linear, so the fallback frame came out encoded twice.

## Already fixed

The fifth item, descriptor invalidation not triggering room recollection, was `clearRooms()` in `freeSrv` emptying the room vectors outside the guard that refills them. That was fixed in `e68a49fa` by the `roomsNeedRebuild` request, which is in #18 and postdates the commit Codex read.

## Verification

Everything here was proved without launching the game.

- `cmake --build --target arx --config RelWithDebInfo` exits 0, no compiler warnings on the touched files.
- The DXR library is compiled at runtime, so the C++ build does not validate it. `kRayLib` was extracted and compiled standalone with `dxc -T lib_6_3`, the same target the runtime uses — exit 0.
- `scripts/Check-MaintenanceDocs.ps1`: 53 greps across 8 files, all pass.

`INV-18` is new, because a `TraceRay` that forgets to set `wantMat` gets whatever the register held — either a black reflection or the frame time back, and neither writes a line to the log.

`applyMoves`: a captured row WITH its X (both rooms and the name read) drops the `movex|night|from|to|name` alert an earlier read raised, through the same key the raise uses. `dropAlert` removes it, saves, repaints the button's count and pulse, re-renders the list if he is on it. author: bohdankhrystov
body:
> **The QA round I reported as finding seven high-severity product defects measured nothing.** This PR is the triage that established that, and the harness tickets that stop it recurring.

## What actually happened

The round reported `COMMIT: ea4bd05c` and drove a dev server and duel server both rooted in `.claude/worktrees/agent-af32ec8cf22f8819c`, whose branch is at `c3e1a830` — **2026-09-07, 92 commits behind** on `web-client/` and `poker-server/`.

The served module says so verbatim:

```
window.$RefreshReg$ = RefreshRuntime.getRefreshReg(
  ".../.claude/worktrees/agent-af32ec8cf22f8819c/web-client/src/profile/ProfileStrip.tsx")
```

`RematchNotice.tsx`, `NameAsk.tsx` and `device-standing.ts` **do not exist on disk** in that tree. I confirmed both independently: `:8080` carries pid 92553 with that cwd, and the file is absent.

## The mechanism needed nobody to be careless

`db-up` dies (compose derives its project name from the checkout basename and `docker-compose.yml` publishes a fixed `"5432:5432"` — three postgres containers exist here, one per checkout) → the new JVM cannot bind `:8080` → Vite has no `strictPort` so it moves to `:5174` and says so only in a background log → `wait-server`/`wait-web` pass because they ask only whether **something** answers → `drive.mjs` hardcodes `:5173` → and `COMMIT:` is `git rev-parse --short HEAD` in the agent's own checkout, not in the tree being served.

Every link is individually reasonable. Together they let a round name a commit it never ran.

## Triage

`ROUND: 1 · VERDICT: STOP_INFRA · B(1): 0 · NEW 3 · HARNESS 8, excluded`

- **Eight of nine findings are harness defects** under `ADR-0089` §4 — withdrawn as *unverified*, not as absent. Round 2 retests them against a stack that can name itself.
- **The ninth** — Ukrainian dates — is not a defect: `ADR-0061` §Consequences decides that `finishedAtText` renders instants *"in the reader's locale"*.
- **`PASS` is refused** although `B(1) = 0` implies it arithmetically. Here it would mean *nothing was measured*, not *nothing is wrong*, and emitting it is the coverage inflation `ADR-0089` §2c forbids.

Three harness tickets filed against `EPIC-12`: name the tree being served, record the tree a round drove, one database wherever `stack.sh` runs from. A fourth (back-to-back chrome binds) is deferred — QA itself called it local contention and retried past it.

## The one real finding, which QA could not see

Read from source at `ea4bd05c`: `RematchNotice` renders only while `shown !== "first"`; the three controls that open a chosen screen exist **only** in `Lobby.tsx`'s front-door branch; the result branch renders `DuelResult` and nothing else; `grep -rn 'href='` finds exactly two links in the client, both `href="/"`.

So **the set of screens a player can reach while holding a finished room is empty**, and `STORY-1415`'s thirteen tickets ship a surface no press can produce. `ADR-0123` §Context rests on a premise the markup does not carry, and §1 carves out the exact case the human's own quoted sentence names.

Registered as **`DEC-162`, the human's** — because the sentence being reinterpreted is the human's own. I added its row to `docs/adr/README.md`; the triage had it in `BOARD.md` only.

## Cycle

**Stop.** Only a new instruction opens round 2 (`ADR-0089` §2b).

author: tobyclemson
body:
# [0184] Refuse template resolution on a wrong plugin root

## Summary

Extends 0182's *absent*-root refusal to the *wrong*-root case: a present
plugin root that carries no `templates/` directory is not an Accelerator
installation, so every template command and the visualiser compose path now
refuse with a dedicated diagnostic instead of degrading to a silent empty
answer or a false template-not-found. The refusal names the offending root,
the invalid `templates/` layout, and `ACCELERATOR_PLUGIN_ROOT`, and fails
closed even under `--fail-safe`.

## Changes

- **New error variant** — `ConfigError::PluginRootNotAnInstallation { path }`
  (`cli/config/src/error.rs`), classified `is_refusal() == true` so it fails
  closed identically to `PluginRootUnavailable`, with a message that names the
  path and states the root is not an installation (distinct from the
  absent-root "unknown, set the variable" message).
- **Shared installation-detection helper** — `require_templates_dir`
  (`cli/config-adapters/src/store.rs`) validates `templates/` with a single
  `fs::metadata` probe and becomes the one choke point for `template_names`,
  `plugin_template_path`, `plugin_default`, `eject`, and `resolve_template`'s
  plugin-default tier.
- **Structural shapes fail closed** — a missing `templates/`, a `templates`
  that is a file, and a root that is itself a file all refuse; a genuinely
  *unreadable* fault (permission, filesystem loop) stays the degradable `Io`
  and does not name the variable.
- **Preserved behaviour** — a resolving user override still renders at exit 0
  under a wrong root (override tiers precede the plugin-default check), a valid
  installation missing one template still reports a template-not-found naming
  the template, and the root-independent config families are untouched.
- **Compose boundary** — no production change; the existing `?` at
  `compose.rs:157` propagates the refusal into `ComposeError`, pinned by a new
  contract test.
- **Fixtures** — regenerated the config `public-api.txt` for the new public
  variant and seeded `templates/` in the shutdown-test plugin-root fixture,
  which compose now correctly refuses without.

## Context

- Work item: `meta/work/0184-template-enumeration-swallows-a-wrong-plugin-root.md`
- Plan: `meta/plans/2026-09-09-0184-template-resolution-wrong-plugin-root.md`
- Research: `meta/research/codebase/2026-09-08-0184-template-resolution-wrong-plugin-root.md`
- Validation: `meta/validations/2026-09-09-0184-template-resolution-wrong-plugin-root-validation.md`
- Builds on 0182 (CLI derives plugin root from its own location).

## Testing

- [x] Error-crate unit tests — `cargo test -p config` (new variant Display + `is_refusal`)
- [x] Store unit tests — `cargo test -p config-adapters` (10 new tests: three structural refusals, the `Io` arm, the override hoisting crux, genuine-not-found preservation)
- [x] Launcher integration — `cargo test -p accelerator --test config_read` (152 passed, all six commands on a wrong root)
- [x] Compose contract — `cargo test -p accelerator-visualiser --test compose_contract` (wrong root refuses to compose)
- [x] Format + lint — `mise run cli:check` (rustfmt, clippy, store-duplication)
- [ ] Full local CI mirror — `mise run` recorded green in the work item after the docs-site advisory rebase; not re-run in this validation session

## Notes for Reviewers

- **AC8 semantics moved.** The work item's AC8 originally treated a
  `templates`-is-a-file root as the representative `Io` fault; this change
  reclassifies that shape as a structural refusal and reserves `Io` for
  genuinely unreadable faults. AC8 was revised and AC13 added for the two extra
  structural shapes — both reflected in the work item.
- **Deliberate residual duplication.** `compose.rs:155` still reconstructs
  `plugin_root.join("templates")` to build each tier's absolute default path;
  the validity gate is centralised, but relocating the per-name path
  construction behind a store accessor is a wider compose-tier refactor left
  out of scope. The `store-duplication` lint passes.
- Worth focusing on: the ordering invariant that keeps a resolving override
  ahead of the root check (`resolve_template`), and the `NotFound |
  NotADirectory` collapse in `require_templates_dir`.

author: thebeninwebdev
body:
## Summary

This PR synchronizes the current `dev` branch with `main` to establish the latest stable SwiftDU codebase as the production baseline.

Previously, `main` was intentionally kept behind `dev` because SwiftDU operations are currently suspended. This update removes that dependency by making the operational state configurable, allowing the latest application code to be deployed while keeping live customer ordering disabled.

## Key changes

### Operational suspension control

* Added `OPERATIONS_ENABLED` as the central configuration for whether live SwiftDU operations are active.
* Operations default to suspended unless the environment variable is explicitly set to `true`.
* Normal live ordering remains blocked while operations are disabled.
* Preserved authorized test/training order behavior for internal testing.
* Added focused tests around operational state and suspension redirects.
* Added `.env.example` documenting the expected configuration.

Production will remain configured with:

`OPERATIONS_ENABLED=false`

This allows `main` to contain the current application without reopening SwiftDU to live orders.

### Authentication and ordering experience

This merge also brings the current development baseline into `main`, including:

* Magic-link authentication improvements.
* Centralized authentication routing.
* Updated ordering experience.
* Swifty mascot integration and supporting UI updates.

### Café inquiry workflow

Includes the new two-phase café inquiry flow for cases where customers need a Tasker to check what food is currently available before making a final selection.

The workflow includes:

* Tasker assignment and café checking states.
* Tasker-submitted available items and prices.
* Customer selection after availability is confirmed.
* Server-side validation of selections and prices.
* Protection against stale/concurrent option updates.
* Integration with the existing pricing, payment, notification, Socket.IO and test-order systems.
* Café inquiry visibility across customer, Tasker and admin interfaces.
* Additional authorization protection on admin order mutations.
* Focused tests covering pricing, selections, invalid inputs and compatibility with existing order behavior.

The existing order model and major order statuses remain compatible with older orders.

## Why this PR

The goal is to make `main` represent the actual current SwiftDU codebase rather than using an outdated production branch as the mechanism for suspending operations.

Application version and operational availability are now separate concerns:

* `main` represents the current stable application.
* `OPERATIONS_ENABLED` determines whether live operations are available.
* Authorized test/training workflows can continue while public operations remain suspended.

This establishes a clean production baseline before the next development cycle.

## Deployment note

Before deploying/merging, ensure the Production environment contains:

`OPERATIONS_ENABLED=false`

Live customer operations should remain suspended after deployment.

body:
Advances #2495. This is the follow-up I flagged in #3365, now that
`model_scene_setup.c` is free.

`model_scene_setup.c` declared the model slot reset for itself:

```c
extern void func_8005611C(int), func_80059AE0(int);
```

`func_8005611C` is `matching_c` and is defined in `model_slot_setup.c`, whose
header now exists (from #3365) and already carries the unit's other function.

### No conflict

The definition is `void func_8005611C(s32 arg0)` and `src/types.h` has
`typedef signed int s32`, so the local declaration's `int` was already the same
type. Nothing to resolve.

### The header now describes the whole unit

`model_slot_setup.c`'s own note says these two functions are one initializer and
its consumer, and with both declared the header can say so:

- `func_8005611C` zeroes the slot's first `0x388` words through `func_8005B5FC`,
  then writes the defaults -- `MODEL_FIXED_HALF` at `+0xDA0/+0xDA4/+0xDA8`,
  `MODEL_FIXED_ONE` at `+0xDB0/+0xDB4/+0xDB8`, `0x80` at `+0xDC0..+0xDC2`, and
  the mode byte at `+0xE16`;
- `func_80056250`, the layout pass declared below it, switches on that same
  `+0xE16`.

The two are contiguous -- `0x8005611C` is `0x134` bytes and ends exactly where
`0x80056250` begins.

### What is left

The dense declaration block inside `func_800533D8` now holds only
`func_80059AE0`. That one is defined in `model_state_setters.c`, a unit with no
header yet and two setters in it, so it needs its own change rather than being
folded in here.

### Verification

- clean `make match` -> `84a54ed74f3d0edd6d81380839f7e4ef5bfb21ecea18be9a062bd6bfa5a45c88`
- `make match-overlays` -> 5 of 5 `overlay match` lines
- `make basic-types` -> OK (703 C sources), no follow-up edit needed
- `make verify-overlays check-metadata check-candidate-headlines check-candidate-index check-notes external-attempts`

As with the earlier changes to this block, the edit touches a line whose
formatting is part of a matched function's source, so the match gate is doing
real work here.

Rebased on current master (`23598a68`). Touches no file in any other open PR.

author: phazzie
body:
Run 23 of the scheduled worst-feature routine. Logged in `WORST_TO_BEST_LOG.md`; plan in `plan.md`, written before any code.

## The feature, and why it was the worst

Making a coloring page ends in packaging: `OutputPackagingSeam` turns the finished picture into a printable PDF and a square share PNG. That step runs **entirely on the reader's own device** — no network, no provider, no quota — and the picture it works from has already been generated and already been paid for.

So it is the cheapest step in the app to run a second time. It was the only failing step in the app with **no way to run it again**.

### 1. Three copies of one function, six raw-string sites

| Site | Line | What was written into a field a reader sees |
|------|------|---------------------------------------------|
| `src/routes/studio-state.svelte.ts` | 2280 | `result.error.message` |
| `src/routes/studio-state.svelte.ts` | 2285 | `error.message` — **a caught exception** |
| `src/lib/components/page-artifact-state.svelte.ts` | 144 | `result.error.message` |
| `src/lib/components/page-artifact-state.svelte.ts` | 150 | `packagingError.message` — **a caught exception** |
| `src/lib/components/MeechieTools.svelte` | 566 | `result.error.message` |
| `src/lib/components/MeechieTools.svelte` | 572 | `packagingError.message` — **a caught exception** |

`summarisePageExportFailures` then quoted each verbatim into the reader's sentence, so the one sentence the app wrote about a failed download was half authored for a reader and half written for whoever wrote the adapter:

> Your page is on the paper. The square share image could not be built: **Canvas context unavailable for resizing**.

The exception half is worse. pdf-lib's `embedPng`, `embedJpg` and `save` all throw, and whatever they said reached the screen unread.

### 2. The seam already answered the question the app threw away

`SeamErrorSchema` carries `code` next to `message`, and the packaging adapter emits **ten** distinct codes. All three call sites read `.message` and discarded `.code`. So nothing in the app could tell `CANVAS_UNAVAILABLE` — this browser never will — from `PNG_ENCODING_FAILED` — that missed, and a second attempt runs against a heap the first one has released. That is the only distinction that decides whether pressing a button is worth the reader's time, and it was being returned and dropped at each of three doors.

### 3. No retry, and the nearest control was the paid one

The only button anywhere near a failed download was "Make the page", which buys a generation and returns a **different** picture. The most natural response to a free local step failing was to pay for a fresh page and lose the one they liked. And nothing named what survived: a failed print PDF leaves the original image and the in-app Print button; a failed square leaves the PDF.

This is the third and last surface of the pattern `generation-failure.ts` removed for AI calls and `storage-failure.ts` removed for storage.

## What shipped

- **`[NEW] src/lib/core/export-failure.ts`** — pure classifier, same shape family as the other two. Seam `code` or thrown value plus the variant asked for becomes `{ variant, cause, message, retry, detail }`. An exception's or the seam's words become `detail` and never `message`. Unlike `storage-failure.ts` there is **no verbatim allowlist**, because none of the ten strings the packaging seam can emit was written for a reader.
- **`[NEW] src/lib/components/page-packaging.ts`** — the only call to `outputPackagingAdapter.package` in the app. A test walks `src/**` and fails if a second one appears, the same rule `SharePageButton` holds for `navigator.share`.
- **The free rebuild.** "Build the downloads again" re-runs packaging on the picture already on screen, re-using the existing `pageFileBaseName` so rebuilt files still match an original image the reader may already have grabbed, and taking `pageSize` off the attempt being rebuilt rather than from the live Page Controls, which stay enabled. Offered **only** where a failed variant's cause could land differently, and carrying its own busy flag rather than `isGenerating`, so it does not disable every paid button on the surface.
- **One line per failed variant** instead of one run-on sentence, because two variants can fail for two different reasons — one rebuildable, one not.
- **`[NEW] playwright.local.config.ts` + `npm run test:e2e:local`.** Two runs of this log have now rebuilt the same `executablePath` override by hand and thrown it away. Env-driven (`PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH`) rather than hardcoded, and with the variable unset it behaves exactly like the pinned config, so it cannot quietly change what is being tested.

## Scope

No file under `contracts/`, `probes/`, `fixtures/`, `src/lib/mocks/`, `src/lib/adapters/` or `src/lib/seams/` is touched. `git diff --name-only a87af7a HEAD` against those six paths returns nothing. `code` was already in the contract's error schema and already emitted by the adapter; this change stops discarding it. **No Cipher Gate required.**

## Evidence

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run check` | 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm test` | **1,953** passed, 1 skipped (from 1,927 — 26 new) |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| `npm run verify` | exit 0, `docs/evidence/2026-09-10/` refreshed |
| `npm run test:e2e:local` | **83** passed (from 82 — 1 new) |

The new browser test forces the failure by breaking `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.toDataURL` rather than by stubbing a route, because **packaging never touches the network — there is no request to intercept.** That break takes the square share image only: a PNG source is embedded in the PDF without going through a canvas at all, which is exactly the split the two separate packaging calls exist to preserve. So the test proves the real thing in a real browser: the PDF survives, the notice names the square in the app's own words, the rebuild appears, and pressing it produces the missing file without a second generation.

## Deferred, and recorded in the log

`src/lib/core/meechie-quote-scoring.ts` has **zero importers anywhere in the repo** — a complete 107-line deterministic quote scorer nothing calls. author: sageryza
body:
Sophie, 2026-09-10: *"add a button to each scene that automatically puts all the right references in the same text to footage so I can edit it or press go myself"*. The belt side (the button on each scene card) is another chat's; this is the **receiving door** on `/footage`.

## The key

Her belt pages are served from the same origin, so the hand-off needs no route and no doc — one `localStorage` key, **`footage_handoff`**:

```
{ prompt: string,
  refs: [{url, kind:'image'|'video'|'audio', poster?, name?}],
  model?: 'mini'|'fast'|'2.0'|'2.5', seconds?: number, res?: '480p'|'720p', ratio?: string,
  from?: string, title?: string, at: number }   // Date.now()
```

The page **CONSUMES** it: reads → applies → `removeItem`. Removing the key is what makes it land exactly once and never re-apply on a later load.

**Nothing is ever sent.** It only fills the box — the star is still her tap, which is the whole of what she asked for.

## Four read moments

The app keeps a tool's web view alive for the whole app process (CLAUDE.md: *A WRAPPED PAGE CAN BE DAYS STALE*), so walking here from the belt usually fires no load at all:

1. **on load**, right after `loadCtl()` — the order is what makes the hand-off beat the restored draft
2. **`visibilitychange`→visible** — coming back to the tool inside the app, the ordinary case
3. **`pageshow`** — the back-forward cache hands the page over with neither a load nor a visibility change
4. **the `storage` event** for that key — another same-origin *document* writing it while this one is on screen; the only moment the page can act immediately

## Rules

- A hand-off **replaces** the draft (it is a deliberate button press; her words were going into `footage_draft` all along, and the hand-off is saved there too).
- Refs dedupe by url; an **unknown `kind` rides as a picture** — `slotsOf` counts per kind and would otherwise name a slot `[AudioNaN]`.
- Model / res / ratio / seconds are set live on `S`, so **`paintControls` validates them** against the served table: 99 seconds clamps to the model's max, an unknown model falls to the first row. The page holds no copy of that table.
- **Older than a day is dropped** (she has moved on), and a **malformed value is dropped silently** — a belt page with a bug must not throw a page error here. Either way the key comes off the shelf rather than being re-read at all four moments.

One correctness fix alongside it: a shape the server does not carry lit **no** chip and left the server silently clamping the job to 1:1, so `paintControls` now drops an unknown ratio to the first one it does carry (this also covers a stale `footage_ctl`).

## Test

`node scripts/test-footage-handoff.js` — the real page headless against a stub. Every assertion is a MEASUREMENT: a hand-off that parses and never reaches the box, one that leaves the key behind, and one whose seconds skip the clamp all look identical in the source. The `storage` moment is driven by a **second page in the same context**, and each scene gets a fresh context so `footage_draft` cannot bleed from one into the next.

- **31 pass**; **verified failing 20** against the pre-fix page.
- `node scripts/test-footage.js` — **138 pass**, unchanged.

body:
Opening a project from the desktop app could dispatch `project.create` twice for the same workspace root: two activation requests can reach `handleDesktopAppActivationRequest` before the client projection shows the first create (the broker re-dispatches after a renderer blip, and the coordinator's serializing queue lives in a `useRef` that resets when the component remounts), so the second create is rejected by the server's `Active project '...' already exists for workspace root '...'` invariant and the open fails.

Racing activations now share a single in-flight create keyed by environment plus normalized workspace root, and a rejected create falls back to whatever project has since appeared for that root instead of failing the request outright. Other create call sites (command palette, welcome wizard, mobile add-project) are single user-initiated dispatches, not this race, so they are out of scope.

author: salman1993
body:
## Why

The ACP SDK validates `session/new` before pi-acp handles it. Its current schema omits the provisional top-level `systemPrompt` field, so validation strips Buzz's replacement prompt. The committed `dist/index.js` also predates #5 and still uses the old `_meta.systemPrompt` contract.

## What

Preserve top-level `session/new.systemPrompt` through SDK validation and rebuild the committed distribution bundle.

## How

A stream adapter shadows the prompt behind a process-only token in `_meta`, which the SDK preserves. `PiAcpAgent` extends `NewSessionRequest` and recovers the prompt after validation. Clients cannot use the internal metadata key as a second prompt contract because only tokens created by the stream adapter resolve to values.

The adapter still negotiates ACP protocol v1 and accepts only the top-level replacement string added in #5.

## Risk

The stream adapter changes only `session/new` requests that contain top-level `systemPrompt`. All other ACP messages pass through unchanged.

## Testing

Ran Buzz PR [#7508](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/7508)'s real-adapter test against the rebuilt bundle:

`BUZZ_TEST_PI_ACP=/absolute/path/to/pi-acp/dist/index.js cargo test -p buzz-acp real_pi_preserves -- --ignored`

The test passed and verified prompt delivery, launch skills, and prompt restoration.

## Bigger picture

This unblocks the native Pi system-prompt transport in [block/buzz#7508](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/7508) without claiming ACP protocol v2 support while the system-prompt RFD remains open.

author: neurekadev
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
Adds application-managed PUID/PGID support so the container reconciles the data volume's ownership itself instead of relying on Compose to start the process as a specific user.

**Runtime identity handling**
- Introduces a new `internal/privilege` package with an `Identity` type (UID/GID), environment parsing for `PUID`/`PGID`, and an `Apply` function. Parsing rejects half-configured pairs (only one variable set), empty/non-numeric/negative values, and mixed root/non-root pairs, so a typo cannot silently run the daemon as the wrong user.
- On unix, `Apply` recursively changes ownership of the working root to the target identity and then permanently drops root via `setgroups`/`setgid`/`setuid`, verifying the drop took effect. A non-root start keeps the runtime-forced identity (warn when it differs from PUID/PGID), and a non-unix build reports that PUID/PGID is unsupported (except for an explicit root identity, which is a no-op).
- `chownTree` skips entries already owned by the target identity, so volumes that forbid re-owning (e.g. NFS `root_squash`, CIFS) remain usable when already owned correctly, and re-owns symlinks themselves rather than their targets.

**Startup wiring**
- `main.go` now resolves the working root and applies the runtime identity before the listener, watcher, or scheduler start any work. When neither variable is set the current identity is kept; when both are `0` it warns and continues running as root; an unreachable configured identity fails startup instead of running with the wrong ownership.
- `resolveWorkingRoot` is refactored to compute the path first, then `MkdirAll` it, so the directory exists before ownership is applied.

**Image and deployment**
- The runtime image switches from the nonroot default to `USER 0` and sets `PUID`/`PGID` defaults of `1000`, so the binary can take ownership and then drop root itself.
- `compose.yaml` drops the fixed `user:` directive and instead grants only the capabilities the startup step needs (`CHOWN`, `DAC_OVERRIDE`, `SETGID`, `SETUID`) while still dropping `ALL` and keeping `no-new-privileges:true`.
- README is updated to describe the automatic per-start ownership, the precedence of an explicit `user:` over PUID/PGID, and the recommended least-privilege `docker run` flags.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: stlynn13-lgtm
body:
Found while preparing to ship the `eas update` for #8. **Publishing from a normal shell would have silently stripped the API token from every device that took the update.**

## The trap

`extra` ships inside the update manifest, so whatever `app.config.ts` resolves at publish time is what every device gets. Two values had no usable fallback:

```ts
appToken: process.env.APP_TOKEN                     // -> undefined
environment: process.env.APP_ENV ?? "development"   // -> wrong bucket
```

`eas.json`'s per-profile `env` blocks and the EAS secret store both apply to **`eas build`**, which runs on EAS servers. Neither applies to **`eas update`**, which evaluates this config on whatever machine you run it from — and `APP_TOKEN` is a *secret*-visibility EAS variable, so it can't be pulled down locally at all.

Verified by evaluating the config in a bare shell:

```
apiUrl:          "https://eat-out-better-api.vercel.app"   ok (has a fallback)
dailyScanLimit:  5                                          ok (has a fallback)
environment:     "development"                              wrong — should be preview
appToken:        undefined                                  token stripped
```

## How bad, today

Survivable. The API's `APP_SHARED_TOKEN` gate is still unset, so it fails open — confirmed against the live endpoint, where an unauthenticated `POST /api/analyze` returns `400 INVALID_IMAGE`, not `401`.

It stops being survivable the moment that gate is switched on. Every device carrying such an update is then 401'd on every scan, with no token to fall back on — and unlike a bad build, there's no store review to catch it. Project memory already flags that switch-on as the dangerous step.

## The fix — two halves, because a guard on `APP_ENV` alone isn't enough

**1. `resolveAppToken()` throws** when `APP_ENV` is `preview`/`production` and `APP_TOKEN` is missing:

```
APP_TOKEN is not set, but APP_ENV="preview".

  'extra.appToken' ships in the update manifest. Publishing now would
  strip the API token from every device that takes this artifact.
  ...
  Fix: APP_TOKEN='<token>' npm run update:preview
```

Development is exempt — the API is fail-open and demanding a secret to run `expo start` would be hostile. `ALLOW_MISSING_APP_TOKEN=1` is an explicit escape hatch for a deliberately token-less preview build.

**2. `update:preview` / `update:production` npm scripts** that set `APP_ENV`.

This second half matters more than it looks. The failure I actually hit had `APP_ENV` **unset**, defaulting to `"development"` — which a guard keyed only on `APP_ENV` would have waved straight through. The scripts remove that path from the normal workflow.

## Verification

| path | expected | result |
|---|---|---|
| local dev, no env vars | evaluates clean | ✅ |
| `APP_ENV=preview`, no token | throws | ✅ |
| both set correctly | passes, token present | ✅ |
| `ALLOW_MISSING_APP_TOKEN=1` | passes | ✅ |

`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

## Note

This does not change what any currently-installed build does — it only affects what future publishes are allowed to produce. The pending `eas update` for #8 should go out **after** this lands, using `npm run update:preview` with `APP_TOKEN` supplied from your own environment.

author: dungbanguyen
body:
Refs #1781. The store half is here; the surface half is filed — see the last
section.

## The gap

`is_current_primary` is kept true at the three moments a caller **states**
something: a person's only current employment lands primary, ending one clears
the flag, and a job already over never takes it. This is the moment nobody
states anything — the primary edge is retired — and the answer silently becomes
*nobody* while the person is plainly still employed somewhere.

## The rule, and why it is two rules

**One remaining employment is not a choice.** It is the only answer there is, so
writing it invents nothing. Leaving it unset there would mean the product knows
the answer, has no alternative to weigh, and declines to say it.

**Two remaining IS a choice, and this does not make it.** Picking between two
employers on somebody's behalf writes a fact nobody asserted, and
`is_current_primary` is a column humans set deliberately — worth keeping exactly
where it means something.

## Retired, not merely changed

The distinction the implementation turns on, and the one I got wrong first: a
caller sending `is_current_primary = false` is **stating** that this is not the
person's primary employer. Promoting the same row straight back overrules a human
with the answer they had just rejected. So the patch door fires only where the
patch ENDED the employment; the archive door always does.

`TestClearingTheFlagOnTheOnlyEmploymentIsNotOverruled` is that case, and it is
the one that separates "an employment was retired" from "an employment changed".

## Both doors, spelled once

`promoteLoneSurvivingEmployment` is one statement asking its own question. Both
call sites hand it a person and no verdict, so neither carries a second spelling
of "is this employment over" to drift from the one in the patch — that pair
produces a row whose flag and whose dates disagree about the same job.

The two predicates inside are deliberately different questions, and the kernel
says why: the candidate must be a **current** employment (date-aware — a job
somebody leaves next month is still theirs), while whether the slot is free is
**date-blind**, because that is what `uq_rel_current_primary_employer` asks.

## The archive path now takes the lock

Its comment said it needed none: it *"frees the current-primary slot but never
DECIDES anything from a read of it"*. It decides now, so it takes the per-person
employment write identity — first, in the order create and update take it, since
two writers taking one pair in opposite orders is a deadlock.

## Tests

Three shapes × two doors, plus the statement case: one remaining (promoted), two
remaining (unset), none remaining (unset), and a human's `false` left alone.

Mutation-checked three ways: `count >= 1` fails the two-survivors case,
`count = 0` fails the promotion case, and dropping the `in.EndedAt != nil`
condition fails the not-overruled case.

## Two things to flag

**The surface half is filed, not built.** The ruling's item 2 asks the unset
state to render as *"no primary employer — choose one"* rather than blank.
`personrail.tsx` is frozen at its exact line count by the frontend length
ratchet, so adding that line means extracting the employment panel (~200 lines)
into its own module — which would roughly double this diff, in another module,
for a state that is already reachable today by a human clearing the flag. Filed
as #5223, naming the employment form from #1155 as its real hook.

**Two lead-SLA tests fail on main tip** (`TestAnOwnerlessBreachReachesTheConfiguredIntakeSeat`,
`TestAnIntakeSeatThatCannotWorkIsTreatedAsUnset`), and they are not from this
branch — they fail with my working tree stashed, before and after rebasing.
Reported to the session that holds main. If CI reds on those, that is why.

## Checks

- `make check-backend` green.
- `craft static --strict` over the diff: 0/0/0.
- The employment lock cases (`TestCaptureWaitsOnThePersonsEmploymentLock`,
  `TestTheDomainBacklogWaitsOnEachPersonsEmploymentLock`) still pass with the
  archive path taking the same lock.
- Both new relationship reads declared in the edge-reader gate with their
  verdicts.

author: johnrtipton
body:
Closes #2722

## The gap

`scripts/run-django-template-suite.py compare` ratcheted two aggregate percentages. A change that fixes five Django `template_tests` cells and breaks five different ones leaves both numbers identical, so `compare` exits 0 and the blocking CI job is green.

## The fix

**Baseline** (`scripts/django-template-suite-baseline.json`) gains `not_ok`: every id whose status is not OK, keyed to that status. It is the NOT-OK set rather than the OK set because the real run has **29 not-OK ids of 1470** (14 ERROR + 1 FAIL + 14 SKIP) against ~1441 OK ids. SKIP/XFAIL are included so a cell that was never counted cannot read as "was OK" (a SKIP→FAIL flip is still caught — by the percentage arm, since the denominator grew). The set is built by `report.summarize` from the run's records and written only by `--write-baseline` — never hand-typed (#2727).

**`compare`** gains a per-cell arm, independent of the percentage ratchet (which is kept):

- every id that is FAIL/ERROR now and not in the baseline's `not_ok` is a regression → listed with its message, exit 1;
- a baseline not-OK id **absent** from the run (removed/renamed upstream, or a `--label` subset) is listed as informational, not a regression — the same rule the tag-mismatch arm uses;
- a cell that was not OK and is OK now is listed with a nudge to regenerate;
- a baseline without the set, or a run JSON without `tests`, warns and ratchets the percentages alone (so an old baseline degrades, never breaks).

## Dogfood (#1060)

Ran the real scoreboard once with `--write-baseline` on the unchanged tree: 98.57% / 98.97%, identical to the committed aggregates. The baseline diff is **only** the 29-entry `not_ok` set plus `generated_at`; both `<!-- django-suite-claim -->` docs untouched. `compare --json .django-src/last-run.json` against the updated baseline → `OK: no drop against the baseline`, rc 0.

Empirical swap canary on the REAL run JSON: flipped `test_nodelist.NodelistTest.test_for` ERROR→OK and `test_if.IfTagTests.test_if_tag01` OK→ERROR (1-for-1). Both percentages print identical; `compare` → `FAIL: 1 cell(s) were OK in the baseline and are not now: ERROR …test_if_tag01`, **rc 1**.

## CI trace (#1713)

The "Compare against the stored baseline (blocking ratchet)" step in `django-template-suite` runs `compare` with no `continue-on-error` on the step, the job, or `test-summary`; a non-zero exit fails the job, `needs.django-template-suite.result != "success"` falsifies the `&&`-chain in `test-summary`, which runs `exit 1`. The job comment is updated to name the per-cell arm.

## Gate-off per mechanism (#2135 / #1468)

Harness asserts the mutation text was found, the mutated source differs, counts errors as well as failures, and refuses a number if the module broke.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| (unmutated) | 0 failed |
| M1 regressed-detection off (`and False`) | 3 failed: swap, net-drop, cli-swap |
| M2 per-cell code not propagated (`max(code, 0*per_cell_code)`) | 2 failed: swap, cli-swap |
| M3 absent ids treated as regressions | 1 failed: absent-id-is-informational |
| M4 `not_ok` never collected in `summarize` | 1 failed: `test_as_dict_is_the_baseline_schema` |
| M5 SKIP/XFAIL dropped from `_NOT_OK` | 1 failed: `test_as_dict_is_the_baseline_schema` |
| M6 tag-mismatch short-circuit removed | 1 failed: tag-mismatch-short-circuits-per-cell |

## Tests

New cases in `TestPerCellRatchet` (`python/tests/test_django_template_suite_2517.py`): run JSON built from a status map so aggregates are computed, not hand-set — the swap case asserts both percentages are EQUAL before asserting rc 1 with the ids named; pure gain → 0; unchanged → 0; upstream-removed id → 0 with a note; SKIP→FAIL is not reported as an OK regression; net drop → 1; tag mismatch short-circuits; missing set / missing `tests` warn; CLI swap → 1; the committed baseline's set agrees with its own aggregates. `test_as_dict_is_the_baseline_schema` and `test_baseline_schema` pin the key. Full file: 93 passed against the real checkout.

Two-commit shape: impl+tests+baseline, then `changelog.d/2722.changed.md`.

author: vibecoderst
body:
## Summary A milestone child run now brings its milestone branch level with the default branch **before** it cuts its issue branch, and defers the whole run when it cannot — so no child branch is ever based on a milestone branch that is behind. Closes #1780. - **New `worker/deno/lib/milestone_presync.ts`.** `presyncMilestoneBranch` is one paced attempt at merging the default branch down, and every rule it applies is the periodic sweep's own: the ledger transitions from `milestone_sync_streak.ts`, the ledger key `syncStreakKey`, the pacing guard `conflictAttemptDue`, the failure verdict `judgeSyncFailure`, the agent grant `grantAgentRun`, the success transition `recordSuccess` and the conflict report `escalateSyncConflict` — imported, never restated, so a child run and the sweep can never disagree about what a branch has spent. The ordinary path is one fetch of the default branch (which is what makes the comparison truthful) plus one `rev-list --count`; at zero behind, nothing else runs and the ledger is not touched. - **New `worker/deno/lib/milestone_conflict_agent_binding.ts`** — the one binding of the ladder's agent rung, now called by both the sweep and the pre-cut sync, so the grant-sized timeout (#1693) cannot drift between them. - **`setup_branch_phase.ts` calls it** immediately after `ensureMilestoneBranchExists`, in the shared `${WORK_DIR}/` clone the sweep uses — never in the lane's worktree, whose checkout of the milestone branch git would then refuse to every other lane and to the sweep. - **A deferral costs no agent spend and changes nothing on the issue.** The phase returns `early_exit` with reason `deferred: milestone behind default branch`, `expectedSkip: true` and its own `expectedNoPrOutcome` — so the issue keeps its pickup label, no failure is tracked, no `needs-human` is applied, no `Depends on` line is written, and the only comment is the ordinary claim-release comment, which states the reason. `issue_worker.ts` now carries a setup-phase `expectedSkip`/`outcome` through (it previously dropped both on the `early_exit` path). - **Loop guard.** `findNextIssue` reads `milestone_sync_failures.json` once per scan — a local file, no API call — and `find_oldest_issue.ts` skips **every tier's** candidates in a milestone whose `deferUntil` is still in the future, logging `skipped: milestone behind default branch (paced until )` once per paced milestone per scan and recording the new `milestone-behind` skip reason. Without it a paced milestone was claimed, deferred and commented on again every 30 seconds. - **Docs.** `docs/INTERNALS.md` gains "Sync before new work — the child run's own pre-cut sync" (with a Mermaid flow) beside the conflict-ledger section, and the paced skip is listed in the issue-finder filtering-criteria table. ### Two deliberate judgements worth a reviewer's attention **The child's attempt is granted the agent rung.** Only an attempt that climbed the whole ladder may charge the branch's budget — `judgeSyncFailure` concludes `not-charged` for a conflict the agent was never offered — and charging is what writes the `deferUntil` that paces every other slot off the milestone. An uncharged child attempt would therefore give the loop guard nothing to read, and three uncharged children could otherwise spend a budget the agent never tried. The grant is bounded by `grantAgentRun` against the run's own cycle deadline, so a run without the runway for a full agent run climbs the deterministic rungs only and its conflict is `not-charged`, exactly as in the sweep. **An unwritable ledger warns and still merges.** Bringing the branch level is idempotent, useful work; what a failed ledger write loses is the *pacing*, so the fault is logged with that consequence named (`… cannot be charged or paced`) rather than swallowed or turned into a hard stop that would park every milestone child on a host with a bad work volume. An unreadable *behind count*, by contrast, defers: a base nobody could measure is a base no branch is cut from. **Known bound: only a charged failure paces the milestone.** A ruleset-refused push, a merge-gate refusal or any other `not-charged` verdict writes no `deferUntil`, so the selector does not skip the milestone for it — charging the branch for a fault that is not its own is exactly what Issues #1772 and #1778 removed. Those deferrals are bounded by the per-issue expected-skip cooldown instead: one bounce per issue, then the issue is in cooldown. Recorded here because both reviewers raised it; extending the pacing to uncharged verdicts would need a second pacing signal and is a separate change. ## Evidence Backend/CLI change — no web interface to screenshot. Evidence is the test suite and the full gate: ```text deno test tests/milestone_presync_test.ts tests/milestone_presync_git_test.ts \ tests/setup_branch_presync_test.ts tests/find_oldest_issue_milestone_paced_test.ts \ tests/issue_worker_test.ts tests/milestone_branch_sync_test.ts \ tests/setup_branch_resume_test.ts ok | 193 passed | 0 failed deno run --allow-all check_manifests.ts ok | 633 passed | 0 failed ./quality.sh < /dev/null Result: PASSED (with skipped checks) ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD A["child run claims a
milestone issue"] --> B["ensureMilestoneBranchExists"] B --> C{"rev-list --count
milestone..origin/default"} C -- "0" --> D["cut the issue branch
from origin/<milestone>"] C -- "unreadable" --> X C -- "> 0" --> E{"ledger: attempt due?
budget left?"} E -- "no" --> X["early exit
deferred: milestone behind
default branch"] E -- "yes" --> F["open attempt, merge default down
(ladder + agent rung)"] F -- "landed" --> G["reset budget,
record tip"] --> D F -- "conflict unresolved" --> H["charge 1 attempt,
set deferUntil"] --> X X --> Y["selector skips the milestone's
issues until deferUntil passes"] style D fill:#2d6a4f,stroke:#1b4332,color:#fff style X fill:#9d4e15,stroke:#6b3410,color:#fff ``` ## Acceptance Criteria - **met** — Milestone behind by N > 0, sync succeeds → branch cut from the new tip (test asserts the base SHA) — evidence: `worker/deno/tests/milestone_presync_git_test.ts::#1780 - the issue branch starts at the milestone tip the pre-cut sync produced` (real git: `createFeatureBranchFromBase` leaves `HEAD` at the post-sync `origin/` tip, and the default tip is an ancestor of it) and `worker/deno/tests/setup_branch_presync_test.ts::a behind milestone branch is synced before the child branch is cut` — reviewer: met — reason: the reviewer's caveat was that a stale `origin/` could read as "level"; fixed in this diff by reading (and so fetching) the default tip before the count, covered by `milestone_presync_test.ts::the default tip is read (and so fetched) before the branch is measured` - **met** — Sync fails → early exit `deferred: milestone behind default branch`, ledger charged once, issue labels untouched, no comment other than the release comment — evidence: `worker/deno/tests/setup_branch_presync_test.ts::a failed sync defers the run, charges the ledger once and cuts no branch` asserts the reason, `expectedSkip`, the `no_pr_expected` outcome, `conflictAttempts === 1`, a live `deferUntil`, no branch cut and no `gh` comment/label call — reviewer: met — reason: the reviewer flagged that comment-absence was unasserted (added here) and that "charged once" holds only for the agent-granted unresolved-conflict class — true, and stated as a known bound in the Summary - **partial** — Ledger `deferUntil` in the future → the selector skips the issue with the log line and no claim is made — evidence: `worker/deno/tests/find_oldest_issue_milestone_paced_test.ts::a paced milestone's issue is skipped and the unpaced one selected` (skip, `milestone-behind` reason, diagnostic count) and `worker/

author: jkzing
body:
## Summary

Promotes this branch to the release that serves the site root. Stacks on #1428, which brings in the Edge Function; the diff here is only the promotion once that lands.

- `current_version` points at 4.1, whose `docs_link` is `/`, so `SITE_BASE` resolves to the root and the build picks up the right base. Since #1221 the base comes from `version.json`, so `rspress.config.ts` is not touched — the one step that differs from how 3.9 was promoted.
- 4.0 takes `/4.0` here as well, matching the demotion PR on release/4.0.
- `LYNX_VERSION` is 4.1.0 and `PRIMJS_VERSION` is 4.1.1, identical to #1424. PrimJS is versioned on its own cadence and has no 4.1.0 on Maven Central; its 4.1 line starts at 4.1.1. See the verification below.
- The released deployment owns the cross-version routing table, because it is the one behind the apex domain: development docs and every previous release are proxied to their branch deploys, and `/4.1/*` stays as a permanent redirect so versioned links keep resolving.
- `indexName` moves from the developing index to `lynx`, which is the index for whichever release is current.

The build command keeps main's two SSG workers (#1267) rather than the single worker release/4.0 was pinned to before that change.

## Published dependency check

Every coordinate the docs substitute these two values into, checked against the registries today:

| Coordinate | Registry | 4.1.0 | 4.1.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org.lynxsdk.lynx:lynx` and the other 18 Lynx artifacts | Maven Central | resolves, POM and AAR both 200 | — |
| `org.lynxsdk.lynx:primjs` | Maven Central | **absent** | resolves |
| `pod 'PrimJS'` | CocoaPods | present | present |
| `pod 'Lynx'`, `LynxService`, `LynxDevtool`, `XElement` | lynx-family/Specs | resolves | — |

So `PRIMJS_VERSION` is 4.1.1 here.

Lynx no longer publishes its iOS pods to the CocoaPods trunk; they are hosted in [lynx-family/Specs](https://github.com/lynx-family/Specs), which has 4.1.0 for all four. `Lynx/4.1.0` there pins `PrimJS/quickjs` at 4.1.1, which is where that value comes from. The docs have to declare the new source, which #1429 and #1430 do; #1430 should land before this one.

Note that `maven-metadata.xml` for `org.lynxsdk.lynx:lynx` has `<release>` and `<latest>` pointing at a nightly, so a check that reads only those fields concludes there is no stable 4.1.0. The `<versions>` list contains it and the artifacts are served.

## Verification

`pnpm run build` passes and publishes at the root: assets and links carry no version prefix, the sitemap is written against `https://lynxjs.org/`, the published `version.json` reports `current_version: 4.1`, and the client bundle queries the `lynx` index. `node scripts/ci/check-lynx-ui-routes.mjs` passes. `netlify.toml` parses and the version-level rules were reviewed rule by rule.

On the deploy preview: `/4.1/guide/start/quick-start.html` returns 301 to the unprefixed path, and `/4.0/`, `/3.9/` and `/next/` return 200 from their branch deploys.

## Ordering

1. #1427 and #1428 are in. Land #1429, then #1430.
2. Land #1424 and this PR together, as close to the switch as possible.
3. Move the Netlify production branch to release/4.1.
4. Land #1426 to demote release/4.0.

## Related Links

- #1197, #1202 — the same steps for 4.0
- #1221 — where the base started coming from `version.json`
- #1424 — records 4.1 on main
- #1426 — demotes release/4.0
- #1428 — the Edge Function this stacks on

When no photo is loaded, the app now shows a dedicated welcome screen with a “Select a photo” CTA instead of the editing deck. author: martsokha
body:
## Why

#264 raised the credit-card pattern's score above the detection threshold so a Luhn-valid card is caught on its own. That broke `format_txt::context_boundary`, whose whole design used a payment card as the "weak" value to prove a keyword only boosts within a few-word window — with the fix, both the in- and out-of-window cards self-fire, so the test asserted the old (now incorrect) behavior. **`main` is currently red because of this** (my miss: I verified `format_json` + the pattern suite locally but not `format_txt`).

## Fix

Swap the fixture to a bare **bank-account number** (`\b\d{8,17}\b`, score 0.05, no checksum) with an `account` keyword. A bank account genuinely depends on nearby context, so it still probes the window edge:

- in-window account → boosted over the threshold and redacted;
- out-of-window account → stays weak and survives verbatim.

The test's intent (context window has an edge) is preserved; only the example value changes, since a card is no longer a valid stand-in for "weak."

## Verified

Full `cargo test -p elide --all-features` green locally (12 binaries, 0 failures); the rewritten `context_boundary` test passes.

body:
## Summary

- New `public.tax_rulesets` table + `properties.tax_ruleset_id` + `checkins.tax_declared_flags`. Rules belong to the comune, not the property, and are stored as an ordered list of `{when, effect}` in JSONB. Legacy three columns kept as the fallback.
- **Verona seeded** with six rules from the Delibera di Giunta 422/2024 + Delibera di Consiglio 32/2024 (base €3.50, cap 4 nights, minors exempt, 15–25 and over-70 at −20%, groups >25 at −20%, resident/disability declared-gated). Both Marco Polo properties linked.
- New pure `computeGuestTax(checkin, ruleset, context)` — age pinned at arrival, best_single stacking, returns the per-guest working (not just the total). `exportCityTax` refactored around it; the old `exemptNights` counter is now split into taxable / rule-exempt / over-cap.
- Host console renders the linked ruleset read-only (comune, rate, cap, rules, source, verified_at) or the legacy fields. Guest detail modal grows a Tourist Tax section with one checkbox per `declared` rule; ticking PATCHes `tax_declared_flags` via the Round 20.2 pattern.
- Admin Ops tab grows a read-only "Tourist tax rulesets" card. Authoring stays in SQL — a wrong ruleset files wrong in the host's name.

## Migration

`migration_round37_tax_rulesets.sql` — creates the table with RLS + explicit GRANTs and a touch trigger for `updated_at`. Applied via Supabase MCP.

`seed_round37_verona_ruleset.sql` — inserts the Verona ruleset and links the Marco Polo properties. Idempotent (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`).

## Follow-ups documented in the seed

- `max_nights_basis` set to `per_stay` with a TODO. The delibera reads "fino ad un massimo di 4 pernottamenti" with no qualifier; secondary sources read it as per-person-per-month. Confirm with Direzione Tributi in writing before flipping.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verona guest aged 30, 3 nights → 3 × €3.50 = €10.50.
- [ ] Aged 20 or 72 → 3 × €2.80 = €8.40, rule_applied names youth_15_25 / over_70.
- [ ] Aged 14 exempt / 15 reduced / 25 reduced / 26 full rate (the four boundaries).
- [ ] A guest turning 15 during the stay is charged at age at arrival (was 14 → exempt).
- [ ] 6-night stay → 4 taxable + 2 over-cap, reported separately from rule-exempt.
- [ ] Aged 20 also flagged `resident_comune` → exempt (exempt beats −20%).
- [ ] A property with no `tax_ruleset_id` produces the same output as before.
- [ ] The export text names the delibera it used.
- [ ] Non-admin host cannot INSERT/UPDATE `tax_rulesets` (silent 0-row → RLS working).
