author: ekalkutin
body:
## What the customer asked

> Колонку заявитель / Адрес в таблице Дела. Колонку замечаний убрать (либо объединить с одной из Итог / Состояние). Сейчас там 2 колонки дублируют друг друга вообще. Итог + Состояние — объединить.

Six columns become five: **Дело, Заявитель / Адрес, Документы, Состояние и итог, Подано**.

## Applicant / Address

`GET /api/packages` already published `applicantName` and `propertyAddress`; the client was throwing them away in `toViewPackage`. Both are now on the view model and drawn as one column — applicant over address.

These are what the pipeline **read off the package's own papers**, not what the office declared at the counter, so each carries the confidence its reading was made with. A reading below the client's own threshold (`READ_WELL_ENOUGH`, 0.9) shows that figure beside it in the incomplete tone with the same tooltip the intake screen uses, so an unsure reading is never passed off as a fact. A sure confidence is a number nobody reads and is not drawn.

`null` means no document of the package states it yet. It draws as the same `—` every other unknown cell of this table draws — one dash, not two, where the package names neither.

## Standing & outcome, in one column

Remarks / Outcome / Standing were three columns for two questions, and most of the time two of them said the same thing: `ShortOfDocuments` **is** what `IncompletePackage` means for the queue, `NeedsInspector` is what `IssuesFound` means for it, and a submission is `Cleared` because the run found nothing.

One cell now: the standing leads, a stage bar reports a run under way, and the findings counts sit under it in the two groups the report keeps them in. The outcome's own word is drawn whenever it is **news** — `Cleared` + `IssuesFound` is a real row and there the outcome is the whole story — and dropped when it would only repeat the standing.

**Both filters stayed.** The customer asked to merge the columns, not the controls, so a row narrowed by the outcome filter still has to show the word it was narrowed by. `drawsOutcome()` therefore draws the outcome — repetition and all — whenever the outcome filter (or one of the tabs that stands for it) is narrowing the register. The repetition is only harmless to remove while nobody is looking for it.

The decisions live in `entities/verification-package/model/case-state.ts` rather than as ternaries in the cell, because both are judgements about what the words mean.

## Also

- Mobile list and loading skeleton redrawn to the same five cells.
- New `col.applicant` / `col.state` labels in EN / RU / AZ; the now-unused `col.remarks`, `col.outcome`, `col.standing` removed from all three dictionaries.
- `readWellEnough(confidence)` extracted in `packet-reading.ts` so the register's rows and the case sheet ask one threshold in one place.
- Contracts and server untouched.

## Verified

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm prettier:check`, `pnpm test` (web: 244 passed / 23 files), `tsc -b` on `apps/web` — all green.
- New specs: `case-state.spec.ts` (which piece of news the cell tells; when the outcome's word is drawn, including every standing × outcome pair under the filter), `verification-package.spec.ts` (the stated values survive the mapping, nulls stay null, neither is read off `declared`), plus `readWellEnough` coverage in `packet-reading.spec.ts`.
- Ran the app against a stub API covering every row state (reported / mid-run / never read, low-confidence readings, missing readings, a 100-character address) at 1440px, 1280px and 390px, in RU / EN / AZ, and with the outcome filter set — the repeated word comes back exactly there.

author: j-nut
body:
You exported a backup and found nowhere to put it. That's because **the import never existed.**

`exportLog()` in the History tab writes `iron-six-workout-backup.json` — every profile, every session, every journal entry. Nothing in the app could read one back.

## What this adds

**Restore backup**, beside the Export button it pairs with, and in the account panel — where you'd look after signing in and finding your history missing.

It mirrors cloud-sync's existing guest import rather than inventing a second path. Imported profiles are added as **new** profiles owned by whoever is signed in — never merged over an existing one, never deleting anything. The journal is rebuilt from each profile's history by `IronSixJournal.migrateUser`, the same routine that backfills pre-journal sessions, so restored sessions are **replayable and recoverable**, not just rows in a list.

## Behaviour

| | |
|---|---|
| Signed in | Profiles are stamped with your account scope, so they sync up — the exact case you hit |
| Re-importing the same file | Adds nothing. File is fingerprinted; a nervous second attempt can't duplicate a year of training |
| Existing profiles | Untouched. Verified byte-identical after an import |
| Copied profile | Gets a fresh id, never inherits cloud identity, never arrives mid-workout |
| Junk file | Refused with a reason; profile list left byte-identical |
| Format | Accepts the app's export shape **and** a raw device-storage blob |

## Verified

The full round trip in a real browser, not just in tests: exported → cleared local storage to simulate a fresh device → restored. **4 sessions back, equipment intact, fresh profile id, 4 sessions replayable from the journal, second import adds 0.**

The confirmation dialog also proved itself — the first automated attempt was cancelled because the automation dismissed `confirm()`.

**10 new tests, 119/119 pass.**

author: openvoiceos-bot
body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

Two rules in force here contradict each other, and the contradiction is currently costing about seventeen hours of queue time.

Every pull request in this repository opens as a draft. The merge gate needs a CodeRabbit review at the head sha before the review stage passes on any pull request that touches engine code. CodeRabbit does not review drafts.

That is not an inference. CodeRabbit says so itself, on #898:

> **Draft PR not reviewed.** Draft PRs are not automatically reviewed by default.

and names the fix in the same comment, which is what this change adds:

```yaml
reviews:
  auto_review:
    drafts: true
```

Without it the only way to obtain the review the gate requires is an explicit request, and those are rationed to one per hour across the whole organisation. Seventeen open pull requests here touch engine code, so the queue is paced at one per hour by a default setting rather than by anyone's judgement.

This repository has no CodeRabbit configuration at all, so this is a new file and changes nothing else. No code, no tests, no locale data.

Verified against CodeRabbit's own configuration reference: `reviews.auto_review.drafts` is documented as "Include draft PRs" and defaults to `false`, which is why nothing here has been auto-reviewed.

The sequencing question — which branch the file is read from — is settled, and this pull request answered it about itself. Its own branch carries the configuration with `drafts: true`, and CodeRabbit still posted "Draft PR not reviewed" here. So the file is read from the base branch, not from a pull request's head, and it changes nothing for any pull request already open until it merges.

That makes this the one change worth taking out of order. Every other open pull request in this repository stays unreviewable-by-default until this one lands, and seventeen of them need that review before their review stage can pass.

author: kamoras
body:
## Summary

Twelve states (MI, NY, OH, WI, NV, SC, MO, OK, DE, LA, RI, NH) have no
state-specific confirmed-candidates pipeline at all, so their ballot
pages fall back to a heuristically-tiered guess from raw FEC filer data
instead of the clean, confirmed list every other state gets. This adds
**Google Civic Information API** (`voterInfoQuery`) as a confirmation
source for their **Senate races** — the same race Michigan's original
ballot-clarity bug ([kamoras/civitas#535](https://github.com/kamoras/civitas/pull/535)) was about.

**Senate only, deliberately**: `voterInfoQuery` resolves to the one
precinct a fixed address sits in, so one address per state can only ever
honestly cover the statewide Senate race, not every House district too.
Real House coverage would need one hand-curated address per
congressional district (~97 across these states) — a separate, larger
effort this PR doesn't attempt.

**No new DB column, no `elections.py` change, no frontend change
needed**: `_candidate_source()` already forks `"confirmed"`/`"nominees"`
purely from `Candidate.confirmed_general` plus a state-level config flag
(NJ's own certification-PDF entry is already live precedent for a
non-primary-derived source going through this exact fork), and the
frontend's tiered-vs-flat rendering already treats anything but
`"filers"`/`"primary"` as the flat, confirmed view. So a Civic-confirmed
Senate candidate gets highlighted differently, fully automatically.

**Ships dormant.** Verified live 2026-09-10 against production's real
`GOOGLE_CIVIC_API_KEY` that Google's election index carries nothing for
the November 2026 general yet, for any state — this self-activates once
Google populates real data, matching `civic_info.py`'s own precedent (it
shipped in August against zero live data too). A genuine fetch failure
is distinguished from "nothing published yet" via an explicit sentinel —
collapsing the two would have silently reported every state's real
outage as a healthy empty run, every night, until real data exists to
reveal the difference.

**Also fixes a real interaction with the weekly source-discovery
crawler**: a hand-verified entry normally shadows `crawl_for_new_sources`'
search for a real vendor. Since `google_civic` is a national fallback,
not a real per-district source, it's carved out so these 12 states keep
getting probed weekly for a genuine vendor regardless — a find still
can't auto-override the hand-verified entry, it just becomes visible in
the discovered-sources file for a human to promote.

author: halildeu
body:
Tracked by Halildeu/platform-backend#882 (ES-301). First testable slice: the **escalation event model** — recorded per case and per obligation, on the WORM audit ledger, visible on the staff API. Not the whole of #882.

## What
- `ethics.sla.escalation.{enabled,steps}` — owner-supplied policy, **off by default**; `steps` are offsets after the statutory deadline for level 1..n (max 5, strictly increasing, ≤ 90d, no empty entries). Fails at boot otherwise. The policy arithmetic takes two instants only; a pause cannot reach it (pinned by test).
- `ethics_case_escalation` — V25 (portable) + V26 (PostgreSQL append-only trigger). `UNIQUE (case_id, obligation, level)`; rows are self-describing (`due_at`, `threshold_at`, `escalated_at`).
- `EscalationSweeper` — deterministic on `now` (truncated to microseconds, like the column); one `REQUIRES_NEW` transaction per case that takes the case row with **`FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`** so acknowledgement/closure writes serialise with the decision and a held row is *deferred* to the next cycle instead of stalling the rest; escalation row + `ethics.case.escalated` audit outbox row atomically; level-index collision skipped only after rollback; any other integrity failure is a fault; per-case failure isolation; `recorded` meter incremented only from the committed count; disabled = no-op through `runCycle` too. Payload = exact six-field allowlist (no actor, no free text, no person). Logs carry a failure class name and counts — never an exception message or trace (log-capture test with PII sentinels).
- `CaseSummary`/`CaseDetail`: `escalationLevel` (highest level ever recorded — history, not activity) + `escalatedAt`; timeline detail `OBLIGATION L<n>`.

## Deliberately not in this slice
- A notification event type. The outbox→orchestrator transport uses one fixed template and one subscriber; a `CASE_ESCALATED` ping would be identical to the daily `SLA_BREACH` signal. Second-tier routing (orchestrator template + OpenFGA topic tuples + recipient) is Halildeu/platform-backend#1153 on the Etik Speak board.
- mfe-ethic column for the level (next slice, platform-web).
- The feedback window stays `createdAt + ethics.sla.feedback-within` as the service already measures it (owner's product threshold); this slice records against it, unchanged.
- Backfill: if the sweeper is down while a threshold passes and the obligation is met before it returns, no row is invented for the interval (documented on the class).

## Evidence
`./mvnw -pl ethics-service -am test` (local, Testcontainers via colima), after the Codex revisions (head 0ee47655): **Tests run: 422, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0**.
- `EscalationSweeperTest` 18 (fixed clock: strictly-after threshold, nanosecond vs microsecond boundary, level progression, idempotency, ack/close stop, ack-committed-before-lock, held row deferred, disabled no-op, collision vs fault, isolation, rolled-back level not counted, exact payload keys, no exception text in logs)
- `EthicsSlaEscalationPropertiesTest` 10 (incl. the microsecond precision contract for nanosecond steps/deadlines)
- `EscalationIntegrationTest` 4 (H2: two sweeps → one row per level, audit rows, detail/list/timeline JSON, late ack keeps level, ack-first → no level, schema refuses duplicate)
- `EscalationRollbackTest` 1 (audit write failure → no escalation row)
- `EscalationPostgresIntegrationTest` 6 (two concurrent sweeps; sub-microsecond step agrees with the CHECK constraint; held row deferred without stalling the case behind it and no level after its acknowledgement commits; V26 trigger; unique index message; nanosecond/microsecond boundary against the CHECK; `ddl-auto=validate`)

## Cross-AI (thread `01a089ec`)
- Plan-time: Codex REVISE, nine findings absorbed (commit 01adaaee body).
- Post-impl: Codex REVISE, four findings absorbed (commit 965c04d0: no exception text in logs, NOWAIT + deferred, commit-counted meter, microsecond boundary); re-review REVISE, one P2 absorbed (commit 0ee47655: one microsecond contract for deadline, threshold and record); **final re-review AGREE** on `965c04d0..0ee47655` (GPT-6-based Codex, read-only, tests reported by implementer).

Consultation mode: single
Implementer: Claude (Anthropic)
Reviewer: Codex (OpenAI) — AGREE (thread 01a089ec)

author: aterrylu
body:
## What & why The agent-row context menu (ADR-093) shipped without **Rename** — deferred over a CC `customTitle` ownership wrinkle and a PTY-injection concern. Terry brought it back with a concrete motivation: people trying autonomOS **resume agents from the Projects tab from existing Claude Code sessions that "never had a name to begin with,"** and there was no way to give them one. This adds a **Rename…** item to the context menu (running rows) that renames by **restarting the agent under a new name** — Terry's specified design (ADR-096), warned so the restart is never a surprise. ## How A CC agent's name is baked in at spawn via `--name`; there's no live-rename primitive. So rename changes the **record** name first, then restarts so the resumed session boots with the new `--name`: ```mermaid flowchart LR R["Rename… (menu)"] --> F["inline input + warning:
'Renaming restarts this
session — resumes'"] F -->|submit| P["PATCH /api/agents/:id
patchAgent name, version"] P -->|409 namesake / stale| E["error inline,
form stays open
(nothing torn down)"] P -->|ok| K[kill] --> A["attach
(re-reads agent.name → --name)"] --> S["switchPane
(pane refocused, #353)"] ``` - **Server:** re-adds `PATCH /api/agents/:id` (the once-removed route, now on the body-`version` optimistic-concurrency convention) → `patchAgent(id, {name})`, emits `agent.updated`. A **namesake collision** (another *running* agent already holds the name) is a **409 at PATCH time — before anything is killed** — mirroring `spawnAgent`'s guard so the restart's attach can't leave the agent stopped under a half-applied rename. - **Client:** `agentsApi.rename` + `store.renameSession` = patch → `restartSession` (reusing its `kill → attach → switchPane` compose, incl. the #353 pane re-open). The rename **rethrows before** the restart, so a failed rename kills nothing. - **Menu:** the body swaps for a pre-filled name input + the warning. An **unchanged name is a no-op** (never a bare restart); a failure shows the reason inline and keeps the form open (mirrors the Delete inline-confirm); **Escape peels rename mode first** (LIFO escape stack), then the menu. - **customTitle caveat (documented, ADR-096):** the new name is authoritative for the **sidebar/record** and for the motivating no-name case (no `customTitle`). A session `/rename`-d *inside Claude* keeps that in-session title on the **Projects tab** + name-lookups until re-`/rename`d — accepted for v1; making the record name authoritative there is a scoped follow-up. - **Scope:** rename is **running-only** (it restarts under the new name) — the motivating flow is Resume→then→Rename on the now-running managed agent. A one-step "Resume as…" for exited/external Projects rows is a possible follow-up. ## Testing - **`make check`-equivalent green locally:** biome ✅, `tsc --build` (dashboard + server) ✅, **dashboard vitest 568** ✅, **server 1041** ✅. - **Server route** (`agents-rename-route.test.ts`, 6): rename+version-bump, trim, empty→400, whitespace→400, namesake→409 (name unchanged), stale-version→409, unknown-id→404. - **Store** (`store.renameSession.test.ts`, 4): patch-**before**-restart ordering, trim, **rethrow-before-teardown** (restart never fires on a failed rename), empty-name guard (no API call). - **Context-menu dom** (5 new): Rename… present on running / absent on exited; pre-filled input + restart warning; submit calls `renameSession` + closes; Cancel returns to the menu; unchanged/blank name = no-op; failure keeps the form open with the reason. **Screenshots** (both themes) in the first comment: the menu with Rename…, and rename mode (input + warning). ## Checklist - [x] `make check`-equivalent passes locally (biome + tsc + dashboard vitest + server tests) - [x] Conventional-commit title (`feat:`) - [x] Architectural decision recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-096) - [ ] `make hero` — N/A (the context menu is transient; not in the static hero, same as #353) - [ ] **HOLD for Terry's visual gate** (his go before merge) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01CwEqcpy5nXYCCqL2V6wf6k

author: dante-dan
body:
## Description

Accept OpenAI Responses lifecycle events from compatible providers when they omit metadata that Cherry Studio does not need to parse streamed content. Sparse `response.created` events no longer discard subsequent text, and sparse `response.failed` events retain partial output and surface numeric provider error codes.

Content-bearing response chunks remain strictly validated, so malformed deltas and tool events still produce schema errors.

Fixes #20282

## Changes

- make `response.created` ID, timestamp, and model metadata optional in public and internal Responses adapters
- accept omitted `sequence_number` and numeric error codes on `response.failed`
- avoid constructing an invalid timestamp when `created_at` is absent
- add real `doStream` SSE fixtures for sparse created and failed lifecycle events

## Checklist

- [x] Focused main-process tests pass (`5/5`)
- [x] ESLint passes for the new regression test
- [x] The combined pnpm patch applies cleanly to a pristine `@ai-sdk/openai@3.0.109` package
- [x] Lockfile patch hashes are regenerated
- [x] Commit is GitHub Verified and includes DCO sign-off

## Release notes

Fixed compatible OpenAI Responses streams failing after HTTP 200 when lifecycle events omit optional metadata.

Every engineer's master CI is red: `Python code quality` fails on the scheduled Python CI run and on any PR that reaches that job.

author: hneyra
body:
Cierra #61.

## El defecto, y no hubo que provocarlo

`espera-al-motor` —el `initContainer` que #44 inyecta en todo proceso que habla con la base—
declaraba `runAsNonRoot: true` **sin `runAsUser`** sobre la imagen del motor, que **arranca como
root a proposito** y por tanto no declara ningun `USER`. El kubelet no puede comprobar que no sea
root sin ejecutarla, y se niega a crear el contenedor.

Medido en `stg` el 2026-09-10, en el diagnostico que el tope de `aplicar-stg` dejo volcar por
primera vez (#59):

```
Warning  Failed  4m45s (x395 over 89m)  kubelet
  spec.initContainers{espera-al-motor}: Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root
```

**395 intentos en 89 minutos**, en todos los `Job` de migracion e implantacion y en los `CronJob`
de los cinco sistemas. La migracion de `identidad` nunca corrio, su base se quedo sin esquema, y de
ahi cuelga que su `Deployment` no llegara a `Ready` y que el `pulumi up` se pasara quince minutos
esperandolo.

La contradiccion ya estaba escrita en este repositorio: `BaseDeDatos.ts` le omite `runAsNonRoot` al
contenedor del motor **con su motivo**, y la espera corre con **la misma imagen** declarando lo
contrario.

## Lo que se arregla

1. **La espera lleva su UID escrito**: `runAsUser: 65534`, el que este repositorio ya usa para toda
   imagen que no declara uno propio (`mailpit`, `curlimages/curl`, los cuatro exportadores). Es
   #157 y #268 por tercera vez, y las tres se cierran igual.
2. **`pg_isready` dice con que usuario pregunta** (`-U postgres`). Con un UID que la imagen no
   tenga en su `/etc/passwd`, un `pg_isready` sin `-U` devuelve codigo 3 —«no attempt»— que este
   bucle no distingue de «el motor no contesta»: cinco minutos de espera y un mensaje que acusa al
   motor de algo que no ha hecho. No autentica nada.
3. **La guarda se muda y pasa a mirar el ambiente entero.** «todo contenedor endurecido fija su
   `runAsUser`» la escribio #268 y vivia en `componentes.test.ts` leyendo `construirManifiestos`,
   o sea **la plataforma**: medido, **12 contenedores de los 56**. No fallo — *dejo de mirar*, que
   es C-16, `E` y #10 otra vez. Ahora vive en `verificaciones/usuario-de-los-contenedores`, lee los
   dos ambientes, llavea la exencion por **imagen** (un nombre no es una imagen) y **relee** el
   `USER` numerico del `Dockerfile` de cada clon en `origin/main`, en vez de creerselo de un
   comentario.
4. **Y queda dicho por que la auditoria tampoco lo veia**: `conEsperaAlMotor` inyecta la espera
   *despues* de componer y auditar, asi que el unico contenedor que no audita nadie es el que dejo
   el ambiente parado.

## La medida que decide la forma de la guarda

Un «todo `runAsNonRoot` exige `runAsUser`» habria sido #437: **47 de 55 contenedores lo declaran
sin `runAsUser` y 46 funcionan**, porque su imagen fija un `USER` numerico (`10001`/`10002` en los
cinco `backend/Dockerfile`, `101` en las dos interfaces, `1000` en Keycloak, `472` en Grafana). El
unico que revienta es `espera-al-motor`. La regla no es «declara un UID» sino «declara un UID **que
el kubelet pueda verificar**».

## Como se demostro que muerde

**La primera rotura es el estado de `origin/main`.** En un banco —*worktree* de `e29ba87` con los
cinco clones hermanos al lado— `yarn verificar` da **936 de 936 en verde** con el ambiente sin
poder desplegarse; copiando ahi los dos archivos de la guarda nueva salen **4 en rojo**, dos por
ambiente, nombrando los **dieciseis** contenedores uno a uno con el mensaje del kubelet dentro. La
guarda vieja verde y la nueva roja sobre el mismo codigo.

Y seis mas, cada una **sola** y restaurada por copia comparada con `cmp` («RESTAURADO IGUAL» las
seis):

| | rotura | rojo |
|---|---|---|
| M2 | quitar el `-U` de `pg_isready` | 2 |
| M3 | quitar del censo `kamayuk-rentas`, que si se despliega | 2, nombrando sus cuatro contenedores |
| M4 | declarar una imagen que no despliega nadie | 1 |
| M5 | declarar `USER 10009` donde el Dockerfile dice 10001 | 1: «declara «10001» (linea 83), «10002» (linea 96)» |
| M6 | vaciar `USER_POR_NOMBRE_PENDIENTE` | 1: «`catastro frontend/Dockerfile nginx`» |
| M7 | el censo **sin sujeto** | 5 |

**M7 es el contraste que justifica el centinela**: con el censo vacio, las dos comprobaciones por
las que existe este PR pasan en **VERDE** —«ninguno se queda sin UID» es cierto sobre el conjunto
vacio— y lo unico que cae son los centinelas y los censos.

**M6 nombra un defecto latente real y ajeno**: `catastro/frontend/Dockerfile` declara `USER nginx`
donde `rentas` y `caja` declaran `USER 101`. Hoy no rompe nada porque su interfaz no la despliega
su descriptor (#12); el dia que la despliegue, no creara el contenedor. Queda **declarado** con su
issue y en las dos direcciones, y no se arregla desde aqui.

## Cifras

- `yarn verificar` **936 → 948**, `Test Files 45 → 46`, **0 rojas antes y despues**; `eslint` y los
  dos `tsc` verdes en las dos. Las **+12** son −2 (las dos que salen de `componentes.test.ts`,
  143 → 141) +12 del archivo nuevo +2 del `-U`.
- **Lo desplegado se movio exactamente donde tenia que moverse**: `yarn manifiestos` cambia **48
  lineas en cada ambiente** = 16 `runAsUser: 65534` nuevos + 16 guiones con `-U` + sus 16 lineas
  viejas, o sea **los dieciseis `espera-al-motor` y nada mas**. `stg` 390 913 → 391 737 bytes,
  `prod` 383 782 → 384 606.
- `yarn capacidad` **identico** en los dos, «cabe» y «no-cabe» incluidos: un `runAsUser` no ocupa
  nodo.
- **Ningun `pulumi up`.**

## Lo que NO cierra

- **No se ejercio contra el cluster**: aqui no hay `kubectl` ni demonio de Docker. Que el contenedor
  arranque lo dira `aplicar-stg` en la corrida siguiente — y con #59 dentro, si algo sigue parado
  el diagnostico lo volcara.
- **65534 no es «el UID de postgres en esa imagen»**: el `blob` de configuracion esta detras de una
  redireccion que el proxy de este puesto rechaza, asi que no se pudo leer. Es el UID que este
  repositorio usa para las imagenes que no declaran ninguno, y `-U postgres` es lo que hace que esa
  eleccion no dependa de que exista en su `/etc/passwd`.
- **`stg` tiene un segundo bloqueante, ajeno a este PR**: el `Job` del realm sale con «FALLO: el
  realm «sgtm» no tiene el ambito «kamayuk-servicio»» — su camino de actualizacion no importa el
  ambito que #21 anadio.
- **El diagnostico de #40 no vuelca los pods en `CrashLoopBackOff`**, porque los elige por fase y
  esa fase es `Running`. Queda dicho y sin arreglar.

author: omgbabyweb
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two background-review failure modes without changing the foreground Codex runtime:

1. Selecting a different Codex model for `auxiliary.background_review` can leave the detached fork on `codex_app_server`. The inherited/same-model branch already converts this to `codex_responses`, but the different-model branch does not. Apply the same conversion there so the supplied review history and Hermes tool restrictions use the intended detached execution path.
2. A review snapshot or later tool-expanded request can exceed the review model's context threshold before the cumulative input-usage budget can help. Check each prepared review request against its own compressor threshold before provider dispatch, including the first request.

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. Searched existing open/closed PRs and issues. #105830/#105835 address primary-runtime selection during fallback; #94832 addresses routed reasoning-effort settings. Those are separate from this change.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/background_review.py`: normalize routed Codex runtime selection, reject residual app-server mode before detached fork construction, and classify size-guard exits as skipped reviews.
- `agent/turn_preflight_gate.py`: reuse the already-prepared request-pressure estimate and the review agent's `context_compressor.threshold_tokens`. Skip invalid sizing or over-threshold requests, refund the unused call, and preserve existing cleanup.
- Add synthetic regression fixtures in `tests/run_agent/test_background_review_{routing_guard,request_size}.py`.

The guard applies only to snapshot background-review forks, not foreground turns, `/btw`, or standalone curator runs. Later detached compaction still runs normally; rebuilt requests are rechecked on the next loop pass. The guard does not compact the parent, truncate stored transcripts, add a tokenizer/configuration key, or guarantee exact agreement with provider token accounting. Normal review cadence remains unchanged. Existing cumulative review-usage budgets remain separate.

## How to Test

With development dependencies installed:

```sh
python -m pytest tests/run_agent/test_background_review*.py tests/run_agent/test_preflight*.py tests/agent/test_preflight*.py tests/agent/test_engine_preflight_wire.py tests/agent/test_native_preflight_estimate.py -q
```

**106 passed** on macOS with Python 3.11, pytest 9.1.1, and pytest-asyncio 1.3.0, based on upstream `cfdbbb6e35010ace89fbe8243ee82fa4de143e10` plus this branch. The test process emitted a non-failing auxiliary title-generation warning because no provider was configured for that task.

Coverage includes routed/same-model/non-Codex selection, preserved runtime fields, digest forwarding, default Responses medium effort, oversized initial and subsequent requests, invalid estimates, review-model capacity rather than parent capacity, compaction rebuilds, unaffected non-review paths, and skipped-review cleanup.

The same runtime changes were also exercised in a local deployment through an automatic Codex background review using real Responses calls. That deployment has other local patches, so the clean-upstream synthetic test result above is the portable evidence for this PR. No private transcripts, credentials, profile settings, or deployment machinery are included.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution guidance and searched for related PRs.
- [x] Conventional commit messages; only changes related to this fix.
- [x] Added regression tests and ran the focused suites listed above.
- [ ] Full `pytest tests/ -q` suite — not run.
- [x] Tested on macOS; no new platform-specific code or dependencies.
- [x] Updated resolver docstring and explanatory comments.
- [x] Config examples, tool schemas, and architecture instructions: N/A; no new settings or tool capabilities.

AI-assisted contribution, inspected and tested. The routing and guard changes are separate commits if maintainers prefer splitting them.

body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This PR does not apply its own patch. One `cp` by a human completes it — see
> `.dev/features/canon-write-denylist/proposed/APPLY.md`.**

Addresses `canon-write-denylist-open` (HIGH, dimensions B3/D).

## Why the agent could not land it

**All three write-guard scripts are protected by the very hook this patch edits**, so *no* version of
this fix is agent-writable. Probed live:

```
echo '{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":"<path>"}}' | node .claude/hooks/protect-trusted-paths.cjs
  .claude/hooks/protect-trusted-paths.cjs  -> exit 2   (denied)
  .claude/hooks/enforce-writes-scope.cjs   -> exit 2   (denied)
  .claude/hooks/set-writes-scope.cjs       -> exit 2   (denied)
```

CLAUDE.md is explicit — _"do not try to edit them or work around the hook; if a change is genuinely
needed, say so and let a human edit them outside the agent loop"_ — and it names routing an in-repo
write through Bash to dodge the guard as the thing not to do. **Nothing was bypassed.** The complete,
verified replacement is staged under `proposed/`.

## The defect

`THREAT-MODEL.md` maps **memory poisoning** — its own _"worst persistence vector"_ — to _"gated write /
pre-write hook."_ That mapping did not hold:

- `/pharn-build` scopes from an **untrusted `PLAN.md`'s `## Files`** via `--from-plan`
- `enforce-writes-scope.test.cjs` **pins** that a scope of `[memory-bank/lessons-learned.md]` is **ALLOWED**
- `set-writes-scope.cjs` refuses only the `.claude/` control paths
- `protect-trusted-paths.cjs` had **zero** `memory-bank` references

So the human accept/deny gate on canon — the entire point of `/pharn-memory-promote` — was **bypassable
by a `## Files` entry**, and no human approves a *product* `PLAN.md`.

## The escape is not self-grantable — the hard part

The hook reads `PreToolUse` JSON on **stdin**, so an argv flag (the `--allow-claude-dir` shape) is
unavailable. Authorization is instead derived from the writes-scope record's **`set_by` provenance**: a
canon write is permitted only when the active scope was set **from one of the two promote command
files** *and* names **exactly that one canon path**.

**A scope whose `set_by` is a `PLAN.md` does not authorize** — probe case F, the finding's exact vector.

## Verified by execution, not by reading (L37)

`proposed/probe.mjs` stages the hook into a throwaway fixture repo and asserts every claimed bound:
**59/59, exit 0.**

Case variants + Unicode full-fold (`ſ`) · file / **directory** / **dangling** symlinks · hard-link
aliases · 13 near-miss refusals · all four write tools · both deny-message branches with each remedy
**absent from the other** · an **L34 non-vacuity control** so the suite cannot pass by denying everything.

### The probe found a real defect that reading had not

The first draft AND-ed `!aliased` into the authorization test. A canon file that merely **carries** a
second hard link has `nlink > 1`, lands in `CANON_INODES`, and was therefore **denied on its own declared
path** — `/pharn-memory-promote` would have broken on any hard-linked canon file.

The branch now splits on `ck !== null` first, and §H pins the pair: alias denied **and** the same scope
still authorizes the real path.

## Narrowed, and stated (P0)

This covers `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` only. **Bash-tool writes bypass `PreToolUse` entirely**,
exactly as for the trusted docs. It **narrows** the gap; it does not close it.

## To complete this PR

```bash
cp .dev/features/canon-write-denylist/proposed/protect-trusted-paths.cjs .claude/hooks/protect-trusted-paths.cjs
git diff .claude/hooks/protect-trusted-paths.cjs        # review
node .dev/features/canon-write-denylist/proposed/probe.mjs   # 59/59
npm run check
```

Then bump `SKILLS_VERSION` (`.claude/hooks/*.cjs` is product surface) with the matching README badge and
CHANGELOG entry.

body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Wait for a successful query through the Hive Metastore Thrift endpoint before starting Python integration tests. Bound readiness commands and polling with a deadline, and clean up the container if initialization fails.

### Why are the changes needed?

The image's Hive CLI check can use an embedded metastore and report success while port 9083 is unavailable. The previous asyncio timeout cannot interrupt synchronous Docker calls and sleeps.

Observed in [PythonIT](https://github.com/apache/gravitino/actions/runs/34436219502/job/102745773502), where relational-table setup and catalog-tag cleanup failed with Metastore connection refused.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Only Python integration-test infrastructure changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Four regression tests cover readiness retries, deadline handling, Docker errors, and failed-startup cleanup. All passed for 50 consecutive runs (200 executions, with mocked Docker and clock). Black, Pylint, and spotlessApply passed. Full Docker PythonIT was not rerun locally.

CI repetition results for commit `958bcfc88d` (each complete PythonIT attempt covers Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12):

author: chrisyoung
body:
## What

A new `qa/stress_domains/waybill` — the first `process_manager` (saga) anywhere in this corpus to `dispatch` into a NESTED ENTITY's own command, rather than a plain aggregate's.

Per `.claude/skills/hecks_qa/SKILL.md`'s "Authoring a new stress domain" section: `pizzas`/`banking`/`ledger_ordering`/`nested_pieces` have all had many consecutive clean passes, and this session's five bugs (BUG#1-5, all merged) never touched saga/process_manager machinery at all. Checked directly against every existing saga in the corpus before authoring — banking's own `Onboarding`/`Settlement`/`ExternalSettlement`, `quality_control`'s own `BugCiWatch` — none dispatches into an entity command, and `nested_pieces` proves entity nesting fuzzes correctly but never declares a `process_manager` at all. The combination was genuinely untested.

## What it found, first real run

The combination does not work today. `SagaInterpreter#qualified` (`lib/hecks/runtime/saga_interpreter.rb`) decides whether a dispatch's own `command_name` already carries an explicit domain qualifier with one heuristic — `command_name.include?("::")`. That's correct for a plain aggregate command and for a genuinely cross-domain one, but a bare, same-domain entity command reference (`dispatch Manifest::Slot::Fill`) collapses to the identical one-`::`-remaining shape after `Naming.command_ref`'s rewrite, for a completely different reason (entity nesting, not a domain qualifier). `qualified` picks the cross-domain reading, so the dispatch never gets prefixed with its own domain, and `ReactionInvocation.resolve_target` reads the aggregate name as a nonexistent domain — `UnknownVerb`, treated (correctly, by its own lights) as an ordinary domain refusal. `PolicyInterpreter#deliver` does **not** share this bug — confirmed by direct comparison, not assumed: it carries a cross-domain qualifier in a separate `target_domain:` field, never inferred from the command reference string.

A sibling of this exact `Naming.command_ref`-shape ambiguity is already named in `lib/hecks/bluebook/model_check.rb`'s own `ALLOWED_FINDINGS["quality_control"]`, for `PolicyBuilder`'s own port-operation triggers — so this isn't a one-off; it's a second confirmed instance of a known-but-unfixed family.

## Not fixed here, on purpose

Same restraint `nested_pieces/NOTES.md` already exercised for BUG#4: this domain was authored from an isolated worktree with no access to `qa/bluebook/quality_control.bluebook`'s own persisted ledger, so the `Bug.log`/judgment/fix lifecycle belongs to the session that holds it, not to this PR. Full account — including why `lib/hecks/bluebook/model_check.rb`'s own `ALLOWED_FINDINGS` was deliberately left untouched (stress domains aren't in its own CI-gated corpus, and there's a documented sharp edge in `spec/model_check_spec.rb`'s own stale-allowlist check for exactly this situation) and a suggested fix for whoever picks this up — is in `qa/stress_domains/waybill/NOTES.md`.

## Verification

- `spec/waybill_spec.rb` (3 examples) demonstrates the finding directly: the saga's two working aggregate-level legs (`Manifest.Open`/`Manifest.AddSlot`), the entity-level leg's refusal (`Manifest::Slot.Fill`, with the exact recorded reason), and the downstream consequence (the saga always cancels — `ConsignmentShipped`, its own `ends_on`, is unreachable today).
- `bin/fuzz qa/stress_domains/waybill --seeds 40 --steps 30` — clean, 0 property violations, 0 crashes. The refusal is caught as an ordinary domain refusal, so property fuzzing alone never surfaces this — only the hand-written spec does.
- `bin/model_check qa/stress_domains/waybill` — 1 documented, expected error (`unknown_dispatch`, `Packing`) and 2 harmless `stuck_state` warnings (terminal lifecycle states). Not part of `bin/model_check`'s own default sweep or `spec/model_check_spec.rb`'s `MODEL_CHECK_CORPUS` (same as `ledger_ordering`/`nested_pieces`), so no `ALLOWED_FINDINGS` entry was added — see NOTES.md.
- Full local suite: 2534 examples, 0 failures.
- `rubocop`: clean.
- Pre-push gate (suite, fuzzer, engine agreement, model checks, doc coverage, rubocop): all green.

## Not registered as a Target

Per the task's own restriction: this was authored from an isolated worktree with no write access to the persistent ledger (`qa/data/*.heki` lives in a different worktree). Registering `waybill` as a real `Target` (`identify`) and logging the finding as a `Bug` is left to the session that holds that ledger.

body:
## Summary

- merge concurrent multipart part registrations with conditional state retries instead of exposing storage CAS conflicts to clients
- accept the request conventions emitted by common S3 clients: case-insensitive checksum mode, explicit `STANDARD` storage class, and the `RestoreStatus` list hint
- treat validated empty trailing-slash PUT/DELETE requests as virtual filesystem directory hints without adding marker blobs to Git
- report Git trees as absent objects so filesystem clients can fall back from HEAD to prefix listing
- update the frozen protocol contract and crate README with these compatibility boundaries

## Why

This is a follow-up to #166 based on live compatibility qualification rather than synthetic request construction alone. PyArrow, rclone, Spark/S3A, and Trino each exposed a distinct real request shape that the gateway previously rejected. Each source fix is generic to the S3 contract and has a regression test.

## Live interoperability proof

All clients used the release gateway against the same RustFS-backed Crab repository. Writes were then read through the client and recovered through an independent `crab://` clone.

| Client | Qualified behavior |
| --- | --- |
| DuckDB 1.5.1 | Read 1.5M-row Parquet, filtered it, and wrote/read 35,289,510 bytes with exact row invariants |
| LanceDB 0.38.0 | Opened, added, vector-searched, and persisted Lance transaction, manifest, and data objects |
| PyArrow 25.0.1 | Ranged Parquet reads plus a 250k-row write/read round trip |
| Polars 1.44.2 | Predicate read plus a 200k-row write/read round trip |
| delta-rs 1.6.3 | Overwrite, append, history, and four simultaneous optimistic commits; 190k unique rows at version 5 |
| rclone 1.75.1 | 500 MiB, 16-part concurrent multipart upload; eight-stream exact-SHA readback; server-side copy, move, and delete |
| PyIceberg 0.12.0 | Two snapshots/appends with 150k rows and durable metadata, manifest, and Parquet objects |
| Spark 4.2.0 / Hadoop 3.5.0 | Standard S3A temporary-directory/rename flow; 100k unique rows across four Parquet parts plus `_SUCCESS` |
| Trino 483 | Native-S3 ranged read of 1.5M rows; Hive write/read of 1,000 rows remained readable after a fresh Trino process |
| ClickHouse 26.8.2.7 | Read 1.5M Parquet rows and wrote/read 100k rows with exact bounds and uniqueness |

The retained rclone object is 524,288,000 bytes. A fresh build from this branch returned an unaligned `bytes=1048573-2097159` request as 1,048,587 bytes with `Content-Range: bytes 1048573-2097159/524288000`.

An independent Crab clone passed `git fsck --full --strict`. Direct Git blobs and S3 logical objects matched SHA-256 for PyArrow, ClickHouse, Spark, and Trino samples.

## Compatibility findings

- A deliberately excessive Delta Lake burst exceeded the gateway's 32-request admission bound and received S3 `SlowDown`; the same four-writer optimistic-commit workload at normal file fanout completed correctly. No partial Delta commit became visible.
- The qualification repository reached 345 immutable packs and emits Crab's existing repack recommendation. Clone and strict Git validation still succeed; pack compaction is an operational follow-up, not changed here.

author: yiliang114
body:
## What this PR does

Grants the scheduled desktop packaging check the two permissions the release workflow's own jobs declare, so it can start.

## Why it's needed

The first dispatch of the check died in two seconds with no job, no step and no annotation — the shape of a startup failure. A workflow that calls another must grant every permission the called workflow's jobs declare, and the release workflow's publish job declares write access to contents while the OSS mirror job asks to read actions. The check granted read access to contents and nothing else.

The trap is that this validation happens when the file is loaded, before any condition is evaluated. Both of those jobs are unreachable from this check — it hardcodes a dry run, and each of them is additionally gated on a real publish — but being unreachable does not exempt their declared permissions from the comparison. So a check that can never write still has to say it may.

Nothing here writes. The dry run leaves the publish and mirror jobs skipped on their own conditions, exactly as it did in the release runs this reuses.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Dispatch the check against `main` and confirm it now starts and fans out into the release workflow's four build jobs, and that the publish and mirror jobs report skipped rather than running. Before this change the same dispatch produced a run with zero jobs.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: run [34444598159](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/34444598159), `startup_failure`, 2 seconds, no jobs. After: a run that reaches the build matrix.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A  |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️ not tested  |

Workflow permission resolution only happens on GitHub's side, so this can only be confirmed by dispatching after merge.

### Environment (optional)

N/A

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a scheduled workflow now declares write access to contents that it never exercises. The narrower alternative would be relaxing the permissions the release workflow's publish job declares, which trades a real safeguard for a cosmetic one on the caller.
- Not validated / out of scope: whether the check passes once it starts. Its first real run is still ahead of it.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follows #11519.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

为定时的桌面打包检查授予被调用 workflow 各 job 所声明的两项权限，使其能够正常启动。

## 为什么需要

该检查的第一次触发在两秒内结束，没有 job、没有 step、也没有任何注解——这是启动失败的典型形态。调用方 workflow 必须授予被调用 workflow 中各 job 所声明的全部权限，而发布 workflow 的 publish job 声明了对 contents 的写权限，OSS 镜像 job 则请求读取 actions。该检查只授予了 contents 的读权限。

陷阱在于：这项校验发生在文件被加载时，早于任何条件求值。这两个 job 从本检查出发都是不可达的——它把 dry run 写死为 true，而两者各自还有以真实发布为前提的门槛——但"不可达"并不能让它们声明的权限免于比对。因此一个永远不会写入的检查，仍然必须声明它可能写入。

这里不会有任何写入。dry run 会让 publish 与镜像 job 按各自条件保持 skipped，与它所复用的那些发布运行中的表现完全一致。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

针对 `main` 触发该检查，确认它现在能够启动并展开为发布 workflow 的四个构建 job，且 publish 与镜像 job 报告 skipped 而非实际运行。在此改动之前，同样的触发产生的是一个零 job 的运行。

### 证据（Before & After）

之前：运行 [34444598159](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/34444598159)，`startup_failure`，2 秒，无任何 job。之后：能够走到构建矩阵的运行。

### 测试平台

| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  N/A  |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️ 未测试  |

workflow 的权限解析只发生在 GitHub 侧，因此只能在合并后通过触发来确认。

### 环境（可选）

N/A

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：一个定时 workflow 现在声明了它从不使用的 contents 写权限。更收敛的替代方案是放宽发布 workflow 中 publish job 所声明的权限，但那是用一项真实的防护换取调用方形式上的收敛。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：该检查启动之后能否通过。它的第一次真实运行仍在前方。

1957 页 EPUB（212 万字）提炼：读页 50 分钟、198 段并发提炼、最终收紧时 EvoLink 回 103 字坏内容被当成功 → 保留 23 万字 / 581 节原稿 → 前端排出 212 页（5,136 积分）。旧代码 120 分钟总时限也差点把它杀在半路。用户拍板：文件与时间都不设上限、每一步有百分比、成稿档两档到最后仍可切、派生交给便宜模型。

- `invokeDistillLlm` 加 `validate`：坏内容当失败换下一家网关（0910 事故 OpenAI 官方根本没被试到）；final 阶段输出上限 65,536 token、超时 15 分钟。
- 归并停滞后仍喂不下 → 按 `refineMaxChars` 分组强制收紧到目标份额，再做一次全局统稿。
- 挑参考页每组回报 `select` 进度；日志按「第 i/n 组」记。

author: hdkiller
body:
## Summary

Adds `openpapir case import --archive <root> --from <dir> [--json]`, operation
`case.import`: the other direction of `case export`. It reads a directory the
export wrote, checks it in full against the manifest before anything is
written, and publishes the whole record set under the writer lock or none of
it.

## What changed

- **New core module** `crates/openpapir-core/src/export/restore.rs` with
  `restore/{manifest,objects,records,publish}.rs`. The manifest is
  authoritative: nothing outside it is read. Passes run in this order, and the
  first three touch nothing in the archive: read and check the manifest, read
  and parse every record it names, re-digest every object it names. Then the
  writer lock is taken, the record set is probed against the archive, the
  objects are stored through the existing content-addressed store, and the
  records are staged and published.
- **All or nothing at the record level.** Every document is staged in the
  directory it will be published into before any of them is published; a
  publish that fails removes the records already published and the objects
  this import created, so an interrupted import leaves the whole case or
  nothing of it and `archive check` stays clean either way.
- **Idempotence.** A record the archive already holds byte for byte is not
  written again and is not a conflict, and an object it already holds is left
  untouched. An import event is written only for an object this import
  actually stored, so a second import of one export writes nothing at all.
- **Five new codes in the `export` bucket**, all exiting `4`:
  `export.manifest_missing`, `export.manifest_malformed`,
  `export.object_mismatch` (with a closed `reason` set of `absent`, `digest`,
  `length`), `export.record_missing`, `export.record_conflict`. Refusals
  inside a source carry `scope` `export_source`, the counterpart of the
  export's `export_destination`. An export written under another archive
  schema version is refused by the existing schema rules.
- **Import events with `source` `export`.** `ImportEvent` gains an additive
  optional `source` field, absent on every event `import` writes, so an
  archive written by an earlier build reads unchanged. The exported import
  event is restored as a record beside the new one, so the provenance of the
  user's own import survives the round trip.
- **CLI**: `crates/openpapir-cli/src/restore.rs`, one hook in `main.rs`, one
  human renderer in `report.rs`. Human output echoes the `--from` argument
  exactly as `case export` echoes `--to`; no JSON field carries either.
- **Docs**: architecture (invocation list, a new `case import` section, the
  codes table, the decisions section, the privacy rule, the operation count
  from fifteen to sixteen), error-contract (the five codes, the privacy rule,
  what is implemented), archive-layout (Export and backup), specification,
  roadmap (milestone 3 and the local-organiser item, now implemented), index,
  receipt-discovery, README, AGENTS.md, SKILL.md, CHANGELOG.

## Verification

- `./scripts/check.sh` clean.
- `cargo +1.88 check --workspace --all-targets --locked` clean.
- `cargo build --release --locked` and
  `cargo run --locked -p openpapir-cli -- capabilities --json`, which now
  lists sixteen operations.
- `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --locked --fail-under-lines 90`: 96.77% lines.
- New integration tests in `crates/openpapir-cli/tests/restore.rs`, including
  the full round trip: export, `case delete --purge`, import, `archive check`
  clean, `case show` and `association list` byte-identical to before, and the
  new import events carrying `source` `export`. Also a second import that
  changes nothing, a move into a second archive, and one test per refusal,
  each asserting the archive tree is unchanged.

## Goldens changed

- `tests/golden/capabilities/json.json`, `tests/golden/capabilities/human.txt`
  regenerated for the added operation.
- `tests/golden/case.import/` added (success).
- `tests/golden/case.import.manifest-missing/` added (refusal).
- `tests/golden/README.md` lists both new cases and the widened `<root>`
  placeholder note.

## Decisions

1. **An import event is written only for an object this import stored.**
   Writing one per manifest object would make a re-import leave two extra
   records each time, so the acceptance criterion that a second import is
   idempotent and the design's rule that an event is history are both kept by
   tying the event to the object actually created.
2. **`export.object_mismatch` also covers a copy the export does not hold.**
   The manifest is authoritative, so an absent copy and a changed copy are the
   same statement, that the export is not what it claims to be. The closed
   `reason` detail tells them apart without naming a path.
3. **Records are re-rendered from the parsed record rather than copied
   verbatim**, so the archive only ever holds a document this build wrote. For
   an export of this schema version the bytes are identical, which the round
   trip test asserts.
4. **The `--from` argument is echoed in human output**, matching `case export`
   echoing `--to`. The privacy rule in error-contract and architecture is
   widened by exactly that one argument, and no JSON field carries it.
5. **The import caps are the caps of `import`**: the same single-file and
   per-operation byte caps apply while the copies are read and stored.

## Exceptions to Owned Paths

These files are outside the ticket's Owned Paths and were edited because the
change could not be made without them. Each edit is section-local.

- `crates/openpapir-core/src/error.rs`: the five new code constants.
- `crates/openpapir-core/src/archive/mod.rs`: `check_schema_version` made
  `pub(crate)` so the manifest reader refuses an export of another schema
  version by the same rule.
- `crates/openpapir-core/src/archive/import.rs`: the additive `source` field
  on `ImportEvent`, plus the `SOURCE_EXPORT` constant.
- `crates/openpapir-cli/src/report.rs`: the human lines for the new command.
- `crates/openpapir-cli/tests/golden.rs` and
  `crates/openpapir-cli/tests/golden_support/mod.rs`: the two new golden cases
  and the setup they need.
- `crates/openpapir-cli/tests/{archive,contract,records}.rs`: the pinned
  `capabilities` operation list.
- `docs/index.md` and `docs/receipt-discovery.md`: the operation count.

author: szechunyiu
body:
## GSA6 revival levers (#221 morphology zoo)

Implements the four revival levers attributed by the GSA5 rate-read (2.267x distinct-yield collapse from duplicates + 2.171x CPU overhead), each measurable in isolation. One commit per lever. All work in `research/ocm-morphology-zoo-v1/`.

### Lever 1 — novelty-gated allocation (flag `novelty_gate`, default OFF)
- `hpc/gs_run.py:150-176` surrogate arm `rank_prepare`: computes the novelty arms' archive-based `_vec`/`_nov` for the viable cohort (identical recipe: `novelty_vector_of` + `novelty_score` vs `archive.pool()+cohort`, feeding `rng_archive.consider`).
- Rank key gated to `s / (nov + eps)`, `GS_NOVELTY_GATE_EPS = 1e-9` (`gs_run.py:46, 208-212`) — "surrogate proposes, novelty disposes"; simplest defensible multiplicative gate. The gated `rank_fn` also diversifies the SH parent-pool refresh for free (it sorts by the same `rank_fn`), so no separate `successive_halving` refresh change was needed.

### Lever 2 — promotion dedup by phenotype_digest (flag `dedup_promotion`, default OFF)
- `search/successive_halving.py:48-89` `promote()`: new `dedup` + `exclude_digests` kwargs — collapses viable to distinct digests before ranking; tie-shuffle runs before filtering so the rng stream is identical with/without flags.
- Cross-round seen-set seeded from `survivors`, updated as T2 survivors land (`:176, 270`), applied at BOTH promotion sites T0->T1 (`:223`) and T1->T2 (`:250`); echoed in the result dict.

### Lever 3 — GSA5_HOLDOUT_MAE_NAN fix (bugfix, always on)
- `search/surrogate_allocate.py:136-140` `_StumpTree._build`: internal nodes store the subtree-leaf mean, never the NaN marker that `predict()`'s depth guard could return.
- `:208-232` `train_t1`: holdout MAE computed with the ranking impl — builtin stumps for `builtin`, fresh sklearn head fit on the train split (one batched predict) for `sklearn`; asserts finite.
- `hpc/gs_run.py:189-191`: asserts `holdout_mae_t1` finite when stats are assembled.

### Lever 4 — cumulative surrogate + batched predicts (flag `surrogate_cumulative`, default OFF)
- `hpc/gs_run.py:194-208` `on_round_end`: carries ONE `EnsembleSurrogate` across rounds (train_t0 appends; train_t1 refits on all accumulated T1 pairs via `t1_pairs_all`).
- `search/surrogate_allocate.py:298-306` `allocation_scores()`: one feature pass + ONE predict per sklearn head instead of two per-row calls per candidate; verified equal to per-row `allocation_score` (< 1e-9, both impls).

### How GSA6 arms turn each flag on
Flags live in the batch-spec/arm_cfg layer as siblings of `rank` (`gs_run.py:113-116, 128-130`); they are allocation-only, absent from `_FORBIDDEN_SPEC_KEYS`, and pass `submit_gs.py` `validate_batch_spec` unchanged. GSA6 runs one adaptive batch (`submit_gs.py ... --batch spec.json`) of `base_arm: GSA5_surrogate` tasks with `rank: surrogate_allocation` plus exactly one flag per arm: L1=`novelty_gate`, L2=`dedup_promotion`, L4=`surrogate_cumulative` (L3 is already on everywhere). Each task spec is freeze-bound (`freeze_sha256`), and results carry `revival_levers` for per-lever attribution against the GSA5 baseline.

### Notes
- Defaults reproduce frozen GSA5 behavior exactly (verified end-to-end: flags off -> fresh ensemble/round `n_train_t0=9` after 3 rounds, novelty archive untouched, per-row scores). Only lever 3 changes default behavior — it is a bugfix.
- `gs_run.py` asserts `code_digest == freeze["code_digest"]`, so GSA6 must run under a NEW freeze (existing `GRAND_SEARCH_R1_FREEZE.json` is untouched here).
- Pre-existing on origin/main, unrelated to this PR: `tests/test_gs.py::test_gs_run_lane_samplers_produce_genomes` fails on fast hosts (`cpu_seconds > 0.05`; this Mac runs 27 T0 evals in 0.004s). 9/10 tests pass; sanity validated via /tmp synthetic scripts (never committed).
- Not merged — the centre owns merges.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes promotion ranking and surrogate retraining for GSA5/GSA6 experiments; default-off flags preserve frozen behavior except the holdout-MAE fix, which alters surrogate stats logging.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **GSA6 revival levers** for the GSA5 surrogate successive-halving arm: three **default-off** allocation flags (`novelty_gate`, `dedup_promotion`, `surrogate_cumulative`) wired through batch specs and recorded in run output as `revival_levers`.
> 
> **Novelty gate** (`gs_run.py`): optional archive-based novelty on the surrogate arm; promotion rank becomes `allocation_score / (novelty + ε)` and can use batched `allocation_scores` when cumulative mode is on.
> 
> **Promotion dedup** (`successive_halving.py`): optional collapse by `phenotype_digest` before ranking at T0→T1 and T1→T2, plus a cross-round exclude set for digests already promoted to T2.
> 
> **Cumulative surrogate** (`gs_run.py`): optional reuse of one `EnsembleSurrogate` across rounds with monotonically growing T1 training pairs instead of a fresh ensemble each round.
> 
> **Always-on bugfix** (`surrogate_allocate.py`): stump internal nodes no longer store NaN (fixes poisoned holdout MAE); T1 holdout MAE is computed with the same impl used for ranking (sklearn vs builtin), with finite-MAE asserts in training and `gs_run`.

Checked every address in `docs/demo-video-script.md` against the chain rather than against `deployments.md`, on the day it gets read aloud.

```
0x0524a353…    163 bytes  AQUA ok   ← current HelicoMandateSwap, a proxy
0xe8515af9…    163 bytes  AQUA ok   ← current HelicoOracleBoard, a proxy
0xeb480C09…  7,872 bytes  AQUA ok   ← the FIRST board, superseded twice

0xb0A125F5…  5,789 bytes  no AQUA   ← CompoundVenue over cWETHv3, a venue not an app

**The board.** Lines 84 and 85 named `HelicoOracleBoard` as `0xeb480C09…C760` — the 9 September first attempt. It moved to `0xF0aB4fF0…` in #325 and then behind a proxy at `0xe8515af9…` in #338, and the script followed neither.

**The byte counts**, stale in the same direction and more quietly. `HelicoMandateSwap` was quoted at 7,707 bytes and answers **163**, because it is a proxy now. 163 is the interesting number rather than an embarrassing one — a proxy is a delegatecall and nothing else, and the address a maker ships to is the proxy's — so the line now says why instead of hiding it.

author: manggo-cd
body:
Scaffolds the HelloHacks registration portal behind the form key `hello-hacks-2026`, following the `mis-2026` pattern. Logic is wired end to end; every page component is a deliberately unstyled stub so the Figma work can be split across per-page tickets.

## What's wired

- **Flow** — eight steps (welcome, avatar, song, role, application, confirm-details, review, success) in a reducer, including the review screen's per-section Edit jump-backs: editing a row returns to that step, and continuing from it comes straight back to review.
- **Questions + validation** — six `hh_`-prefixed question IDs per the Notion custom-forms doc, plus a Zod schema with the 300-character limits from the designs and per-step validation on Continue.
- **Payload** — `basicInformation` and `dynamicResponses` built and submitted through the existing `onSubmit` lifecycle. No changes to registration status meanings, payment rules, or application transitions.
- **Audio** — Jade's four royalty-free tracks committed under `public/assets/2026/hello-hacks/audio/`, behind a `useTrackPreview` hook that owns one shared audio element and stops playback on step change.
- **Success route** — mirrors the MIS split: the register page redirects to `/register/success` on submit, so the real screen is the route-level one, gated by `isHelloHacksEventId`.

## Verification

Typecheck clean, `next lint` clean, production build compiles. The flow reducer was checked against 13 navigation cases covering forward walks, back navigation, edit jump-backs, and the guards on `EDIT` / `SUBMISSION_SUCCEEDED`.

Not verified against a live event — no event with this form key exists yet. That's the last ticket in the queue.

## Needs a decision before reg opens

- **Event ID and URL slug.** The registry key must equal the event slug; `hello-hacks-2026` and the IDs in `constants.ts` are placeholders.
- **`isApplicationBased` must be true** on the event record — the designs are an application ("Application sent", "we'll let you know your status"), not an RSVP like MIS.
- **Avatar and track IDs are placeholders.** They're stored verbatim in `dynamicResponses` and can't be renamed after the first real submission.

Full decision list and the eleven follow-up tickets are in the handoff doc.

author: karczurf
body:
Closes task **0116**. Documentation only — no schema, ingestion or read-path change.

## The defect

A bucket whose entire volume is one or two **stroops** (`1e-7`, the smallest amount Stellar can represent) in a single trade takes its `close` from an order too small to carry price information. Someone sells a millionth of a token for two XLM and the implied unit price is millions of dollars.

The arithmetic is correct and the trade really happened — `close_usd / close` recovers the right XLM/USD rate for the month. **This is not an enrichment defect.** It costs a fraction of a cent to mint one.

Re-measured on production `price_ohlcv_1h`, covering both populations the task required:

| month | one-stroop buckets over $1,000 | worst `close` |
|---|---|---|
| 202502 (repaired history) | **85.0%** | $29,606,748 on ~$3 of volume |
| 202608 (live-written) | 22.3% | $3,517,649 on $0.35 of volume |

It decays cleanly with trade size — buckets holding at least one whole token exceed $1,000 just **0.11%** and **0.008%** of the time. The task's original $29.6M headline reproduces exactly.

## Why the planned fix is not built

The task proposed flagging `is_dust` on `trade_count = 1` plus a volume threshold. **Measurement says that rule would be wrong.**

Of the dust buckets that can be checked against a non-dust reference price for the same pair, **38 of 116 (a third) are priced correctly** — within 0.1-10x of it. One stroop of a genuinely expensive asset is a real one-cent order at the right price. A bare size threshold misclassifies precisely the assets worth the most, which is the false positive the task's own acceptance criterion warned about.

Two further findings pointed the same way:

- **Notional value is a poor discriminator.** The >$1k rate *rises* with bucket value ($0.01-1 → 2.6%, ≥$10k → 12.2%), because active tokens legitimately cost more.
- **93% of dust buckets cannot be adjudicated at all** — their asset has no non-dust trading anywhere in the month, so no reference exists. Filed as **0274**.

## What this PR does instead

`volume_base` and `trade_count` are already on every candle, including price-less ones, so the discriminator needs no new field — only a consumer who knows to apply it. Documented in the three places a reader might look:

| Where | Audience |
|---|---|
| `Candle` doc comments (`dto.rs`) | maintainers — carries the measurements and task numbers |
| `descriptions.rs` → published OpenAPI | integrators — same substance, no internal references |
| design doc §4.2 | design readers |

Each states the mechanism, the measured false-positive rate so the naive threshold is not re-proposed, and that **`volume_quote_usd` is unaffected** (these buckets carry a few dollars, so volume aggregates are undistorted).

The `descriptions.rs` change moves the published document, so `web/portal/public/openapi.json` is refreshed per the procedure in `verify-openapi-bundled.mjs`.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p prices-api` — **440 passed, 0 failed**, including `every_published_text_is_present_and_reader_facing`, which rejects task IDs and internal section marks in published text.
- `npm run openapi:lint` — valid; `verify-openapi-bundled` — bundle matches.
- `cargo clippy -p prices-api` — clean.
- All prod queries were read-only via mTLS as `dev_read` (`readonly = 1`). Nothing was written.

## Why

Three backend gaps, one branch (three reviewable commits):

1. Path B's per-segment Rime calls are sequential — the acknowledged worst case in `RIME_EVIDENCE.md` — with no way to measure the fair parallel number.
2. Every demo/rater replay rebills Rime + Groq; nothing caches successful syntheses.

## What it adds (commit per feature)

Default stays sequential — published numbers unaffected.
- **TTL response cache** (`backend/cache.py`): bounded, thread-safe; native caches full results, baseline caches segmentation + per-segment audio and renders only misses; `cached:true/false` on every response; `run_eval.py` bypasses by design; `GET /api/cache/stats`, `POST /api/cache/clear`.
- **Blind-rating votes + tally** (`backend/ratings.py`, `ratings_routes.py`, `scripts/tally_ratings.py`): file-backed one-vote-per-(rater,question) store (latest wins, atomic writes), blind-by-design API (`POST /vote`, `GET /tally`, `POST /clear`), and an offline unblinder that maps `responses.csv` via `rater_key.json` to A/B and prints the acceptance-test verdict plainly.

- add regression coverage proving legacy clients remain locked while fresh selectable deployments still require explicit confirmation

## Root cause
Older client databases can pre-date the `industrySetup` object. Setup Status already treats a missing object as a locked legacy deployment, but Client Setup and the Go-Live evaluator were reading the raw missing value. That produced contradictory state: Setup Status said locked while Client Setup said unconfirmed.

## Safety
- does not unlock or re-profile any existing deployment
- does not change the selected business type
- fresh selectable deployments still require explicit confirmation
- no WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, AI reply, Pipeline, lead, follow-up, or Ops Registry polling behavior changed

## Validation
- branch is based on current `main` after PR119
- changes are limited to config decoration, Client Setup evaluation, and regression tests

Do not merge until reviewed and CI passes.

body:
## 릴리즈 범위

지난 릴리즈(#309, 약 10분 전) 이후 **PR 1건 / frontend 4파일**.

- **#308** `fix(fe)/tutorial-hole-thumbnail-only` — 첫 사용 튜토리얼

`frontend/` 변경이 있으므로 머지 시 `production` 채널 OTA가 발행된다. 전부 런타임 동작이라 **새 스토어 빌드 없이 OTA로 닿는다.**

## 내용 — 첫 사용 튜토리얼 4건

실기기 제보로 시작해 expo web(iPhone 16e 390×844 에뮬레이션)에서 세 단계를 재현하며 고쳤다.

**1. 구멍이 카드 전체를 뚫었다** — 화면 높이의 78%를 차지해 설명을 둘 자리가 없었다. 썸네일만 뚫는다. 기하 계산은 카드가 소유한다(`featuredCardArtworkRect`).

**2. 드립 단계가 실제 라이브러리와 달랐다** — 직접 그린 알약(`오늘 아침 도착 · 2편`)을 리스트 안쪽에 두고 있었다. 실제 `LibraryBanner`(`새 콘텐츠 N개 도착`, 탭 아래 전체 폭)로 교체했다. 컴포넌트 주석이 *"튜토리얼과 실제가 다르면 안내가 오히려 방해가 된다"*고 경고한 그 상황이었다.

**3. 점선이 설명과 이어지지 않았다** — 시작점을 구멍 기준으로 짐작했다. 양 끝을 둘 다 실측한다. 설명 View 는 구멍이 잡히는 순간 **위치만** 옮겨가 `onLayout`이 오지 않아, `key`로 재마운트시켜 다시 재게 했다.

**4. 설명이 화면 끝에 고정돼 구멍과 멀었다** — 점선이 배경을 세로로 관통했다. 구멍 옆에 붙이고, 배경 글자와 겹쳐 뭉개지던 것은 **글자 그림자**로 떼어냈다(불투명 판은 가리키려는 배경을 지워 어색했다).

죽은 코드도 함께 정리: `onLayout={... ? undefined : undefined}` 삼항, 미사용 `styles.note`, 교체로 쓸모없어진 `dripRow`·`dripLabel`.

## 검증

- typecheck · lint · jest(11 suites / 80 tests) 통과
- 세 단계 전부 iPhone 16e 크기에서 눈으로 확인

**알려진 잔여** — 1·3단계는 설명이 놓이는 자리에 배경 콘텐츠가 있어 그림자에도 배경 글자가 약간 비친다. 배경 예시의 카드 수를 줄여 자리를 비우는 쪽이 근본 해법이며, 별도로 다룬다.

## 머지 후 확인

`eas-update` 워크플로가 `Branch production`으로 **한 건** 발행하는지.

body:
## Превью в поле медиа

Показывалось ноготком: базовые 132×84, а слой редактора слайда прибивал ему **108px** через `!important` — при том что ряд там шире 1400px, и три четверти его пустовали. Для полноэкранной фоновой фотографии 1920×1080 это значит, что по превью нельзя понять ни кадра, ни того, та ли вообще фотография.

Размер теперь принадлежит самому компоненту: `.image-field__row` — сетка с дорожкой `clamp(132px, 22%, 280px)`, у превью пропорция 16:10. Нижняя граница равна прежнему размеру, поэтому в узких местах (половина колонки репитера) ничего не изменилось, а в форме слайда превью выросло вдвое. Слой редактора слайда больше не задаёт ему размеров вовсе — минус 6 `!important`.

Эталон вычисленных стилей записывает пропорцию, а не ширину: точная ширина зависит от того, в каком месте формы стоит поле, и падать на каждой правке соседней колонки он не должен.

## Дашборд

**Убрано:**

- **График «Активность заявок»** — целая карточка под семь точек одной величины, которая на госсайте почти всегда состоит из семи нулей.
- **«Последние заявки»** — предпросмотр присланного показывал персональные данные посетителей на первом же экране панели; сколько заявок не прочитано, говорит плитка со ссылкой в журнал.
- **Плитки «Формы» и «Активные языки»** — первая считала определения форм, вторая настройку; оба числа месяцами не меняются, то есть занимали место, ничего не сообщая. Плитка репозитория показывается только когда файлы в нём есть.
- **Наивный «Статус системы»** — версия PHP статична, «База данных: подключена» тавтологично (страница и так собрана из неё), «Ошибки очереди: 0» — это «всё хорошо», сказанное там, где смотрят в тревоге.

**Добавлено:**

- **«Требует внимания»** — факты берутся из `SystemHealth`, того же источника, что и раздел «Состояние системы»: второй, наивный список рядом с первым разъехался бы при первой же новой проверке. На первый экран идут только `fail` и `warn`; `unknown` («ни разу не использовалась») — не поломка, а на свежей установке таких строк большинство, и они утопили бы настоящие. У каждой строки написано, что делать. Нечего показать — одна спокойная строка «Всё в порядке».
- **«Битые ссылки»** — журнал 404: по этим адресам посетитель уже приходил и ничего не нашёл, а починка — один редирект, и он в одном шаге отсюда. Пара к «поискам с 0 результатов», которые уже были.

Карточка без находок не рисуется вовсе, а ряд виджетов переведён на `auto-fit`: условная карточка больше не оставляет рядом с собой пустую колонку.

## Проверки

- `php tests/run.php` — 1733 пройдено, 0 провалено;
- PHPStan уровень 7 — без находок;
- визуальные эталоны админки: изменилось только поле медиа (пропорция вместо ширины), остальные 12 экранов зелёные без правок;
- бюджет `!important` в CSS админки опущен по факту: **273 → 268**;
- `npm run check:styles`, smoke-обход публички и всей админки — чисто (два 404 на `/script/latn|cyrl` воспроизводятся и на `main`).

## 1) Step-by-step development order (recommended sequence)

### Phase 0 — Baseline + safety rails (brownfield prerequisites)
1. **Run the app end-to-end** (login → product list → cart) and confirm current API routes and data source (in-memory arrays vs JSON file vs DB).
2. **Add/confirm test harness** (even minimal): API smoke tests + basic UI sanity checks.
3. **Introduce a single “source of truth” for data models** in the backend (even if still in-memory) to avoid scattered product/order logic.

### Phase 1 — Backend foundations (enables all 3 features)
4. **Refactor `server.js` slightly** to separate concerns:
   - middleware/auth utilities (JWT/session parsing)
   - product repository functions
   - order repository functions
   - route handlers
5. **Define/extend Product model fields** to support categories and search (see section 3).
6. **Add Admin role support** (minimal RBAC):
   - user object includes `role: "admin" | "user"`
   - middleware `requireAuth`, `requireAdmin`

### Phase 2 — Product Search & Category Filters
**Backend first**
7. Update `GET /products` to support query params:
   - `q` (keyword search across name/description)
   - `category` (exact match)
   - optional `sort` (e.g., `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `name_asc`)
8. Add `GET /categories` (optional but recommended) to populate dropdown reliably.

**Frontend next**
9. Add search input + category dropdown on product listing page.
10. Wire UI to call `GET /products?q=...&category=...`.
11. Add “Clear filters” and empty-state (“No products found”).

### Phase 3 — Order History (Checkout → Orders)
**Backend first**
12. Add Orders API (scoped to logged-in user):
   - `POST /orders` (create order from cart)
   - `GET /orders` (list user orders)
   - `GET /orders/:id` (order detail; ownership check)
13. Decide how cart is stored (client-side vs server-side). For brownfield, keep existing cart behavior and, on checkout, **send cart line items to backend** but compute totals server-side.

**Frontend next**
14. Add Checkout action to cart page (or wherever it currently exists).
15. Add “Order Confirmation” view (simple modal or page).
16. Add “My Orders” page (history list) and “Order Detail” page.

### Phase 4 — Admin Dashboard (Catalog CRUD)
**Backend first**
17. Add admin-only product management endpoints:
   - `POST /admin/products`
   - `PUT/PATCH /admin/products/:id`
   - `DELETE /admin/products/:id`
18. Add validation (required fields, numeric price, etc.).
19. Decide delete strategy:
   - **Soft delete** recommended (so historical orders still reference products)
   - or hard delete with snapshotting order item fields (see section 3)

**Frontend next**
20. Add Admin Dashboard route, guarded by role.
21. Add admin product list with edit/delete actions.
22. Add add/edit product form.
23. Ensure storefront product list refreshes after admin changes.

### Phase 5 — Hardening
24. Add API error handling and consistent response format.
25. Add integration tests:
   - search/filter correctness
   - order creation + retrieval + authz
   - admin authz + CRUD
26. Final regression pass: existing login, cart, product browse.

---

## 2) File modification list (what to update/create)

Because I can’t inspect the repo contents live from here, I’m listing this in two layers:
- **Definite**: files you will almost certainly touch given typical ShopLite structure.
- **Conditional**: depending on whether your app is React/Vite/CRA, or plain HTML/JS.

### Backend (definite/very likely)
- **`server.js`** (update)
  - Add query filtering for products
  - Add order endpoints
  - Add admin endpoints + RBAC middleware
  - Add/extend in-memory data structures (or file persistence)
- **(Recommended new files to keep server.js sane)**
  - `middleware/auth.js` (new) — `requireAuth`, `requireAdmin`, parse token/session
  - `routes/products.js` (new) — product list + categories
  - `routes/orders.js` (new) — create/list/detail
  - `routes/adminProducts.js` (new) — CRUD protected endpoints
  - `data/products.js` (new) — product seed + repository helpers
  - `data/orders.js` (new) — order store + helpers
  - `utils/id.js` (new) — id generation (UUID or incremental)
  - `utils/validation.js` (new) — request validation utilities
- **`package.json`** (update, if you add deps)
  - e.g., `uuid`, validation lib, test libs

### Frontend (conditional; choose the matching set)

#### If React (common capstone pattern)
- `src/App.js` or `src/main.jsx` + router config (update)
  - add routes: `/orders`, `/orders/:id`, `/admin`
- `src/pages/ProductList.jsx` (update)
  - add search input + category dropdown + query-string sync
- `src/components/SearchBar.jsx` (new, optional)
- `src/components/CategoryFilter.jsx` (new, optional)
- `src/pages/Cart.jsx` (update)
  - add checkout button and call `POST /orders`
- `src/pages/Orders.jsx` (new)
- `src/pages/OrderDetail.jsx` (new)
- `src/pages/AdminDashboard.jsx` (new)
- `src/components/AdminProductForm.jsx` (new)
- `src/components/AdminProductTable.jsx` (new)
- `src/services/api.js` (update/new)
  - centralize fetch calls + auth header injection
- `src/context/AuthContext.jsx` and/or `src/context/CartContext.jsx` (update)
  - include role in auth state
  - ensure cart clearing on successful checkout

#### If plain HTML/JS or minimal frontend
- `public/index.html` or `public/products.html` (update)
  - add search input + category dropdown
- `public/cart.html` (update)
  - add checkout CTA
- `public/orders.html` (new)
- `public/order-detail.html` (new)
- `public/admin.html` (new)
- `public/js/products.js` (update)
- `public/js/cart.js` (update)
- `public/js/orders.js` (new)
- `public/js/admin.js` (new)

### Shared / QA
- `README.md` (update)
  - new endpoints, admin user creation, run steps
- `tests/` (new/update)
  - API tests (supertest) and/or UI tests (cypress/playwright)

---

## 3) Proposed data structure changes in `server.js` (Products + Orders)

Below is a pragmatic brownfield approach: **keep products as an in-memory array** (or persisted to JSON later), add fields needed for filtering/admin, and introduce **order + orderItems** with snapshotting to protect history from later product edits.

### Product structure (extend existing)
```js
// PRODUCTS (existing array -> extend shape)
let products = [
  {
    id: "p-1001",              // string id recommended (uuid or prefixed)
    sku: "SKU-TSHIRT-001",      // optional but helpful for admin ops
    name: "Classic T-Shirt",
    description: "100% cotton ...",
    category: "Apparel",        // NEW: required for filtering dropdown
    price: 19.99,
    currency: "USD",            // optional: keep single currency for now
    imageUrl: "/images/..",     // if supported by UI
    isActive: true,             // NEW: supports soft-delete/hide without breaking orders
    createdAt: "2026-09-10T10:00:00Z",
    updatedAt: "2026-09-10T10:00:00Z"
  }
];
```

**Why these fields matter**
- `category`: enables dropdown filter and categories endpoint.
- `isActive`: lets admin “delete” without removing from historical data / references.
- `createdAt/updatedAt`: useful for auditability and admin work.

**Filtering logic (conceptual)**
- `GET /products?q=&category=` returns only `isActive === true` products.
- `q` matches `name` and `description` case-insensitively.

### Orders structure (new)
Recommended approach: orders store **snapshotted line items** so order history stays accurate even if the product price/name changes later.

    createdAt: "2026-09-10T10:10:00Z",
    updatedAt: "2026-09-10T10:10:00Z",
