author: shaharshvarts
body:
Adds isolated DEV and STAGING deployments on one Linux host, with production Next.js builds and independent PostgreSQL containers, tenant databases, DB/upload volumes, networks, credentials and project/container names. Host Nginx routes dev.shopnest.co.il and staging.shopnest.co.il to loopback ports 3001/3002; PostgreSQL has no published ports. The Linux runbook covers separate feature/master checkouts, provisioning, lifecycle commands and DNS/TLS setup. Cardcom production-mode settings and adapter calls are rejected in these environments; payment activation remains disabled.

Uploads are now validated by decoding actual content with Sharp before tenant storage, rather than trusting browser MIME types or filename extensions. Strict full-frame decoding and a GIF structure check reject corrupt/unsupported files. JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, AVIF and SVG fixtures pass; formats follow the installed Sharp codecs rather than an application allowlist. Accepted uploads become static PNG catalog images with EXIF orientation applied and metadata removed; all animation pages are validated and the first frame is stored. Existing stored images remain readable.

The existing 5 MiB upload byte limit is enforced at the storage boundary, with 6 MiB multipart request headroom. Public environment variables no longer determine validation rules. Async admin form validation returns image-field errors. Tenant authorization, path isolation and replace-after-database-success behavior are preserved. Private environment files and uploaded data are excluded from Docker build contexts.

Validation:
- npm run build passed, including lint/type checking and production page generation.
- 394 npm-suite tests passed, including 15 new real-image/security tests and 16 admin image/navigation tests.
- Both deployment configuration and payment guard regression tests passed (396 total in the latest run).
- Docker Compose rendering confirms separate resources, ports and database connections.
- git diff --check passed.

Remaining server validation: Docker daemon is unavailable on this Windows host, so Linux image/container and PostgreSQL integration checks, Nginx and TLS must be verified on the server. Check the legacy production stack's existing port 3002 before starting STAGING. STAGING stays on master and uses these deployment files only after separate review and merge. No automatic deployment or merge performed.

body:
## Description

The quota hook used to tell the model to ask the user to run `/handoff` or `$handoff`. That skill is manually invoked, is not in this repository, and defaults to an OS temp directory. After a quota crossing the agent now wraps up in-session: surface the window, decide whether later work would lose session-only context, ask before writing a handoff document, and reply with the path.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  flag[CodexBar writes provider flag]
  hook[Stop or PostToolUse claims flag once]
  tell[Tell user quota window, percent, reset]
  observe[Observe conversation only]
  empty[No unrecoverable unfinished work]
  ask[Ask to write a handoff with one-line summary and dest]
  stop[Stop the turn]
  later{User replies later}
  write[Write a new file at the named dest]
  skip[Do not write]
  flag --> hook --> tell --> observe
  observe -->|none| empty --> stop
  observe -->|some or unsure| ask --> stop
  stop --> later
  later -->|yes| write
  later -->|no| skip
```

Destination is resolved in the hook script, not by the model inventing a project slug:

- `~/.agents/skills/to-memory` present and cwd is a git repo → `proj-memory-path.sh` directory, `YYYY-MM-DD-handoff-<topic>.md` (no `--ensure`)
- to-memory present otherwise → `~/.agents/memories/YYYY-MM-DD-handoff-<topic>.md`
- to-memory absent → `$(pwd)/YYYY-MM-DD-quota-handoff.md`, never a temp dir

Plugin id stays `codexbar-quota-handoff`; version `1.2.0` (new reminder contract).

body:
## Motivation

Fixes #31896. With `--cp 8` (`attn_cp_size=8`), Prometheus gauges such as `sglang:num_running_reqs` are inflated by roughly the CP size.

Root cause: under attention CP every CP rank runs its own scheduler over the **same** global requests, and with `attn_tp_size == 1` the rank arithmetic in `dp_attention.py` makes `attn_tp_rank == 0` on every CP rank while `tp_rank` runs 0..7. `SchedulerMetricsCollector.init_new` gated `is_stats_logging_rank` on `attn_tp_rank == 0` alone, so all `attn_cp_size` schedulers exported the same request gauges and Prometheus sums inflated by the CP size.

The KV-cache event export one block below already gates on `attn_cp_rank == 0`; request stats now use the same predicate.

## Modifications

- `metrics_collector.py`: `is_stats_logging_rank` now requires `ps.attn_tp_rank == 0 and ps.attn_cp_rank == 0`. `enable_metrics_for_all_schedulers` remains as the explicit opt-in to export from every rank.
- New CPU unit test `test_metrics_collector_rank_gate.py` locking the predicate: cp rank 0 logs/exports, nonzero cp rank does not, `enable_metrics_for_all_schedulers` still exports from every rank, and metrics-disabled never exports.

Note: an earlier attempt (#31909) with the same one-line guard was closed by its author before review; this picks it back up with focused tests on current main.

## Accuracy Test

Pure CPU unit tests (`test/registered/unit/observability/test_metrics_collector_rank_gate.py`) covering the rank predicate through the real `init_new`; no model/GPU surface is touched.

## Benchmark & Profiling

N/A — one boolean predicate on the metrics init path; no hot-path or numeric behavior change. Nonzero CP ranks simply stop emitting duplicate log lines and duplicate gauge series.

author: sachiniyer
body:
Fixes #4161.

## The defect

`RedactAccessTokenURL`'s doc comment promises it "replaces **every** access_token value in raw". It did not, for one shape — a token inside a **percent-encoded query value**, which is exactly what a nested or callback URL produces. The same payload was redacted in a fragment and in a path. Only the query leaked.

Three passes can see decoded bytes, and none covered it:

| pass | why it missed |
|---|---|
| `redactAccessTokenQuery` | walks `url.Query()` but compares only the **key** against `access_token` — never a value's content |
| `redactAccessTokenComponents` | sweeps `Opaque`/`Host`/`Path`/`Fragment`/`User`; `RawQuery` is not in that set |
| the `!found` text fallback | runs the **non-decoding** matcher over `parsed.String()`, where the value is re-encoded as `access_token%3D`, so the literal needle is absent |

The sharp part: `url.Query()` had **already decoded** that value, so the plaintext token was sitting in the map `redactAccessTokenQuery` was iterating. The redaction pass was holding the secret and not looking at it.

The unencoded spelling `next=/ws?access_token=TOK` survived only because `RawQuery` happens to keep the literal needle for the text fallback — which is why the behaviour looked inconsistent rather than plainly broken.

## The fix

Scan each decoded query value with `RedactAccessTokenText`; `Encode()` re-escapes the replacement on the way out. Neighbouring parameters are untouched.

## Verification — mutation probe, actually run

`agentproto` is a leaf package with no daemon, so unlike #4165 I could run this rather than reason about it.

**With the fix reverted:**
```
--- FAIL: TestRedactAccessTokenURL/token_inside_a_percent-encoded_query_value
--- FAIL: TestRedactAccessTokenURL/percent-encoded_query_value_redacted,_neighbour_kept
FAIL	github.com/sachiniyer/agent-factory/agentproto
```
**With the fix applied:** `ok github.com/sachiniyer/agent-factory/agentproto`

Observed red→green, not inferred.

Three cases were added to the existing `TestRedactAccessTokenURL` table:

1. **the leak** — `?next=%2Fws%3Faccess_token%3Dsekrit`
2. **neighbour preserved** — `?keep=hello&next=…`, so redacting a value cannot coarsen into rewriting the rest of the query
3. **plain nested** — `?next=/ws?access_token=sekrit`. This one **passes without the fix**; I added it as a pin, not a fix, because it is served by a different path (the literal-needle fallback) and a future refactor of either path could silently drop the one it does not touch. Calling it a regression test would overstate it.

Also ran `gofmt`, `go build ./...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint --fast`, `scripts/lint-file-length.sh`, and the consumer packages `./log/` and `./internal/credscrub/` — all clean.

## Review posture

Another self-approval, for the same reason as #4165: Codex capacity does not return until Sep 12 (#4150) and this is a credential leak in shipped code. The mitigating difference from #4165 is that this one has an executed mutation probe behind it. **Please re-review when capacity returns.**

Related: #4115's live finding is the same family — a transform handled at one layer while a *composition* (here percent-encoding inside query structure) falls between passes.

author: marevol
body:
fix: use the bundled JavaScript engine in tests instead of the removed Groovy one

The test build stopped compiling because org.codelibs.fess.script.groovy moved
out of fess core into the fess-script-groovy plugin and is no longer on the
classpath.

The tests register a script engine by hand because the unit-test container does
not load Fess's fess_se.xml. They now register the JavaScript engine that ships
in fess core, and pass script_type explicitly, because a data store resolves an
unset script_type to the legacy "groovy" name.

The templates in these tests are member access, string concatenation and a
ternary, which evaluate the same under either engine, so what they cover is
unchanged. Asking for the bundled engine keeps the test build from depending on
another plugin, which would otherwise have to be built and published before this
one.

author: jeong-sik
body:
#34837 을 고칩니다.

## 무엇이 안 돌았나

`test/` 아래에 실행 파일을 링크하지 않고 **node 스크립트를 돌리는 dune rule 이 5개** 있습니다. 각각 확장(`connectors/browser/extension/background.js`)과 OCaml 드라이버(`lib/browser_interaction.ml`, `lib/browser_page_script.ml`, `lib/browser_scene_script.ml`)가 **같은 주입 스크립트**를 들고 있는지 봅니다. 손으로 맞춰야 하는 동일성입니다.

CI 에서 한 번도 안 돌았습니다. 막는 데가 셋입니다.

1. `dune build @check` 는 `test/` 를 링크만 하고 돌리지 않습니다.
2. 타깃 러너는 `<dir>/<name>.exe` 를 짓는데, 이 rule 들에는 실행 파일이 없습니다.
3. edited-test 선택기는 `test/test_*.ml` 만 봅니다.

이슈가 든 실측: PR #34831 이 그 소스 셋 중 셋과 node 스위트 둘을 같이 고쳤는데, 체크 로그에는 OCaml 스위트 하나만 나옵니다.

## 무엇을 했나

`Build` 단계가 목록을 갖지 않고 **읽어서 씁니다**.

```
node_targets=$(python3 scripts/ci/list-node-alias-targets.py)
dune build @check @test/stanzas/runtest ${node_targets}
```

`@test/stanzas/runtest` 를 이미 그렇게 쓰고 있으니 alias 를 짓는 방식은 이 줄이 증명해둔 것입니다.

읽는 쪽은 `(rule (alias runtest-...) ... (action (run node ...)))` 만 고릅니다. `python3` action 38개는 안 고릅니다 — 그중 브라우저 드라이버가 필요한 `.py` 는 Linux 잡에서 그냥 돌리면 안 된다고 이슈가 짚었습니다. 하나도 못 고르면 **exit 1** 입니다. 확장되면서 빈 문자열이 되는 build 줄은 성공을 보고합니다.

`.inc` 안의 rule 은 그 `.inc` 가 있는 디렉터리가 아니라 **include 한 dune 의 디렉터리**에 속합니다. 그래서 트리를 걷지 않고 `(include ...)` 를 따라갑니다.

## 이슈는 3개라고 했고, 읽어보니 5개입니다

| alias | 지켜보는 파일 |
|---|---|
| `runtest-test_browser_interact_extension` | `background.js`, `lib/browser_interaction.ml` |
| `runtest-test_browser_scene_resource` | `background.js`, `lib/browser_scene_script.ml` |
| `runtest-test_browser_elements` | `background.js`, `lib/browser_page_script.ml` |
| `runtest-test_browser_screenshot` | `background.js` |
| `runtest-test_browser_connection_extension` | `background.js` |

`test_browser_elements` 와 `test_browser_connection_extension` 이 이슈 목록에 없었습니다.

## 통과하는 게 아니라 잡는지 확인했습니다

`background.js` 의 `interactInPage` 에 **공백 한 칸**을 넣고 돌렸습니다:

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: live and WebDriver use the same closed DOM implementation
```

그리고 복구했습니다.

## 곁들여: lister 를 가드로 센다

`check-guards-are-wired.py` 의 이름 패턴이 `(lint|check|guard|gate|ratchet|audit)` 였습니다. 제 스크립트 둘 — 이번 것과 #35035 의 `list-dashboard-backend-coupled-tests.py` — 은 어디에도 안 걸립니다.

그런데 **CI 가 이 스크립트들이 출력한 것을 그대로 돕니다.** 호출이 끊기면 레인 하나가 통째로 사라지고 빌드는 초록입니다. 가드보다 하중이 큽니다.

측정: `list` 를 넣으면 이름에 걸리는 스크립트는 **정확히 이 둘**이고, 둘 다 reached 이며 `guards-not-wired.txt` 는 움직이지 않습니다 (가드 114 → 116).

이것도 심어서 확인했습니다. 두 호출부를 감추면:

```
FAIL: a check script is reached from nothing CI runs.
  scripts/ci/list-node-alias-targets.py
```

## 비용

5개 합쳐 **3.3초** (node 시작 시간 포함). 로컬에서 다섯 개 다 통과합니다. `Build` 단계는 지금 6~8분입니다.

## 로컬 검증

- `python3 scripts/ci/list-node-alias-targets.py --self-test` — PASS (node rule 은 타깃, python rule 은 아님, include 된 rule 은 include 한 디렉터리 소유)
- `python3 scripts/ci/check-guards-are-wired.py` — 116/97, baseline 불변
- `yaml.safe_load(pr-check.yml)`, `bash -n run-lint-suite.sh`
- 다섯 스위트 `node <file>` 직접 실행 — 전부 통과
- 위반 심기 2종 → 둘 다 FAIL → 복구

## 미검증

- dune 이 실제로 이 alias 들을 짓고 action 을 돌리는지. 로컬 dune 빌드를 안 하니 **이 PR 자신의 `Build` 단계가 첫 실측**입니다. 로그에 `browser parity suites:` 다섯 줄이 찍히고 그 다음 build 가 통과하면 확인된 것입니다.

body:
Match previously retained the loudest level seen since it was enabled, so quieter upstream changes could not reach the target without restarting. Peak and RMS matching now use roughly three seconds of recent measurements, including recent RMS crest headroom. Quieter candidates must remain stable for about 300 ms before the existing gain smoother applies them; louder evidence still reduces gain promptly.

Leave Match enabled, adjust the upstream sound, and allow roughly three to four seconds of steady material for quieter changes to settle. Startup, silence handling, held gain, and sample-peak protection remain covered by regression tests. Documentation describes the updated workflow.

Validation: local CI and VST3 CI, repeated loud/quiet/loud adaptation in both modes, decaying-tail protection, and RMS headroom recovery. Independent DSP/realtime review found no meaningful issues. A fresh macOS VST3 bundle is available for manual DAW audition; audible acceptance remains pending.

author: dasabhinaba34
body:
`expo.version` has been `1.0.0` since MBOS shipped and `android.versionCode` was never set at all, so it defaulted to `1` on every build. `buildLabel()` sends both halves up on sign-in into `mbos_devices.app_version` — a column whose own comment calls it "the column somebody needs the moment anything is wrong in the field". It has answered `1.0.0 · embedded` for every handset on every build for a year: present, populated, carrying no information.

The check-in radius (#324) is the release that makes that cost real. It refuses a salesman at a shop door, so "it will not let me check in" is a support call, and the first thing the office needs is whether that phone has the gate or last week's build. Without a bump the answer is the same string either way.

**Both halves move**, because they are two facts: `versionCode` is what Android compares when deciding whether an install is an upgrade, `version` is what a person reads, and `buildLabel()` prints them together.

**Nothing pins either.** `expo.version` is read in exactly two places — the APK filename in the release workflow, and that label. `runtimeVersion` is the `fingerprint` policy precisely so OTA updates never depend on a number somebody has to remember to move.

DEPLOY.md now makes the bump a **step of releasing** rather than something to notice, and the comment in `updates.ts` asserting this project has never bumped it is corrected — it was true when written, which is the reason it is being fixed rather than deleted.

Shipping immediately after merge as the APK carrying #324.

author: dajiaohuang
body:
## 问题 / The problem

Watcha（观猹）是仓库里已经完整接好、线上也已启用的第二种登录方式，但它的配置变量在**任何地方都没有被记录过**：

```
$ grep -c WATCHA .env.example
0
$ grep -rn -i "watcha|观猹" README.md README.zh-CN.md README.ja.md docs/ .env.example
（无输出）
```

它并不是占位功能：

- `api/auth/watcha/start.js` 与 `api/auth/watcha/callback.js` 走完了带 PKCE 的授权码流程；
- 登录界面里有 "Continue with Watcha / 使用观猹登录" 按钮，以及 `watchaNotConfigured`、`watchaSessionExpired`、`watchaDenied`、`watchaLoginFailed` 四类错误文案；
- 线上已经启用：对生产站点请求登录入口会返回真实跳转：

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://gpt-image2.canghe.ai/api/auth/watcha/start
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://watcha.cn/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&
          redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fgpt-image2.canghe.ai%2Fapi%2Fauth%2Fwatcha%2Fcallback&
          scope=read&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256
```

变量本身在 `api/_lib/watcha.js` 的 `getWatchaConfig()` 里读得很明确：

```js
clientId:       process.env.WATCHA_CLIENT_ID || '',
clientSecret:   process.env.WATCHA_CLIENT_SECRET || '',
isPublicClient: process.env.WATCHA_PUBLIC_CLIENT === 'true',
redirectUri:    process.env.WATCHA_REDIRECT_URI || `${appUrl}/api/auth/watcha/callback`,
scope:          process.env.WATCHA_SCOPE || 'read email',
authorizeUrl:   process.env.WATCHA_AUTHORIZE_URL || 'https://watcha.cn/oauth/authorize',
tokenUrl:       process.env.WATCHA_TOKEN_URL     || 'https://watcha.cn/oauth/api/token',
userinfoUrl:    process.env.WATCHA_USERINFO_URL  || 'https://watcha.cn/oauth/api/userinfo'
```

`WATCHA_CLIENT_ID` 加上 `WATCHA_CLIENT_SECRET`（或 `WATCHA_PUBLIC_CLIENT=true`）决定 `isWatchaConfigured()` 是否成立。照着文档部署的人既不知道要设这些变量，也无从得知变量名，点登录只会看到"观猹登录还没有完成配置"。

README 的缺失其实更显眼：三个语言的 README 都有一个 `## 🔐 Website Auth & Generation` 段落，里面写着 "Required Vercel environment variables" 并列出 13 个变量，Watcha 一个都没有。支付宝和付费交流群虽然也不在这个代码块里，但配置清单里有条目并链接到 `docs/alipay-web-payment.md` 和 `docs/paid-community.md`；Watcha 则是完全没有任何线索。

顺带还有一处同类遗漏：`api/_lib/supabase.js:6` 的服务端回退 `process.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL || process.env.SUPABASE_URL`，其中 `SUPABASE_URL` 也没有被记录。

## 改动 / What this PR does

只动文档，加一个守卫：

1. **`.env.example`** 增加 Watcha 段：`WATCHA_CLIENT_ID`、`WATCHA_CLIENT_SECRET`、`WATCHA_PUBLIC_CLIENT`、`WATCHA_REDIRECT_URI`、`WATCHA_SCOPE`，以及三个 watcha.cn 端点覆盖变量（按文件里 `ALIPAY_GATEWAY` 的写法把默认值一并列出）。注释说明了开关条件，以及 `{APP_URL}/api/auth/watcha/callback` 和 `read email` 两个默认值。同时补上 `SUPABASE_URL`，注明它只在 `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` 未设置时作为服务端回退。
2. **`README.md` / `README.zh-CN.md` / `README.ja.md`** 在各自的环境变量代码块之后，增加一小段标注为可选的 Watcha 配置，写清开关条件和两个可选覆盖项。原来的 "Required Vercel environment variables" 代码块保持不动，因为 Watcha 确实是可选的，这样标题也仍然准确。
3. **`api/_lib/env-example.test.js`**（新增）：扫描 `api/` 下所有非测试模块里出现的 `process.env.*`，断言每一个都能在 `.env.example` 里找到。它匹配 `npm test` 已有的 `api/_lib/*.test.js` glob，因此不需要改 `package.json`，和已有的 `api-imports.test.js` 是同一个思路。

没有改动任何运行时代码、依赖、CI 或权限。

## 验证 / Verification

新测试确实能抓到这个问题 —— 把它对着改动前的 `.env.example` 跑，会列出全部 9 个缺失变量：

```
$ git stash && node --test api/_lib/env-example.test.js    # 对着改动前的版本
AssertionError: Environment variables missing from .env.example:
  SUPABASE_URL (read by api/_lib/supabase.js)
  WATCHA_AUTHORIZE_URL (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_CLIENT_ID (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_CLIENT_SECRET (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_PUBLIC_CLIENT (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_REDIRECT_URI (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_SCOPE (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_TOKEN_URL (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
  WATCHA_USERINFO_URL (read by api/_lib/watcha.js)
```

改动之后：

```
$ npm test
ℹ tests 41   ℹ pass 41   ℹ fail 0

$ npm run test:apimart
ℹ tests 24   ℹ pass 24   ℹ fail 0

$ npm run build
✓ built in 6.92s
```

另外单独核对过注释里写的默认值和开关行为，都是直接调用 `getWatchaConfig()` / `isWatchaConfigured()` 断言的：不设变量时不启用；只设 `WATCHA_CLIENT_ID` 不启用；加上 secret 或 `WATCHA_PUBLIC_CLIENT=true` 后启用；`redirectUri` 回退到 `{APP_URL}/api/auth/watcha/callback`；`scope` 回退到 `read email`；三个端点变量回退到 watcha.cn 的地址。

三个 README 改动后重新核对了围栏配对（各 20 个，成对）和相对链接（0 个失效），和改动前一致。

`data/cases.json` 和 `agents/skills/gpt-image-2-style-library/references/style-library.md` 因为 `prebuild` 被重新生成过，核对后与提交内容一致（只有行尾差异），已还原，不在本 PR 里。

## 没有动的地方 / Left alone

- 两个安装脚本里的 `CLAUDE_HOME`（#30 已覆盖）、`docs/gallery.md` 的索引缺失（#29 已覆盖），都不在本 PR 范围内。
- 守卫只覆盖 `.env.example`。README 里有意只列了一个"必需"子集（支付宝、付费交流群的变量走配置清单和 docs 链接），把它也纳入自动校验会需要按语言解析三份 README 的代码块，容易变脆，所以 README 部分靠人工核对，这一点如实说明。
- `scripts/alipay-webpay-sandbox-server.mjs` 的 `ALIPAY_SANDBOX_PORT` 同样未被记录，但只在本地沙箱脚本里使用且有默认值 `4174`；守卫只扫描 `api/`，所以没有一并处理。
- 没有在本 PR 中写出任何密钥类信息。上面输出里的 `client_id` 属于公开的 OAuth 客户端标识（它本身就会出现在跳转 URL 中），且已截断。

---

**English summary:** Watcha is a fully implemented and production-enabled second sign-in option — a PKCE authorization-code flow in `api/auth/watcha/`, a "Continue with Watcha" button in the UI, and a live `302` to `watcha.cn/oauth/authorize` from the deployed site — yet none of its eight environment variables were documented in `.env.example`, in any of the three READMEs, or anywhere under `docs/`. The README gap is the more visible one: each locale has a "Required Vercel environment variables" block listing thirteen variables, and Alipay and the paid community at least get checklist entries pointing at their runbooks, while Watcha gets no mention at all. This PR documents the five behavioural variables and the three endpoint overrides in `.env.example` and in a clearly-marked optional block in all three READMEs, adds the undocumented `SUPABASE_URL` server-side fallback, and adds `api/_lib/env-example.test.js`, which asserts that every `process.env` name read under `api/` appears in `.env.example`. The guard is proven to fail on the previous file, listing all nine missing names, and needs no `package.json` or CI change because it matches the existing `npm test` glob. No runtime code, dependencies, CI or permissions are touched.

author: hamadalrumaihi
body:
## Summary

Adds the Confidential Informant (CI) Management System as a server-enforced compartment (fourteen tables, 35 RPCs, `/informants`, the case **CI Intelligence** tab, sanitized release into cases) and completes the portal cleanup: `/inbox` is the Action Center, the Command Center is the single command home, an Owner nav category, "More…" case tabs, Membership Review, a lightweight bell, one `ViewsMenu`, a typed notification registry, soft delete everywhere, and the docs archive.

## Why

Informants and informant-derived intelligence must be invisible to everyone outside the compartment — no counts, no placeholders, no search hits, no notification titles — while handlers keep working inside their own CIs and command keeps oversight. The cleanup items are the remaining clutter recommendations from the Phase 8 handoff (`docs/HANDOFF-PORTAL-IMPROVEMENTS.md` §7), now all done.

## Changes

- **Access model** — Full CI Access: Bureau Lead, Deputy Director, Director, the Owner, every active SIB member. Handler Access: only the CIs the caller holds an active handler row for. `canAccessCI = hasFullCIAccess(user) || isAssignedHandler(user, ci)` on the server (`private.has_full_ci_access`, `private.can_access_ci`); the client only mirrors it (`useCiContext`, `ciInvolved`).
- **`/informants`** — roster (handler view vs. full view), stats, capacity panel (6 by default, individual overrides), recruitment wizard (`CI-0001` identifiers, seven statuses, twelve motives), CI profile (handlers, contact log, reliability assessments, intelligence + corroboration, payments, audit), requests panel (additional capacity / assignment / access), export (audited). Uninvolved users see a neutral "Nothing here".
- **Handlers and capacity** — primary/secondary handlers, handoff and removal revoke access at once; the seventh CI at capacity is refused with a "Request additional capacity" path; command overrides need a reason and are audited.
- **Case tab "CI Intelligence"** — present only when the caller can see at least one linked source (`ci_case_count > 0`), never in "More…", no lock or count for anyone else. Case access ≠ CI access.
- **Sanitized release** — `ci_release` refuses text that names the source; the released text lands in `case_intel_releases` (no CI column, visible to case members) with the back-link in the restricted `ci_releases`.
- **Protection everywhere** — search, graph, timeline, exports, Discord, realtime (`ci_events` shadow carries no detail), `case_audit_feed`, Trash labels, notifications (nine `informants` kinds, portal-only).
- **Portal cleanup** — `/inbox` = Action Center (personal preset), `My Dashboard` at `/dashboard`, Division Overview panels folded into Command Center sections and `components/command/` deleted, one Analytics, Owner category (Owner Console, Audit, Handbook, Report Templates), `/action` `/command` `/tools` + tool routes as `LEGACY_REDIRECT_TABS` (out of `PAGE_META`), case tabs "More…", Approval Queue → Membership Review, bell "View All" → Action Center Activity lane, one shared `ViewsMenu`, notification registry typed (`{title, category, destination, mutable}`) as the single source of truth, Owner Console alert tiles removed, soft delete for case templates and commendations (the last hard deletes), "Deleting things" documented once, docs archived under `docs/archive/`, one `[Unreleased]` in the changelog.

## Security and permissions

- 14 new tables, all SELECT-only for `authenticated` (no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grant or policy); every write is a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC with `set search_path to ''` that checks authority before reading anything and refuses identically whether the row exists or not.
- `permission_catalog` rows 600–690 (CI) and 700/710 (template / commendation soft delete); `private.perm_dispatch` re-emitted with the CI arms before the registry arm.
- Tests: RLS `tests/rls/v191a–c.test.ts` (the 35 numbered security cases of the contract in 34 tests: access model, handler scope, capacity, release, plumbing), vitest (`ciModel`, MSW `ci` handlers, notification registry, nav, trash), e2e `tests/e2e/informants.spec.ts`.
- Read-only security review folded in as the second commit (applied live as `confidential_informants_review_fixes`): self-recruitment through `ci_create` only for callers already inside the compartment, so an outsider's call raises P0403 before the person is looked at and can no longer learn whether a person is a source (refused designations of a live source are audited); `private.ci_sanitized` normalises both sides and refuses name tokens and former handlers; the merge-blocking trigger answers neutrally outside the compartment; a capacity override stores a neutral marker on the handler-readable row (the reason lives in the audit); the Trash label of a deleted intelligence row no longer carries its summary. Accepted as is: definer RPCs executable by `authenticated` (the project pattern) and the fixture-email gate on `rls_test_ci_sweep`.

## Database changes

- `20261103120000_confidential_informants.sql` — applied live in four parts (`confidential_informants`, `confidential_informants_rpcs`, `confidential_informants_plumbing`, `confidential_informants_review_fixes`). Additive: sequence, tables, helpers, policies, RPCs, plumbing re-emissions, sweep `ci-contact-sweep`, catalog rows.
- `20261104120000_soft_delete_templates_commendations.sql` — applied live as `soft_delete_templates_commendations`. Additive: soft-delete columns + triggers + policies on `case_templates` / `commendations`, plumbing re-emissions, catalog rows.
- `src/lib/database.types.ts` hand-updated; `supabase/schema-snapshot.sql` rebuilt from a live dump (`check:schema`, `check:freshness`, `check:realtime` pass); `supabase/MIGRATION-HISTORY.md` documents both. Advisors re-run: no new lint class (the two WARN groups are the pre-existing `pg_net` extension location and the by-design definer RPCs).

## Verification

- Gates: `typecheck`, `eslint src tests --max-warnings 0`, `vitest run` (1809 tests), `build`, `check:bundle` (128.9 KB gzip of 142), `check:dead`, `check:submit`, `check:schema`, `check:freshness`, `check:realtime`, `check:notif-titles`, `gen:permissions --check` (171 rows), `gen:handbook`, `gen:guide` — all green on the final head.
- Live verification in rolled-back transactions (details in `supabase/MIGRATION-HISTORY.md`): an uninvolved detective gets no rows, nulls and no counts, and the same P0403 from `ci_create` for a live source and a random id; handler scope; capacity 6 → refusal → request → approval → 8; handoff revokes instantly; unsanitized release refused (including `c.i.-0001`, spaced aliases, dotted names, handler names); case member sees the sanitized text only; direct INSERT 42501; role demotion revokes at once; sweep Owner-only; soft delete / Trash / restore for a CI; `search_all('CI-0')` returns no CI rows.
- RLS suites `v191a–c` need the fixture accounts (#299) to run against the test project.

## Screenshots

Not captured in this session (no preview account). Surfaces: `/informants` roster and profile, the case "CI Intelligence" tab, the Sanitize & Release dialog, the Owner nav category, the "More…" case-tab menu.

## Deployment notes

- Redeploy the `discord-notify` edge function: `titles.json` carries the nine `informants` kinds and the function now skips portal-only categories. Until redeployed, the live function skips those kinds with `{skipped:'no title'}` (fail-safe, nothing leaks).
- Scheduled job `ci-contact-sweep` (`40 * * * *`) is live; the Owner can run it by hand with `ci_sweep_run`.
- Legacy URLs `/action`, `/command`, `/tools` and the fourteen per-tool routes redirect; bookmarks keep working.

author: erwan-joly
body:
Pins every non-GitHub-owned action in this repo to a full-length commit SHA, keeping the version tag as a trailing comment.

A tag is a moving pointer — whoever controls the upstream repo (or compromises that maintainer's account) can repoint it and change what executes here. These steps run with `contents: write` or cloud credentials in scope, so that matters.

No version changes: each SHA is the exact commit the pinned tag resolved to today. Part of a sweep across the org so `sha_pinning_required` can be turned on afterwards.

Closes #454.

The audit finds a writer by searching scripts for an artifact's literal basename. The generator writes `{category}_index.json` and `by_source_{source}_index.json` from f-strings, so the twelve category and source indexes were `UNKNOWN / no writer found` while `recipe_index.json`, named literally, was `CURRENT_VIEW` with the same writer. author: krshk30
body:
## Superseding operator ruling — 2026-09-10

This PR intentionally follows the operator's later ruling: ATR is a **live arm/pull check**, not a permanent day rejection. Purple or unavailable ATR withholds the resting order; a later cyan/long state may re-arm it, with no retroactive fill. This supersedes the 2026-09-07 permanent-day interpretation cited in the withheld review. The four-red rule remains a one-time `day_gate` evaluation whose outcome delays only the first 09:30 minute.

Every new gate decision now names its classification in both the reason and structured evidence: `LIVE_CHECK` for ATR and `DAY_GATE` for the opening-red check. Combined evaluations also carry `checks_evaluated`.

## Scope

Builds only the two operator-settled ORB paper entry rules. No momentum, choppiness, caps, break-body, exit, broker, OMS, or live-v2 behavior changes.

- ATR is a live arm/pull gate on the one modeled resting order. Completed-bar cyan/long arms; purple/short or unavailable ATR pulls or withholds. A later cyan/long state may re-arm.
- Four or more red bars among 09:25-09:29 ET delay entry only through 09:30:59. The name may re-arm at 09:31 ET; this is not an all-day rejection.
- Re-arming never backfills a break that happened while the order was pulled. If price is already above the fixed level, it must return to or below that level and then make a fresh upward crossing.
- A completed ATR flip is applied before the rollover trade can fill.
- Every gate decision and held crossing is durable and visible in the ORB paper state, with decision and crossing denominators.
- Service health states whether each switch reached the running process.

## Safety and rollout

Both rules ship independently dark:

- `orb_paper_atr_entry_gate_enabled = False`
- `orb_paper_four_red_delay_enabled = False`

The isolated environment builder carries explicit values through but does not force either on. Existing behavior is preserved with both flags off. The ORB path remains structurally broker-disconnected; the hostile-settings, AST/dispatch, and no-intent controls remain green.

## Verification

- Focused ORB entry/lifecycle/isolation set: 72 passed.
- All ORB-selected unit tests: 248 passed.
- Full controlled pair on macOS: base 55 failed / 3503 passed; head 55 failed / 3515 passed. The 55 failure names are identical; +12 is exactly the new test module.
- Ruff clean and `git diff --check` clean.

Targeted mutations, all RED:

- unknown ATR allowed to fail open
- purple ATR ignored
- red threshold changed from four to five
- first-minute red delay changed into an all-day block
- re-arm allowed to fill an already-crossed level
- shipped ATR gate default changed from dark to enabled

## Status

Exact head: `6b2ec4da2d7442f5ec9f9680d8228fae9df15f62`.

Not deployed and not enabled. Claude-1 review and exact-head pin are required before merge; activation remains a separate operator decision.

author: thevladbog
body:
## What changed

After a local shift close, a delayed active list response could offer Rejoin again once synchronization removed the close outbox row. Pending closures now show **«Закрывается»** with **«Присоединиться»** disabled. Acknowledged closures disappear from selection, and stale bundles cannot overwrite the durable closed status.

Selection rechecks the local close state after acquiring its entry barrier and blocks entry when that state cannot be read. Close acknowledgement repairs an older regressed mirror before removing its outbox event. Added SQLite-backed regression coverage for validation/duplicate-printing and aggregation shifts, delayed responses, remounts, conflicts, and entry races; updated the lifecycle specification.

## Validation

- Station suite: **1,412 tests passed** across 96 files; no skipped tests.
- Final focused rerun: **69 tests passed** across selection, closure, and mirror tests.
- Station typecheck, lint, build, changed-file Prettier check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Chromium at **1280×800**, using the actual Station components, local SQLite, and mocked server replies: closing state and disabled Rejoin survive reload; acknowledgement removes the stale active card; another active shift remains accessible. No overflow or page errors.
- Windows/Tauri and physical station hardware were not exercised: this validation used the local browser/SQLite harness. No deployment is included.

## Checklist

- [ ] `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test build --concurrency=1 --force` passes — not run repo-wide; Station package gates passed.
- [ ] `pnpm format:check` passes — not run repo-wide; all changed files passed Prettier.
- [x] Database-backed tests ran with `DATABASE_URL` exported (or were not touched) — Postgres paths unchanged; Station tests used local SQLite.
- [x] Intentional skips and external/browser/hardware verification are reported in the PR description.

author: bacbacta
body:
Une capture d'un vrai téléphone, envoyée avec « les changements ne sont pas
visibles ». Elle avait raison.

La production avait bien tout — l'agent répond, contre le vrai modèle. Mais sur
l'**écran de repos**, celui de la capture, il n'y avait rien à voir : l'agent
n'apparaissait qu'après avoir tapé quelque chose. Il fallait deviner qu'il
existe pour le trouver.

La personne qui l'avait commandé ne le voyait pas. Un commerçant à Douala ne
l'aurait jamais vu.

## Ce que ça change

L'écran de repos annonce ce que l'atelier sait faire quand la grille ne suffit
pas :

> ✳ **Ton outil n'est pas dans la liste ?**
> Décris-le en français : l'atelier le fabrique sur mesure, en discutant.

Il **mène au champ** plutôt que d'ouvrir la conversation : un tour se paie, et
une conversation ouverte sans demande n'aurait rien à répondre. Le bouton
conduit là où l'on décrit, et c'est la description qui déclenche. Il s'efface
dès qu'on a tapé — la réponse prend sa place.

## Et la même capture en a montré un deuxième

Que je n'avais pas cherché : « Reconnaissance de dette » sortait par la droite
de sa carte. Mesuré au navigateur, à **360 pixels** — la largeur que le brief
vise, répétée dans les commentaires, et que personne n'avait jamais mesurée :

```
avant : 360px → 12 débordements   (dont « Attestation », un seul mot)
        390px →  3 débordements
après : 360px →  0
        390px →  0
```

`min-width: 0` était déjà là et laissait la boîte rétrécir ; c'est le **mot**
qui ne se coupait pas. `hyphens: auto` d'abord — le document est en `lang="fr"`,
la césure tombe donc où le français la met — puis `overflow-wrap` en filet pour
ce que le dictionnaire ne sait pas couper.

## La garde

Aucun essai unitaire ne pouvait voir ça : happy-dom ne fait pas de mise en page.
Elle vit donc dans `e2e/fumee.mjs`, qui tourne déjà dans un vrai navigateur à
360 × 740, et refuse tout élément dont le contenu dépasse sa boîte.

## Vérifié

- `pnpm verif` : 2 207 essais, couverture **96,04 / 90,54 / 95,84 / 97,66**
- Coquille 24,9 Ko / 120 · Établi 11,8 Ko / 30
- `e2e/fumee.mjs` : « rien ne déborde de sa boîte à 360 px » ✓
- Au navigateur, en clair **et** en sombre : la porte est visible au repos et
  mène bien au champ de saisie

## 概要

リリース手順が未文書化で、`CLAUDE.md` にブランチ戦略が1行あるだけの状態だった。デバッグAPKのGitHub Release配布手順とバージョニング規則を `docs/release-process.md` にまとめる。

author: berndhueckstaedt
body:
## What

On an iPhone the small match discs on the matching map could hardly be hit — step 1 practically not at all, step 2 only with effort. Found by Bernd at his phone (F-10).

## Why it happened

The marker box is click-through on purpose (a 104 px glow must not steal a neighbour's tap). The tap was taken only by the disc (light and normal map) or by the invisible core inside the glow (dark map), and both were exactly as big as the disc of the step: 20 / 28 / 38 / 48 px. Apple's floor for a tap target is 44 × 44 pt, and a CSS pixel is a point on the iPhone. The crowd radius (`CLUSTER_PX = 26`) was only evaluated after a hit and did not help a tap beside the disc.

## The change

- `displayCore.js`: `HIT_MIN = 44`, `hitSizeOf(disc)` (never below the floor, never below the disc) and `crowdRadiusOf(discSizes)` (the largest tap area).
- `MatchingMap.vue`: the disc keeps the size of its step — the size carries the strength — but no longer takes the tap. An invisible core of `hitSizeOf(disc)` px does, on all three looks. On the light maps the marker box grows to the tap area and the disc sits centred in it (`position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`).
- The crowd radius is derived instead of a number of its own: two tap areas overlap when their centres are closer than the largest tap area, a tap there is ambiguous, and the map zooms in instead of guessing whose area took it. With that, no stacking rule ("the brighter one wins") is needed.
- Comments that described the old footprint ("the size of the disc look's dot", "core or disc inside") now say what the code does.

No change to thresholds, colours, sizes of the discs, or locale files.

## Tests

- `displayCore.spec.js`, new `tap areas`: 20/28/38 → 44, 48 → 48; the crowd radius is 48 for the four steps, 60 once a fifth step of 60 px exists, and 44 when every disc is below the floor.
- `MatchingMap.spec.js`: for the first time the page builds real Leaflet in jsdom (one line of feature-test stub: jsdom has no `createSVGRect`, so Leaflet found no renderer and died at its first circle). A step-1 person on the light map: disc 20 px, tap core 44 px, box 44 px centred; on the dark map: core 44 px inside the 48 px glow. Two step-1 people 40 px apart: a tap zooms in (their areas overlap); 60 px apart: the same tap opens the profile — the control.
- Injection round, one change at a time: crowd radius back to 26, tap area back to the disc, light box back to the disc, disc look without its core, floor 40, radius from the discs instead of the tap areas — each one fails at least one of the tests above, by name. The CSS itself (disc click-through and centred) cannot be measured in jsdom; it is checked in the served bundle and at the device.
- Frontend chain locally: lint, stylelint, locales, 2521 tests, build.

## Verification after merge

In the served `MatchingMap-*.js`: `gk-hit` twice (before: once, only in the glow), `[401,403]` still once (control). In the served `MatchingMap-*.css`: `.gk-disc{…pointer-events:none…position:absolute…}`.

author: nebuk89
body:
The harness is off until the folder is trusted, and it is silent when
it is off. The README said "once the folder is trusted" and never said
how, so a new session in a fresh worktree gets no hooks and no warning
that it has none.

Measured on the merged harness: trust cascades to child directories.
With only the worktree parent in trustedFolders, a session inside a
child worktree loaded these hooks and refused a `git checkout` of a
path. So the step is to trust the directory that holds the worktrees
once, not each worktree in turn.

Also records the check that tells you whether the harness is live: ask
for `git checkout -- some/file` and see whether it comes back refused.

body:
## Summary

On a phone, a podium trio that ran out of room broke at any space, so a driver's name could split across two lines (`K. Antonelli / L. Hamilton / M.` above `Verstappen`). Two mobile rules made it worse by switching driver spans back to `white-space: normal`. On phones, the combinations table, the Overdue and Unlikeliest leaderboards, and the landing page's "New podiums through the years" timeline now list a trio's drivers one per line. The hairlines inside a trio are faint and the rule between trios uses the stronger border, so each trio reads as its own block.

## Changes

- **Markup**: each driver span now carries the `/` that follows it, and on the combos table the last one carries the shared-car badge. Changed in `build_combos_html.py`, `build_overdue_html.py`, `build_unlikeliest.py` and the timeline renderer in `podigami.js`. Inline layouts therefore wrap only *after* a separator, never mid-name and never with `/` leading a line. Stacked layouts just hide it.
- **CSS (≤600px)**: driver spans are `display: block` with a faint hairline between them (`color-mix` of `--border`, 50%). Row and entry dividers use `--border-strong`, with a little more row padding. Removed both `white-space: normal` overrides on `.driver` (index.css) and `.trio .pdriver` (podigami.css).
- Soulmates pairs are left inline. Tablet and desktop keep the inline `A / B / C` form.
- README: phone description of the combos table, and the test count (788 was already stale → 832). RELEASE_NOTES entry.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest -q` → 832 passed (includes the Playwright e2e tests)
- New e2e test: on all four pages at 360px, every trio name sits on exactly one line, and no two names share a line
- New unit and CSS guards: the separator rides with the name before it, the badge rides with the last name, no driver span is `white-space: normal`, trios stack on mobile, and boundaries use `--border-strong` while the inner lines are faint
- Manual Playwright sweep: at 1200px and 650px all 754 combos, 30 overdue, 30 unlikeliest and the timeline show 0 split names and 0 lines starting with `/`. Screenshots checked in dark and light theme at 390px
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean

- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] `ruff format --check .` passes
- [x] `pytest -q` passes
- [x] No new security vulnerabilities introduced

author: john-sm1z
body:
## Summary

Ten-phase remediation following the Phase 0 diagnostic audit, each phase a distinct area with its own root causes, fixes, and verification:

1. **Dashboards** (`24763b0`) — employee/clinic dashboards not opening correctly
2. **Database / RLS / multi-tenancy** (`4a26910`) — cross-tenant data isolation
3. **Telegram** (`35ace36`) — bot not responding to patients
4. **Real-time conversation / human takeover** (`97a8368`) — operator takeover and reply reliability
5. **Appointment / scheduling** (`0d4f38e`) — unifying the booking workflow across all 4 channels
6. **Application security / red-team** (`9311d7c`) — authorization audit across the role matrix, tenant isolation, and financial-data gating
7. **Clinic operations dashboard completion** (`b7de19b`) — verifying and completing all 10 dashboard areas as a professional clinic operations system
8. **Analytics accuracy** (`676b1cb`) — correcting fabricated revenue and completing `/admin/analytics`
9. **End-to-end QA / two-clinic integration verification** (`f645bee`) — verifying the whole platform coheres across two independently configured clinics
10. **Final production readiness gate** (`e287175`) — code quality, security, Telegram, database, performance, error handling, and deployment-configuration audit, plus a full end-to-end critical-flow confirmation

### Phase 1 — Dashboards

- **`/admin/login` 404**, **3 admin sub-pages silently broken** (routed to a deleted `/api/admin/catalog`), **cross-clinic role bleed** in `getStaffContext()` (a receptionist at Clinic A who is also owner at Clinic B could act as owner inside Clinic A), **no error boundaries** + **Supabase env vars missing from the fail-closed startup check**, **doctor self-service block deletion** silently 403'ing, **`admin/calendar`** dead error state.

### Phase 2 — Database / RLS / multi-tenancy

- **Closed a confirmed payments RLS bypass (P0)** — any owner/admin/manager session could `update({ status: "paid" })` directly, bypassing the legal-transition check and audit trail. A DB trigger now blocks all `authenticated`-role writes to `payments` outright.
- **`doctor_services` had no clinic_id** and nothing at the DB layer stopped a Clinic A doctor pairing with a Clinic B service — added a same-clinic-enforcing trigger.
- Dropped redundant RLS policies, added a missing hot-path index, added UNIQUE constraints on Telegram bot-identity columns.

### Phase 3 — Telegram (root cause was never "just the bot token")

- **`instrumentation.ts` (P0)** — the fail-closed check for `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` only fired when the legacy, optional `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` was *also* set, so a deployment that never sets that legacy token (the common case) started successfully with the real webhook secret unset — **every clinic's webhook then failed closed to 401 on every incoming update**, silently.
- **`notifications/processor.ts`** had the same legacy-token gate blocking every clinic's reminders.
- Webhook idempotency claims could get **permanently stuck** if a request was killed mid-processing — now self-heal after 5 minutes. Not hypothetical: the voice-transcription path's own timeouts (30s + 60s) exceeded the platform's 60s request timeout on both deployment targets — raised to 120s.
- `supabase/full-db-setup.sql` (the one-paste bootstrap script) was silently missing 7 of 29 migrations.
- 5 docs corrected, including a manual webhook-setup example that sent the *raw* shared secret instead of the per-bot HMAC derived from it (would reject every update forever).

### Phase 4 — Real-time conversation / human takeover

The take-over/release state machine was already sound (atomic CAS, verified with a real concurrent-request race test). One confirmed defect: **operator replies (`PUT .../conversations/[id]`)** were persisted and reported as sent regardless of whether Telegram actually delivered them — fixed to store the real outcome and surface a failed delivery immediately and persistently (message-bubble marker, survives reloads).

### Phase 5 — Appointment / scheduling

One authoritative booking engine already existed and is sound (`book_appointment`/`reschedule_appointment`: per-doctor advisory lock + a real GIST exclusion constraint for double-booking, both RPCs revoked from `authenticated` entirely, already covered by genuine concurrent-RPC race tests). All 4 channels already route through it — no duplicate implementation needed consolidating. The bugs were all in the layers around it:

- **`api/catalog/route.ts`** — the per-service eligible-doctors list checked `doctor_services` restrictions across the *whole clinic* instead of per doctor: once any one doctor anywhere had a restriction, every other unrestricted doctor silently vanished from every service's doctor list.
- **`api/availability/route.ts`** — never checked whether a doctor actually offers the requested service (showed "available" slots `book_appointment` would reject outright), and always used the service's base duration, ignoring a doctor's own `duration_override_minutes`.
- **Source tracking** — a genuine self-service website booking was tagged `walk_in`, identical to a real front-desk walk-in entered by staff; analytics couldn't tell them apart. Added `web` as its own `appointment_source` value.
- **`SOURCE_LABELS`** had a `telegram_bot` key that never matched the real enum value `telegram_chat`, and the same map was separately being misapplied to a different enum (conversation channel) where it could never match at all — every affected value showed as a raw, untranslated string across 4+ dashboard views.

### Phase 6 — Application security / red-team

Dedicated authorization audit attacking the app through routes, APIs, server actions, and direct database access — explicitly not UI. Covered the full role matrix (`platform_admin`, `clinic_owner`, `clinic_manager`, `receptionist`, `doctor`) against roughly 20 API routes plus the core RLS policies: cross-clinic ID substitution on every tenant-owned resource (clinic/patient/doctor/appointment/conversation/integration IDs), financial-analytics gating (receptionist/doctor must never reach owner-level revenue data), doctor-to-doctor isolation, payment-webhook signature/idempotency integrity, and hidden/direct endpoint access.

Result: the authorization architecture was already sound almost everywhere it was tested. One real defect found and fixed:

- **`hasRole()` platform-admin bypass** — returned `true` unconditionally for any `platformAdmin: true` context regardless of the requested role, even though platform admins hold zero clinic staff roles by design. Not independently exploitable for data access — every data-facing route goes through `requireStaff`/`requireRoles`, which reject platform admins outright before a role check is ever reached. Still a genuine authorization-primitive defect, so it was fixed at the primitive.

Also added a regression test proving a clinic owner cannot self-escalate (or grant a third party) a `staff_roles` row in a *different* clinic by supplying its `clinic_id`.

### Phase 7 — Clinic operations dashboard completion

Verified and completed all 10 dashboard areas (Overview, Appointments, Calendar, Patients, Conversations, Doctors, Services, Analytics, Settings, Telegram Integration) against an explicit "professional clinic operations system" bar. Confirmed and fixed:

- **Workspace routing gap (most significant finding)** — `admin/layout.tsx` had no role-based redirect at all, unlike the symmetric guard already in `doctor/layout.tsx`. Added `adminWorkspaceRedirect()`: platform admins → `/platform`, pure doctors → `/doctor`, hybrid identities unaffected.
- **"Today" used the browser's local timezone, not the clinic's** — the Overview page and the doctor queue page both now use the clinic-timezone window.
- **No "operational notes" on patients** (explicit spec gap, explicitly non-clinical) — added a column, PATCH endpoint, and editable panel.
- **"Last visit" / "visit count" conflated with raw activity/

author: robhicks
body:
## Summary
- Every crate stops being frozen at `0.1.0`: release-please now computes the product's SemVer version, `CHANGELOG.md`, and a git tag + GitHub Release from Conventional Commits history (`release-please-config.json`, `.release-please-manifest.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gains a `pr-title` job enforcing `<type>(<scope>): <subject>` PR titles (Conventional Commits) and a `release-please` job; `deploy` now runs only when release-please has just cut a release, not on every push to `master` — a deliberate, documented change from `docs/specs/2026-09-08-master-autodeploy-design.md`'s "every push deploys" model.
- Fixed a pre-existing bug: the MCP `initialize` handshake reported `rmcp`'s own crate identity (`name: "rmcp"`, `version: "2.0.0"`) instead of otto-factory's, because the default `Implementation::from_build_env()` resolves inside the `rmcp` crate's own build context. `of-mcp`'s `get_info()` now reports `otto-factory`'s real name/version, with a regression test. A second regression test pins `of-web`'s OpenAPI document version (already correct) against future drift.
- `CLAUDE.md` gains a "Releases & versioning" section recording the new commit/PR-title convention and tying the breaking-change marker to Non-Negotiable Rule 6's existing discipline. `docs/deploy/fly.md` and `docs/clients/matrix.md` are updated accordingly.

## Design docs
- Spec: `docs/specs/2026-09-10-semver-release-design.md` (critiqued pre-implementation, then hardened post-review — see below)
- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-09-10-semver-release.md`

Closes #84

## Review round: rust-pro, architect-reviewer, and an independent (diff-only) security-auditor pass all ran against this PR. Fixed since:
- **[Security, High]** `pr-title` had no `permissions:` block and ran a mutable-tag action while inheriting this repo's write-scoped default `GITHUB_TOKEN` on every internal PR. Fixed: job-level `permissions: pull-requests: read`, action pinned to its exact commit SHA, plus a workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` default so no other job is exposed the same way.
- **[Security/Architecture, converged from 3 independent reviewers]** `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` could cancel the push that merges release-please's release PR — after the tag/Release already exist but before `deploy` runs — with no later push able to re-trigger it (`release_created` only flips once). Fixed: pushes to `master` no longer cancel each other; only PR runs do.
- **[Security, Medium]** `deploy`'s `if:` relied transitively on `release-please`'s own event/branch guard. Fixed: `deploy` now states its own `github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'` guard explicitly.
- **[Code quality, Important]** `release-please-config.json` had no history boundary, so the first changelog would have backfilled this repo's entire pre-convention commit history — contradicting this spec's own stated scope ("`CHANGELOG.md` starts from here"). Fixed: added `bootstrap-sha` pinned to `origin/master`'s tip at PR-open time.
- **[Code quality/Architecture, converged]** `CLAUDE.md`'s new section was missing the paragraph describing the deploy-gating change — arguably the highest-value line in the whole section. Added.
- **[Docs]** A dangling reference to "Non-Negotiable Rule 6" in `CLAUDE.md` (that numbering lives in a skill file, not `CLAUDE.md` itself) now says where to find it. An overstated "job definition... unchanged" claim in the superseded `docs/specs/2026-09-08-...` spec's pointer was scoped down to what's actually still true. A dropped sentence in `docs/deploy/fly.md` about a failing upstream job skipping `deploy` was restored for the new transitive chain.
- **[Correction]** An earlier version of this PR body claimed the first live merge would show whether `release-please`'s own PR passes `pr-title`. That's not achievable: GitHub does not fire `pull_request` events for a PR authored by `GITHUB_TOKEN` (recursion guard), so `pr-title` never runs on release-please's own PR at all — it shows no check, not a green one. The `pull-request-title-pattern` config is still worth keeping (it's what the *squashed* commit on `master` looks like, and insurance for if branch protection or a human re-open ever changes this), but it isn't the thing gating the release path. The actual gate is unaffected: the push that merges the release PR still runs `rust`/`web`/`docker-build` (via `release-please`'s own `needs:`) before `deploy` can fire. Corrected in the spec §2.

## Re-verification round (independent security-auditor re-check of the fixes above)
- **[Medium]** `cancel-in-progress: false` alone only protects a run already *in progress* — GitHub still cancels a *pending* run in an occupied group when a newer one queues in behind it, so a second superseding push could still strand a tagged-but-undeployed release. Fixed: master pushes now key their `concurrency` group on `github.run_id` instead of the shared branch ref, so no master push is ever queued behind another and none can cancel one another.
- **[Medium]** The hardening pass gave `deploy` its own explicit `event_name`/`ref` guard but left `release-please` — which holds *more* privilege (`contents: write` + `pull-requests: write`, vs. `deploy`'s `contents: read` + one app-scoped Fly token) — relying only on `on.push.branches`. Fixed: `release-please` now states the same explicit `github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'` guard.
- Both SHA pins were independently dereferenced against the GitHub API and confirmed authentic (not just present).
- **Explicitly not fixed, with reasoning** (all LOW, all pre-existing — not introduced by this PR): `rust`/`web`/`docker-build` still have no `timeout-minutes` (pre-existing gap, matters more now that push runs aren't auto-cancelled by a newer push, but expanding this PR into a general CI-hardening pass over jobs it didn't touch is its own change); `deploy`'s `actions/checkout@v4` step is left on a mutable tag like five other first-party `actions/*`/`docker/*` refs in this workflow (low risk, first-party, and SHA-pinning only the one step beside an already-pinned step is inconsistent without doing the rest); the repo's `can_approve_pull_request_reviews: true` setting is an org/repo setting outside this diff, currently inert since `master`'s ruleset requires zero approvals, flagged for whoever administers the repo rather than fixed here.

## Operational prerequisite for the first live run
release-please needs the repo setting **"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** enabled, or its first attempt to open a release PR fails. Not something this PR can verify or set from the diff — flagging for whoever merges this.

## Notes for reviewers
- **`web/package-lock.json` version drift**: its root `"version"` field isn't covered by `extra-files` and will lag `web/package.json`'s version by one `npm install` after a release — the same accepted, cosmetic drift as `Cargo.lock`'s per-crate versions (neither breaks a build; `npm ci`/unlocked `cargo build` both tolerate it — confirmed empirically for `npm ci`).
- **This PR touches no `web/` source**, so `npm run check`/`lint`/`test`/`build` are vacuously satisfied rather than run.
- This is a deliberate, documented behavior change to deploy cadence (every merge → every release-please PR merge, and only for `feat`/`fix`/`perf`/breaking commits — a run of purely `docs`/`chore`/`ci` commits deploys nothing at all) — see the spec's Assumptions and Risks sections.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"`
- [x] `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('release-please-config.json')); json.load(open('.release-please-manifest.json'))"`
- [x] No `web/` source changed — `npm run check`/`lint`/`test`/`build` vacuously satisfied

author: copilot
body:
PR #64 recorded that cross-project import of the source vocabularies "needs them frozen as exportable at the source plus an import contract; neither exists." The source project `GFLK-Taaqol-GPT` now exports `gflk.origin_type.v1` (270 rows over `ORIGIN_LEDGER_AR_v1`) with a deterministic content id and a self-declared `FROZEN_LOCAL` scope. This adds the receiving half: the import contract inside Alghanem.

The boundary the module keeps is `ForeignFrozenExport != LocalFreeze` — `Canonicalization != Authority` (A0.PP.1b) one level up. Importing bytes transfers a *checked content identity*, never a permission.

### `src/alghanem/arabic/imported_feature_vocabulary.py` (new, inert documentation layer)

- **The foreign scope is read, never promoted** — `ForeignFreezeScope.FROZEN_LOCAL` is a one-valued closed vocabulary. No function converts it to `SpecificationFreeze.FROZEN`, a kernel `Freeze`, an `E0`, or a birth; promotion would claim a gate this repository does not hold.
- **Genus binding** — `ImportedFeatureVocabulary` refuses any genus but `EvidenceGenus.MORPHO_FUNCTIONAL`. This is the binding #64 named as absent.
- **`UNRESOLVED` is a member, not a gap** — `ImportedOriginType` is closed over `EVENT`/`ENTITY`/`UNRESOLVED`; an unrecognized value is refused rather than folded into `UNRESOLVED`.
- **The distribution is derived, not declared** — counts and row count are computed from `entries`; a declared value that disagrees is refused, so no field exists that the answer can be written into. Duplicate roots are refused because a duplicate hides one entry under another's identity.
- **The digest is re-derived, not trusted** — `ImportedVocabularyContentVerifier` is the sole issuer of `VerifiedVocabularyImport` and `LocalVocabularyContentIdentity`, encoding through the shared `alghanem.canonical_content` primitive (never a second hash implementation), with schema coverage asserted at import against the dataclass fields.
- **The recorded release is pinned** — `assert_matches_recorded_release` refuses any import that does not match 270 rows, 126 `EVENT` / 56 `ENTITY` / 88 `UNRESOLVED`, the source ids, and the declared digest `facf6720…`.

```python
# refused: a declared distribution written over the entries
vocabulary(declared_distribution=((ImportedOriginType.EVENT, 3), ...))

# refused: the export claiming a genus the contract is not bound to
vocabulary_from_export_mapping(payload(genus="DISTRIBUTIONAL"))

# refused: FROZEN_LOCAL upgraded to a local freeze — there is no such function
```

### The two digests attest different things, structurally

The export generator's own self-check computes `content_id` over `(root, origin_type)` pairs only, so `raw_category` and `batch_note` move without moving `facf6720…`. The Alghanem identity covers every entry field. `SOURCE_DIGEST_COVERED_FIELDS` is asserted at import to be a **proper** subset of the entry fields, so the local identity cannot later be read as equivalent to the source's.

### Boundaries

`ImportedVocabulary != BornOntology`: this is not the deferred born morpho-functional vocabulary, and the five distributional features and `RECORDED_PROBE_REPORT` are byte-identical. Scope stays narrow to `OriginType` — the weight and structure vocabularies have not been exported, and a general frame assuming them would be an abstraction ahead of its referent. No result, verdict, or birth field (checked at import); no kernel gate reads it, asserted by a test scanning every `kernel/` module.

Docs: `docs/CONSTITUTION.md` row `A0.PP.3`, plus a README section. 14 tests covering determinism, tamper detection, genus/vocabulary/duplicate refusals, private-token issuance, and the strictly-finer local coverage.

### Not closed, and not papered over

The export JSON payload and the byte-precise `gflk.canonical.v1` schema were truncated in transit, so `examples/imported_vocabulary/origin_type_export_v1.json` is **not** vendored and `facf6720…` is pinned as a declared reference rather than independently recomputed here. `SOURCE_DIGEST_REDERIVATION_NOTE` states exactly that instead of implying a verification that did not happen. Landing the full payload and schema would let the pinned digest be reproduced literally.

author: psgestaoecapital
body:
## O problema (Fábio, 3 chamados, mesmo assunto)
- **#21** "NÃO SOBE A FOTO NO PÁTIO" · **#22** "FOTO NÃO CARREGA" · **#33** "não está baixando foto vistoria nem do veículo".
- Provado no dado (RD-38): o bucket privado `revenda-veiculos` tem **0 objetos desde 03/09** — nenhuma foto de vistoria jamais subiu. `#22`/`#33` ("não carrega"/"não baixa") são **efeito** de nada nunca ter subido, não causa separada.

## Causa raiz
O bucket tem as políticas de storage `veic_foto_insert/select/delete` (migration `20260903150000`) que exigem o **company_id como PRIMEIRO segmento** do path:
```
split_part(name,'/',1) IN (SELECT get_user_company_ids()::text) OR is_admin()
```
A tela da vistoria no pátio (Onda 5B, #1287) reusou o **mesmo bucket**, mas montava o path começando por `vistorias/${companyId}/...`. O primeiro segmento virava a **string literal `"vistorias"`**, que nunca está em `get_user_company_ids()` → a policy de INSERT **negava** e a foto não subia.

Simulei o INSERT sob o papel `authenticated` com o usuário do Fábio (transação revertida):
| path | INSERT permitido |
|---|---|
| `${companyId}/...` (bloco Fotos do veículo) | ✅ permitido |
| `vistorias/${companyId}/...` (vistoria) | ❌ negado |

## A correção
Cirúrgica, **só front**: o `company_id` passa a ser o primeiro segmento — `${companyId}/vistorias/${vistoriaId}/${regiao}/...` — reusando a policy **já provada**. Sem migration, sem policy nova, seguindo a convenção documentada do bucket (`path = <company_id>/...`).

- O bloco **"Fotos do veículo"** (detalhe do veículo) já usava `company_id` primeiro → nunca teve esse bug, segue igual.
- **0 linhas** em `insp_foto` hoje → nada a migrar/orfanizar.
- `tsc` / `eslint` limpos.

## Teste depois do deploy
Fábio abre uma vistoria no pátio, tira a foto de uma região → a foto sobe, aparece na hora e volta a carregar na retomada. Aí os 3 chamados podem ser confirmados.

author: taikitanaka3
body:
## 概要

`shared/cyclonedds.xml` は探索を `lo` に固定していますが、`lo` に MULTICAST フラグが無いホスト（Ubuntu 既定。`ip link show lo` に `MULTICAST` が出ない状態）では CycloneDDS がマルチキャストを諦めて localhost へのユニキャスト探索に落ちます。その探索先は participant index `0..MaxAutoParticipantIndex` に限られ、既定値 9 では**同一ホスト・同一ドメインに ROS プロセスを 10 個までしか立てられません**。11 個目は次のエラーで落ちます。

```
Failed to find a free participant index for domain 0
[ERROR] [rmw_cyclonedds_cpp]: rmw_create_node: failed to create domain, error Error
```

遠隔PCは 4 台構成で zenoh ブリッジ ×4 + joy + manager（6）と RViz 側（launch, robot_state_publisher, map container, relay ×6, rviz2 = 10）で 16 プロセスになり、上限を超えます。`ros2 topic echo` を 1 つ叩くだけでも 1 つ消費します。

`Discovery/MaxAutoParticipantIndex` を 99 に広げ、README に経緯を書きました。zenoh-bridge-ros2dds も `CYCLONEDDS_URI` を読むので、ブリッジ・ホスト側ノード・RViz コンテナの全部に同じファイルが効きます。

## 実測

`unshare -rn` で lo に MULTICAST が無い network namespace を作り、rclpy ノードを N プロセス立てて `ros2 node list --no-daemon --spin-time 6` で見える数を数えました（ros-humble-cyclonedds 0.10.5、rmw_cyclonedds_cpp 1.3.4）。

| 設定 | lo の MULTICAST | 起動数 | 生存 | 発見できた数 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 変更前 | なし | 14 | 9 | 0（`ros2 node list` 自身も index を取れず失敗） |
| 変更前 | なし | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| 変更後 | なし | 14 | 14 | 14 |
| 変更後 | なし | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| 変更後 | なし | 16（4台構成相当） | 16 | 16 |
| 変更前 / 変更後 | あり（このPC） | 14 | 14 | 14 |

MULTICAST がある環境では挙動は変わりません。

## 注意

- 9/10 に統括SD の RViz で「位置が出た後しばらくすると車両が動かなくなる」事象が報告されていますが、**これがその原因だとは確認できていません**。この不具合は「起動時にプロセスが立たない」形で出るもので、動いていたものが止まる説明にはなりません。切り分けには、当日の RViz コンテナログ（`docker compose logs rviz2`）と `output/<ts>/remote/zenoh-*.log` に上のエラー文があるか、遠隔PCで `ip link show lo` に MULTICAST があるかを見てください。
- 本体リポジトリの `vehicle/cyclonedds.xml` も同じ内容です。車両 ECU 側は Autoware のプロセス数が多いので lo の multicast が有効になっているはずですが、揃えるなら同じ変更を入れられます（このPRでは触っていません）。
- `pre-commit run` 通過（check-xml 含む）。

author: surki
body:
## What

Adds `allowed_headers` to the `grpc` transform: when set, only matching headers are included in the request/response protos sent to the `TransformService` server. Empty (default) forwards everything, as today.

```yaml
transforms:
  - name: grpc
    config:
      name: "policy-engine"
      target: "localhost:9500"
      allowed_headers: ["Content-Type", "User-Agent", "/^X-Request-.*$/"]
```

## Why

`send_request_body: false` keeps bodies local, but for an external policy service the sensitive material is usually in the headers: the upstream `Authorization` bearer, cookies, third-party API keys. A policy decision rarely needs any of them, yet today all of them cross to a second service (often over plaintext h2c) and land in its request logs. This is the same knob Envoy's `ext_authz` exposes as `authorization_request.allowed_headers`, and the same posture as the existing `header_allowlist` transform: an allowlist, because a denylist silently leaks whatever nobody thought of.

## Behavior notes

- Syntax mirrors `header_allowlist`: literal names matched case-insensitively against the canonical form, or `/.../` compiled as a case-insensitive regexp. An invalid regex fails at startup.
- Applies to the request headers on both RPCs and to the upstream response headers on `TransformResponse` (so `Set-Cookie` etc. don't cross either).
- Only the proto is filtered. The `http.Request` that goes upstream is not touched — `header_allowlist` remains the tool for stripping headers from the upstream request.
- Docs: `iron-proxy.example.yaml` (the README has no grpc transform section yet, same as #247).

## Testing

- `TestAllowedHeaders_FiltersWhatReachesServer` — through a fake server: only allowed request headers reach it on both RPCs, response headers are filtered too, and the upstream `http.Request` keeps its `Authorization`/`Cookie`.
- `TestAllowedHeaders_EmptyForwardsAll` — default unchanged.
- `TestAllowedHeaders_InvalidRegex` — startup error.
- `TestFactory_ParsesAllowedHeaders` — YAML decoding and case-insensitive matching.
- `go test -race ./internal/transform/grpc/`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run` clean.

author: lorfersilve
body:
## Phase 12.6.1 — camera/layer composition foundation

This PR establishes the CPU-side contract for the next Rendering 2.0 slice without yet introducing multi-camera execution.

### Public composition contract
- adds `RenderLayerRange2D` to `RenderContext2D`; the default range preserves all existing rendering behavior
- `RenderQueue2D` now filters the already-deterministic pass snapshot by the context layer range
- adds header-only `RenderComposition2D`
- each ordered entry borrows one `Camera2D`, selects one `RenderPass2D`, one inclusive integer layer range, and one normalized viewport
- generated contexts carry pass/layer/frame state
- generated views copy the camera view and override only the viewport, so the borrowed camera is not mutated

### Bounded / deterministic configuration
- maximum 16 composition entries
- maximum 128-byte unique entry names
- explicit insertion order; only `moveEntry()` changes order
- transactional rejection of invalid entries, duplicate names, invalid indices, capacity overflow, invalid viewports, and invalid layer ranges
- disabled entries remain configured but do not produce a context/view

### Compatibility
- existing aggregate `RenderContext2D` call sites remain source-compatible because the new layer range is appended with an all-layers default
- objects without `RenderOrder2D` remain World/layer 0
- `RenderLayerStack2D`, `Camera2D`, `RenderPipeline2D`, and existing Scene rendering semantics are otherwise unchanged
- execution of multiple composition entries is intentionally deferred to Phase 12.6.2

### Validation
- adds focused headless regression coverage for layer-range boundaries, entry validation/order/capacity, generated context/view state, disabled entries, and `RenderQueue2D` layer filtering

Do not merge until all required CI gates are green.

body: ## What Adds a local, keyboard-accessible editable preview for extracted tables so users can correct headers and cells before export. Review follow-up: JSON/download is lossless when headers collide, and Cursor Cloud setup uses plain `npm ci`. ## Why Extraction output often needs small fixes before CSV/JSON/TSV/Markdown copy or download. Those edits should stay in the popup preview and must not rewrite history, current extraction state, or storage. `toJSON()` used `Object.fromEntries`, so duplicate headers (generated `Column N` padding or a user renaming a column onto another) silently dropped a cell. React 19 / `react-dom` 19 are aligned, so `--legacy-peer-deps` is no longer required on Node 22 / npm 10. ## How - `DataPreview` keeps a cloned `ExtractionResult` draft seeded from the incoming `result`. - Generated padding skips already-used `Column N` labels so visible headers stay unique and readable. - `toJSON()` assigns deterministic unique keys (`Name`, `Name (2)`, …) so JSON copy and JSON download keep every cell. CSV, TSV, and Markdown still emit the visible labels, including duplicates. - Cursor Cloud `.cursor/install.sh` runs `npm ci` (no `--legacy-peer-deps`). ## Checklist - [x] Tests pass - [x] No new warnings - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)

body:
## Summary

- Stop automatic Vercel preview deploys on every PR branch. `app/vercel.json` now auto-deploys only `main` and `tnr-preview/*`, so ordinary PR pushes no longer consume Fluid compute or build minutes.
- A collaborator with write access can comment `/tnr-create-preview` to snapshot the current PR head onto `tnr-preview/pr-{N}` and wait for that one preview. Later pushes do not refresh it.
- New PRs get an automatic instructions comment (also added to the PR template and CONTRIBUTING). `/tnr-review-now` resolves on-demand snapshots; `/tnr-repro-now` still uses `tnr-preview/main`. Closed PRs delete the snapshot branch.

## Test plan

- [ ] After merge to `main`, confirm the next production deploy still runs
- [ ] Open a new PR and confirm the instructions comment is posted and Vercel does **not** start a preview for the PR branch
- [ ] As a write collaborator, comment `/tnr-create-preview` and confirm a preview URL is posted
- [ ] Push another commit and confirm the preview URL stays on the old SHA until the command is run again
- [ ] Run `/tnr-review-now` after a preview exists and confirm it finds the snapshot URL
- [ ] Close the PR and confirm `tnr-preview/pr-{N}` is deleted
- [ ] Confirm an unauthorized commenter cannot trigger a preview

author: yameenbux
body:
Four fixes to how the site identifies the business to Google. All verified in code; none of them is a ranking silver bullet, and the honest assessment is at the bottom.

## 1. The review count was structurally wrong

The on-page count read `REVIEWS.length` and the schema hardcoded `"9"`. Both were really answering *"how many reviews did we choose to reproduce?"* — which happened to equal the profile total at build time and doesn't any more. The profile now holds **10**; nine are quoted.

Added `TOTAL_REVIEWS` as the single source for the profile total. The array stays what it always was: the reviews reproduced verbatim.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| On-page count | `REVIEWS.length` (9) | `TOTAL_REVIEWS` (10) |
| `schema.reviewCount` | `"9"` | `"10"` |

The site was understating the business.

## 2. Canonical Business Profile link

Replaced the `share.google` shortener with the canonical profile URL across all 20 pages.

## 3. `sameAs` added

Nothing on the site previously told Google that buxtravel.co.uk and the Business Profile were the same entity. Every page carrying `LocalBusiness` markup now links the profile, Yell and Cylex.

## 4. Full NAP

`PostalAddress` carried only `"Bolton, Greater Manchester, GB"` — no street, no postcode — so there was nothing for Google to match against the profile. Now **Grasmere St, Bolton BL1 8LH**, confirmed by the operator from the live profile, on all 17 pages with `LocalBusiness` markup (one top level, sixteen nested under `provider`).

Matched to the **profile**, not to the directory: Cylex lists "76 Grasmere St" but the profile shows no house number. NAP consistency means matching the profile, not improving on it.

## Verification

- 17 of 17 `LocalBusiness` blocks parse as valid JSON and carry full NAP plus three `sameAs` entries
- Review count renders as 10, schema reads 10, no console errors
- No `share.google` references remain

## What this is honestly worth

**A few percent, not a rank jump.** These changes remove reasons for Google to be uncertain about the business's identity. They will not beat a competitor with a ten-year-old exact-match domain and 90 reviews.

Diagnosis for the record: two likely causes were ruled out — the profile's primary category is correctly "Coach and minibus hire", and the address is public rather than a hidden service area. What remains is **review volume** (10 is a small base) and **proximity** (BL1 8LH sits about a mile from the town centre, and distance from the searcher is not something any code change touches).

author: jmbrunick
body: ## Description Port of [#53](https://github.com/jmbrunick/openpilot/pull/53) onto **nap-release**. Intersecting / off-route roads (and v3 MN statutory fills) were poisoning `nextSpeedLimit`, so Map MAX walked down on a continuous highway (US 12 tagged 60/50) as if braking for a lower posted limit that was not on the road. **Root cause:** `osm_db.lookup` prefers along-way next, then falls back to geodesic heading-ray probes. On a long same-speed way (remaining > 600 m) along-way returned nothing, so the heading ray ran. `_best_match` only *penalized* off-heading ways by 15 m, so a nearby residential 30 (cross street, or anything the ray hit after a slight curve / ~5° GPS heading error) became `nextSpeedLimit`. **Fix (mapd matcher, from #53):** - Next-limit matching requires **bearing continuity** (`HEADING_ALIGN_DEG` is a hard gate, not a 15 m penalty). - Major ways (trunk/primary/secondary) do not jump onto residential/living_street fills unless the road name matches (`_continues_route`). - If the matched way continues at the same limit past the 600 m horizon, that is a resolved “no change” — **no geodesic fallback** (`_next_limit`). - Geodesic is only used for OSM gaps after the way ends, and still route-filtered. **Also:** bump `maps-index.json` to revision 3 (`osm-us-speed-limits-v3`) and matching first-install fetch constants so Download US Maps matches nap-dev Benson fills **with** this matcher. Intentionally **not** included: speed-sign logger, Force Offroad, wipers/beams, MN Refresh-maps statutory overlay policy. **Preserved:** Map Follow/Cap, sticky MAX, 1.5 s GNSS offset, +110 m map drops, Accel-5 brake feel, wheel-speed live speed. **Note:** Refresh maps on nap-release still overlays tagged OSM maxspeed only. A live refresh in Minnesota can drop unmarked v3 pack fills until that policy is ported separately. Do not merge until Justin reviews. ## Verification ```bash pytest --noconftest selfdrive/mapd/tests/test_osm_db.py \ selfdrive/mapd/tests/test_fetch_maps.py \ selfdrive/mapd/tests/test_map_speed_policy.py -q ``` **CI-equivalent local run:** 72 passed, 11 skipped. New cases: curved 60 + 30 fill, long 60 + grid of 30s with GPS heading 70–90°, on-route 60→50 still wins over a 30 cross street, OSM gap still finds on-route 50, Benson US 12 60 ignores a Minnesota Ave 30 fill. **On-device (Justin, Benson MN, comma 3X, Map Follow/Cap):** 1. Download US Maps so the device has `osm-us-speed-limits-v3`. 2. Drive a continuous tagged stretch of **US 12 60** (and 60→50) through town. Nearby unmarked residential 30 fills should **not** make MAX walk down. 3. LIMIT (posted OSM) should stay 60 until the real US 12 50/30. MAX should only ease for an **on-route** decrease (kin + 110 m), not for a side street.

Pins every non-GitHub-owned action in this repo to a full-length commit SHA, keeping the version tag as a trailing comment.

A tag is a moving pointer — whoever controls the upstream repo (or compromises that maintainer's account) can repoint it and change what executes here. These steps run with `contents: write` or cloud credentials in scope, so that matters.

No version changes: each SHA is the exact commit the pinned tag resolved to today. Part of a sweep across the org so `sha_pinning_required` can be turned on afterwards.
