author: anderssjoeberg75
body:
Varje körning började blint. Agenten fick bränna steg på att lista mappar och gissa innan den ens visste vilket språk projektet var skrivet i — och med ett litet kontextfönster hann den ibland aldrig fram.

## Vad som händer nu

När du väljer en arbetsyta läses projektet igenom **en gång**. Vyn säger vad som pågår och vad som hittades:

> 🔎 **Analyserar repot…** läser igenom filerna för att se vad projektet innehåller och var funktionerna finns. Det tar oftast bara någon sekund – du kan börja skriva under tiden.

> ✓ **Repot är analyserat.** 3 filer · Markdown (1), JavaScript (1), Python (1) · 4 funktioner/klasser hittade — Codex vet nu vad projektet innehåller och kan slå upp var något definieras i stället för att leta.

Det här repot: **0,12 s, 833 funktioner och klasser**.

## Två delar, med flit åtskilda

**Projektöversikten** läggs först i systemprompten — språk, storlek, nyckelfiler, toppnivåns mappar, och vilka filer som innehåller mest kod:

```
PROJEKTET (analyserat när arbetsytan valdes):
- 49 filer, Python x36, Markdown x3, Shell x2, JavaScript x1.
- Nyckelfiler: README.md.
- Toppnivå: studio (30), (roten) (14), tests (4), docs (1).
- Mest kod i: studio/web/assets/app.js (225 def), tests/test_ollama_web.py (210 def), …
- Använd TOOL find_symbol {"name": "..."} för att hitta var något definieras.
```

Hårt begränsad till ~1400 tecken — för det här repot blir den **519**. Frestelsen är att lägga hela kartan där; då tar den plats från det agenten faktiskt läser under körningen, och kontextbudgeten är hela poängen med det tidigare arbetet i grenen.

**Symbolindexet** ligger *utanför* prompten. Nytt verktyg:

```
find_symbol {"name": "berakna_moms"}
  → src/betalning.py:1  berakna_moms (function)
```

Python tolkas med `ast` (funktioner, klasser, metoder); övriga språk med enkla mönster som hittar definitioner på radens början.

## Detaljer värda att nämna

- **Indexet görs om när något skrivs** i arbetsytan — annars pekar det fel efter en ändring. Testat.
- **Analysen får aldrig sänka en repo-hämtning.** Misslyckas den rapporteras det, och Codex fungerar som förut.
- Cachad per arbetsyta med TTL, så den körs inte om i onödan.

## Test

Fyra nya fall: att kartan stämmer, att `find_symbol` pekar rätt (och säger till ärligt när något inte finns), att översikten håller sig under taket, och att indexet görs om efter en skrivning.

**223 tester gröna** på Python 3.10–3.13. Sju webbläsarflöden körda, inklusive ett nytt som kontrollerar infotexten och att agenten får kartan i systemprompten.

author: nicolaidolmer
body:
## Hvad

Rytterprofilen fyrede 15 API-kald pr. rytter uanset hvilken fane spilleren stod paa, og tre af kaldene var globale (samme svar uanset rytter) men blev hentet forfra ved hvert mount. Denne PR deler de globale kald og henter fane-data foerst naar fanen aabnes: 15 kald bliver til 8 paa en kold profil, 16 til 7 paa en klient-navigation.

Refs #5089

## Hvorfor (og hvad evidensen faktisk baerer)

`apiBaselineLimiter` (`backend/routes/api.js:541`) er sat til 600/min pr. bruger-eller-IP, og kommentaren over den siger at en 429 herfra betyder enten et loebsk klient-loop eller at spillerbasen er vokset ud af tallet. Railway-loggen 10/9 kl. 10:12:24 UTC viste flere hundrede 429'ere paa fire millisekunder, fordelt paa mindst 8 rytter-id'er.

**Det loggen VISER:** rytterkortets endpoints var blandt de kald der blev AFVIST, og fan-outen paa 14-15 kald pr. rytterkort staar i koden.

**Det loggen IKKE viser, og som denne PR derfor ikke paastaar:** at fan-outen alene braendte budgettet. 8 rytterkort x 14 kald er ca. 112 requests, og graensen er 600/min. De loggede 429'ere er dem der blev afvist, dvs. budgettet var allerede brugt af noget andet i det vindue. Issuet skriver selv at det ikke kan afgoeres om burstet kom fra en spiller eller et test-/verify-script, fordi noeglen er `userOrIpKey` og bevidst ikke logges. Fan-outen skaeres her fordi den er maalbart spildt arbejde, ikke fordi kausaliteten er bevist.

**#5089 lukkes IKKE af denne PR.** Efter aendringen koster en profil stadig 8 kald, dvs. ca. 75 profil-visninger/min rammer graensen igen. Der er hverken concurrency-graense eller backoff i diffen. Udestaaende i issuet: punkt 1 (samle kortet i EET endpoint), punkt 2b (ingen backoff/concurrency-graense), punkt 3 (respektér `Retry-After`) og punkt 4 (giv op ved gentagne 401). Derfor `Refs`, ikke `Closes`.

**Rate-limit-konfigurationen er UROERT.** Ingen graense haevet, ingen `RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED`.

## Kortlaegning: hvad blev kaldt, og hvorfra

Alt herunder er laest i koden paa `origin/main` (4aebe1f1d) og verificeret med den nye maaletest.

### Per rytter (alle fra `frontend/src/pages/RiderStatsPage.jsx`, fyret i EEN effekt paa rytter-skift, linje 1425 foer PR'en)

| Endpoint | Loader | Linje foer | Forbruges af |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/riders/:id/history` | `loadHistory` | 1055 | KUN Historik-fanen (2036) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/interest` | `loadInterest` | 1078 | KUN Interesse-fanen (2026) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/view-count` | `loadVisits` | 985 | KUN Interesse-fanen (2031) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/watchlist-count` | `loadWatchlistCount` | 966 | KUN Interesse-fanen (2029) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/development` | `loadDevelopmentHistory` | 1120 | KUN Udvikling-fanen (2055) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/development-projection` | `loadDevelopmentProjection` | 1145 | KUN Udvikling-fanen (2061) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/value-trend` | `loadValueTrend` | 1164 | Hero (1850) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/level-correction-receipt` | `loadLevelCorrectionReceipt` | 1182 | Over fanerne (1952) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/bid-timeline` | `loadBidTimeline` | 1100 | Historik-fanen OG realtime-kanalens noegle (1425-1483) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/retirement-status` | `loadRetirementStatus` | 1002 | Hero-banner |
| `POST /api/riders/:id/view` | `loadRider` | 1378 | Besoegslogning (#963) |
| `GET /api/riders/:id/extend-quote` | `RiderManageActions.jsx:281` | 264 | Kontrakt-panelet, kun egne ryttere |
| `GET /api/pro/rider-history/:id` | `RiderAbilityHistoryPro.jsx:96` | 88 | Allerede fane-gatet (kun Udvikling) |

### Globale kald der blev gentaget pr. rytter

| Endpoint | Kaldested foer | Hvorfor globalt |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/deadline-day/status` | `RiderStatsPage.jsx:1386` + `TeamPage.jsx:1110` | Sæson-tilstand, ikke rytter-specifik |
| `GET /api/transfers` | `RiderStatsPage.jsx:302` (`TransferListButton`) | Hele den aabne transferliste; kun rytterens egen linje bruges |
| `GET /api/scouting/me` | `useScouting.js:73` + `useScoutingCentral.js:33` | Holdets scout-tilstand. `useScoutingCentral` mountes af `Layout` paa HVER side, saa profilen kostede TO kald |
| `POST /api/scouting/estimates` | `useScouting.js:114` | Se "Bevidst ikke aendret" nedenfor |

## Hvad er aendret

**Nyt: `frontend/src/lib/sharedRequestCache.js`** (+ `sharedRequestCache.test.js`, 7 node --test-cases)

In-flight-dedupe + kort TTL omkring en loader-funktion. Ingen React-context, ingen store, ingen abonnenter; komponenterne beholder deres egen `useState`. Kontrakt:

- fejl caches ALDRIG (noeglen ryddes, naeste kalder proever igen)
- TTL er kort med vilje (15-60 s) og daekker "samme klik-serie", ikke sessionen
- hver mutation invaliderer sin egen noegle. Listen er sat op mod ALLE skrivninger til `transfer_listings` i `backend/routes/api.js` (create, delete, patch, bulk-price, release-zombie-guard paa linje 1834), saa der ikke findes en skrive-vej uden invalidering:
  - `TransferListButton.submit/removeListing` (`RiderStatsPage.jsx`)
  - `TeamPage.RiderActionModal.listTransfer`
  - `TransfersPage.handleRemoveListing` / `handleUpdateListingPrice` / `handleBulkApply`
  - `RiderManageActions.confirmReleaseAction` (release lukker rytterens aabne listing server-side)
  - `useScouting.scoutLegacy/startTargetJob`, `useScoutingCentral.startTarget/startMission/cancelAssignment`
- TransfersPage-siderne og release rydder noeglen UANSET svar-status: bulk-price svarer 200 med delvise fejl i `failed[]`, og en overfloedig refetch koster ét kald
- `SIGNED_OUT` i `App.jsx` rydder hele cachen, saa naeste bruger paa samme enhed aldrig ser en TTL-kopi af den forriges holdtilstand
- ingen auth-viden i modulet (kalderen bygger loaderen), saa det kan unit-testes uden supabase-klienten

**`RiderStatsPage.jsx`:** mount-effekten er delt i to. Eager = det hero'en og de altid-synlige flader bruger. Fane-gatet = `history`, `interest`, `view-count`, `watchlist-count`, `development`, `development-projection`, hoejst een gang pr. (rytter, fane). Guarden nulstilles ved rytter-skift, ellers ville A -> B -> A vise B's historik under A's navn.

`bid-timeline` blev bevidst i den eager gruppe: den er ikke kun Historik-fanens tabel, den er ogsaa noeglen realtime-kanalen abonnerer paa (`auction_id` + `status`), og uden den holder hero'ens live-pris op med at opdatere under en auktion.

## Maaling foer/efter

`frontend/tests/e2e/5089-rider-card-request-count.spec.js` taeller faktiske HTTP-kald mod rytterkortets egne endpoints (app-skallens inbox/presence/forum/academy taelles ikke med; de har intet med #5089 at goere og ville goere ratchetten stoej-foelsom).

Foer-tallet er maalt paa den samme spec med `frontend/src/`-aendringerne stashed, ikke estimeret.

| Scenarie | Foer | Efter |
|---|---|---|
| Kold sideindlaesning af rival-profil (`/riders/rider-2`) | **15** | **8** |
| Klient-navigation fra `/team` ind i egen rytterprofil | **16** | **7** |

Efter-fordelingen paa den kolde profil: `scouting/me` 1 (var 2), `value-trend`, `level-correction-receipt`, `deadline-day/status`, `bid-timeline`, `retirement-status`, `POST view`, `POST scouting/estimates`.

Efter-fordelingen paa klient-navigationen: `value-trend`, `level-correction-receipt`, `bid-timeline`, `retirement-status`, `POST view`, `transfers`, `extend-quote`. `deadline-day/status` og `scouting/me` er 0, fordi holdsiden allerede har hentet dem.

Ratchetterne staar i specen og maa saenkes, aldrig haeves uden at issuet genaabnes.

## Bevidst IKKE aendret

- **`POST /api/scouting/estimates`.** Baandet er viewer-maskeret pr. (rytter, hold) og aendrer sig naar en scout-opgave modner. Et delt cache uden en invaliderings-kontrakt kunne vise et foraeldet baand, og det er praecis den klasse fejl `#1543`/`#2798` handler om. Kaldet er allerede batched til EET request pr. side-load. Begrundelsen staar ogsaa i specen.
- **`GET /api/riders/:id/extend-quote`.** Pre-hentningen i `RiderManageActions.jsx:264` er der med vilje (#3186): knappen er disabled indtil vi ved om rytteren staar paa forlaengelses-lo

author: cpoder
body:
Step 3a of the plan. **This does not delete Raft**, deliberately: the replacement is proven side by side first. Removing the working implementation before the new one has run is the mistake the audit was full of.

Off unless `VARPULIS_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` is set, so linking the feature changes no deployment's behaviour.

## The prize: fencing

Today no coordinator→worker command carries an epoch. A worker that is partitioned, declared dead, migrated away from, and then returns keeps writing to its sinks — duplicate alerts for as long as it lives, with no mechanism to stop it. There is no fix for that inside the Raft design as it stands; the CAS revision on a KV key *is* the fencing token.

Verified against a real `nats:2.10-alpine -js`, 16 tests, all passing:

```
zombie write refused with: fenced out of workers/w1: another writer advanced past revision 2
stale command refused with: command for workers/w1 carries fence 1, but this
  incarnation acquired at 3 — refusing a command addressed to a previous incarnation
a_partitioned_worker_self_fences_without_hearing_anything: guard closed after 231ms (ttl 150ms)
second acquire refused with: workers/w1 is already held by a live owner
releasing_and_reacquiring_an_id_never_recycles_a_fence: fences across four
  incarnations: [1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11]
the_reconciler_drives_a_migration_and_fences_the_source_at_cutover:
  source refused after cut-over with: fenced out of workers/w-src
```

That fence sequence is measured, not assumed: a delete leaves a tombstone at a *higher* sequence, so a re-registered id never recycles a fence. The whole scheme rests on it.

**Fail-before/pass-after**: replacing `renew`'s CAS precondition with an unconditional write — the Raft-log semantic — makes the zombie's write land at revision 4 and turns 2 of 16 tests red. The file also keeps the side-by-side control: `without_a_cas_precondition_the_zombie_write_lands` asserts that on the identical scenario the *current* `apply_command` accepts the zombie's metrics, so a future change to Raft's behaviour fails loudly.

## Losing the total order, argued rather than assumed

Four things get attributed to Raft's ordered log here. Only one was real:

| | provided? | after |
|---|---|---|
| per-entity linearizability | yes | a CAS'd key is a linearizable register |
| cross-entity atomicity | **no** — every command already writes one key, so an observer already sees torn state | unchanged |
| a single serialized writer | yes | **this is the real loss** |
| exactly-once side effects | **no** — the log records the decision; the HTTP POST is already at-least-once | unchanged |

The replacement is a level-triggered reconciliation loop: every write is a guarded read-modify-write, the migration record is made self-contained so no transition needs two keys to agree instantaneously, and each tick re-derives every decision from durable state rather than consuming change events. Leadership is a lease, but **advisory for scheduling only** — safety comes from the per-key CAS, not from `is_leader()`. That distinction is load-bearing.

Monotonicity of the phase machine is verified exhaustively over the reachable evidence space, not by example.

## Not reproduced, named precisely

1. **The migration executor is not rewired.** The decision machine and the fencing are built and proven standalone; `coordinator/rebalance.rs` still drives migrations imperatively. This is the biggest gap and nothing else matters until it closes.
2. **No linearizable multi-key read.** Sound only because every current guard is a predicate over a single key. A future guard needing two keys to agree instantaneously is not expressible here.
3. **No replayable log**, so no "replay the last N control-plane decisions" for debugging or audit.
4. No cluster membership API, no leader HTTP address, no Raft metrics equivalent.
5. Durability is delegated: a single-replica bucket on a single-node broker is a SPOF in a way a 3-node Raft group is not. `num_replicas` is exposed but untested at 3 — one broker was available.
6. **Connector credentials are refused, not relocated.** `ClusterConnector.params` is a bare map; credential-shaped params are rejected by default rather than written cleartext into a replicated on-disk bucket. #223 is the other half.

## Before Raft can be deleted

In dependency order: rewire the migration executor; **make the sinks consult `FenceGuard::is_valid()`** — until they do, the duplicate-alert hole is closed in the control plane and still open in the data plane, which is the one gap that still costs a user; stamp the fence on the real coordinator→worker path; land credential encryption; port leader forwarding, membership and metrics; then run a 3-replica bucket on a real NATS cluster and repeat the chaos suites. Raft must not be deleted on single-broker evidence.

## Verification

| configuration | result |
|---|---|
| KV suite, real broker | 16 passed |
| `varpulis-cluster` default | 290 passed |

author: izagood
body:
에이전트 팀 3단계의 첫 PR. 계획은 스레드에서 합의한 뒤 `docs/plans/2026-09-10-team-delegation.md` 에 적었다.

2단계까지의 팀장은 나눌 수는 있지만 **나눈 것이 돌아오지 않았다** — 팀원이 스레드에 답해도 팀장은 깨지 않는다(`thread_reply` 는 스레드 루트 작성자에게만 간다). 그래서 #726 의 프롬프트는 팀장에게 *"넘긴 답을 기다리지는 마라"* 고 적어야 했다. 이 PR 이 그 문장을 지운다.

## 어휘 — `message.delegate` (팀장만)

`to` 를 명시해 넘긴다. 새 도구인 이유 둘:

1. **서버가 "이것이 위임이다"를 알 방법이 없다.** 그것을 알려면 *"이 작성자가 지금 팀장으로 도는 중인가"* 를 알아야 하는데 그 사실은 러너의 턴에 있고 메시지에는 없다.
2. **`to` 가 명시되면 "본문 맨 앞에 이름을 둬야 턴이 뜬다" 함정이 사라진다** — 인용·코드 블록 안이든 문장 가운데든 결과가 같다.

`ask`(043)로 대신할 수 없다(선택지 2~5개). 다만 **구조는 같다**: 의무를 남기는 말이고 상대가 답하면 낸 쪽이 깬다.

## 왜 표인가

`ask` 는 답이 하나라 `meta.ask.answeredWith` 한 자리로 끝났고 `where answeredWith is null` 이 경합을 걸렀다. 위임은 상대가 **N 명**이라 jsonb 배열에 담으면 둘이 동시에 답할 때 lost update 가 난다 → **한 명당 한 행**(`team_delegation_item`).

## 무엇이 의무를 닫는가

| 무엇 | 결말 |
|---|---|
| 팀원의 답(`countsAsReply`) | `done` |
| 팀원의 `fail` | `failed` |
| 러너가 3회 소진·사용량 한도·세션 충돌 | `failed` — 러너가 **이미** `message.fail` 을 올린다 |
| 기한 경과 | `timeout` |

`progress`·`wake` 는 닫지 않는다(#687 의 `countsAsReply` 를 그대로 쓴다) — 진행 한 줄로 닫히면 팀장이 결과 없이 깨어난다. **하네스 실패가 별도 배선 없이 풀리는 것**이 이 표의 값어치다.

## 정확히 한 번 깨운다

팀원 둘이 동시에 답하면 **둘 다 "내가 마지막"으로 볼 수 있다.** 위임 행을 `for update` 로 잡아 닫힘을 직렬화하고 `notified_at is null` 로 기한 스위퍼와의 경합을 한 번 더 거른다(043 이 `answeredWith is null` 로 한 것과 같은 모양).

**부분 취합은 하지 않는다** — 하나 닫힐 때마다 깨우면 스케줄러가 같은 스레드에 턴 하나만 돌리므로 팀장 턴이 순차로 여러 번 돌아 최종 답을 여러 번 쓴다.

## 기한 10분

팀원이 죽으면 아무 신호도 오지 않을 수 있다. 그때 팀장은 기다리는 것이 아니라 **없다**(위임하고 턴이 끝나면 프로세스가 죽는다) — 되살리는 길은 예약된 시각 하나다.

`agent_wake`(040)를 쓰지 않았다: 그 sweep 은 `reason='wake'` 를 만드는데 기한이 지난 팀장에게 필요한 것은 **결말 목록**이고, 사유를 뭉치면 러너가 그 목록을 프롬프트에 못 싣는다(043 이 `wake` 를 재사용하지 않은 자리와 같은 판단). sweeper **패턴**은 그대로 쓴다.

**기한이 지나면 의무를 닫는다** — 열어 두면 늦게 온 답이 이미 끝난 라운드를 다시 깨우고, 사람에게 넘긴 일이 되살아난다.

## 층 0 · 라운드 3

- 러너가 안 붙은 팀원에는 **의무를 만들지 않는다**(`unreachable` 로 돌려준다). 전원 불가면 **메시지조차 만들지 않는다** — 위임 메시지만 남으면 사람은 넘어간 줄 알고 기다린다. 판정은 #757 이 쓴 `mcp/presence.ts` 그대로다.
- **`MENTION_CHAIN_LIMIT` 은 이 왕복을 막지 못한다**(실측): `mentionDepthFor` 는 *나를 부른 메시지가 없으면 0* 을 주고, 돌아오는 길은 멘션이 아니라 깨움이다 → 깨어난 팀장은 깊이 0 에서 다시 시작한다. 그래서 라운드를 따로 세되 **저장하지 않고** *"사람의 마지막 발화 이후"* 로 센다(사람이 한마디 하면 리셋된다).

## 실측으로 잡은 결함 — 같은 팀원이 두 번 불렸다

첫 시험이 빨갛게 나왔다. 팀장이 본문에 `@done1 은 서버, @dtwo 는 화면` 처럼 이름을 적는 것이 **자연스럽고**, 그러면 멘션 스캔이 만든 `mention` 위에 `team_delegated` 가 더해져 한 팀원이 같은 메시지로 두 번 불린다 — 그 팀원의 턴이 순차로 두 번 돌고 두 번째는 위임인 줄 모르는 평범한 턴이다.

그래서 더하지 않고 **바꿔 단다**(`mention` → `team_delegated`). 같은 메시지에 대한 두 사실 중 위임이 더 구체적이다.

## 결말 프롬프트

팀원마다 `끝남` / `실패 — 그 일은 아직 남아 있다` / `무응답 — 기한이 지났다`. 끝나지 않은 것이 있으면 **셋 중 하나**를 준다(직접 / 다시 넘긴다 / `message.fail(retryable: true)` 로 사람에게), **남은 라운드와 함께**. 0 이면 *"다시 넘길 수 없다"* 를 명시한다 — 숫자만으로는 모델이 그 결론에 이르지 않는다.

기한만으로 깨어난 턴에는 **새 메시지가 없다.** 그래서 이 블록은 `wake` 처럼 델타를 대신할 수 있어야 하고, 빈 프롬프트 가드가 이 값을 함께 본다 — 아니면 러너가 하네스를 돌리지 않고 커서만 전진시켜 팀장이 깨어난 것이 흔적 없이 사라진다(040 이 `wake` 를 만든 함정).

## 검증

- **서버 시험 7개** — 부름·의무 생성 / **도달 불가는 의무 없음**(전원 불가면 메시지도 없음) / 팀장만·팀원만·자기 제외 / **미결 0에서 한 번만** / 진행은 안 닫고 실패는 `failed` / **기한 → 무응답, 늦은 답으로는 안 깨움** / **라운드 상한 + 사람 발화로 리셋**. MCP 클라이언트로 실제 도구를 부르고, presence 는 **MCP 로 붙은 것 자체가 신호**라 실제 배선을 그대로 쓴다
- **러너 시험 6개** — 결말이 글자로 온다 / **기한만으로 깨어난 턴도 프롬프트가 비지 않는다** / 세 갈래와 남은 횟수 / 0 이면 못 넘긴다 / 전부 끝나면 취합 지시 / 팀원 보고가 함께 실린다
- `packages/server` 1,173 통과 / 3 실패(avcs 허브가 필요한 `proposals`·`collabRoutes` — 이 diff 가 건드리지 않는 경로), `packages/desktop` **2,801 통과**, `packages/shared` 123 통과, `packages/agent` 708 통과 / 4 실패(`turn.ts`·자격증명 경로의 환경 의존)
- `tsc -p .` 다섯 패키지 다 깨끗. `Record<InboxEntry['reason'], …>` 두 표가 새 사유 둘을 빠뜨린 것을 컴파일에서 잡아 줬다
- **`channelDelete` 회귀선이 실제로 잡았다**: `SET NULL` 참조를 "처리 안 된 것"으로 보고 빨개졌다. 그 판정을 넓혔다 — `SET NULL` 은 삭제를 터뜨리지 않고(열이 null 이 될 뿐), 그 행이 남지 않는 것은 부모의 cascade 가 답한다

## 다음

- **3-2**: 팀원 프롬프트 강등 → `agentExchange.addressesHuman` 이 그 구간을 접는다(접힘 규칙은 이미 있다)
- **3-3**: `waitChain` 위임 마디 + 팀 단위 중단(중단이 의무를 `취소` 로 닫는 것도 그 PR 이다)

author: fahad0208
body:
## Summary
- Follows up on the discussion around `SubscriptionUsageCurrent`: the requirement was to let a direct-Mongo reader (no API access) see a subscription's entitlement keys and the plan's feature bag without an API call.
- `SubscriptionUsageCurrent` is keyed per `(subscription, meter, period)`, so it can't carry this alone: a plan with no metered entitlement has no row at all, and a plan that does would need every entitlement duplicated onto every meter's row just to make them discoverable.
- Adds a sibling projection, `SubscriptionEntitlementsCurrent` — one row per subscription, carrying the plan's entitlement keys, limit kinds, capped limits, the meter key each count entitlement draws down, and the plan's `FeaturesJson` bag verbatim.
- Published from inside `UsageProjectionPublisher.RefreshAsync`, the same method that already keeps the usage projection current, so it rides every existing trigger (activation, cancellation, plan change, the repair sweep, the backfill) with **no new call sites** — including the free/card-free-trial path fixed in #491. Publish is unconditional on the subscription having any metered window at all, so a plan with only boolean entitlements still gets a row. Best-effort: a publish failure here is logged and does not fail the caller.
- New collection `SubscriptionEntitlementsCurrent`, one index (`OrganizationId`, `SubscriptionId`). Ordered by `SubscriptionVersion` alone — unlike the usage projection there is only one version track here, since nothing metered ever moves this document.
- This document is not an authority for a metered entitlement's balance — that stays on `SubscriptionUsageCurrent` / the enforcement path. It only answers "what are the terms."

## Test plan
- [x] Added `Refreshing_publishes_the_plans_entitlements_and_features` and `A_subscription_with_no_meters_still_gets_its_entitlements_published` to `UsageProjectionPublisherTests`

author: kristofferremback
body: ## Why The Deploy Cloudflare run for `6afc7c3`/`df3b3c4`/`1162774` ([34470436700](https://github.com/threahq/threa/actions/runs/34470436700)) failed outright: ``` [retain-assets] revived 20718 old chunk(s), pruned 93, 21127 retained ✘ [ERROR] Error: Pages only supports up to 20,000 files in a deployment for your current plan. ``` Cross-deploy chunk retention (#2098) bounded the store by age only — 14 days. At ~400 chunks per build and many deploys a day, that is not a bound at all; the store grew past the Pages ceiling and the deploy stopped. The rerun "succeeded" only because the retained-assets cache came back empty (`revived 0, pruned 0, 409 retained`), so production currently has no retention at all and old tabs are back to `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module` until the store refills. That is the second reason to land a real bound now rather than let it refill toward the same wall. ## Changes - **Cap the store at 10,000 files**, half the Pages budget, evicting oldest-first by mtime. A file in the current build is never evicted, so a build larger than the ceiling still deploys whole. - **Never retain `*.map`**, and prune any a previous run stored. The deploy strips maps before upload, so retaining them only consumed the budget. `maxRetained` is injectable the same way `retentionMs` already was, so the caps are exercised at small numbers rather than by writing 10,000 files. ## Verification `apps/frontend/scripts/retain-assets.test.ts` — 9 passing, 3 new: the ceiling evicts oldest-first, the current build survives a ceiling smaller than itself, and maps are neither stored nor revived. ## Residual risk The ceiling is a count, not a byte budget; a build whose own asset count approaches 10,000 would leave little room for history (today's is ~400). The failure mode is degraded retention, not a failed deploy — the current build is never evicted. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01Mn5zvJYpLaxhtLd7iwvB3Z --- Need help on this PR? author: bgzstephen
body:
## Summary

First of five stacked PRs for ENT-352. Lets the Microsoft Teams node create online meetings with the Service Principal (app-only) credential.

- Adds an **Organizer** field, shown only for the Service Principal credential. Pick a user from the list or enter an ID. Meetings are created on that user's behalf.
- Under this credential the Operation dropdown only lists operations that work app-only. This PR enables **Create**. The next four PRs enable Get, Create or Get, Delete, and Update.
- Without a Teams application access policy, Graph returns a bare 403. The node now says what to grant and which PowerShell commands to run.
- The user picker's 403 now says it needs `User.Read.All`.

No node version bump: this path was hidden before, so no existing workflow used it. Docs follow in n8n-docs after release.

## How to test

1. Use a Service Principal credential whose app has `OnlineMeetings.ReadWrite.All` (plus `User.Read.All` for the picker), and grant it an application access policy for a test user with `New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy` and `Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy`.
2. Teams node, Service Principal credential, Online Meeting, Create, with that user as Organizer. You get a join URL back.
3. Try a user without the policy. The error names the permission and the commands.
4. Switch to an OAuth2 credential. Nothing changes.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ENT-352

## Review / Merge checklist

author: velvetmonkey
body:
This draft declares, rather than broadens, the resource-policy boundary.

`ResourceLimits` is owned by `LimitedEventLog`, explicit
`EventLog::from_wire_bytes_for_with_limits` loading, and `DurableReplica` mutation
and restart. Plain `EventLog` mutation and decoding, plus the documented in-memory
`LocalReplica`, retain legacy unconfigured semantics. They do not promise a
history bound. The compatibility forms of the policy-owning APIs use development
placeholders, not operator-approved ceilings.

For a bounded consumer, select a policy-owning API before accepting work. A
`ResourceLimit` refusal retains the unprocessed history; export or reopen with an
operator policy that admits the retained history before migrating it. Tightening a
policy controls future work and does not erase retained bytes.

The earlier commit subject's "persisted and durable boundaries" is scoped to those
named APIs; this PR does not claim global `EventLog` or `LocalReplica` enforcement.
No persisted format or dependency changes.

Validation is run on the rebased branch by the safemesh CI gate.

## Summary
Closes #126 ( bounty).

This PR implements automatic note closing when a changeset is closed (or auto-closed due to inactivity), following the specification in #126:

1. **Tag Parsing**:
   - Parses the `closes:note` changeset tag for numeric IDs separated by `;`.
   - Skips empty, non-numeric, or invalid tokens safely.

4. **Testing & Quality**:

author: tsekaluk
body:
## What the probe found

```
app_user              rolcanlogin=true   rolbypassrls=false   ← the RLS-subject role
connection role       pscale_api_*       rolbypassrls=true
membership chain      pscale_api_* → postgres → app_user      ← present
SET ROLE app_user     permission denied
```

The role exists and the chain exists. PostgreSQL 16 stopped letting membership alone convey `SET ROLE`, so the grant has to be direct and `WITH SET TRUE`.

## Why this is not an escalation

`app_user` has `rolbypassrls = false`; the connection role has it **true**. Today every wallet read runs as the bypassing role — outside RLS entirely. The grant is what lets `getTenantDb()` step *down* into the restricted role. Leaving it ungranted is the weaker state, not the safer one.

## Safety

Dry run by default — prints the statement and changes nothing unless `confirm` is exactly `GRANT`. Verifies by assuming the role afterwards, so a grant that did not take fails the job instead of reporting success.

Fixes the 500 on `/v1/limits`.

## Problema

Não existia nenhum teste no repositório nem workflow de CI — lint, checagem de tipos e build só rodavam quando alguém executava manualmente. Nada impedia um erro de passar despercebido até chegar em produção.

author: xuchunmei000
body:
## Why

ANOLISA 1.4 releases on 2026-09-10 with six components updated and three breaking compatibility changes, but the repository CHANGELOG still stops at 1.3. Without a 1.4 entry, users have no in-repo reference for the shipped component versions, or the migration steps required by the Tokenless Protocol v2 removal — they would have to reconstruct that from per-component changelogs.

## What changed

Add the `[1.4] - 2026-09-10` entry to both `CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG_zh.md`, derived from the Agentic OS release note:

- **Component Versions**: full ten-component table (`cosh-ng` 0.24.1, `agent-sec-core` 0.12.0, `agentsight` 0.12.1, `tokenless` 0.8.1, `anolisa` 0.3.11, `agent-memory` 0.2.7, plus the four unchanged components).
- **Highlights / Updated**: one entry per updated component, each stating the version and the user-visible outcome.
- **Compatibility**: Tokenless Protocol v2 lifecycle-only requests, AgentSight wall-clock timestamp calibration, and the `anolisa` `kind = "config"` state record format, each with its migration or downgrade note.

Two deliberate choices: the version table keeps all ten components (matching the 1.3 and earlier entries as a complete stack manifest) rather than listing only the changed ones, with unchanged components called out in a note; and the release date and image identifier are preserved verbatim from the source release note rather than derived from commit dates.

## Related issue

`no-issue: release documentation for an already-decided 1.4 release; no behavior change`

## User / Agent impact

No code, CLI, or runtime behavior change. Users reading the repository root now find the 1.4 version manifest and the three compatibility notes they need before upgrading; the breaking changes themselves were introduced by the component PRs, this only documents them.

## Risk and compatibility

- [ ] Public CLI, API, configuration, or documented behavior changed
- [ ] Privileged or security-sensitive behavior changed
- [ ] Cross-component contract changed
- [ ] Migration or rollback guidance is needed

Low risk — documentation only, no shipped artifact is affected. The migration guidance in the Compatibility section describes changes already landed in the component PRs; this PR does not introduce them.

## Validation

- `./scripts/docs-lint.sh` — documentation lint per `specs/documentation-standard.md`
- `python3 scripts/docs-link-check.py` — no broken links in the new entry
- Manual: EN/ZH entries checked for section parity and identical version numbers; each listed version cross-checked against the corresponding component's `CHANGELOG.md`; heading format verified against the existing 1.3 entry (Keep a Changelog + SemVer).

## Documentation and rollback

Documentation is the entire change: `CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG_zh.md` gain the 1.4 entry; no user-guide or component docs touched. Rollback is a plain `git revert c6772eb` — nothing depends on this content at build or runtime.

body:
## Summary

**UI/UX polish** on `JeetOS.html` — no business logic touched, verified with `node --check` on the extracted script before/after every change.

- Tap/press feedback (scale) on every button, plus a shared `.jos-tap` class for the check-list rows and card headers that use `<div onClick>` instead of `<button>`
- Check-list items and collapsible cards are now keyboard-accessible: `role`, `tabIndex`, Enter/Space handling, `aria-expanded`/`aria-checked`/`aria-current`
- `:focus-visible` outlines added app-wide (there were none before), with `!important` so it isn't silently defeated by the many inline `outline:"none"` inputs
- Card accordion now animates its height open/close (CSS grid `fr`-unit technique) instead of popping instantly
- Fade-in transition when switching tabs and when a card expands
- Scroll-fade mask on the crowded 10-tab bottom nav so it visually reads as scrollable
- Nicer toast entrance animation (slide + fade) with a checkmark
- Food search shows a "no matches" empty state instead of a silently blank list
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`
- Added `env(safe-area-inset-top)` padding to `body` — the app is a home-screen PWA (`viewport-fit=cover`, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable`) but had no top safe-area padding, so content could sit under the iOS notch/status bar

**Backend addition** — the client was calling Groq, Gemini, and Anthropic directly from the browser with API keys hardcoded in the page source (visible to anyone who views source on the live site). There was also a broken, misplaced `api ai.js` file at the repo root (Vercel only picks up functions under `api/` — this one never actually served anything) that also had hardcoded keys.

- Added `api/ai.js`: a proper Vercel serverless function that proxies to Claude / Groq / Gemini using **server-side env vars** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`), matching the existing `api/telegram-*.js` functions' conventions. It tries the requested provider first and falls through to the others, so the app keeps working with whichever key(s) are actually configured.
- Removed the broken root-level `api ai.js` and its hardcoded keys.
- Rewired the client's `ai()` / `groq()` / `gemini()` helpers to call our own `/api/ai` instead of hitting provider APIs directly — no keys ship to the browser anymore. Same call signatures, so every existing caller (coach chat, daily debrief) is unaffected.
- Bonus fix: this also fixes the previously-broken `ai()` (daily debrief / legacy coach chat), which was calling Anthropic directly with **no API key at all** and always failed.

### ⚠️ Action needed before/after merging
The Groq and Gemini keys that were committed in git history are compromised (they're in this repo's history regardless of this PR) and should be **rotated**. In Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables, set `GROQ_API_KEY` (and optionally `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY`) to **new** keys, then redeploy. The Supabase anon key already in `JeetOS.html` was left as-is since Supabase's anon/publishable key is designed to be public and relies on Row Level Security policies server-side — worth double-checking those policies are actually restrictive if you haven't already.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --check` on the extracted inline script and on `api/ai.js` after each change (no build step exists for this project)
- [x] Manual diff review of every edit for correct JSX-less `React.createElement` nesting/parens
- [x] Repo-wide grep for leaked key patterns — none remain in tracked files
- [ ] Manual click-through in a mobile browser (not performed in this session — no running instance/browser test was done here)
- [ ] Live verification that `/api/ai` responds correctly once env vars are set in Vercel (can't be tested without deployment access)

body:
Pins every non-GitHub-owned action in this repo to a full-length commit SHA, keeping the version tag as a trailing comment.

A tag is a moving pointer — whoever controls the upstream repo (or compromises that maintainer's account) can repoint it and change what executes here. These steps run with `contents: write` or cloud credentials in scope, so that matters.

No version changes: each SHA is the exact commit the pinned tag resolved to today. Part of a sweep across the org so `sha_pinning_required` can be turned on afterwards.

The mode selects FilC-compatible compiler and linker settings, keeps pointer metadata intact in the affected execution paths, and substitutes portable implementations where FilC does not yet support a Linux API or assembly path.

The change also updates bundled dependency revisions with their FilC compatibility patches. The build is disabled by default and all source adaptations are guarded by `__FILC__`, `ENABLE_FILC`, or an existing portable-code switch enabled only for FilC.

The x86 build uses a source-built FilC compiler with large-code-model support. It links a 9.04 GB non-PIE ClickHouse executable with 1,278,804 ELF sections. The server answers HTTP and native-protocol queries, completes zstd-compressed system-log writes and merges, and passes focused modulo, array, cardinality-estimator, and string-grouping queries without a FilC safety diagnostic. A one-worker run over all 14,675 stateless functional tests is in progress; WebAssembly tests are skipped because that optional feature is disabled in the reduced FilC configuration.

author: joelstoddard
body:
## What
- Five new Flux layers: `cluster-secrets`, `cert-manager`, `cert-manager-issuers`,
  `traefik`, `traefik-middlewares`
- One wildcard `Certificate` served to every route via `TLSStore/default`, issued
  over Cloudflare DNS-01; staging and production `ClusterIssuer`s
- Shared `default-headers` and `basic-auth` middlewares, plus a `ServersTransport`
  for a future Proxmox route's self-signed certificate
- Pi-hole wildcards the root domain at Traefik, with a passthrough per
  publicly-hosted name (OpenTofu)
- The Longhorn UI moves behind Traefik, behind basic auth
- `make -C kubernetes lint` now fails on a plaintext `*.sops.yaml`
- `docs/design/ingress-tls.md`, plus README, CLAUDE.md and TODO updates

## Why
Every cluster service should be reachable at `https://<name>.<domain>` with a
publicly-trusted certificate and no per-service TLS configuration. Exposure is
LAN and tailnet only, which forces DNS-01 — that is what makes internal-only
names certifiable at all. A single wildcard also keeps individual service names
out of the public Certificate Transparency logs.

## How
- **Variable substitution, not SOPS-per-file.** Traefik's pinned LoadBalancer IP
  lives in Helm values, which are a `configMapGenerator` input that SOPS cannot
  encrypt. Flux `postBuild` substitution covers that and keeps every future
  app's ingress readable in a diff.
- **`dns01RecursiveNameserversOnly` is load-bearing.** Pi-hole becomes
  authoritative for the domain and answers NODATA for TXT instead of forwarding,
  so the DNS-01 self-check would otherwise never see its own record.
- **Two CRD-ordering splits.** `cert-manager`/`cert-manager-issuers` and
  `traefik`/`traefik-middlewares` are separate layers because a CR cannot be
  applied in the same pass that installs its CRD.
- **Staging issuer first.** The flip to production is a deliberate one-line
  follow-up, gated on confirming the chain live.
- **bcrypt is mandatory** for htpasswd hashes: substitution runs after SOPS
  decryption, and envsubst would destroy an `$apr1$` hash.

### Reviewer notes
- Nothing here has been reconciled — Flux tracks `main`, so this runs on merge.
  Status markers use `[-]`, and the design doc claims nothing as observed.
- Tailnet reach needs a split-DNS nameserver for the domain in the tailnet
  policy; that is outside this repo and tracked in TODO.md.
- The Proxmox routing itself (Service/EndpointSlice/IngressRoute) is a follow-up
  needing the node addresses.

author: scottf
body:
`batch-publish`, `counters` and `schedule-message` were shipping their example classes inside the main published artifact. Examples are meant to compile, so they stay correct, but not to be carried into a jar somebody puts in production, where they are only bloat.

### Cause

Each project has two separate things:

```groovy
tasks.register('bundle', Bundle) {
    from sourceSets.main.output
    exclude("io/synadia/examples/**")
}

jar {
    bundle { bnd(...) }
    exclude("io/synadia/examples/**")
}
```

`tasks.register('bundle', Bundle)` registers an additional task. The published artifact comes from the `jar` task by way of `from components.java`, so only the exclude inside `jar{}` affects what ships. These three had it in the registered task but not in `jar{}`. The six other bundle-publishing projects already had both.

### Measured

Example classes in the main published jar, before and after:

| project | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| batch-publish | 9 | 0 |
| counters | 1 | 0 |
| schedule-message | 21 | 0 |
| chaos-runner, direct-batch, encoded-kv, js-publish-extensions, request-many, retrier | 0 | 0 |

The `examples` classifier jar still carries them — batch-publish 4, counters 1, schedule-message 21 — which is the artifact intended to.

Examples still compile in all three; `srcDirs = ['src/main/java','src/examples/java']` is unchanged. No source, dependency or publishing coordinate changes. One line per project.

author: powange
body:
## Pourquoi

`/check-error-logs` a remonté une **400 sur `GET /api/users/search`** en production, émise depuis `/editions/22/gestion/stock/6` : « Données invalides (emailExact: Invalid email address) ».

L'appel vient du sélecteur de responsable d'emprunt, qui vérifie pourtant l'adresse avant d'appeler — mais avec une expression plus permissive que celle du serveur. L'interface jugeait la saisie bonne, l'émettait, et le serveur la refusait. L'utilisateur voyait un résultat vide ; le journal gardait une 400.

## Ce qui a été prouvé plutôt qu'affirmé

La divergence est vérifiée, pas supposée. Six formes passent l'expression maison et sont refusées par `zod` :

```
a@b..com          jean@exemple.fr.       jean..dupont@exemple.fr
jean@-exemple.fr  jean@exemple..fr       a@b.c
```

Ce que je ne peux pas prouver, c'est que c'est exactement ce qui a été tapé ce jour-là — je ne dispose pas de la saisie. La divergence, elle, est un fait, et elle produit précisément cette erreur.

## Ce que ça change

La même expression `/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/` était **recopiée dix-sept fois dans dix fichiers**, y compris côté serveur dans le filtrage des adresses en copie cachée. Elles sont remplacées par `shared/utils/adresse-email`, sur le modèle exact de `regles-mot-de-passe` — même problème, même remède : le schéma partagé **est** celui que le point d'API applique, il n'y a plus deux règles à faire coïncider.

Les espaces qui entourent la saisie ne comptent plus. C'était déjà l'intention du serveur, qui élaguait l'adresse *après* l'avoir validée — donc trop tard pour une adresse collée depuis un message avec un espace de trop.

## Vérifications

Quatorze tests, dont un par forme divergente. Une sonde de mutation — remettre l'ancienne expression dans le schéma partagé — en fait tomber sept : la règle est tenue par les tests, et non par hasard.

Suites complètes vertes : 1719 tests unitaires, 2349 tests Nuxt. Porte de typage verte ; la dette du dépôt recule d'une erreur et n'en gagne aucune.

Au passage, une erreur de typage **préexistante** dans `apply.vue` bloquait la porte, qui hérite de la dette des fichiers touchés. La condition d'affichage porte désormais sur la date limite elle-même, ce que le calcul supposait déjà.

## Ce qui reste ouvert

Rien de ce lot n'a été vu à l'écran. L'effet visible est d'ailleurs nul pour l'utilisateur : l'appel était déjà dans un `catch` rendant une liste vide. Le gain est un journal d'erreurs qui ne signale plus que de vrais problèmes, et une règle unique là où il y en avait deux.

author: mertso13
body:
## What this adds

   A star toggle for media items, and a filter to show only starred items.

   - Each grid card gets a star button.
   - The lightbox action bar gets a star button.
   - The toolbar gets a star toggle that filters the grid to starred items.

   The star filter combines with the kind buttons, the subfolder picker, and search. All active filters apply together.

   ## Storage

   Stars live server side in `sidebar_gallery_favorites.json`, next to `sidebar_gallery_config.json` and `sidebar_gallery_settings.json`. The file is gitignored, so it never ships to other users and a fresh install starts with no stars. Every browser pointed at the instance sees the same set.

   | Method | Path | Purpose |
   |---|---|---|
   | GET | `/sidebar_gallery/favorites` | Returns the starred relpaths for one root |
   | POST | `/sidebar_gallery/favorites` | Stars or unstars one file |

   The `/poll` payload now includes `favorites_version`, so an open tab picks up a change made in another tab.

   Writes use a temp file and `os.replace`, so a crash cannot leave a half written file. A lock serializes the read-modify-write, so two tabs cannot lose each other's change. The file is rewritten only when the stored state actually changes.

   The client toggles optimistically and reverts on failure, so the button never shows a state the server rejected.

   ## Known limits

   - Identity is the `(root_id, relpath)` pair. Renaming or moving a file drops its star.
   - Deleting a starred file leaves an entry in the JSON file. The entry is inert, because the grid only renders items present in the index. Nothing prunes these entries yet.
   - The file sits in the extension folder, next to `sidebar_gallery_config.json` and `sidebar_gallery_settings.json`. It uses the same location as those two files, so it inherits the same behavior on update. An in-place update keeps the stars. An update that deletes and recreates the folder loses them, along with the config and settings.

   ## What I tested

   Manual testing in the browser, on 370 indexed images (365 jpg, 5 png):

   - Star and unstar from a grid card
   - Star and unstar from the lightbox
   - The starred-only filter, combined with kind buttons, subfolders, and search
   - The empty state when nothing is starred
   - Stars persist across a browser reload

   Automated checks, run locally:

   - Python store: missing file, malformed JSON, non-dict document, add, remove, repeat toggle without a rewrite, and 8 threads x 40 concurrent toggles with no lost writes and no leftover temp file
   - Client store: cache reuse, toggle, subscriber notification, revert after a failed request in both directions, and the version signal

   ## What I did not test

   Audio and video were never tested. My test library contains no audio or video files, so those paths never ran.

   The star code has no branch per media kind. Images, audio, and video all go through the same card and lightbox code. I think the risk is low, but I would rather leave it visible than claim coverage I do not have.

   Two points worth checking with real audio and video files:

   1. The badge stays readable next to the star. Video and audio both render their extension badge in the top right, which is why the star is top left.
   2. The star button does not interfere with the play icon overlay on video cards.

   ## Star position

   The star sits at the top left, not the top right. The extension badge for video and audio occupies the top right, so a star there would overlap it. If you prefer the star on the right, the badge needs to move first.

   ## Tests in the repo

   I did not add a test suite. The repo has none, and the only CI workflow publishes to the registry. The checks above ran locally.

author: antonellof
body:
## What was wrong

`body_quant`'s doc comment used `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-IQ4_XS.gguf` to
teach that a filename is not a quantization, and got the example
backwards:

> `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-IQ4_XS.gguf` contains no IQ4_XS tensors at all
> -- 96 of its per-layer weights are `IQ4_NL`

Counted from the file's own GGUF header:

| | count |
|---|---|
| IQ4_XS | **96** |
| Q5_K (every `attn_v`) | 16 |
| Q6_K (`token_embd`, tied head) | 1 |
| F32 norms | 34 |
| **IQ4_NL** | **0** |

The count was right and the type inverted.

## Why it mattered

It is inverted across the one line that decides a verdict.
`llama_dots_this_against_q8k` lists `IQ4XS` and does **not** list
`IQ4NL`, because ggml declares `vec_dot_type = Q8_K` for IQ4_XS and
`Q8_0` for IQ4_NL. So the comment described a file whose `DRIFT` would
be *unexplained*, while the real file's `DRIFT` is the expected §10
case.

That is how this was found. I ran `ferrox parity` on the file, got
`DRIFT`, isolated it with `FERROX_METAL=0` (still `DRIFT`), and went to
the comment to confirm the cause — where the comment said the file was
IQ4_NL-bodied, i.e. that it should have matched. Checking the claim
against the file gives the opposite answer, which destroys the
authority of the rule it was illustrating.

## No behaviour change

`body_quant` already returned `IQ4_XS` for that file and the verdict was
already correct. The comment was the whole defect. The rule it teaches
is kept, with better evidence: the same file carries **three**
quantizations, so the name gets the body right and says nothing about
the other 17 quantized tensors.

## The test the old ones could not be

`the_q8k_predicate_uses_the_dtype_debug_spelling` walks whatever
`Q8K_DOTTED` and `Q8_0_DOTTED` contain, so moving `IQ4NL` from one list
to the other keeps every assertion green while inverting what the tool
says about a real checkpoint. `iq4_xs_is_q8k_dotted_and_iq4_nl_is_not`
pins the two neighbours to their ggml facts directly.

Sabotaged with the mutation grep-confirmed in the file: removing
`"IQ4XS"` from the `matches!` turns it red (along with two others).

## README

Gains the same warning. The sentence "on `Q8_0` and `IQ4_NL` ferrox's
logits match llama.cpp's" sits in a repo whose only IQ4-family
checkpoint is IQ4_XS, so the obvious thing to try returns `DRIFT` and
reads as the docs lying.

## One thing I did not change, for you to decide

`CLAUDE.md` line 51 carries the same sentence ("MATCHES on
Q8_0/IQ4_NL"). I left it alone rather than edit the repo's constitution
mid-task. Worth knowing: **no checkpoint in `models/` has an IQ4_NL
body** — I censused all 19 — so the IQ4_NL half of that claim is not
reproducible on this machine. It is theoretically sound (IQ4_NL really
is Q8_0-dotted), so I have not called it wrong; it is unevidenced
locally.

`cargo test --workspace` green, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`
clean, `cargo fmt --all`.

body: **Does this PR address a related issue?** Closes #1341 and closes #1342 (the two remaining storyboard screens of the add-location redesign #1134, paired per the issues' own notes). **A description of the changes proposed in the pull request** The form becomes two steps inside the in-map panel, and the success screen stops over-promising. - **Review step (#1341):** the submit button becomes "Review & submit"; a "Here's what will be published" summary shows exactly the fields going out (only the filled ones), with the identity line ("Submitted by" account name or Anonymous) — honest framing per the design deck. One `onsubmit` handler branches on the step; native validation still guards the transition, and the two rules it can't express (category "Other" text, at least one payment method) run before the switch. - **The captcha moves to the review step** and is fetched on first entry — the edit fields lose their `disabled={!captchaSecret}` gate entirely, so people can type immediately instead of waiting on the captcha fetch, and abandoners cost no fetches. The focus-when-captcha-unlocks workaround dies with the gate. - **Edit fields stay mounted, CSS-hidden, during review** — most are uncontrolled inputs read through element refs, so unmounting would wipe them. "Edit details" round-trips losslessly. - **The reviewed snapshot is what gets submitted**, pin coords included: the desktop map stays pannable beside the panel, so coords are frozen at review entry — a pin nudged mid-review can't silently diverge from the summary. The address-suggestion effect pauses during review for the same reason (a lookup landing then could flip the hidden address field to required-but-empty and block the confirm invisibly) and re-runs on return to edit. - **Honest success track (#1342):** the "we'll add it ASAP" one-liner is replaced by the truthful three steps — Submitted ✓ (received just now) → Volunteer review (typically 1–2 days, sometimes longer) → Live on the map (BTC Map and OpenStreetMap). No notification promises, since nothing emails submitters today. The #1334 account nudge stays. - New analytics events `add_place_review_enter` and `add_place_submit_success`, completing the funnel around the existing `add_place_confirm`. - 15 new i18n keys and `formSuccessText` retired, across all 9 locales (registers matched: du/tú/je informal, vous/Вы formal). Key parity with `en.json` verified; the 558 pre-existing divergences are untouched. - New hermetic e2e spec `add-location-review.spec.ts`: fields usable with no captcha stub, review summary contents, lossless edit round-trip, and a stubbed submit asserting the posted payload (reviewed fields + frozen coords + captcha answer) landing on the success track. All existing add-location/map specs pass unchanged — none of them submitted the form (the captcha gate made that untestable, fittingly). **Screenshots** (attached below: desktop + mobile review step, desktop + mobile success track) **Additional context** The captcha keeps living on the website's own `/captcha` server route (a server-secret flow, per the accounts-and-sessions guidance). Merge note: #1366 (OSM fork card) touches neighboring lines in `AddPlaceFormPanel`/`analytics.ts`/locales — whichever lands second gets a trivial rebase. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01NjZ7qPmjDm85vTn9MbS2uS ![desktop-review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d56c04d-fc50-487b-8a73-1671d03cb96b) ![mobile-review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b2f6fa1-8752-4091-8432-f2ab4eff7ec8) ![desktop-success](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d427a12e-3471-49c5-83ed-2b89e5f47fc8) ![mobile-success](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49ef4989-125f-40c9-872b-3a5f70cf511c) ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added a two-step location submission flow: enter details, review the frozen submission, then submit. - Captcha verification now appears during the review step. - Added editing support to return from review to the form. - Added submission progress tracking for submitted, volunteer review, and live-on-the-map statuses. - Prevented late address lookups from changing reviewed location details. - **Localization** - Added review and submission-status translations across supported languages.

author: richardorchard
body:
## Agent

**Agent:** Claude Code

## Summary

Investigating #1478. The issue proposed three things; measuring each on the SQL Express mirror showed only one of them was worth doing, and that one turned out to matter a lot.

### What shipped: the index gap

`IX_ModernForumPost_AuthorMemberId` had a single key column, so `WHERE AuthorMemberId = @id ORDER BY PostedAt DESC` could seek but not read in order. Measured plan for `/members/{id}`:

```
|--Sort(TOP 20, ORDER BY:([p].[PostedAt] DESC))          <-- blocking
   |--Nested Loops
      |--Index Seek(IX_ModernForumPost_AuthorMemberId) ORDERED FORWARD
      |--Clustered Index Seek(PK_ModernForumPost) LOOKUP   <-- per matching row
```

The sort is blocking, so it consumed **every post the member had written** — paying a clustered key lookup for each — before returning twenty.

Replaced with `(AuthorMemberId, PostedAt DESC) INCLUDE (ThreadId, AuthorDisplayName, IsHidden)`:

```
|--Top(TOP EXPRESSION:((20)))                             <-- no sort
   |--Nested Loops
      |--Index Seek(IX_ModernForumPost_AuthorMemberId_PostedAt) ORDERED FORWARD
      |--Clustered Index Seek(PK_ModernForumPost) LOOKUP
```

Cost is now independent of how much the member has posted. It also **subsumes most of the `BodyHtml` over-fetch** this issue raised separately: the lookups that fetch the body now run only for the rows actually returned.

The existing `IS NOT NULL` filter is kept, so the index stays **16 KB over 28 member-linked rows** rather than spanning all 1,164,852 imported posts. Filtered indexes are often unusable with parameterised predicates, so I verified rather than assumed — SQL Server still picks it for `AuthorMemberId = @a`, since an equality comparison already excludes NULL.

The old single-column index is dropped rather than kept alongside: the replacement leads with the same column under the same filter, so it serves every seek the old one did. Net index count and size are unchanged. Every other `AuthorMemberId` query in the codebase is a leading-column seek; the one `AuthorMemberId == null` predicate (`EfForumWriteRepository`) could not use the old filtered index either, so there is no regression there.

### What did not ship, and why

**The value converter for a single UNION ALL — does not work.** Full evidence is [on the issue](https://github.com/richardorchard/QueenZone.Modern/issues/1478#issuecomment-5619270000). In short: it compiles, the blast radius is only five call sites, the UNION translates, and all four SQLite unit tests pass — then SQL Server throws `InvalidCastException: Unable to cast 'System.DateTimeOffset' to 'System.DateTime'`. SQL Server's UNION type precedence promotes the result column to `datetimeoffset`, but EF reads it using the forum branch's converter provider type; it does not unify provider types across a set operation. Making the union type-consistent would need `ALTER COLUMN` on a 1.2 GB table plus the stored procs projecting `PostedAt AS TOPIC_DATE` — disproportionate for five round trips becoming three. Reverted.

**The `BodyHtml` two-phase fetch — not worth it.** I claimed this was a problem when filing the issue. Measured: average `BodyHtml` is **0.72 KB** (max 15.6 KB), so 80 surplus rows cost about 58 KB. Not worth an extra round trip and the added complexity, and largely moot after the index change.

**Multi-author sort** — raised separately as #1484 (top-N-per-author `CROSS APPLY`), with a recommendation to leave it until #337 provides telemetry.

## Testing

- [x] `dotnet restore QueenZone.sln`
- [x] `dotnet build QueenZone.sln --configuration Release --no-restore`
- [x] `dotnet format QueenZone.sln --verify-no-changes`
- [x] `dotnet test QueenZone.sln --configuration Release --no-build` — **3,774 passed, 0 failed**
- [x] Coverage gate passed locally (`-BaseRef origin/main`): global **91.28%**, changed-line **100%** (2/2)
- [ ] Mobile — not applicable, no `src/QueenZone.Mobile` changes
- [x] EF migrations: `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes` reports no pending changes; migration applied to the SQL Express mirror locally
- [x] Route/page tests avoid brittle markup assertions

## Legacy database checks

- [x] Ran against the local SQL Express mirror (`localhost\SQLEXPRESS` / `queenzone_legacy_sync`)

Every plan and measurement above came from the mirror. `dotnet ef database update` applied the migration cleanly, and `scripts/Probe-MemberActivity.ps1` passes against the resulting schema.

EF reports the migration cannot run in a transaction (`suppressTransaction: true`, matching the sibling index migrations), so a failure mid-apply would need manual cleanup. Both statements are guarded by `IF NOT EXISTS` / `IF EXISTS`, so re-running is safe, and `Down` restores the original single-column index.

**Note on test coverage:** the unit tests run on SQLite and prove nothing about any of this. The value-converter defect above passed all four of them and was caught only by `EfMemberPublicActivityLiveProbeTests` against real SQL Server.

## Issues

Closes #1478
Relates to #312
Relates to #1484

## Follow-up

- #1484 — top-N-per-author `CROSS APPLY` for the multi-author `/following` feed. Needs raw SQL; recommended to wait for #337.
- If `ModernForumPost.PostedAt` ever moves to `datetimeoffset` for unrelated reasons, the single-UNION rewrite becomes viable — recorded on #1478.

author: jagottsicher
body:
## What

Two fixes to the filter dropdown:

1. It's now fully keyboard-operable: `/` correctly opens it (it was
   already bound but didn't actually work), `Tab`/`Shift+Tab`/arrows
   cycle through all five of its own pieces, `Space`/`Enter` toggles a
   checkbox row, and `Escape` closes it from anywhere.
2. The "Nx" indicator turns bright red whenever a filter is currently
   hiding every entry a directory would otherwise show — previously
   indistinguishable from a genuinely empty folder.

## Why

Direct report: "the filter dropdown doesn't close via keyboard. can you
even open it via keyboard? can you navigate inside it like the tab
dropdown? — otherwise we're mouse-dependent."

Right after, a related report: "a filter *.mp4 works in tab 1 but in
tab 2, where I copy a bunch of .mp4 files in from tab 1, nothing is
shown, like an empty folder... only disabling the filter in tab 2
shows the .mp4 files. This must not be!"

## How

**Keyboard access** — three confirmed gaps, all in `filtermenu.go`:
- `/` called `Application.SetFocus(r.panel.filterField)` directly
  without ever opening the dropdown's own overlay — `filterField` only
  receives real input once it's part of the shown page tree, so this
  went nowhere (confirmed live: typed text landed nowhere). `/` now
  calls `r.openFilterMenu()`, the same path a click on "Y" already
  takes.
- Escape never closed it: `filterField`'s own `SetDoneFunc` only moved
  focus to the table, never called `r.hideOverlay()` — the dropdown
  stayed open on the overlay stack regardless.
- No navigation existed inside the dropdown at all — the two stub rows
  (size/modified-time) had mouse capture only.

`renderFilterMenu` (already rebuilds the whole dropdown fresh on every
open) now also wires five focusable stops in order — glob checkbox,
glob/regex button, pattern field, size row, modified-time row,
wrapping back to the first — hand-rolled the same way `chmoddialog.go`
already hand-rolls its own multi-field Tab-cycling, since `tview` has
no built-in way to cycle Tab between different `Primitive` types.
`filterRegexBtn`/`filterField` keep their own native key handling
(Button: Enter toggles mode; field: normal typing); only Up/Down are
added on top, since neither `Button.SetExitFunc` nor
`InputField.SetDoneFunc` ever sees those two keys. The two plain
checkbox rows get one shared `InputCapture` handling everything
themselves, plus new focus-based highlighting to match.

**Red indicator** — reproduced live and confirmed not a code bug: the
direct, correct consequence of `filter_persistent` (just shipped in
#198) — a filter carried over from browsing an unrelated directory
keeps hiding content it was never meant to apply to, and a
filtered-to-zero listing looks identical to a genuinely empty one. New
`Panel.filterMatchesNothing` (comparing entry counts before/after
filtering, distinct from a directory that's simply empty).
`renderFilterMenuBtn` colors "Nx" in `EntryError`'s own red whenever
it's true — the same indicator the user already pointed to as the
intended warning, just impossible to miss now.

## Testing

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` — clean
- `go test ./... -race -count=1` — all packages pass
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
- New/updated tests, each confirmed to fail against the relevant piece
  reverted before confirming it passes: `TestFilterMenuEscapeClosesDropdownFromAnyRow`,
  `TestFilterMenuSpaceTogglesRowFromKeyboard`,
  `TestFilterMenuTabCyclesFocusThroughAllFiveStops`,
  `TestFilterFieldDoneReturnsFocusToTableWithoutClearing` (updated for
  the new semantics), `TestFilterMatchesNothingColorsIndicatorRed`,
  `TestFilterMatchesNothingFalseForGenuinelyEmptyDirectory`,
  `TestFilterMatchesNothingFalseWhenSomeEntriesStillMatch`.
- Confirmed live via tmux for both fixes: `/` opens the dropdown, Tab
  from the pattern field visibly moves the petrol highlight to the
  size row, Escape closes it; and the exact reported mp4-hiding
  scenario reproduced with a real SGR true-color capture showing
  `38;2;255;0;0` (pure red) on the "1x" indicator.
- README.md / docs/user-guide.md updated.

author: shy7777
body:
Reusing a configured decorator currently lets different functions share cached results:

```python
cached = cache(60)
inc = cached(lambda x: x + 1)
double = cached(lambda x: x * 2)

inc(3)     # 4
double(3)  # 4, but should be 6
```

The same problem affects `memoize()`. Create the memory when the decorator is applied to each function, so reusing a timeout or key configuration keeps the functions' cached values and invalidation separate. The cache-hit path stays unchanged.

The regression test covers both decorators, repeated calls, and `invalidate()` / `invalidate_all()` affecting only their own function. Both cases fail before the fix. On Python 3.12, `python -m pytest -W error -q` passes all 221 tests, and both flake8 commands from the repository's CI pass.

author: parsofish
body:
## What

`runRepeatStep` has two exhaustion modes and reported one of them.

- Gate handle present each pass → rounds get answered, `until` is never met. "the act kept being available, so the product never moved on" is exactly right.
- Gate handle absent on every pass → the loop spends the whole bound in its poll branch, `rounds` stays 0, and that same sentence is the precise opposite of what happened.

## Why now

Lane A measured the cost on S9 run 3: beat 13's repeat stood on a page that does not carry its act, burned its full **600 000 ms**, and was then told the act kept being available. An operator reading that looks at the agent; the fault is in the authoring.

Probing it showed the claim is worse than sometimes-wrong. The message is only reachable from the top of `while (left() > 0)`; when the bound expires mid-round the loop dies on the round error instead. In practice the sentence is reachable **almost only from the poll branch** — which is to say almost only when it is false. Measured on a press-only repeat standing on `/monitor`:

```
PRESS-ONLY REPEAT: took=4001ms of 4000  → "the act kept being available"   ← false
BARE PRESS:        took=2001ms of 4000  → "standing on the wrong page: /monitor …"  ← true, at t+0
```

## What changed

Split into the two branches that are actually knowable:

- **never saw the gate** — name the act and the page it stood on for the whole bound, and offer both readings (wrong page, or the affordance never arrived);
- **saw the gate** — name the round count and the unmet `until`, and drop the availability clause, which was never checked and is not knowable at the instant the bound expires.

## What this is NOT

It does **not** re-instate a route compare inside a repeat. Ruling 569 removed that for a reason that still holds: between rounds the gate is legitimately gone while the agent takes its turn, so absence at any one moment proves nothing. Absence for the **entire bound** is a different claim, and it is the only one made here — after the bound, never before it. No wait gets shorter or longer; only the sentence changes.

## Tests

Two added to `beats-repeat.test.ts`, both red before the change:
- a repeat whose act never appears says so, names the act and the page, and still spends the bound;
- positive control: a gate that WAS there keeps the round-count verdict and gains neither new sentence.

The five page fakes in that file gained `url()`. A real Playwright `Page` always answers it; a fake that cannot is simply incomplete, and a failure path that TypeErrors reports nothing at all. That is how the regression surfaced — the existing `6.11.52(B)` control went red with `page.url is not a function`.

Gate: **20/20 PASS** on `69615f66`, all five pin manifests 0 FAILED.

author: op-q
body:
Two halves of one problem: the direct path's rendezvous was compiled in, so a network with egress filtering could not use the direct path at all, and the lab could not test it hermetically.

## The feature

`DROP_RENDEZVOUS_RELAY` and `DROP_RENDEZVOUS_BOOTSTRAP` point the iroh relay and the DHT bootstrap somewhere else. Environment variables rather than flags: rendezvous is a property of the network a machine is on, set once and never changed between two transfers.

**A malformed value is an error, never a silent default.** An operator who meant to keep rendezvous inside their network and quietly got the public DHT has lost exactly what they configured, invisibly.

Recorded as `decisions.md` entry 15, with what an operator takes on in `security.md`.

## The lab

`netlab/rendezvous/` runs an iroh relay and a three-node mainline testnet in one process, deliberately outside the workspace — `iroh-relay`'s server feature pulls in hyper, rustls and an ACME client, none of which belongs in a binary shipped for four targets.

Three findings changed the lab rather than the code:

- **Phase 4's assertions tested nothing.** `Carrier::Direct` is reported as soon as rendezvous and connect succeed; nothing consults whether a hole was punched. A punch is now measured by counting bytes on the rendezvous link, and NAT mapping behaviour by comparing source ports seen by two destinations.
- **The lab died where it should have skipped.** `user_namespaces_available()` read two sysctls that both say yes on Ubuntu 24.04+, where the refusal comes from `apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns`. `conftest` acts on that with `execvp`, so a wrong yes left no process alive to report anything. The probe now attempts a namespace instead of predicting one.
- **Outbound UDP is not blocked, only port 53 is.** Two DHT routers answered, and the reply carried this host's public address.

## Known failure

First run 2026-09-10: **7 passed, 1 failed.** `test_a_full_cone_nat_is_punched_through` reproduces three runs of three.

It is not the direct path in general — topology 1 completes with no `api` process anywhere, and topology 3 completes over the rendezvous relay. The NAT measures as endpoint-independent (`37848` to two destinations) and nothing fell back to a relay. The sender reports a QUIC `authentication failed`; the receiver times out.

Landed as a known failure with the evidence in the plan. Next step is packet capture, not another assertion.

## Verification

171 Rust tests, `fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `check-secrets.sh` — all pass.
