author: haksungjang
body:
The accessibility gate walked only the 8 screens the visual baseline also walks, because both gates shared one register (representativeScreens.ts). Axe violations are a property of the markup, not the pixels, so a screen exempted from a visual baseline for reusing another screen's layout template can still carry its own missing labels or focus-order defects. This adds `A11Y_ONLY_SCREENS`, a superset the a11y gate alone walks, covering 13 more primary screens (project creation, search, inventory, groups list/detail, policies, integrations, profile, about, and three admin list pages) without growing the visual-baseline set that `coverage-manifest.ts` deliberately keeps small.

The first local scan against these 13 screens found three real violations that were never caught before (search, about, admin-scans, in both themes). They are not fixed here: they land in the CI-generated `a11y-baseline.json` instead, matching the gate's existing ratchet design for a screen scanned for the first time (see the spec's own header comment on why demanding zero violations on day one gets the gate turned off instead). Once this merges I'll dispatch `ui-gates.yml` with `update_baselines=true` to capture that baseline from CI, per the documented recipe, and push it as a follow-up commit.

Also closes the other two gaps #425 named: a `prefers-reduced-motion` test that actually emulates the media feature and checks the app shell's animation collapses (mutation-tested against a revert of the CSS override), and one keyboard-only E2E scenario per named flow (login, project creation, approval workflow) using `.focus()` + `toBeFocused()` + `page.keyboard.press()`, the same pattern `tableSemantics.spec.ts`'s existing "S4" test already established in this codebase, rather than `.click()`/`.fill()`. Both mutation-tested locally.

## Summary

From a bot-response QA spreadsheet the team put together, testing real questions against real answers with corrections from Youssef Singer (Sourcing Coordinator) and Seif. Content corrections below were confirmed with the user before applying, since they touch compliance-sensitive legal content and previously-documented process facts.

### Content corrections (confirmed)
- **Buy-out 19.5% fee basis** — replaces "ambiguous, confirm before quoting" across all three legal docs with a clear date rule: candidate compensation/salary basis for deals before July 2025, client fee basis on/after.

Add a bounded development selector for structured evidence. Selecting one short citation can discard another source used to rule out a conflict. A covered key now requires every nominated root plus the union of all agreeing dependency paths, with complete active revisions and the original task and public contract preserved.

Exact coverage enumerates at most 4,096 source subsets. Its recency comparator uses the same full input, resolver, decision groups and byte accounting; it considers complete groups in a documented deterministic order. The budget includes the exact UTF-8 request-plus-contract envelope. Original conflicts, malformed permitted sources and unresolved alternatives cannot earn coverage through pruning. Re-resolving the selected payload checks that covered keys retain their original groups and no additional key becomes resolved. author: coleml
body:
Answers the question raised on #64: yes, there is a good solution, and it is a one-line router swap.

## What was actually wrong
Hono's default SmartRouter parses a path segment with `/^\:([^\{\}]+)(?:\{(.+)\})?$/`. `[^{}]+` is greedy and permits colons, so `:recipe:scale` becomes a single parameter **named** `recipe:scale` — the real parameter never binds, and the request fails validation on a field the caller did send. A `{regex}` constraint can't rescue it either, because the regex must be anchored at the end of the segment.

## The fix
All four of Hono's routers, against four candidate patterns:

| Router | `/recipes/:recipe:scale` |
|---|---|
| RegExpRouter (the default, via SmartRouter) | parameter unbound |
| TrieRouter | parameter unbound |
| LinearRouter | parameter = `"fajitas:scale"` |
| **PatternRouter** | **parameter = `"fajitas"`** |

So `recipes/{recipe}:scale` is a real URL again, with no rewrite layer and no divergence between the routes and the generated OpenAPI document. The cost is that PatternRouter compiles a regex per route and scans them rather than building one matcher — slower than RegExpRouter, irrelevant at twenty-odd routes on a household app.

All 41 existing API tests passed unchanged under the swap, so nothing else depended on the old router's behaviour.

## Guards
A test asserts the parameter binds, and **fails if the router is changed back** — verified by removing `PatternRouter` and watching exactly that one test fail. Another asserts the resource path appears in the document.

## Two things found on the way
- Two tests were still calling the old collection path. One had been **passing for the wrong reason**: it expected 404 and got 404 because the route was absent, not because the recipe was.
- I briefly claimed `/v1/weather` and `/v1/units:convert` were unmounted dead code. That was wrong — I'd run the check against `main`, which doesn't contain #64. They are mounted correctly, and all 18 paths appear in the document.

Based on `feat/weather` so it stacks on #64 rather than conflicting. 384 tests, lint, typecheck and build all pass.

author: localtrade1
body:
### Description
This pull request addresses high- and medium-severity mathematical, resource management, and supply-chain findings in `tools-and-analysis` identified during the workspace-wide security audit (**T1–T5**).

Most notably, the CPI consensus calculation in the market surprise notebook suffered from a critical scale error that rendered renormalisation dead across all realistic ladders, divided consensus by an incorrect factor of 100, and triggered zero-division crashes on illiquid markets. Furthermore, credential file descriptors were leaked, `poetry.lock` was ignored by version control, and 14 dependency packages contained 75 known security vulnerabilities.

### Key Changes & Remediations

#### 1. Arithmetic & Calculation Safety (T5 - `projects/market_surprise_calculator/main.ipynb`)
* **Scale-Aware Renormalisation:** Replaced the dead `accounted_probability < 1` check with `< 100`, accounting for Kalshi cent quotations (0–100 percentage points).
* **Divisor Scale Fix:** Updated `consensus /= accounted_probability / 100`, correcting a 100x scale error that skewed expected CPI consensus and downstream S&P 500 regression outputs.
* **Division by Zero Protection:** Added a check for `accounted_probability <= 0` that raises a descriptive `ValueError` instead of panicking with a `ZeroDivisionError` when all markets are filtered out as illiquid.
* **Resilient Data Ingestion:** Added explicit guards for unsettled markets (`true_cpi_value is None`) and empty pricing windows to prevent loop crashes (`TypeError`, `IndexError`).
* **Typed Return:** Updated `predicted_index_change` to return the predicted float value rather than returning `None` implicitly.

#### 2. Deterministic Credential Resource Handling (T2 - `client/kalshi_client.py`)
* **Context Manager Adoption:** Wrapped credential reads in `with resolved.open(...)`, guaranteeing file descriptor release and clearing buffers containing authentication tokens.
* **Filesystem Permission Guard:** Added POSIX permission checks that warn if `credentials.yaml` is readable by group or world (`0o077`).
* **Preserve Error Lineage:** Wrapped YAML parse errors in `from exc` to maintain line/column context.

#### 3. Supply-Chain & Dependency Resolution (T1 - `requirements.txt`)
* **Resolved 75 Vulnerability Advisories:** Upgraded 14 pinned packages to advisory-free versions according to `pip-audit`:
  * `requests==2.33.0`, `urllib3==2.7.0`, `cryptography==50.0.0`
  * `pillow==12.3.0`, `tornado==6.5.8`, `lxml==6.1.0`
  * `fonttools==4.60.2`, `idna==3.15`, `scikit-learn==1.5.0`
  * `scipy==1.10.0`, `soupsieve==2.8.4`, `jupyter-core==5.8.1`, `certifi==2024.7.4`, `pygments==2.20.0`
* **Resolver Compatibility:** Raised `cffi==2.0.0` to meet `cryptography>=50.0.0` specifications without breaking resolver constraints.

#### 4. Git & Pre-Commit Hardening (T3, T4 - `.gitignore`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`)
* **Track Build Manifests (T3):** Removed `poetry.lock` and `pyproject.toml` from `.gitignore` to ensure dependencies remain reproducible.
* **Canonical Hook Upstream & Secret Detection (T4):** Migrated flake8 from the retired GitLab mirror to `https://github.com/PyCQA/flake8`, and added the `detect-private-key` hook to prevent local credential leaks before commit creation.

### How to Review
1. Inspect `CPIRelease.kalshi_consensus()` in `projects/market_surprise_calculator/main.ipynb` to verify the `< 100` threshold and `/ 100` divisor correction.
2. Verify `load_credentials` in `client/kalshi_client.py` for context-managed file handling and permission checks.
3. Review `requirements.txt` and run `pip-audit -r requirements.txt` to confirm zero remaining advisories.

author: bertcalm
body:
Finding 14 — the app was working and looked broken.

`ETERNAL` measured **1.77 s** on a desktop JVM (SKIM 480 ms, DUB 247 ms,
GHOST 162 ms), and a phone is several times slower. While that ran the
chips silently stopped accepting taps — no label change, no dimming, no
spinner. You tap the chip, nothing happens, you tap again, still nothing.

## The fix

- The header reads **"TREATMENT · DRONE…"** while the work runs — the
  chip's own word, via `PadSheet.displayLabel`, not the segment id.
- The chip being applied wears the pad's colour at half strength — lit
  enough to find, not so lit it reads as already finished.
- Every other chip steps back to `ink3`, so *"you can't tap this yet"* is
  visible rather than merely true.

Naming the treatment matters as much as the ellipsis: it makes the wait
attributable to the thing you asked for, rather than to the app.

Both entry points record it — the chip tap **and** the AMT commit, which
re-runs the same second-and-a-bit of work at a new amount.

The copy is `Copy.treatmentBusy` in `:shell`, tested. A function rather
than a constant so it carries the segment's name — and so the reflective
"every `Copy` constant shouts and stops" law, which scans constants,
needs no exemption for a progress line.

## How the in-flight segment is threaded

`busy` is a single flag shared by **fourteen** call sites in this file, so
clearing a companion value in each coroutine's `finally` would have meant
surgery in several places I can't compile locally. Instead:

- both entry points record the segment,
- one `LaunchedEffect(busy)` clears it whenever *any* operation ends,
- the card reads `applyingSegment.takeIf { busy }`.

**That last gate is what makes it correct rather than merely tidy.** An
`applyTreatment` that returns early — no model, no pad, no treatment for
the segment — can leave the value set. Gating on `busy` makes a stale
value invisible, where a chip stuck claiming to be in flight would be a
bug.

## Not changed

**NONE is still display-only.** Finding 13 — there is no un-treat — is a
real gap and its own piece of work, not a ride-along on this one.

## Verification

- Full JVM suite green.
- The rendered headers were **printed rather than assumed**:
  `ETERNAL -> TREATMENT · DRONE…`, `BODY -> TREATMENT · BODY…`.
- `:app` compiles only in CI. The first attempt at the chip edit
  **asserted and wrote nothing**: `raisedBevel(… if (selected) …)` appears
  six times across this sheet's cards, so the anchor was ambiguous.
  Re-anchored on the block that owns `onSegmentTap`.

## Corrections after review

Two review findings, both real, fixed in `d0716c3`:

1. **AMT was a hole in the fix.** `onAmountCommit` started the same work
   without recording the segment, so dragging the slider left the header
   silent. Scope error on my part — finding 14 is the treatment path, not
   just the taps that begin at a chip.
2. **This description originally claimed the header reads
   "TREATMENT · ETERNAL…".** It never could: the card passes the display
   label, and `ETERNAL`'s is `DRONE`. The test asserted the same
   impossible string. Both corrected, and the test now asserts the segment
   id does *not* appear.

author: charlescnorton
body:
**Change** - `eqfor.f` accumulates `chi` as `twopi*signgs*chi1` under a `UNSIGNED_CHI` define, and the root `CMakeLists.txt` carries `OPTION (USE_UNSIGNED_CHI "Use unsigned chi" ON)` beside `USE_EXT_PRESSURE`, so the historical output is the default and the signed one is opt-in.

**Cause** - every other flux quantity in the same wout carries the Jacobian sign and `chi` does not: `fileout.f:211` writes `phi = (signgs*twopi*hs)*phi`, `wrout.f:1299` and `1301` write `phipf` and `chipf` as `twopi*signgs*...`, and `eqfor.f:220` forms the threed1 poloidal flux with `fac = twopi*signgs`. With the usual negative Jacobian the file therefore holds `chi = -integral(iota dphi)`, so `dchi/dphi` read back from it has the opposite sign to `iotaf` beside it, and `chi` has the opposite sign to the integral of the `chipf` stored next to it.

**Evidence** - on a cth-like fixed-boundary case at ns = 25 with `signgs = -1`, the median of `(dchi/dphi) / iotas` over the half grid is -1.000000 with the option on and +1.000000 with it off, and `chi(ns)` is +4.007483e-02 against -4.007483e-02, where the integral of the file's own `chipf` is -4.006393e-02. On `solovev` the same median goes from -1.000000 to +1.000000. Only the sign moves; the magnitude is unchanged. Built both ways from the same tree.

**Scope** - `chi` is written to the wout and to the threed1 file and is read by neither the force balance nor any other quantity, so no equilibrium changes either way. Default on, the output is what it was.

The same change is proposed for VMEC++ in https://github.com/proximafusion/vmecpp/pull/772.

body:
Adds a new skill (`conventional-commits/`) that drafts Conventional Commits-style messages from the actual working-tree diff and, once the developer approves, stages and commits them locally via git. It complements the existing `cl-creation` skill, which only drafts PR titles/descriptions — this one is scoped to local commit creation and does not push or touch GitHub.

Included:
- `SKILL.md` — the skill's instructions (type(scope) prefix, 50/72-wrapped body, footers).
- `references/git-commands.md` — read-only git commands the skill relies on to build the diff/context.
- `scripts/validate_commit_message.py` — validates a drafted message against Conventional Commits formatting before it's committed.
- `evals/evals.json` and `assets/conventional-commits-eval-review.html` — an eval suite and its results report, used to check the skill's message-drafting quality.

Also: commits produced by this skill intentionally omit the session's default `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer — since the skill drafts the message but the developer owns the resulting local commit, crediting authorship of the draft doesn't belong in it. This overrides the session-wide attribution default specifically for commits this skill creates.

`.gitignore` now excludes `.claude/` so local Claude Code state doesn't get tracked.

author: cardosofiles
body:
## Summary
Implementação ponta a ponta de autenticação por chaves de acesso (Passkey WebAuthn / FIDO2) com @better-auth/passkey@1.7.2, encerrando o **GAP-03** (phishing-resistant auth) e a metade passkey do **GAP-09** (UNIQUE(credential_id), aaguid, ON DELETE CASCADE em user_id).

## O que foi feito
1. **Schema Drizzle & Migração 0004:**
   - Criada tabela `passkey` com 11 colunas canônicas per Spec 08 §6.3: `id`, `name`, `public_key`, `user_id`, `credential_id`, `counter`, `device_type`, `backed_up`, `transports`, `created_at`, `aaguid`.
   - Chave estrangeira `user_id -> user(id)` com `ON DELETE CASCADE` estrito (GAP-09).
   - Constraint de unicidade `UNIQUE(credential_id)` em nível relacional (`passkey_credential_id_unique`).
   - Índice B-Tree `passkey_user_id_idx` para aceleração de buscas por usuário e deleções em cascata.
   - Gerada migração versionada `drizzle/0004_eager_argent.sql`.

2. **Configuração do Better Auth (`auth.config.ts`):**
   - Instalado `@better-auth/passkey@1.7.2` com paridade exata de versão com `better-auth@1.7.2`.
   - Plugin `passkey` registrado com `rpID` derivado estritamente do hostname de `BETTER_AUTH_URL` (`localhost` em dev, `api.cardososound.com` em prod) sem esquema nem porta (D-54).
   - Emissor `rpName: 'Cardoso Sound'`, `origin: env.BETTER_AUTH_URL` sem barra final.
   - Padrão `requireSession: true` mantido: registro exige sessão ativa de usuário.
   - Adicionada a 13ª regra mandatória ao dicionário `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_RULES`: `'/sign-in/passkey': { window: 60, max: 10 }` (Spec 08 §3.3).

3. **Segurança e Conformidade (D-31):**
   - Endpoints de gerenciamento (`delete-passkey`, `update-passkey`) rejeitam credenciais pertencentes a outros usuários com HTTP 404 (Not Found), nunca 403 (Forbidden), garantindo anti-enumeração estrita.

4. **Testes & Qualidade:**
   - 5 testes unitários de configuração (`tests/unit/modules/auth/passkey-config.test.ts`, T1–T5).
   - 7 testes de integração de schema (`tests/integration/schema-passkey.test.ts`, T6–T12).
   - 10 testes de integração de autenticação e WebAuthn (`tests/integration/auth-passkey.test.ts`, T13–T22).
   - Atualizada asserção de rate limit em `tests/integration/auth-rate-limit.test.ts` (13 endpoints).
   - Total de 422 testes passando (100% verde) em 47 arquivos.
   - Determinismo comprovado via `--sequence.shuffle` (179 testes executados em ordem randômica com 100% de sucesso).
   - Zero erros em `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format` e `pnpm build`.
   - Plano persistido em `docs/agents-plans/plan-f5-s06-passkey-webauthn.md` e memória registrada em `.agents/memory/F5-S06.md`.

author: stormer78
body:
`fetch_did_secrets_bundle` now dispatches `vta/contexts/secrets/1.0` instead of
walking the context itself — `get_context`, then `list_keys`, then one
`get_key_secret` per key.

## This fixes a latent bug, not just an N+1

`get_key_secret` dispatches `seeds/export-mnemonic/1.0`, whose handler opens
with `auth.require_admin()` — and `require_admin` demands `Role::Admin`
exactly, not admin *of a context*.

`room-host`'s own onboarding instructions tell the operator:

    vta import-did --did <ephemeral> --role application --context <CONTEXT>

So a host set up exactly as documented would enrol, receive its grant, connect,
and then fail at the secrets fetch with `admin role required`. It has never
worked as written; the only way to run it was to grant global Admin — authority
over every other context in the VTA — to a process that wanted the keys of one.

The new task is `require_write()` (Application or higher) plus `require_context`
on the context asked for, so the documented grant is now the grant that works.
`room-host` needs no change: it calls `fetch_did_secrets_bundle`, which is the
seam.

## The other two things the walk got wrong

- The kid-selection rule (`select_secret_kid`) had to be applied by every
  caller, so a second implementation could quietly disagree about which secrets
  belong to the DID. It now lives on one side of the wire.
- A bundle assembled from N independent answers has no single point at which the
  VTA decided to release it — nothing to audit as one act, and nothing for a
  future "this key may not leave" rule to hook.

## Falling back, and why it is temporary

A VTA older than the task answers `unsupportedType`, and this falls back to the
old walk so a service can be upgraded before the VTA it talks to is. Only that
rejection triggers it: a `Forbidden` must surface as itself rather than send the
caller down a path it is even less entitled to, and there is a test for that.

The fallback is the last caller of `seeds/export-mnemonic`. One of the tests
asserts it still reaches that URI — so when that assertion has nothing to find,
the fallback and the task can both go.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

author: antash-mishra
body:
expo-blur rendered differently per platform: iOS ran a real UIVisualEffectView while Android painted a flat scrim unless a surface passed experimentalBlurMethod, and only two of our eight frosted surfaces did. The same component therefore blurred on one platform and not the other.

Add a shared FrostedSurface primitive that decides once per surface and applies the same treatment to both platforms, Android's opt-in included. Surfaces with a hard edge beneath them blur (Create Event cover chip, cover-picker check badge, avatar edit badge); the rest take a flat tint from the new src/theme/materials.ts, whose multipliers were fitted to the iOS material within 1% across four surfaces, both tints, intensities 15-60 and backdrops from rgb(39) to rgb(162). Android's Dimezis blur uses blurReductionFactor 2; at the stock 4 it blurs far more weakly than iOS.

AvatarEditBadge also drops Android elevation in favour of boxShadow. Android tessellates an elevation shadow into a polygon drawn behind the caster, which showed through the translucent badge as an octagon once the opaque BlurView that had been masking it was gone. It was visible even at elevation 1. boxShadow is a real Gaussian shadow and lands within 3/255 of the iOS shadow; iOS keeps its original shadow props untouched.

Remove the now-dead live-material gating from EventSharedTransition: hero buttons are a flat fill, so nothing is captured per frame during a transition. Also remove componentTokens.overlay.heroButtonTint, which pushed Android ~28/255 darker than iOS rather than compensating for it.

Verified on an iPhone 15 Pro simulator and a Galaxy A56. Edit Profile renders pixel-identical to the previous build on iOS (718,620 samples, max delta 0), and the Android cover chip and avatar badge now match their iOS counterparts.

body:
## Summary
Google Search Console's Events enhancement report flagged game detail pages as **invalid** (missing field `location`) and suboptimal (missing `endDate`, `offers`, `image`, `description`, `performer`, `organizer`). The `SportsEvent` JSON-LD added in #1914 only ever populated `name`, `sport`, `eventStatus`, `startDate`, `speakable` and per-team scores — every other field was simply never set, for any game.

- `location` — sourced from `Gameday.address` as a `Place`; omitted (not fabricated) when the gameday has no address on file
- `endDate` — `startDate` + an estimated 70-minute game length, since no per-game duration is stored (matches `ScheduleManager.DEFAULT_GAME_LENGTH`)

author: svyable
body:
## Scope

Revises only **The Nucleus That Waited — Ch 6, “Argonne Turns Up the Light”**, plus its existing book-local source log. This PR is stacked directly on draft PR #1584 (`author/the-nucleus-that-waited`) and does not touch neighboring chapters or repository surfaces.

## What changed

- Replaces the chapter’s qualitative “orders of magnitude” treatment with the actual experimental confrontation between the 1999 Collins claim and the 2001 APS null.
- Makes the original result concrete: roughly 4% increases in selected decay-cascade gamma lines were interpreted as an energy-integrated triggering cross section near 10^-21 cm² keV.
- Adds the primary APS result: no induced decay, with an upper limit below 2 × 10^-27 cm² keV over 20–60 keV—more than five orders of magnitude below the earlier reported value—and a 5 × 10^-26 cm² keV limit at 8 keV.
- Sharpens the strongest counterargument rather than claiming the null excludes every possible isomer-control mechanism. Narrow resonances, other energies, plasma pathways, or different intermediate states remain separate hypotheses; they do not rescue the specific 1999 cross section without new prospective predictions.
- Separates the undisputed fact that hafnium-178m2 stores nuclear excitation for decades from the disputed engineering bridge: a sufficiently strong controllable trigger.
- Removes generic mini-morals about skepticism and classification and lets the numerical cross-section gap carry the argument.

## Research added / checked

Freshly checked September 10, 2026 against the primary journal record:

- I. Ahmad et al., **Search for X-Ray Induced Acceleration of the Decay of the 31-Yr Isomer of 178Hf Using Synchrotron Radiation**, *Physical Review Letters* 87, 072503 (2001): https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.072503
- C. B. Collins et al., **Accelerated Emission of Gamma Rays from the 31-yr Isomer of 178Hf Induced by X-Ray Irradiation**, *Physical Review Letters* 82, 695 (1999): https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.82.695

Both primary papers are now identified directly in the source log with the relevant quantitative claim boundaries.

## Why this improves the book

The previous chapter had the right skeptical conclusion but made the decisive replication sound mostly like “a brighter source found nothing.” The revision exposes the actual scientific collision: a published coupling estimate near 10^-21 cm² keV confronted a purpose-built synchrotron limit more than 100,000 times smaller in the tested broad energy band. That is both more rigorous and more narratively useful, while preserving the legitimate possibility that different isomer-control mechanisms occupy different parameter regimes.

No README/TOC, neighboring chapters, rights, catalog, Reader, tooling, workflow, or Shelf files changed. Auto-merge is not enabled.

author: bradbor23
body:
## Summary

Refs #105. `.activity-dashboard` capped at 1100px, so on a 2000px display **900px — 45% of the
screen — sat idle while eight conversation names were clipped to an ellipsis**. The page was
discarding information and leaving nearly half the width unused at the same time.

Raises the cap to `100rem`, centred, matching the roster decision in #114.

## Root cause

A fixed 1100px cap on the widest content in the portal: a five-column table over 35 rows. Measured
on the live table at a 2000px viewport:

| | 1100px (before) | `100rem` (after) |
|---|---|---|
| dashboard | 1100px | 1600px |
| table | 1052px | 1552px |
| idle | **900px (45%)** | 400px (20%) |
| clipped cells | **19** | **5** |
|   — Conversation | 8 | **0** |
|   — Agents | 11 | 5 |

Every column gains: Conversation 526 → 776, Agents 210 → 310, Status and Channels 95 → 140, Last
activity 126 → 186. Laptops gain too — at 1280px the dashboard was 1100px and is now the full 1280.

## Changes

- `.activity-dashboard` `max-width: 1100px` → `100rem`. That is the whole change.
- Cache-buster `ds41` → `ds42`.

## Validation

**Before** — 1100px cap. Purpose lines clipped to "Reconcil…", "Check m…", "Provision …", with
900px idle either side:

![Before: clipped purpose lines and 900px of idle margin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bradbor23/botnexus/pr-evidence/ui-layout-optimization-870343/activity/01-before-1100.png)

**After** — every purpose line in full:

![After: purpose lines complete at the wider cap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bradbor23/botnexus/pr-evidence/ui-layout-optimization-870343/activity/02-after-100rem.png)

Measured two ways. On the **live table** (35 rows, real data) by overriding the cap in the browser:
clipped cells 19 → 5, all remaining in Agents. And in a **replica** built from the extracted
`.activity-*` rules, which reproduces the defect's shape independently: Conversation 5 → **0**,
Agents 5 → 5. The replica carries 10 rows rather than 35, so its absolute counts are lower; the
shape is what matters, and it agrees.

### What this does NOT fix, and why width is the wrong lever

The five remaining clipped cells are all in Agents, and they are **not a layout problem**. A
sub-agent chip renders `assistant--subagent--coder--49c606cd1ee6485bbaac3acdf57dc2dc` — the raw
agent id including a 32-hex GUID — at roughly 400px per chip, so one cell needed **1730px inside a
310px column**.

The measurements prove width does not touch it: going from a 1300px cap to a 1500px cap bought
**zero** reduction in Agents clipping. That is visible in the after capture, where the Agents column
still ends in an ellipsis.

The cause is in `AgentLabel` (`ActivityDashboard.razor:565`): sub-agents are ephemeral and absent
from the client store, so `Store.GetAgent` returns null and the method returns `agentId` verbatim.
Its own doc comment says it falls back to *"a title-cased id"*, which it does not — so this is a
defect against a stated contract rather than a deliberate choice.

Left out of this PR deliberately: it changes user-visible copy, and deciding what a sub-agent chip
should say is a labelling call rather than a layout one.

## Tests

`BlazorClient.Tests` **2149/16/2165** (passed/failed/total) — the 16 are the known pre-existing
`node`-dependent failures, diffed by name against the baseline in **both** directions: no new
failures, none silently fixed. Filtered `Activity` suites: **246/0/246**. Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

No new tests. bUnit renders markup without layout, so it cannot assert a column width or a clipped
cell — which is why a 1100px cap and 19 clipped cells sat behind 246 green Activity tests. The check
that can see this is the viewport measurement above.

## Anti-reinvention

One declaration changed. Centred rather than full-bleed, and expressed in `rem` rather than `px`, to
match the conventions established in #114 and #118. No new tokens, no markup change.

## Documentation impact

- [ ] Documentation updated in this PR
- [x] `no-docs-impact` — reason: presentation only; no route, contract, config or API surface change.

## Risk & rollback

- **Risk**: very low. A single `max-width` value on one container. `table-layout: fixed` and the
  declared column percentages are untouched, so column proportions are unchanged — every column
  simply gets more pixels.
- **Rollback**: revert this commit; the cache-buster reverts with it.
- **Cache-buster**: `ds41` → `ds42` is load-bearing.
- **CI integrity**: no tests removed, renamed, skipped or weakened.

## Known limitation

On an ultra-wide display the table stops at 1600px and the surplus returns to margin. That is
deliberate — a five-column table stretched across 3440px is harder to scan, not easier — but it is a
judgement, and it is one value in one place if it reads wrong in practice.

## Merge notes

Screenshots live under `activity/` on the orphan branch `pr-evidence/ui-layout-optimization-870343`,
alongside the #106, #110, #114, #118 and #120 sets. **Keep that branch** — deleting it breaks the
images in six merged PR bodies.

## Summary
Implements the contact form on the official site so it actually sends an email instead of being a dead button.

### Changes
- **New:** `dhankund_official_site/functions/api/contact.ts` — a Pages Function that:
  - accepts a POST with `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `message`
  - validates required fields + email format
  - sends the enquiry to `info@dhankund.com` via the existing `SEB` `send_email` binding, with the visitor's email set as `replyTo`
- **Updated:** `dhankund_official_site/src/app/contact/page.tsx` — converted to a client component with controlled inputs, submit handler that POSTs to `/api/contact`, and success/error feedback banners.

### How it works
The site already had `[[send_email]] name = "SEB"` in `wrangler.toml` but it was unused. This wires it up:
- `from`: `noreply@dhankund.com` (must be a verified sender in Cloudflare Email Routing)
- `to`: `info@dhankund.com`
- `replyTo`: the visitor's submitted email, so you can reply directly

### ⚠️ One-time setup required (out of band)
Cloudflare Email Service requires the `from` address's domain to be verified/onboarded, otherwise sending fails with `E_SENDER_NOT_VERIFIED`:
1. Verify `noreply@dhankund.com` (or whichever sender you prefer) in **Cloudflare → Email → Email Routing / Email Service**.
2. If you'd rather use a different sender (e.g. `contact@dhankund.com`), tell me and I'll update `SENDER_EMAIL` in the API route.
3. Make sure the `SEB` binding is present in the deployed worker (already in `wrangler.toml`).

CI (`ci_official_site.yml`) will run on this PR.

author: ystk-hsn
body:
### Description
The `wildcard` field indexes trigram tokens while its doc values hold the original value, so its postings term dictionary and its doc values enumerate different term sets. Four aggregation optimizations assume the two match and silently return wrong results on `wildcard` fields:

- `terms`: `GlobalOrdinalsStringTermsAggregator#tryCollectFromTermFrequencies` maps postings ordinals onto doc-values ordinals — bucket counts sum to `sum_doc_freq` (214 over a 32-doc index in the repro)
- `rare_terms`: `StringRareTermsAggregator#tryPrecomputeAggregationForLeaf` uses postings terms as bucket keys — every trigram's doc frequency exceeds `max_doc_count`, so all real values are dropped
- `cardinality`: the dynamic pruning collector iterates the postings dictionary — returns 11 instead of 32
- `composite`: `TermsSortedDocsProducer#processLeaf` walks the postings dictionary — collapses everything into one bucket

This PR introduces `MappedFieldType#indexedTermsMatchDocValues()` (default `true`; `wildcard` returns `false`) and guards the four call sites (five including `BinaryValuesSource`, kept symmetric with `GlobalOrdinalValuesSource`). It is the aggregation-side counterpart of #18568, which fixed the same postings/doc-values mismatch for sort pruning.

Each new unit test reproduces the reported wrong values before the fix and passes after. The REST test runs the four aggregations in separate requests on purpose: a sibling aggregation disables the affected precompute paths and would mask the defect — which is likely why bundled tests never caught this.

One behavioral note for review: the change only disables postings-based shortcuts for fields whose indexed terms differ from their doc values; results come from doc values via normal collection, matching `keyword` semantics. The added Java API method is additive (`:server:japicmp` passes).

### Related Issues
Resolves #22992

### Check List
- [x] Functionality includes testing.
- [ ] API changes companion pull request created, if applicable. *(N/A — no REST API change)*
- [ ] Public documentation issue/PR created, if applicable. *(N/A — restores documented behavior)*

author: krystalgamer
body:
Refines the raw-indexing rule in `notes/decompilation-workflow.md` with a second, independent observation.

Two #2500 conversions failed in the same shape this week, and both split cleanly into a half that lands and a half that does not:

| change | result |
|---|---|
| `Password_SetDigitCursorTarget` — naming `target_x`/`target_y` in `PasswordCursorView` and using them (#3746) | **free** |
| `Password_UpdateDigitCursor` — the same two fields, plus `x`, `y`, `timer`, `updateFlags`, through the same view | password overlay stops matching |
| `name_entry_runtime.c` — taking `display_object_config.h`'s `DisplayObjectConfigView *` prototype, casts at six call sites (#3753) | **free** |
| `NameEntry_UpdateGlyphShatter` — naming the seven fields it reads through that view | password overlay stops matching |

A struct member, a prototype and a cast at a call site are all cheap: they change what the *source says*, not what the function *does*. The expression a matched function uses to reach memory is not cheap — and both failures were functions that read one field several times or mix access widths across it, which is where GCC's base-register choice and reload points get pinned.

### Why it is worth writing down

It changes how to split the work: **by that line, not by file.** Land the name and the declaration, then measure each function reaching through them separately. A failure in one function then costs nothing already landed, and the record keeps its documentation either way.

Both PRs above ended in exactly that state — the header now says what the offsets mean, while the function bodies still spell them as retail needs. Without the rule, the natural instinct is to revert the whole file when the last step fails, losing the naming that was fine.

Recorded next to the raw-indexing rule it refines: that section says *when* a conversion is dangerous, this one says *which part to attempt first*.

Notes only, no source change.

- `make match` → `84a54ed7...a45c88`
- `make check-notes` OK

## 为什么

A 股年报 4 月才披露，扫描器此前只取年报（`_annual_rows` 硬编码 `end_date` 为 12-31），所以每年 5 月到次年 4 月，模型看到的都是一份**最多滞后 9 个月**的基本面。

长电科技（600584.SH）是个刻度清晰的例子：

| 口径 | 归母净利 |
|---|---|
| 2025 年报 | 15.65 亿 |
| TTM（2025H2 + 2026H1） | **19.39 亿（+24%）** |

2026 上半年归母净利同比 +79.4%、扣非 +84.7%，这个拐点纯年报口径要到 2027 年 4 月才看得见。

**注意：这次没有新增任何同步。** 季报/半年报本来就已经在库里——`_sync_statement_data` 按 `ann_date` 拉取、不按 period 过滤，`report_type` 也在 `_STATEMENT_REPORT_KEY_COLUMNS` 主键里。只改了扫描器的取数口径。

## 怎么做的

A 股定期报告是**年初至今累计**口径，所以 `TTM 流量 = 最新累计 + 上一年年报 − 上一年同期累计`。`_ttm_overlay()` 把年报序列的最后一期换成这个 TTM 行，前面的年报历史原样保留，按科目性质分三类：

| 科目 | 处理 | 为什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 流量（营收/净利/经营现金流/EBIT/资本开支） | 按上式滚动 | 累计口径 |
| 存量（总资产/有息负债/少数股东权益/投入资本） | 取最新一期 | 时点数，做差是错的 |
| 比率（ROE/ROIC/资产负债率） | **置空** | 半年 ROE 2.92% 不是年化值，年报 5.5% 不是最新值——两个都不能用 |

比率置空后，`debt_to_assets` 会从最新资产负债表重算、`roic` 退回 `NOPAT/投入资本` 自算，那才是真正的 TTM 值。

滚不出来（缺去年同期或上一年年报）就退回年报，`applied=False`。**流量列滚不出来时不会只换时点数**——年报的 EBIT 配最新的投入资本会算出一个假 ROIC。

## Reviewer 需要重点看的

1. **只有估值换了口径。** 质量闸门、近 5 年平均 ROIC/ROE、FCFF 为正年数、**内在价值同比**全部仍走年报序列。同比那一项尤其不能换：它要回答"这一年公司创造的价值是升是降"，拿一个和上一年重叠半年的滚动窗口去比，差值里一半是重叠期。`_snapshot()` 因此调用三次——TTM 一次出估值，年报两次出同比。有测试逐字段锁住这四项在两种口径下相等。
2. **`use_ttm=False` 可退回全年报口径**做对照，默认 `True`。
3. **输出新增 `valuation_basis` / `valuation_period_end`**，前端个股详情页（标签）和估值明细（「估值口径」行）都会显示，避免有人把 TTM 数字当年报数字读。
4. 顺带修了两个坑：`pd.concat` 拼全 NA 的比率列会退化出对不上的 dtype（pandas 已告警）；`datetime`/`pandas.Timestamp` 是 `date` 的子类，`isinstance(value, date)` 会放过带时分秒的值，`isoformat()` 带出 `T00:00:00`。

## 验证

新增 `backend/tests/test_value_investing_ttm.py`，10 个用例，数据直接取自长电科技三份真实定期报告：

- 滚动算得对：TTM 营收 397.93 亿、归母净利 19.39 亿，并显式断言 **≠ 半年报×2**（那样得 16.89 亿，差 2.5 亿）
- 和年报口径的差距就是报告说的那个数：15.65 → 19.39，+23.9%
- 最新期就是年报时不滚动 / 缺去年同期时退回年报 / 资产负债表取时点数不做差 / 比率置空且 `safe_float` 返回 None / 流量滚不出来时整个 overlay 放弃
- 端到端跑扫描器：`valuation_basis`、`valuation_period_end` 正确；TTM 能看见半年报的利润跳升而纯年报口径看不见；`avg_roic_pct`、`avg_roe_pct`、`fcf_positive_years`、`value_growth_pct` 在两种口径下逐字段相等

后端全量 **681 passed**；前端 25 tests passed、eslint 干净、build 通过。

## 未验证

- **三季报的滚动没有真实用例**。逻辑上和半年报一致（按「月-日」匹配去年同期，9-30 同样成立），但没有实测数据。
- 没在生产分析库上跑过全市场，不知道有多少只股票能成功滚出 TTM、多少只会退回年报。上线后建议看一眼 `valuation_basis` 的分布。

方法论背景与完整设计记录见 `docs/value-investing-scanner-handoff.md` 第 14 节。

author: rubensworks
body:
`countDistinctTerms(terms, filters)` selects its index with `getBestIndexTerms(componentOrders, terms)`, which scores component orders on `terms` alone and never looks at `filters`. When the filters pin the leading components, the chosen order may not be able to serve them, the `matchTerms.includes(false)` guard fires, and the call materialises every matching term through `getDistinctTerms`.

The effect is large enough to make the natural call unusable. Measured on a 1.08M-quad WatDiv dataset, counting the distinct objects of one predicate in one graph, both forms returning 1173:

| call | 2.5.0 | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `countDistinctTerms(['object'], filters)` | 410 ms | 0.45 us |
| `countDistinctTerms(['graph', 'predicate', 'object'], filters)` | 0.59 us | 0.45 us |
| `countDistinctTerms(['graph', 'predicate', 'object'])` (no filters) | 1.07 us | 0.92 us |

Timings are the median of five 50000-iteration samples after 20000 warm-up calls, each in a fresh process.

## Changes

- **Score the filtered components when picking the index.** `getBestIndexTerms` takes the filters and weighs a filtered component twice as heavily as a looked up term, so the order that matches the filters first wins. Without filters the scoring is unchanged.
- **Let a filter-pinned depth satisfy the distinctness check.** `countTermsInner` descends into exactly one sub-map at a depth whose filter is defined, so such a depth cannot count a term twice; only a depth that is neither counted nor pinned fans out. The guard now tests for that, and reduces to the old `matchTerms.includes(false)` when no filters are given.
- **Scan for the best score instead of sorting scored objects.** This drops an array allocation per lookup and accounts for the improvement in the two calls that were already fast.

## Compatibility

The new third parameter of `getBestIndexTerms` is optional and existing callers are unaffected. `getComponentOrderScore` is untouched. Every existing test passes unchanged, and coverage stays at 100%.

## Tests

`countDistinctTerms` under filters is asserted against every index configuration the suite parameterises over. Because the fast path requires an index order that can serve it, the path itself is asserted separately against the default index combinations, by spying on `getDistinctTerms` and requiring that it is not called. A companion test keeps the fallback honest: filtering on the subject alone still materialises. The first of these fails on the unpatched library.

## Benchmarks

CodSpeed reported all 34 benchmarks as untouched, because the one filtered counting case in the suite sits inside the `terms` scope, where ingestion and the unfiltered cases dwarf it.

This adds a `terms-filtered` scope that ingests and then only counts under filters: once for the distinct objects of one predicate in one graph, and once for the distinct predicate-object pairs of one graph. Both bind every component that precedes the counted terms in an available index, so both are answered from the index on this branch and materialised terms before it. The two cases cover the two halves of the change: the first is picked up by the filter-aware scoring, while the second selects the same index as before and only becomes fast through the relaxed distinctness check.

Measured locally on the `3 Map indexes (number) OPT-QUERY` approach at the benchmark dimension, as the median of 41 runs after 20 warm-up runs, the scope takes 7.97 ms with the previous index selection and 1.79 ms with this branch. The `terms` scope is unchanged at 14.6 ms either way, which matches what CodSpeed reported.

Because the scope is new, CodSpeed has no baseline for it on `master` and will list it as a new benchmark here rather than an improved one. It becomes a comparison point once this lands.

author: nathanclevenger
body:
Consumer side of dot-do/payments.do#2 for the `api` worker (apis.do). Pairs with the dot-do/payments.do PR that adds the `PaymentsInternal` entrypoint and the dot-do/headless.ly PR that bumps this submodule. No secret is created, read, or required.

## Call site

`src/index.ts` `GET /:id`, branch 2b (Stripe-native ids). Before: `c.env.PAYMENTS.fetch(new Request(url, { headers: c.req.raw.headers }))` to `/api/:id` — it forwarded the end user's inbound headers verbatim (including any `Authorization` and `Stripe-Account`) to a path payments.do never served (500). After:

- `wrangler.jsonc`: `{ "binding": "PAYMENTS", "service": "payments-do", "entrypoint": "PaymentsInternal" }`
- `PAYMENTS_RETRIEVE` (`src/type-synonyms.ts`) maps `cus/sub/inv/ch/prod/price` → `getCustomer/getSubscription/getInvoice/getCharge/getProduct/getPrice`; the handler calls `payments[method]({ id })` and returns the object. Only the id leaves this worker.
- `pi/pm/si/il/txn` have no read on payments.do → `404` with a `TODO(dot-do/payments.do#2)` naming the old `/api/:id` mismatch.
- RPC failure → `502 { error: { code: 'PAYMENTS_ERROR' } }` with payments.do's already-sanitized message; missing binding → 404.
- `src/payments-rpc.ts`: verbatim copy of payments.do `src/rpc-types.ts`; the binding is cast to `PaymentsInternalApi` at the call site (same pattern as the `AUTH`/`EVENTS` RPC casts).
- `worker-configuration.d.ts` regenerated (`PAYMENTS: Service /* entrypoint PaymentsInternal from payments-do */`).

## Tests (`test/entity-payments.test.ts`; 81 pass in the workers pool, `tsc --noEmit` clean in `src/`)

- `cus_*` resolves through `getCustomer` called exactly once with `{ id }` — the fake binding's `fetch` spy is never called
- each of `sub/inv/ch/prod/price` reaches only its method
- an inbound `Authorization`, `Stripe-Account`, `Cookie`, `x-tenant` never reaches the binding (input keys are exactly `['id']`)
- `pi/pm/si/il/txn` answer 404 and call nothing
- RPC rejection → 502 with the message; absent binding → 404
- `PAYMENTS_RETRIEVE` keys ⊆ `STRIPE_PREFIXES`

## Review fix (03b7bce): verified caller required

`GET /:id` is optional-auth, so the lookup would have returned full Stripe objects (PII, card details) to anyone holding an id. The Stripe branch now requires `verifiedUser` — set by the auth middleware only after `AUTH.verifyToken` succeeded or from the tamper-proof `cf.actor` (`user` alone is filled in for anonymous callers too). Anonymous or unverifiable callers get `401 AUTH_REQUIRED` before the binding is touched, which also closes the id-existence oracle. Tests: anonymous → 401 and no method call; forged token → 401; anonymous missing id → 401 with `getCustomer` never called; the two stale `landing.test.ts` assertions (accidental 500) now assert 401. **84 pass.**

Known leftover (pre-existing, non-blocking): `STRIPE_PREFIXES`/`PAYMENTS_RETRIEVE` use `inv`, but real Stripe invoice ids are `in_…`, so that mapping never fires in practice.

## Deploy

Deploy payments.do (with the entrypoint) **before** this worker; a consumer deploy binding a missing entrypoint fails. Then `pnpm deploy` here.

author: koufan-de-king
body:
## Summary

Adds `provisionAccount`, an admin-only RPC mutation that creates a target subject's anchor
`accounts` row **and** its mandatory default `projects` row, transactionally — closing a real gap
where a Keycloak-authenticated user with no `accounts` row had no path, self-service or admin, to
ever get one, and could never complete sign-in.

## Related Issues

Closes #720

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] CI/CD or tooling

## Changes Made

- New `Permission::AccountProvision` (`account:provision`), admin-only via `lightbridge-admin`'s
  `*` — never granted to `lightbridge-editor`/`lightbridge-viewer`.
- New `procedure.provisionAccount(subject, email, name?): Account` in `authz.cstack`, wired through
  `rpc_authorize.rs` — same self/admin split shape as the existing `revokeSubjectSessions`.
- `StoreRepo::provision_account`: one transaction, mints the subject's ANCHOR account
  (`id = subject`) plus its default `projects` row (`is_default` computed by the existing
  `projects_set_is_default` trigger); a duplicate subject or colliding `billing_identity` is
  `Error::Conflict`, never a partial write.
- `docs/rbac.md`: new permission table row + "Account provisioning" narrative section.
- Tests: repo-layer conflict coverage (duplicate subject, colliding `billing_identity`), RBAC
  gating (forbidden without permission, admin success over real RPC dispatch), and an end-to-end
  regression test driving a real mock-Keycloak `/idp/callback` flow through a provisioned
  subject — proving both halves of the incident (missing account AND missing default project) are
  actually fixed, not just the account row in isolation.

## Checklist

- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Tests added/updated for changes
- [x] All tests pass (`just all-checks`)
- [x] Documentation updated if needed

## Security Considerations

Does this PR have security implications? (authentication, certificates, cryptography, etc.)

- [ ] No security impact
- [x] Security impact reviewed (describe below)

This adds a new admin-write capability that creates an `accounts` row for an arbitrary,
operator-supplied subject — a meaningful trust boundary, given the same rigor as the existing
`revokeSubjectSessions` precedent it mirrors:

- Gated behind a brand-new permission (`account:provision`), reachable only via
  `lightbridge-admin`'s `*` wildcard — never granted to `editor`/`viewer` by default, unlike
  `account:create`.
- Does **not** reopen ADR-0024's decision to remove implicit mint-on-login: no self-service or
  automatic path is added, only an explicit, permission-gated admin action, structurally
  incapable of running without the RBAC gate passing first (enforced in the generated schema
  `@allow` clause, not just application code — verified via `schema_policy_sync_tests`).
- Transactional: a partial write (an orphaned account with no default project, or vice versa) is
  not possible — verified by a dedicated test that a `billing_identity` collision on the second
  insert rolls back the account row inserted earlier in the same transaction.
- No new dependency, no change to existing authentication/token-validation logic, no change to
  `createAccount`'s self-service semantics.

## Testing

How was this tested?

- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [ ] Manual testing with `just it-test`
- [x] Other: schema/permission-map drift-check (`schema_policy_sync_tests`, verifies the hand-written
  `@allow` clause byte-for-byte matches the generator's expected output)

---

## Intent / Source of Truth

A production user (`sub = c0b57b18-7f4e-4fdf-b9b7-8d60378acd8a`) hit `/ui/error` on every sign-in
attempt, WebAuthn or password, because `authz-idp`'s `/idp/callback` refuses to complete sign-in
for a Keycloak-authenticated subject with no `accounts` row (ADR-0024's 2026-08-25 correction
deliberately removed the old auto-provisioning branch). Investigation found no supported recovery
path exists today: `createAccount` is self-service only and cannot target another subject;
ADR-0025's `NoAccount` bootstrap fallback (a brand-new subject's own raw Keycloak token calling
`createAccount` directly) is structurally unreachable in production, since `authz-api`'s bearer
middleware there validates against `authz-idp`'s own JWKS, not Keycloak's — so that token never
passes signature verification. The user was unblocked with a manual SQL `INSERT` directly against
production, which is what `provisionAccount` now replaces with a safe, auditable, RBAC-gated tool.

Source of truth: #720 (filed from this incident, citing ADR-0024/0025/0026 and the live production
investigation).

## Verification

- `cargo test -p lightbridge-authz-api-key --features it-tests --test provision_account_repo_tests`
  — 3/3 pass (anchor account + default project creation, duplicate-subject conflict,
  colliding-billing-identity conflict with rollback verified).
- `cargo test -p lightbridge-authz-rest --features it-tests provision_account` — 2/2 pass
  (`provision_account_without_permission_is_forbidden`,
  `provision_account_admin_creates_account_for_target_subject`).
- `cargo test -p lightbridge-authz-rest --features it-tests provisioned_subject_completes_browser_sso_callback`
  — 1/1 pass, the regression test proving a `provisionAccount`-only seed is sufficient for a real
  `/idp/callback` browser flow to succeed end-to-end.
- `cargo test -p lightbridge-authz-rest --test schema_policy_sync_tests` — confirms the hand-written
  `@allow` clause in `authz.cstack` matches the generator's expected output exactly.
- Full `it-tests` suites: `lightbridge-authz-api-key` 14/14 binaries clean;
  `lightbridge-authz-rest` clean aside from two pre-existing, unrelated parallel-test flakes
  (different tests failed across two separate full-suite runs, neither touching this change, both
  confirmed passing in isolation — a known flake class this repo's own docs already describe).
- `just all-checks` equivalent (`cargo fmt`, `cargo deny check`, `cargo fix`,
  `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --all-targets --all-features`)
  — all clean.

- [x] Verified locally (`just all-checks`)

## AI Usage Declaration

Declare whether/how AI was used:

- [ ] Not used
- [x] AI-assisted (describe what AI was used for below)

Investigated the production incident, drafted issue #720, designed the implementation plan
(reviewed and approved before coding), wrote the schema/permission/repo/procedure changes and all
new tests, and ran the full local verification (it-tests, schema drift-check, all-checks) described
above. All generated code and tests were reviewed against this repo's existing precedents
(`revokeSubjectSessions`, `create_account`) before being written, and every test was run against a
live Postgres/Redis stack, not merely inspected.

> AI may accelerate the work, but it must not launder ignorance into polished artifacts.
> Governance: https://adorsys-gis.github.io/ai-governance/

body:
## Summary

Two related changes, both driven by the same finding: of 35 live paper-trading books, 17
were near-duplicate factory-combo strategies — just two leg-family pairings (`tsmom+tsmom`,
`tsmom+low_vol_xsec`) reparameterized by lookback window, because the daily promotion
ranking never checked what was already live.

- **Backend cap** (`research/factory_run.py`): live combo books are now capped at 3 per
  "shape" (the sorted pair of the two legs' primitive families, via a new shared
  `factory.combo_shape()`). A cycle whose combo wins the ranking but whose shape is already
  at 3 live books falls back to the best individual candidate instead. The combo is still
  fully evaluated and logged to `graveyard.csv` either way — existing over-cap books are
  never touched (retirement stays Dave's manual call per DOCTRINE v1.6; this is
  forward-looking only). Documented in `CLAUDE.md`'s "Strategy factory" section, same
  category as the existing `MAX_FACTORY_PROMOTED`.
- **Dashboard grouping** (`frontend/src/components/RowList.tsx`): the Paper Books default
  view now groups books by a new `group_key`/`group_label` pair — computed server-side by
  `dashboard.book_group()` (splitting the existing catch-all "combo" family bucket by shape)
  and exposed as two new, purely additive fields on `/api/books/summary`.

Built via `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` against
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-combo-shape-cap-and-grouping.md` — 5 tasks, each with its
own passing task-scoped review, plus a final whole-branch review (0 Critical/Important
findings; 3 cheap Minor findings fixed in a follow-up commit and re-reviewed clean; 2 Minor
findings parked — a missing test pinning group-ordering behavior, and adding a member count
to group headers, which is a product/UI call for Dave rather than something to build
unilaterally).

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` — 726 passed, 1 skipped, **2 known pre-existing failures
  unrelated to this branch** (confirmed identical on `main` before this branch started, from
  an earlier same-day commit — see below).

- [x] `cd frontend && npx tsc -b --noEmit` — clean.

- `tests/test_claude_md_budget.py::test_claude_md_stays_within_its_token_budget` — `CLAUDE.md`

  further. The addition earns its place per the test's own docstring criteria (a load-bearing
  rule, not narrative) — but the budget itself could use a trim or a raised cap as a

- Turkey: (1) new real-estate-only 4th disclaimer (title deed/property valuation), added via the same conditional-append pattern as Latvia/Vanuatu; (2) GCS legal & processing fee is now route-based — 20,000 bank deposit / 15,000 real estate (5,000/dependant unchanged); (3) the main-applicant fee line drops the "— main applicant" suffix whenever the per-dependant fee is $0 (confirmed unique to Turkey — no other program uses this exact fee-name pattern).

author: mrchypark
body:
Add membership recovery across Rhiza's Go/Rust hosts and Kubernetes Operator. With a surviving quorum, the Operator replaces a fenced voter with a fresh WAL-bound learner. After quorum loss it restores a sealed source into a new generation, rotates credentials, and preserves archived data and request deduplication.

The opt-in automatic loop detects faults, verifies an authenticated quorum, persists incident identity and policy, and orchestrates fencing and recovery. It provisions learners, fences and explicitly aborts a lost learner before retrying a fresh identity, and resumes through Operator restarts. Immutable workload ownership prevents manual requests from bypassing the automatic journal.

Kubernetes fencing uses immutable namespaced `RhizaFence` requests. Before dispatching recovery, the Operator validates identity-bound evidence for process termination, recreation blocking and storage quiescence. Its service account cannot write fencing status. HTTPS fencing remains supported; absent or incomplete executor evidence leaves recovery pending.

Real chaos exposed learner startup failure while writers advanced archive HEAD. Archive loading now retries with validated immutable extent references retained only for that bounded load, preserving the exact final HEAD/version and manager CAS checks. This avoids restarting the complete historical download after every append. Internal publication/trim reloads use the same path. Errors remain bounded, cancellation and corruption preserve installed state, and no partially validated head is published.

## Validation

- The kind CI harness runs the real Operator, Kubernetes API, three voters, learners and MinIO. Its CI-only fencing executor enforces admission barriers, verifies CRI termination and quiesces dedicated storage. The harness injects faults without manually creating recovery requests, learners or fencing approvals.
- **Final candidate `32877c73bd985ebb9ada7f281d73382f654a66b4` passed all seven CI jobs**: Go tests/race/vet, Rust on Linux/macOS, containers, real membership E2E, manual Operator chaos and automatic Operator chaos. [CI run](https://github.com/mrchypark/rhiza/actions/runs/34558473644).
- **Seven unattended scenarios passed**: intact-WAL restart, emptyDir loss/replacement, executor outage with Operator restart, learner deletion with automatic fence/abort/fresh retry, completed barrier persistence across executor restart, live-process QUIC partition barrier, and generation recovery. **371 acknowledged rows / 371 recovered**, abort revision **349**, request deduplication preserved, new-generation write successful. [Automatic job](https://github.com/mrchypark/rhiza/actions/runs/34558473644/job/103136100886); artifact `automatic-operator-chaos-34558473644`.
- The final startup logs show both learners starting successfully during continued writes. Recovery progress records show removal, addition freeze, actual learner loss, certified abort, fresh addition and completion. Expected QUIC quorum errors occur during injected loss; no moving-HEAD startup failure recurred in this final run.
- Deterministic loader regression tests fail on the old implementation and pass with the fix, covering one GET per validated extent across retries, bounded churn, cancellation and corruption. Local recovery/node tests and focused race tests pass; a separate MiMo read-only review found no additional issue in HEAD/CAS/pin handling.
- The separate [Performance workflow](https://github.com/mrchypark/rhiza/actions/runs/34558473721) is still running. No performance improvement is claimed from these correctness tests.

## Operational boundary

StatefulSet + emptyDir remains the deployment basis, with membership opt-in on all voters. The shipped execution fixture is for a disposable single-node kind cluster and dedicated MinIO, **not a production node agent or shared-storage fencing provider**. Production needs a trusted environment-specific executor. Pod DELETE alone is never proof. Physical host isolation and multi-node partitions are not qualified here; passive fixed read replicas do not participate in dynamic membership.

An earlier removal-stage HTTP 500 lacked a saved response body, so its exact cause cannot be retrospectively proven. Bounded/redacted diagnostics and recovery progress artifacts now retain future errors; this is distinct from the subsequently confirmed archive startup failure.

The original dirty worktree is preserved. Deployment instructions, automatic recovery design and instruction-led MiMo delegation rules are included.

author: eduardtomasek
body:
Two commits: take the stray file out of this repository, then stop it happening in every project the tool wires up.

## 1. `Remove docs/.DS_Store and ignore it`

`docs/.DS_Store` was committed by accident in `e87a298` ("version 5 artifacts"). It is macOS Finder state, not content. `git rm --cached` + deleted from disk, `.DS_Store` added to this repo's `.gitignore`. It was the only `.DS_Store` in the repository, tracked or untracked.

## 2. `Make --apply ignore .DS_Store in every project`

`.DS_Store` joins `.grepai/` and `.gitnexus/` in `_DEFAULT_GITIGNORE_ENTRIES`, so `--apply` writes it everywhere.

No consumer needed changing — `_ensure_gitignore`, `gitignore_ok` and both config templates read the tuple generically:

- `_ensure_gitignore` appends **only missing** entries, so a hand-maintained `.gitignore` keeps its own lines and order, and a project that already ignores `.DS_Store` gets nothing appended.
- Projects wired by an older version report `.gitignore += …` as drift until their next `--apply`. `gitignore_entries` in `defaults.toml` opts out.

Both messages that described the tuple as "the index directories" now say "the configured entries" — accurate now that it is not only index directories.

## Verification

- `./test/unit.sh` **294/294** (two new tests), `./test/run.sh` **53/53**.
- Live on a clean project: `.gitignore += .grepai/ .gitnexus/ .DS_Store`.
- Second `--apply` on the same project: `.gitignore already covers the configured entries`, no duplicate line.
- Preview on this repo, which already ignores it: `keep .gitignore covers the configured entries` — no drift.
- New tests cover both the clean-project result and the append-only guarantee against a hand-written `.gitignore` that already has `.DS_Store`.

`gitnexus detect_changes`: low risk, no affected execution flows.

author: axentrio
body:
# Remember a refused reschedule time for the conversation

Branch `fm/axentrio-refused-time-memory`, head `146019914f5677097909cb3768f5ea19c6bb658d`, 3 commits.

## The defect, in customer terms

The customer asks to move an appointment to a time the business cannot take. The
assistant refuses it. One turn later the assistant offers that same time back, as
if the customer had already chosen it. To the customer the assistant forgets what
it said a moment earlier.

The booking path did not have this problem. `api/src/agent/refused-named-time.ts`
remembers a refused named time for the conversation, and `absorbNamedTimeRefusal`
in `api/src/agent/agent.service.ts` records it. The reschedule path did not reach
that recorder.

## Root cause

`reschedule_booking` is in `BOOKING_MUTATION_TOOLS`
(`api/src/agent/agent.service.ts:141`), so its refusal did set the in-run flag.
But the recorder read the time from `startDate`, `startTime` or `preferredTime`
only. `reschedule_booking` names its time in `newStartTime`
(`api/src/agent/tools/booking.tool.ts:1652`). So `localDate` stayed undefined,
the recorder returned one line before it wrote, and the next turn read no
refusal.

`REFUSED_TIME_ARGS` now holds every argument name a refusing booking tool can
carry its time in, `newStartTime` included. The first match wins. The list also
replaces a four-term boolean chain, which keeps `absorbNamedTimeRefusal` inside
the complexity budget and makes a future argument name free.

## Deterministic against transient

Review found that the first fix reached only `rescheduleMode: request`, which is
the default. On an `auto` service the same refusal arrives under a different
error code, so the defect stayed. Widening to the whole `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` code
was rejected, because that code carries two different kinds of "no":

- **Deterministic**: a rule about the clock. Past, the notice window, the
  booking horizon, a closed date, or outside opening hours. Asking again returns
  the same answer, so the refusal is remembered.
- **Transient**: availability. That one slot is taken. It can free up minutes
  later, so a customer who asks again deserves the real answer. Remembering it
  for 24 hours would hide a time that is bookable again.

`refusedByClockRule` in `api/src/agent/agent.service.ts:213` draws that line. It
matches the full error string, not the bare code, because the code alone cannot
tell the two apart.

## Refusal codes, classified

Each cause is read from the throwing code, not inferred from the code name.

| Error | Thrown at | Path | Cause | Remembered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `REQUEST_OUTSIDE_WINDOW` (`requestInPast`, `requestTooSoon`, `requestTooFar`, `requestClosedDay`, out-of-hours) | `internal.provider.ts:2489`, `:2492`, `:2496`, `:2499`, `:2510` | create and request | deterministic: past, notice, horizon, closed date, hours | yes |
| `REQUEST_OUTSIDE_WINDOW` (`rescheduleOutsideHours` and siblings) | `internal.provider.ts:4359` | reschedule, `request` mode | deterministic: same clock rules | yes |
| `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` + `SLOT_NOT_OFFERABLE_ON_RESCHEDULE` | `internal.provider.ts:4053`, `:2854` | reschedule, `auto` mode | deterministic: `occupied` is false, so nothing in the diary overlaps and the engine would never have offered the slot | yes |
| `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` + `SLOT_TAKEN_ON_RESCHEDULE` | `internal.provider.ts:4053`, `:2854`, `:2938` | reschedule | transient: `occupied` is true, or a `23P01` exclusion race | no |
| `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` + `SLOT_NOT_OFFERABLE` | `internal.provider.ts:1761` | create, auto-book | deterministic: same `occupied` is false test | yes |
| `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` + `SLOT_TAKEN_ON_CREATE` | `internal.provider.ts:1761`, `:1917`, `:1933`, `:4652` | create | transient: taken, or a `23P01` / `23505` race | no |
| `CAPACITY_REACHED` | `enforceServiceDayCapacity`, called at `internal.provider.ts:1577`, `:2501`, `:2899`, `:4105` | create and reschedule | day cap. A cancellation frees it, so it is not deterministic for that named time | no, see the gap below |
| `CHANGE_NOT_ALLOWED` | `booking.tool.ts:183` | reschedule and cancel | policy on changing at all, not a statement about the named time | no |

The `SLOT_NOT_OFFERABLE` text names a full day among its possible reasons, which
would conflate the day cap into a deterministic refusal. It does not, at these
two throw sites. `computeSlots` reads the cap only when `business` and
`dayLedger` are supplied (`slot-engine.ts:239-266`), and neither call site
supplies them (`internal.provider.ts:1748-1756` and `:4040-4047`). So the cap
cannot be the reason there.

## Documented gap

`CAPACITY_REACHED` is not remembered. The day cap is a real refusal of that named
date, but a cancellation can free it inside the 24-hour window, so it behaves
like availability rather than like a clock rule. Remembering it would risk the
opposite bug this change exists to avoid. A customer who asks again on a capped
day gets a fresh answer.

## Auto-book parity

The same gap existed on `create_booking` for an auto-book service
(`internal.provider.ts:1761`). It is fixed in the same pass, so the booking path
and the move path now behave alike.

## Preserved

`api/src/agent/refused-named-time.ts` keeps its single store, its fail-open
behaviour when Redis is unavailable, and its 24-hour expiry. None of them are
tightened. The scope stays a refused NAMED time; this is not a general
preference memory.

## Tests

`api/src/__tests__/unit/refused-named-time-reschedule.test.ts` drives two turns
of one conversation over an in-memory Redis, with the real helper and the real
"customer moved off that date" rule. Every assertion reads what the customer is
shown. None asserts a Redis call.

1. **A refused move is not offered again.** Turn one has the notice refuse a
   move to 10:00. Turn two still lists the times. Without `newStartTime` in
   `REFUSED_TIME_ARGS` this fails: the reply ships with no times at all under
   "Kies hieronder een moment", so the customer is asked to pick from an empty
   list.
2. **An auto-mode move and an auto-book create, both refused under
   `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`, are remembered too.** This is the case the first fix
   missed.
3. **A freed slot is still offerable.** A move refused because the slot was
   taken is forgotten. By the next turn the slot is free, the check lists it, and
   it counts as the customer's own hour. This is the guard against the new bug
   the obvious fix would have created: without it, a 24-hour memory would hide a
   bookable time behind retry chips.
4. **The memory still clears.** The customer names another day, that time is
   taken normally, and the times are not listed again.

Documentation: `docs/booking-rules.md` now states that the refusal lasts the
conversation, which refusals count, and pins the new test.

## Pipeline

Run `01M2650T77BWMF7T0XF9RYJ0MV`. Intent, rebase, review, test, document, lint
and push all passed. The `pr` step failed on this repository's known credential
wall:

```
step pr failed: gh pr create: pull request create failed: GraphQL: must be a collaborator (createPullRequest): exit status 1
```

The branch is pushed. No shared configuration was changed.

author: gwendall
body:
v0.6.6 is published and certified on every surface: npm, the GitHub release, the server image, the Python wheel, and the Fly private beta. This advances every public surface to describe it.

| surface | fact |
| --- | --- |
| tag | `v0.6.6` at `dffd2d0` |
| server image | `sha256:b8fcdc83…` |
| Python wheel | `2976b8bd…` |
| release run | [34507952784](https://github.com/gwendall/tasq/actions/runs/34507952784) |
| certification | [34508717494](https://github.com/gwendall/tasq/actions/runs/34508717494) |

The three acquisition manifests advanced automatically for the first time - the gate added in #237 is what made that a step nobody has to remember.

## Two gaps this release found

**PyPI serves two indexes that do not update together.** The wheel digest is read from the JSON API; the certifier's `pip download` resolves against the simple index. Two minutes after publication the certification failed with `from versions: 0.4.0, 0.6.3, 0.6.4, 0.6.5` - the wheel was public and the index it installs from had not caught up. `pypiWheelSha256` now waits until the simple index lists the exact file the certifier will ask for.

**A failed certification forced the rest of the release to be done by hand.** No registry accepts a version twice, so rerunning `release:publish-surfaces` failed on the publication step it had already completed. Hand-dispatching the remainder is how v0.6.2 shipped without two of its surfaces. Publication is now decided by asking the registry whether the version is already there, not by rerunning the workflow, so a resumed release re-certifies and continues. This release was completed that way.

## Verification

`pnpm verify:quick` green.

`DevelopmentBundleVersion` documents itself as tracking "the current release line with a `-dev` suffix so a development bundle is dated honestly". The line moved to 0.9.0 when `gds-v0.9.0-rc.1` was published on 2026-09-08, and `gds-v0.8.0` became a shipped release on 2026-08-30 — but all three version constants still said `0.8.0-dev`, so every development bundle compiled since then, the private estate's included, was stamped with the previous line.

- `core/compiler/types.go` — the constant that stamps development bundles.
- `core/cli/root.go` — the CLI fallback version for a build without ldflags.
- `core/cmd/gds-controller/main.go` — the same, for the controller.

Golden control-plane projections are regenerated because the bundle version is part of their rendered header, and this repository's own `.gds/` projections are regenerated through `gds generate repository --plan/--apply` with a binary built from this commit — otherwise `GDS_CONTEXT_POLICY_BUNDLE_MISMATCH` fails `core/cli`, `core/context` and `core/assurance`.

author: johnitvn
body:
Closes #221

## Description

Root cause, evidence-first — the emitter is proto (moonrepo), not pnpm. Every claim below is labeled: source-verified means read from shipped source (holds for any machine running these pins); observed means measured on the authoring machine only.

1. The emitting binary (observed): /home/johnitvn/.proto/tools/proto/0.60.2/proto carries the exact banner at byte offset 3476854 (grep -aob "Detected an AI" → 3476854), and its CHANGELOG documents the feature ("Added automatic NDJSON output for detected AI agents and bots", plus the global --reporter option and PROTO_REPORTER env var; reporters: text, json, ndjson). No pnpm on this machine contains the string: binary grep for "Detected an AI" / "AI agent" over the corepack dist shim, the nvm node lib, and every cached pnpm (10.32.0, 11.15.1, 11.20.0, 11.22.0, 11.23.0, 11.24.0, 11.25.0, 12.3.2, 12.3.4, plus proto's tool installs) returned zero hits. The repo history hits for the string are only this fixture's own assertion.
2. Why a bare spawned pnpm ever reached proto (observed): inside a moon task the PATH is proto-first. /proc/PID/environ of a live moon-spawned vitest worker begins PATH=/home/johnitvn/.proto/tools/node/24.20.0/bin:/home/johnitvn/.proto/tools/node/globals/bin:/home/johnitvn/.proto/tools/proto/0.60.2:/home/johnitvn/.proto/shims:... — so the fixture's spawnSync("pnpm") resolves to /home/johnitvn/.proto/shims/pnpm, an ELF shim that execs the proto CLI. Outside moon (isolated runs) PATH resolves pnpm to the nvm corepack shim first — no proto, no banner. CI has neither a proto-first PATH nor an agent ambient, hence never failed.
3. The detection inputs (source-verified, and authoritative over any bisect): proto 0.60.2's Cargo.toml pins ai_env = "0.1.3", whose detect_agent_from_vars reads exactly nineteen env inputs — seventeen fire on non-empty presence (CURSOR_TRACE_ID, CURSOR_AGENT, GEMINI_CLI, CODEX_SANDBOX, CODEX_CI, CODEX_THREAD_ID, ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT, AUGMENT_AGENT, OPENCODE_CLIENT, OPENCODE, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE, REPL_ID, COPILOT_CLI, COPILOT_MODEL, COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL, COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN), two are value-gated there (CURSOR_EXTENSION_HOST_ROLE only on "agent-exec"; AI_AGENT only on a self-id the crate classifies). The original empirical bisect (observed on this machine: env -i, one candidate var at a time at a generic non-empty value, proto run pnpm -- --version) fired sixteen of these and is superseded by the source as authority: a generic-value bisect is structurally blind to value-gated checks — it wrongly cleared CURSOR_EXTENSION_HOST_ROLE (AI_AGENT fired only because its tested value was one the crate classifies) — and its candidate list omitted CODEX_CI and OPENCODE entirely. The source also settles two edge cases: CLAUDE_CODE_IS_COWORK is consulted only to refine the classification after CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_CODE already fired (it cannot flip the reporter alone), and the crate additionally probes the filesystem for /opt/.devin, which no env strip can cover.

Intermittency, restated per adversarial review: DETECTION is var-based and deterministic (source-verified, item 3). The banner's APPEARANCE is separately event-gated inside proto (observed): it fires on proto's exec-error paths, and healthy shim invocations print nothing — so a surviving marker is necessary for a banner but not always sufficient on a given run. The prior claim that the residual variance sat in "which binary the task PATH resolves for that particular run", and the evidence offered for it ("100/100 banners under 20x concurrent shim invocations"), are withdrawn: an adversarial reconstruction of that concurrency experiment returned 0/100, the number is not reproducible, and the event-gating above is the observed mechanism. Pre-fix, the failure still needed the two halves it always did — a proto-first resolution (moon-driven runs, the pre-push hook) plus a firing var surviving the strip (agent-driven machines, via the ambient AI_AGENT); isolation (corepack-first PATH) and CI (no proto, no agent ambient) could not fail. The fix removes the necessary half: a firing-var-free env cannot trip the detection through any resolution path.

The fix, test-local, product code untouched: AGENT_MARKERS now mirrors ai_env 0.1.3's detect_agent_from_vars — all nineteen inputs, in the crate's evaluation order, read from the crate source pinned by proto 0.60.2's Cargo.toml — plus AGENT, kept from the original strip as defense in depth for detectors beyond proto's. The exact-key strip covers any value; for the two value-gated inputs this is a deliberate over-strip, correct for a sanitizing fixture whose env pin asserts key absence (a value-conditional rule could not guarantee it) and whose legs need no non-agent extension-host role or self-id to survive the spawn env. A second pin enumerates the nineteen crate inputs (AGENT deliberately unpinned — it is not one of them) and fails loudly on trimming any enumerated entry, on every machine, not only where the entry is ambient. The existing .not.toMatch(/Detected an AI agent environment/) assertion is unchanged. PROTO_REPORTER=text was considered and rejected: forcing a reporter masks detection rather than neutralizing the environment. #189's separate items (--prefer-offline, certification runBin env) are not folded in.

## Type of change

- [x] Foundation / tooling

## Could this fail silently?

- A future proto bump adding or tightening detection inputs could reintroduce the banner when an ambient carries an input the list lacks. The strip is source-derived and explicit rather than a fuzzy prefix match: it covers exactly what ai_env 0.1.3 checks today, so a crate change needs an explicit strip-list addition — new inputs are not silently covered, which is the honest limit of an enumeration. Within this pin, the trim pin fails loudly on deleting any enumerated entry, and the env pin plus the reporter assertion fail loudly wherever a pinned marker is ambient.
- Machines without proto (CI) never exercised this floor; the pins are vacuous there by design — the same posture as #168's GIT_DIR pin, which is also vacuous on machines whose ambient carries no leaked git context.
- Expected and out of this fixture's scope: moon's own task processes (vitest, tsc) are proto-shimmed too, so with an agent-bearing ambient a banner can still prefix the TASK's stream — that is the task process's env, not the install's output, and cannot satisfy the leg's assertions.
