author: mmushrif05
body:
## What broke

From the moment #121 (`a482fa5`) deployed at 17:41, **the live site answered `503 DEPLOYMENT_UNSAFE` on every route**. The sign-in screen showed it as *"This deployment is not configured safely enough to serve requests."*

## Root cause — two faults, both in #121

1. **It measured the wrong thing.** The new check in `config.validate()` summed the whole of `process.env` inside the running function. That is the Lambda *runtime's* environment — its session token (~900 bytes on its own), its paths, its trace id — none of which count against the 4 KB ceiling it was measuring. An ordinary deployment therefore read as past the warning line.
2. **It refused on it.** The finding went onto the `problems` list, and `netlify/functions/fintech-api.js` refuses every route but `/health` on any problem. A warning became an outage.

Every unit test was green while the site was down: nothing loaded the adapter under the environment a function actually has, and the refusal path itself had no test.

## The fix

- `validate()` returns **two lists**. *Problems* are what a server refuses to start on and the function refuses every route but `/health` on. *Warnings* are what nothing refuses on; `/health` lists them under `configured.warnings`.
- The environment-size estimate is a **warning**, because it is an estimate: the runtime's own variables are now left out (`LAMBDA_RUNTIME_OWN`), Netlify's own are not knowable exactly, and a site that refuses every request on a guess is a site that is down on a guess.
- `tests/netlify-function.test.js` loads the real adapter under a Lambda-shaped environment and asserts: a sign-in request is served; a crowded environment is a warning on `/health` and still served; a real problem refuses, naming the variable and never a value. **Three of its four tests fail on `a482fa5`.**
- `.env.example`, `docs/DATA-LAYER.md`, `docs/ENVIRONMENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` corrected to say warning, with the outage recorded beside the limit it was meant to prevent.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| memory suite (`env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY npx jest`) | 2,451 passed |
| PostgreSQL suite | 2,487 passed, 122 suites |
| new test on the broken commit | 3 of 4 fail |
| `npm run lint` · `npm run typecheck` | 0 errors · clean |
| browser journeys | 10 passed |
| six doc generators | regenerated and committed |

author: pandeiro
body:
## Summary

Adds the **UX PR previews** workflow as a repo skill plus the Playwright capture harness it needs, so UI PRs ship desktop+mobile screenshots reviewers can see inline.

- **Skill** — `.agents/skills/ux-pr-previews/SKILL.md`: the end-to-end pattern (shot design → state tier → capture scenario → `docs/previews/<slug>/` README → commit PNGs → embed raw URLs in the PR body → post-merge lifecycle), the 3-tier prod-safety model (component harness / fake session / synthetic user), known traps, and a pre-PR checklist.
- **Harness** — `scripts/src/e2e/previews.ts`: screenshot-oriented sibling of `e2e/helpers.ts`. Owns the boilerplate so per-feature capture scenarios (`scenarios/previews-<slug>.ts`) stay thin:
  - viewport pairs (desktop 1280×800 / mobile 390×844, DSF 1) with per-kind `(pointer: …)` matchMedia pinning
  - fake authenticated sessions: far-future `expires_at` localStorage payload under `sb-<ref>-auth-token` — `getSession()` resolves locally, zero auth round-trips
  - `mockSupabase()`: table/RPC fixtures fulfilled locally + catch-all pass-through to prod with the `Authorization` header swapped back to the anon key, plus a `prodReads()` log of exactly what touched prod
  - visible-filtered waits (`waitForVisible`/`visibleFirst`), settle (fonts + scroll + frozen animations), clip/full-page capture, console-diagnostics surfacing
  - `prSnippet()`: ready-to-paste PR-body markdown with `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<head-branch>/docs/previews/<slug>/<file>.png` embeds
- **Docs pointers** — AGENTS.md PR-workflow note, PLAN.md §7 layout, `scripts/src/e2e/README.md`.

## Field-tested mechanics baked in

1. **CSS-gated duplicate layouts**: bare `waitForSelector` stalls on the hidden DOM-first copy (`hidden md:block` twins) — all waits/clips go through visible-filtered `.first`.
2. **Fake-session 401s**: Supabase's gateway rejects the fake Bearer before RLS, so pass-through reads get the anon key swapped in. Tables the fake user "owns" (`profiles`, `user_rides`) 401 even as anon (no anon policy) and must be mocked; **RPCs have no anon EXECUTE by default** — also mock them. The public catalog passes through fine.
3. **Route precedence is newest-first**: the first handler that fulfills wins, so `mockSupabase()` registers catch-alls *before* fixtures — discovered live when fixtures silently never fulfilled (401 storm), now documented so it doesn't get re-derived.

## Verification

Ran live against a dev server in a worktree (`:5199`, prod Supabase backend):

- fake-session `/me` rendered 3 fixture rides with manufacturer/park embeds, touch-gated hint visible on mobile only (pointer pinning works), fonts loaded, zero console errors
- logged-out board rendered via pure anon pass-through — `prodReads()` showed only `v_coaster_rankings`/`parks`, no unexpected tables
- temp scenario + verification PNGs deleted after the run (nothing stray committed)

`cd scripts && npm run typecheck` and prettier pass. No prod writes anywhere — no synthetic users seeded; anon reads only.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI gates green
- [ ] Reviewer skim of the skill doc + harness docstrings

author: jonasmatthias
body:
Switch the publish workflow to **npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC)** — no long-lived `NPM_TOKEN` secret, and provenance is generated automatically.

- `id-token: write` permission mints the OIDC token npm verifies.
- Node 24 + `npm install -g npm@latest` guarantees npm ≥ 11.5.1 (OIDC minimum).
- `npm publish` with no token / no `--access` / no `--provenance` flags — public access and provenance are inferred for a public package from a public repo.
- `registry-url` is kept; the `cache: npm` step is dropped (recommended for release builds).

## One-time setup on npmjs.com (required before the first release)
Package → **Settings → Trusted Publisher** → GitHub Actions:
- Organization or user: `Graphmasters`
- Repository: `lane-status-viewer`
- Workflow filename: `publish.yml`
- Environment: *(blank)*

Then publishing is just `gh release create v0.1.0 --generate-notes`.

author: streeft
body:
O segundo gargalo do roteiro de plataforma ([`docs/14-plataforma-selecao.md`](docs/14-plataforma-selecao.md)), em sete commits. Decisão registrada como [D-57](docs/DECISIONS.md).

## O problema

O catálogo tinha **um** universo: materiais. Um estágio de árvore só podia ser "filtre por pasta da taxonomia de materiais", e a pergunta que o método de Ashby realmente faz — *que materiais este processo conforma*, *que processos unem estes materiais* — não tinha onde ser feita. É o exercício 9 do manual do EduPack, e ele é uma **junção entre tabelas**.

## O que entrou

- **`ProcessClass`, `Process` e `material_process`** — taxonomia hierárquica com a mesma forma de `MaterialClass`, e uma associação N–N com chave composta.
- **Um terceiro tipo de estágio, `process`** — mantém os materiais que **algum** processo selecionado serve, por pasta (`process_class_slugs`) ou por folha (`process_slugs`), com `include_descendants`.
- **Rotas de leitura** `GET /api/processes` e `GET /api/processes/classes`.
- **Universo demonstrativo semeado** — 7 pastas em 3 famílias, 13 processos, 22 vínculos, tudo `is_demo`.
- **Relatório e laudo** descrevem o estágio novo por extenso, com a palavra "algum de" dita em voz alta.
- **A ficha do material lista os processos compatíveis**, agrupados por família — parte da lacuna do Datasheet.

## Três decisões, cada uma com alternativa plausível

1. **A família do processo é a raiz da taxonomia, não uma coluna enum.** Dado semeado, não schema: um operador acrescenta família sem migração, `app/domain/taxonomy.py` é reaproveitado sem uma linha nova, e não existe uma segunda verdade capaz de discordar da árvore.
2. **A associação não carrega propriedade nenhuma.** Um número sobre o par (faixa de espessura, custo por peça) precisaria da mesma proveniência de `MaterialPropertyValue`; inventá-lo violaria o princípio 1. O vínculo continua vínculo.
3. **Semântica de "algum", não de "todos".** "Soldável **e** forjável" são dois estágios, e a pilha do P0-1 já os intersecta. Há teste provando a composição.

E duas regras herdadas sem exceção: **ausência não passa** (material sem processo vinculado não sobrevive a um estágio de processo — não se seleciona sobre dado que não se tem) e **um estágio é uma pergunta só** (enviar os campos de outro tipo é recusado, nunca ignorado).

## Defeitos achados fora de teste

1. **O funil reportava `in_tree` para um estágio de processo** — ou seja, dizia ao leitor que a seleção filtrou por classe de material quando filtrou por processo. Achado **lendo o documento renderizado**, não a asserção. Virou `in_process`, com `in_tree` preservado literalmente.
2. **Reabrir um estudo salvo passava por um ternário de dois ramos** que teria transformado um estágio de processo em estágio de limites vazio, sem aviso e sem o verificador de tipos reclamar. Virou `switch` exaustivo — e o `tsc` provou a exaustividade.
3. **Aceitar uma sugestão da IA numa pilha sem estágio de limites descartava a sugestão em silêncio** (pré-existente, alcançável agora).
4. **Acessibilidade:** os seletores múltiplos usavam um `<label>` que envolvia legenda **e** dica, então o nome acessível era as duas concatenadas — o controle anunciava o próprio texto de ajuda como parte do nome. Passaram a usar o `Field` do sistema de design, inclusive o do estágio de classes, que já tinha o problema desde o P0-1.

## Migração

`b7e2d9c4a105`, aditiva, no molde do M6/P0-1: três tabelas novas, e as duas colunas de `selection_stage` nascem nullable, recebem `[]` no backfill e só então viram NOT NULL. Um estudo salvo antes disto avalia exatamente como antes.

`app/tests/test_migration_process_universe.py` roda a migração de verdade, **nos dois sentidos**, contra um banco temporário que já contém um estudo com dois estágios. **Conferido por mutação:** sem o backfill, os cinco testes falham no travamento do NOT NULL, exatamente onde a produção quebraria. A migração também foi conferida contra os modelos por `compare_metadata` — zero divergências nas tabelas novas.

## Portão

| Verificação | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `ruff check app` | limpo |
| `black --check app` | limpo |
| `pytest` | **1036** (era 990 em `main`) |
| `alembic upgrade head` + seed em banco limpo | ok, e o seed é idempotente (segunda execução cria 0 vínculos) |
| `npm run typecheck` | 0 erros |
| `npm run lint` | 0 erros |
| `npm run test` | **218** (era 210) |
| `npm run build` | ok |

## O que isto ainda não é

O **exercício 11** do manual seleciona **processos** como resultado — o universo de saída é a tabela de processos, não a de materiais. O P0-2 faz o sentido do exercício 9; o inverso toca `SelectionStudy`, o ranking (um processo não tem `densidade`) e os documentos. Está registrado como **P0-3**, o próximo gargalo do roteiro.

## Escopo e propriedade intelectual

Equivalência **funcional** em arquitetura aberta. Nenhum dataset, texto, ícone, imagem ou nomenclatura protegida da ANSYS entra aqui; os conceitos são de domínio público da metodologia de Ashby e a implementação é própria. O universo de processos semeado é fictício e marcado — e o que é inventado ali é a **compatibilidade**, dito no próprio arquivo.

Cobertura de capacidades inspiradas no EduPack: **~47% → ~57%** (17 de 30 em nível ≥ 3).

author: shman4ik
body:
Открыть лист персонажа, поправить навыки, дождаться рестарта сервиса — и правки исчезали, лист перечитывался из базы. `circuit-persistence.js` тут ни при чём, он свою работу делал. Поломок было две, обе настоящие.

## 1. Пауза перед остановкой сервера не срабатывала никогда

`PauseAllAsync` звалась из `IHostedService.StopAsync` и всегда приходила к пустому трекеру. Трассировка:

```
TRACE disconnected <circuit>, всего 0     ← соединения уже закрыты
Application is shutting down...
TRACE StopAsync вошёл                     ← просить о паузе некого
```

SignalR закрывает все соединения своим обработчиком `ApplicationStopping` (`HttpConnectionManager.CloseAllConnections`), а тот отрабатывает раньше любого `StopAsync`. То есть весь механизм «попроси вкладки сохраниться перед деплоем» простоял мёртвым с рождения — в логе не появлялось ни строчки.

Проверено и по Ctrl+Break, и через штатный `StopApplication()` (тот же путь, что даёт `docker stop`) — не артефакт Windows.

Подписка переехала на `ApplicationStopping` и оформляется **лениво**, при первом подключившемся circuit: обработчики `CancellationToken` идут в обратном порядке регистрации, значит наш обязан зарегистрироваться позже сигналровского, а к первому `OnConnectionUpAsync` `HttpConnectionManager` уже подписан. Отдельный hosted-сервис после этого не нужен и удалён. Теперь при остановке в логе:

```
Остановка сервера: просим 1 вкладок сохранить состояние circuit в браузере.
Остановка сервера: осталось 0 неприостановленных вкладок.
```

## 2. На странице листа нечего было сохранять

Возобновление circuit не оживляет страницу: она собирается заново, `OnInitializedAsync` отрабатывает снова, приватные поля обнуляются, а восстанавливается **только** помеченное `[PersistentState]`. Весь лист лежал в приватном свойстве `Character`, поэтому даже безупречная пауза с возобновлением давала копию из базы.

Добавлен снимок `PersistedDraft` (`CharacterPage.State.cs`) по образцу `CombatService`. Черновик применяется после загрузки из базы и только если совпал `CharacterId` — чужой выбрасывается, иначе на экране окажется не тот лист. При восстановлении показывается уведомление: иначе Хранитель не отличит свою правку от базы.

## Проверка

Полный цикл на живом приложении, дважды — второй раз на финальной сборке, без временной обвязки и штатным сигналом остановки:

1. открыт `/character/<id>`, «Взлом» изменён 40 → 66, **не** сохранён;
2. сервис остановлен, поднят новый инстанс;
3. вкладка возобновилась сама: «Взлом» = 66, половина 33, баннер «Восстановлены несохранённые изменения листа».

Сборка чистая, `TreatWarningsAsErrors` включён. Временный эндпоинт и TRACE-логи, которыми ловилась причина, убраны.

## Что осталось за рамками

Автосохранение листа. Сейчас лист сохраняется только кнопкой, и этот PR держит несохранённую правку в памяти сервера и браузера. Для листа за столом дебаунс-автосейв в базу был бы надёжнее любой circuit-магии, но это продуктовое решение — правки станут видны сразу, без явного «Сохранить».

body:
## ปัญหา

ร้านบอกว่า **"พวกปุ่มกด… ฉันอยากกดแล้วเชื่อมเข้าได้เลย ไม่ต้องเด้งคำพูดบอท"**

สองเรื่องคนละอย่างที่ทำให้กดปุ่มแล้วรก

**1. กดปุ่มแล้วมีคำขึ้นในแชต** — ทุกปุ่มมี `displayText` ซึ่ง LINE จะเอา label ของปุ่มไปโพสต์ในแชตเหมือนร้านพิมพ์เอง กดทีนึงได้คำพูดตัวเองหนึ่งบรรทัดค้างอยู่เหนือคำตอบเสมอ

**2. ปุ่มที่แค่จะเปิดหน้าเว็บ เดินอ้อม** — กด `จดงาน` บนริชเมนู → โพสต์คำว่า "จดงาน" → บอตตอบทักทาย 2 บรรทัด + การ์ด → ต้องกด "กรอกในฟอร์ม" ในการ์ดอีกที ฟอร์มถึงเปิด สามขั้นและสองข้อความ เพื่อไปหน้าที่กดตั้งแต่แรกแล้ว

## สิ่งที่แก้

**ไม่มีคำเด้งอีกแล้ว** — ตัด `displayText` ที่ `lineService` ตอนส่งออก ที่เดียว ไม่ใช่ไล่แก้ทีละปุ่มสี่สิบกว่าจุด (กฎที่เก็บไว้สี่สิบที่ คือกฎที่พังไปแล้วหนึ่งที่) `label` กับ `data` ไม่ถูกแตะ ปุ่มยังทำงานเหมือนเดิมทุกอย่าง

**ปุ่มที่เปิดหน้าเว็บ กดแล้วเข้าเลย** — 4 ปุ่มบนริชเมนูเป็นลิงก์ตรง

| ปุ่ม | ไปที่ |
|---|---|
| จดงาน | ฟอร์มกรอกงาน |
| รายการล่าสุด/แก้ไข | แดชบอร์ด `?tab=today` |
| งานค้าง | `?tab=pending` |
| ตั้งค่า | `?tab=settings` |

อีก 4 ปุ่ม (บันทึก/แนบสลิป · หมวดงาน · ออกใบเสร็จ · ช่วยเหลือ) ยังผ่านบอท เพราะต้องคุยต่อ — รอรูป เลือกลูกค้า เลือกหมวด ไม่มีหน้าเว็บให้เปิด และถ้าไม่ได้ตั้ง `LIFF_ID` ทั้ง 9 ปุ่มถอยกลับไปเป็น postback เหมือนเดิม ใช้งานได้ปกติ

**แก้บั๊กที่จะตามมา** — หน้าแดชบอร์ดรับ `?tab=` แค่ `pending` นอกนั้นเด้งไปงานวันนี้หมด ปุ่ม ตั้งค่า ที่เพิ่งทำจะพาไปผิดหน้า ตอนนี้รับทุกแท็บที่มีจริง

**และกันไม่ให้เงียบซ้ำรอยเดิม** — ชื่อริชเมนูตอนนี้ fingerprint ทั้งรูป **และ** สิ่งที่ปุ่มทำ ถ้าไม่ทำ การเปลี่ยนปุ่มจาก postback เป็นลิงก์จะทิ้งรูปกับจำนวนปุ่มไว้เท่าเดิม แล้วบูตจะข้ามการติดตั้งแบบเดียวกับตอนเปลี่ยนแค่รูปเป๊ะ ๆ

## Tests

`npm test` — 255 ผ่านทั้งหมด เพิ่ม 5 เคส

- ไม่มีอะไรที่ส่งออกไป LINE เหลือ `displayText` แต่ `label`/`data` ต้องอยู่ครบ
- ตัดเฉพาะ postback: ข้อความปกติ ปุ่ม uri และ text ในการ์ด ต้องไม่โดน และ object ต้นทางต้องไม่ถูกแก้ (ตัดตอนส่งเท่านั้น)

author: marcoroth
body:
This pull request adds the hooks a UI package built outside the client needs, so more ambitious component can be ported on top of Herb without living in this package and without depending on Stimulus.

The state side was already there. `stateFor(element)` reads and writes state scoped to the enclosing row, and `slots.subscribe` announces every write. What was missing is a way to attach JavaScript to elements by attribute that rides on the runtime's own observer, and the handful of facts only the runtime has: that an element was just built, that a row is about to move and where from, that a node is about to be destroyed, and where a batch of writes ends.

#### Behaviors

`runtime.behaviors.define(attribute, behavior)` registers callbacks for every element carrying the attribute, bare or valued, under any name. The name is the application's to choose and should stay out of `data-herb-`, which is the runtime's own namespace and the one the linter and language service validate. It rides on the runtime's existing `ElementObserver`, which gained a `watch` method that widens its filter and re-observes, so a behavior connects in the same delivery as the slot index scans the markup, after it. 

Every callback receives the element and a context with the element's scoped state, `slots` and `outbox`, cached per element. `stateFor` was split so the scoped state can be built from a `State` directly, without going through `Runtime.get()`. A behavior that throws is reported as `herb-behavior-error` and the others still run.

```ts
const { behaviors } = Runtime.start()

behaviors.define("data-drawer", {
  connect(element, context) {},
  enter(element, context) {},
  valueChanged(element, value, context) {},
  updated(element, slot, context) {},
  moved(element, { from, to }, context) {},
  settled(element, context) {},
  leave(element, context) {},
  disconnect(element, context) {},
  transition(element, context) {},
})
```

| Callback | Runs when |
|---|---|
| `connect` | The element is on the page when the behavior is defined, arrives later, or gains the attribute. |
| `enter` | After `connect`, only for markup the runtime built. `Slots` announces `built` synchronously before the mutation batch that connects the elements, so `Behaviors` remembers those ranges for one delivery. |
| `valueChanged` | The attribute's value changes on a connected element. |
| `updated` | A slot inside the element is written. |
| `moved` | A collection reorder changed the element's position, with the rect before and after. `Collections.order` announces `itemsMoving` before it moves anything and `itemsMoved` after. |
| `settled` | Once at the end of a batch, for each element that was updated or moved in it. `Slots.building` announces it when the outermost batch wrote anything, and `State.setState` and the optimistic writes in `ServerState` now run inside one. |
| `leave` | The branch or row around the element is about to be destroyed. May return a promise to hold it. |
| `disconnect` | The element left the document, lost the attribute, the behavior was undefined, or the runtime stopped. |
| `transition` | Runs on connect and on every value change. A returned name is written to `data-herb-transition`, so the element takes part in the runtime's view transitions as if the template had named it. |

#### Leaving

`SlotsDelegate` gains `holdBranch(slot, branch)` and `holdItem(slot, item)`. When declared state switches a conditional, or a payload or `outbox.discard` drops a row, `leave` runs for every connected element inside the departing markup first, while it is still on the page. Returning nothing destroys at once. Returning a promise defers the destruction until the promise settles, resolved or rejected, and the condition is then evaluated again. A branch stays when its state flipped back in the meantime, and a row stays when a later payload listed it again. `Slots.dismissItem(slot, key)` is `removeItem` with the hold in front of it, and `applyItems` keeps a held row in its current position among the rows the payload listed, so the list keeps its shape while the row animates out. A branch switched by a server payload is applied as it arrives and is not held.

`State.writeConditionals` was reshaped around this. The switch itself, with its view transition wrapping and refetch fallback, moved into `switchTo`, and the loop now only checks for a hold.

author: leoisadev1
body:
## Problem

Session listing and idle reaping both scaled from the wrong clocks.

`listSessions` loaded every persisted thread binding, then looked each one up, so the call grew with conversation history instead of the live adapter session set. The session reaper treated binding `lastSeenAt` as the only idle timestamp. That stamp is updated when a turn is sent, so a long turn that later completed or aborted could be stopped as soon as it finished instead of getting a full inactivity window.

## Changes

Look up bindings only for the unique thread ids of currently active adapter sessions. Historical bindings stay out of this path.

Idle time is `max(binding.lastSeenAt, session.updatedAt)` after the cheap `lastSeenAt` skip. Ingestion updates `session.updatedAt` when a turn settles, so ready, interrupted, and error sessions get the full window after that transition. Active turns and live `backgroundLiveness` still skip reaping. Akeru still uses `AgentController` rather than `ProviderService` for stop.

## Upstream

Reviewed adaptations of pingdotgg/t3code:

- [#8909](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/8909) bound session lookups
- [#10689](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10689) full post-completion idle window

## Scope

This PR is session listing and idle timing only. Independent of [#220](https://github.com/opencoredev/akeru-bot/pull/220) and [#229](https://github.com/opencoredev/akeru-bot/pull/229).

Assigned checkpoint and attachment ports are in those PRs:

- checkpoint capture, nested git, numstat, git-init resume, capture-before-status-refresh (#9694, #9842, #9841, #10078, #10347) — [#220](https://github.com/opencoredev/akeru-bot/pull/220)
- attachment transaction cleanup and first-send retry (#7941, #8226) — [#229](https://github.com/opencoredev/akeru-bot/pull/229)

Restart continuation remains with the capabilities worker.

## Verification

- `vp test run` of ProviderService and ProviderSessionReaper: 50 tests passed. New cases use Clock overrides and a deferred sweep, not sleeps.
- Targeted lint and format passed (0 errors). One pre-existing unused `dispatch` parameter warning in ProviderService.test.ts is unchanged.

No UI layout or client-visible chrome change. Proof is adapter-session listing and reaper sweep tests.

## Limitations

`backgroundLiveness` skip is preserved. Capabilities-owned restart continuation is not in this PR.

Implemented and verified by Grok 4.6 High in Grok Build via Orca.

author: chirag2796
body:
Desert lane of the seven-lane city-prop pass. PR #31 derived the Nightly City Pass delivery into 92 runtime sprites and deliberately left placement alone. This is Kesara's twelve.

Kesara received no townsfolk in #31, so props are the whole of its improvement. `kesara-courts` goes from 590 to 642 props, and four interiors stop standing in for themselves.

## What was placed

| Sprite | Frames used | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `city-kesara-ward-wall` (CITY-201) | 0 ×24, 1 ×1, 2 ×2 | The ward wall, rows 8–9, continuous x2→x75, a gate bay on each gate, a corner cap on the east end |
| `city-kesara-ward-risers` (CITY-202) | 0 ×41, 1 ×3, 2 ×2 | The three descents at y23/39/59 |
| `city-kesara-ward-stairs` (CITY-202) | 0 ×11, 1 ×9 | The sixteen flights that break those descents |
| `city-kesara-permit-board` (CITY-203) | 0 ×1 (as the sign), 1 ×1 | The Compact board; one carved stall post |
| `city-kesara-yard-ground` (CITY-204) | 0 ×1, 1 ×40, 2 ×5 | Trodden fill through the permit yard; five camp fire-rings; one stall-paving tile |
| `city-kesara-channel-lids` (CITY-205) | 0 ×47, 1 ×1, 2 ×13, 3 ×2 | Every covered run, the gallery spares, the channel-store shelf |
| `city-kesara-dye-court-ground` (CITY-206) | single | Eight setdown rings beside the vats, rinse pool, wool rack and works door |
| `city-kesara-dye-works` (CITY-206) | single | The dye works, replacing a second copy of `w05-water-house` |
| `city-kesara-mordant-shelf` (CITY-206) | single | `kesara-dye-store`, in place of `w02-seed-rack` |
| `city-kesara-water-house-kit` (CITY-207) | 0–3, 4–6, 7–10 | Ledger shelving in the ledger room; tally rods and two raised jar courses in the water house |
| `city-kesara-guest-kitchen-hearth` | single | `kesara-shade-kitchen`, in place of `w04-cook-hearth` |
| `city-kesara-guest-kitchen-bean-jars` | single | `kesara-shade-kitchen`, in place of `w15-clay-water-jars` |
| `city-kesara-guest-kitchen-recipe-board` | single | The `w05:recipe` sign, moved off the floor onto the shade hall's north wall |

All twelve placed; nothing left without a home. `w06-marked-lid`, `w06-broken-lid`, `w05-covered-run` and `w05-run-horizontal` are gone from Kesara — they are black-ridge stone and were the same mistake as the volcanic gravel this map already removed from its rim.

## The design calls, and the reasoning

**The ward wall runs, it does not stagger.** It was thirteen `w05-retaining-wall` blocks scattered over two rows specifically to avoid one sprite repeated in a line. CITY-201 delivers the band, so it can be continuous, which is what a ward wall is for. Cells are three tiles wide; where a segment is not a multiple of three the last cell is pulled back over its neighbour rather than leaving a hole. Checked in-engine: the coping joints are irregular enough that a 16px phase shift does not read, and a gap you can see the scour through certainly would. The delivered cell banks its red-sand drift along the **bottom** edge, so the sand piles against the city face rather than the scour — kept, because the rim ward is already red sand blown over pale masonry, so it agrees with the map even though it is not what the brief described.

**Risers go one row below the blocked row, not on it.** Both descent sheets are two rows tall. Placed on the descent row, the blocked row gets the pale tread and reads as walkable while the open row above gets the dark riser face and reads as a wall — exactly backwards. One row down puts the dark face on the row you cannot cross and the tread on the ward you step onto. Runs are clipped to the ward each descent drops into rather than to the descent row, which spans the whole map: the wards narrow as the city goes down, and the risers should say so. Stairs went onto the sixteen flights, which previously had no art at all — you could see that you could not walk there and not why.

**Channel lids are laid across the channel, because that is how a lid works.** The delivered cell is 32×16, so a horizontal run steps two tiles and a vertical run steps one, and both come out continuous. The lifted cell is placed exactly once, at the repair site with the tools, per its manifest's "do not tile" — an open lid means somebody is standing over it, which is the claim this city makes about its water. The failed cell replaces the broken lid Mirhan reports. No bend cell was delivered, so `w05-run-bend` still turns the two corners; that is an asset request below, not something to fudge.

**The water-house kit is placed as delivered, not re-cut.** It is a 176×80 strip whose three real cells measure 64×80, 48×64 and 64×32 — uneven, hence the uniform 16×80 frame box. That works exactly and is worth keeping: sixteen divides all three cell widths, every cell boundary falls in the transparent gutter between props, and every frame is bottom-anchored, so consecutive frames on consecutive tiles rebuild each prop pixel for pixel with one texture and one palette. Verified in-engine — the ledger shelving and both jar courses assemble seamlessly. **No re-cut needed.**

**Two cells were deliberately not tiled, for content rather than seams.** `yard-ground` frame 0 carries a carved stall numeral and tether sockets, so a field of it is a yard where every stall is stall seven — one tile only. Frame 2 carries a whole campsite including a fire-ash ring — five placed by hand, five families who each lit a fire where they stopped, rather than a field of identical rings. Frame 1 (trodden) does tile and was machine-verified 16-periodic; **checked at 1x for a 16px lattice and there is none.**

**`dye-court-ground` was scaled back.** Scattered at thirty tiles it read as spilled confetti — one recognisable clump of coloured pixels repeated across a screen, which is the repetition its own manifest flags. Eight tiles instead, each beside something actually set down: the two vat stands, the rinse pool, the wool rack, the step outside the works door. Placed that way it reads as the ring a vat leaves. This is the closest thing to a rejection in the batch, and it is a request rather than a fix.

**The dye works is a plan view among elevations.** The delivery came back as a strict top-down plan — mudbrick walls round a working court, vats and setdown rings inside, drying lines radiating over the street — rather than the oblique elevation the brief asked for. **Taken as delivered.** This map's own opening argument is that Kesara is read from above (its ward wall is a parapet run seen overhead), no other building here has a courtyard to show, and the alternative was a second copy of the water house on the same street. It is the one building that does not match its neighbours' presentation; that is a real cost and it is flagged as a low-priority request.

## The carved numeral — my call

`kesara-permit-board` frame 1 carries a carved "3" the asset agent confirms is legible at 1x, against a brief that asked for no readable writing.

**Placed, once.** A numeral is not script: it settles no question the treatise deliberately leaves open — nothing about language, peoples, or Lavan. The board three tiles away already reads *"stalls one to nine … an allocation of water written against the number"*, so a carved stall number is the Compact made visible rather than a new claim. One post only, so the map can never show two stalls both numbered three. The same argument covers `yard-ground` frame 0's carved "7", placed once at the other end of the yard so the two numbers are different stalls.

If Chirag disagrees, deleting two lines removes both.

## Two defects found while doing it

**1. `frame` was inert.** PR #31 added `frame` to `Canvas.decor` and taught the renderer to draw it, but `scripts/content/normalize.ts` still failed any non-zero frame and then wrote `frame: 0` into the map regardless — so a lane placing a gate bay would silently have got a straight run of wall, with nothing failing loudly. Found and patched here; on the rebase before opening this PR the Braid and Hills lanes had already landed t

author: jasisz
body:
Part of #1329 (concurrency epic). This is the I/O layer the coordinator needs, usable today by any poll loop.

## What

Three additions to the `Tcp` capability, on every target.

- `Tcp.readNow(connection, maxBytes) -> Result<Option<Bytes>, String>`. Never blocks. `Ok(None)` means nothing is available right now. `Ok(Some(empty))` means clean end of stream, the convention `readSome` already uses. `Ok(Some(bytes))` is one available chunk. `Err` is a transport failure.
- `Tcp.writeNow(connection, payload) -> Result<Int, String>`. Never blocks. Returns how many bytes the socket accepted, from 0 to the payload length; 0 for a non-empty payload means the socket would block; a partial count is normal.
- `Tcp.Socket.Sending(connection)`: a fourth socket state for `poll`. A `Sending` key is ready when the next `writeNow` will accept at least one byte or fail. `Connected` keeps meaning read readiness; a caller who wants both directions registers two keys. False-positive readiness stays allowed.

Existing operations keep their contracts. Hostile profiles: `readNowNormalOk`, `readNowWouldBlock`, `readNowEof`, `readNowAlwaysErr`, `writeNowNormalOk`, `writeNowPartial`, `writeNowWouldBlock`, `writeNowAlwaysErr`.

## Targets

VM and Rust through `aver-rt` (one-call non-blocking mode, restored afterwards; the reactor merges read and write interest per descriptor). wasm-gc through two new host imports, `aver.tcp_read_now` and `aver.tcp_write_now`, with record and replay. wasip2 through `wasi:io/streams` (`input-stream.read`, `output-stream.check-write`, `write`, `flush`, `subscribe`); `Sending` subscribes the output stream's pollable. Nothing is rejected on any target.

## Certificate wall identity moves

The host import registries in `aver-cert` and in `SchemaCore.lean` gained the new names, so `CURRENT_WALL_ID` changed and both certificate package snapshots were re-pinned. No emitted module bytes changed; the `add_one` package differs only in `format.wall_id`. This is the same rotation as the two earlier registry changes.

## Two shape decisions to confirm before merge

1. `readNow` returns `Result<Option<Bytes>, String>` rather than a dedicated sum type: `None` for would-block and empty bytes for end of stream reuse the shapes `accept` and `readSome` already have.
2. The write-readiness state is named `Sending`, in the pattern of `Listening`, `Dialing`, `Connected`.

The gallery was nested inside .shell, but every rule in it is written for a
full-bleed rail: the rail's own padding, the bar's max-width, the meter's
insets. Inside the shell each of those was applied twice, and the travel was
measured against the window while the rail was clipped to a 1128px box. The
run stopped short by the difference — 312px at 1440, 792px at 1920 — so the
closing card was unreachable, the counter never left 01 on a large screen,
and the first card sat a gutter to the right of the heading above it.

The head was the blank space. It sat outside the pinned stage, so the section
was two screens: a heading with a viewport of air under it, then a strip of
cards adrift in another. It now rides inside the stage in two columns, short
enough to share the screen with the rail, and the stage anchors the browse
hint to the top and the meter to the bottom instead of floating all three in
the middle.

- Measure travel off the last card and the rail's own box, so the run ends
  with the closing card inset the way the first card is.
- Map rail travel 1:1 to scroll; the leftover height is now real dwell on the
  last card rather than a slower run that ends at the release.
- Read the counter off the same progress as the meter, so it lands on 04.
- Give the rail a height that scales with the viewport, and don't pin at all
  for a run shorter than one card or a viewport too short to compose.
- Unpin without script as well as under reduced motion; pinned, the rail
  needs a driver, and without one the run cannot be moved at all.

author: imjustchew
body:
Closes #855. Supersedes #857, which attempted the same swap and silently did nothing.

## Why #857 failed

The Cloudflare Workers build supplies `VITE_ALGOLIA_APP_ID` / `VITE_ALGOLIA_SEARCH_KEY` as **build variables**, and Vite gives process variables precedence over `.env` files. The committed file never decided which application the browser talked to.

So #857 did not promote anything — it moved the *blocked* application into the backup slot, where it matched the build-supplied primary and was dropped by the duplicate-app-id guard. Production was briefly left with no Algolia tier, falling through to Supabase (still working, ~250-900ms instead of ~10ms). Reverted in #858.

Nothing in that diff could have shown this. The configuration was split between a file in the repo and a dashboard, and only the dashboard won.

## This PR

Read the four `VITE_ALGOLIA_*` values out of `apps/web/.env` at config time and compile them in, making that file the single reviewable source of truth. Then apply the swap it was meant to make: the reindexed application becomes primary, the blocked one stays as backup so it returns to service if Algolia unblocks it.

## Verification

Built with a deliberately hostile environment, simulating the dashboard variable:

```
VITE_ALGOLIA_APP_ID=BOGUSBUILDVAR VITE_ALGOLIA_SEARCH_KEY=bogus_key_from_dashboard vite build

working I0RQAS273V   present, positioned before blocked NT48R1WDTS
BOGUSBUILDVAR        absent
bogus key            absent
```

That is the check #857 lacked. Through the real client, the primary tier now answers with no failed request first:

| query | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `thermodynamics` | 1057ms (403 → backup) | **341ms** tier=primary |
| `計算機` | 10ms after demotion | **14ms** tier=primary |
| `IBP 105100` | 10ms after demotion | **14ms** tier=primary |

Typecheck unchanged at 8 pre-existing errors. Timeouts from #857 retained.

Note for whoever has dashboard access: the `VITE_ALGOLIA_*` build variables on `courseweb-web` are now inert and can be deleted.

author: hexrift
body:
## Two `ward-daemon` bug-hunt findings (P2 + P3)

Both are reachable only by a **same-user client** of the 0600 control socket (a misbehaving or compromised `ward`/TamperWard client), not by the sandboxed agent.

### P2 — unbounded control-socket read (DoS)

`serve_stream` (`daemon.rs`) and `serve_connection` (`control.rs`) read request lines with no size limit, so a client that streams bytes without a newline grows the read buffer without bound — an OOM / (with `panic=abort`) process-abort vector. Now each read is bounded to `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (1 MiB, far above any real request) via `Read::take`, and a truncated over-cap line is rejected as `request too large` instead of parsed.

*(Not fixed here: an idle/slow-loris read timeout. A blanket timeout would break the legitimate long-lived `Subscribe` stream and the `Hold` wait, so it needs per-path handling — noted as a follow-up rather than risk a regression in those paths.)*

### P3 — `resume()` commits before the marker is cleared

`resume()` removed the pause state and released approvals + processes **before** `clear_marker`, so a failed `clear_marker` left the on-disk pause marker in place: the session proxies keep refusing egress while the daemon believes it's running, and a retry `Resume` returns `not paused` — a half-resumed wedge. Now the marker is cleared **first** and the function returns early on failure with nothing mutated, so a failed clear leaves the session cleanly, fully paused and retryable.

## Tests

`request_too_large` accepts terminated/short lines and rejects a truncated over-cap line. Existing resume/pause tests still pass.

## Verification

Full CI gate (`scripts/verify/tamperward.sh`) green.

## Versioning

Bug fix → PATCH: `0.3.6` → `0.3.7`.

## Summary

Two releases on this branch.

### v0.34.0 — Gameplay-complete II: the playtest

- `scripts/playtest_engine.py --launch` builds a scratch engine and drives every roadmap loop through its HTTP API (69 steps: creation, `$ I explore`, sect trial and gift manual, commissions taken/abandoned/failed by the tick, live quest edits, narration route store/apply, timed moderation, backup).
- `scripts/playtest_checklist.py` generates `docs/playtest/v<version>.md` — every action with the static columns filled and three live columns for the pass on the server. `docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` is the punch list; `test_playtest_gate.py` holds both.
- Two defects the run found, fixed with Go tests: a commission's last objective could never be turned in (`questProgress` kept it active until `resolveCommissionTx`), and Reset Cooldowns missed the sect trial retry wait.
- Quest Forge's target picker no longer fills its cap with auction floors and stewards.

### v0.34.1 — the #playtest board and the travelling merchants (schema 36)

**The board.** A `#playtest` base channel beside `#bugs`, created by Setup/Repair, bound from the slash path or the dashboard. `/admin → Server → Playtest → Post` puts one message per hub page in it, pre-reacted ✅ ❌ 💡; testers react and reply under the page. `Report` tallies the reactions with names and links every flagged page; `Clear` empties it. The board stores message ids only (`playtest_items`); all three actions are audited.

**The merchants.** Eight merchants (two a world, each a named NPC) walk fixed loops of cities on the simulation tick (`merchants` automation switch). They are the auction floor's last bidder: a lot that ends with no bid is taken at its starting bid by a merchant whose loop passes the house's city and whose purse covers it; the seller is paid and the item goes into the pack at a markup, never below base price. Players buy the pack back through `/economy → Merchants → Buy` in the same city or on the same stretch of road — `merchant.buy` is the one action the engine allows mid-journey — and the travel reply names who is on the road ahead. The merchant NPC moves with the merchant; a merchant's purchase reads **Struck to** on the live auction card.

Go owns all of it (`go_core/internal/game/merchant_actions.go`); Python never writes `merchant_state` or `merchant_stock`, and a contract test holds that.

author: dentiny
body:
Closes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/25582

Two pre-knowledge for this issue:
- An invariant for DuckDB: each index should have its unique name.
- Primary key, unique constraint, and foreign key all create their own index, and are named as `PRIMARY_<table>_<ordinal>`, `UNIQUE_<table>_<ordinal>`, `FOREIGN_<table>_<ordinal>`

In the current implementation, we could mistakenly create two index with the same indexes with the same name.

author: rssilverioo
body:
## O bug, reproduzido ao vivo em produção

Hoje (10/09), testei o checkout de matrícula real até o fim: Anhanguera,
Administração EAD, R$107,22/mês. Usei dados de teste identificáveis (nome
"TESTE INVESTIGACAO CLAUDE", email `teste.investigacao.claude+bcbug@gmail.com`,
CPF de teste público `111.444.777-35` — válido no dígito verificador, não é
de ninguém) e cliquei em **Gerar QR Code Pix**.

Em seguida **não paguei de propósito** — nunca abri banco, nunca escaneei o
QR code.

**Em menos de 5 segundos** a tela mostrou:

> ✓ **Taxa de matrícula paga**
> "Seu pagamento foi confirmado e estamos concluindo a inscrição. Você vai
> receber a confirmação por e-mail e WhatsApp — não é preciso pagar de novo."

Conferi **na hora** direto no banco de produção do Elysium (`railway run`
contra `elysium-api-prod`, sem nunca ler a `DATABASE_URL`):

```
id: a45346b2-d986-499c-b308-0fe8162c0912
status: PENDING
paymentKind: PIX
amount: 1990
createdAt: 2026-09-10T18:00:32.318Z
```

A transação **nunca foi paga**. O site mentiu pro usuário.

## Causa

`app/checkout/matricula/MatriculaPayment.tsx` e
`app/checkout/estacio/EstacioPayment.tsx` têm o mesmo código, copiado:

```ts
if (active && (res.ok || res.status === 422)) {
  confirmPaid(id)
  return
}
```

O comentário logo acima descreve a intenção certa: *"202 (pendente) [...]
mantêm o polling — nunca dizemos 'pago' por um erro de servidor."* Mas o
código não implementa isso. `res.ok` do Fetch API é `true` para **qualquer**
status 2xx — inclusive **202**. E as duas rotas de confirmação devolvem
exatamente `{ status: 202 }` quando o pagamento ainda está pendente:

```ts
// app/api/checkout/matricula/confirm/route.ts:45
// app/api/athena-checkout/confirm/route.ts:33
return NextResponse.json({ status: 'pending' }, { status: 202 })
```

O polling dispara a cada 4s (`POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 4000`) e a primeira consulta
já roda no mount (`void tick()`). Como **ninguém paga um PIX em menos de 4
segundos**, a primeira resposta é sempre 202 — e sempre bate na condição
errada, confirmando um pagamento que nunca aconteceu. Isso não é um caso de
borda raro: é o caminho normal para praticamente **todo mundo**.

## Por que isso é grave pra conversão

Quem gera um PIX vê "pago, confira seu e-mail" segundos depois, antes de
sequer abrir o banco — e tem todo motivo pra achar que não precisa mais
pagar. A tela trava em "pago" (sem erro, sem nova tentativa), então mesmo
quem volta e paga de verdade nunca vê isso refletido.

Bate com o que a investigação da conversão zerada (07-10/09) já tinha
achado: a **única** transação Elysium desde 06/09 (CPF 08632280708, R$19,90
PIX, documentada em `Funil Estácio depois da taxa`) ficou `PENDING` pra
sempre — o mesmo padrão que reproduzi aqui agora.

## Não é falha de segurança

O servidor não é enganado: nenhuma inscrição real foi criada (o
`confirm-matricula.ts`/`confirm-estacio.ts` só chama `upsertCandidato`
depois de o Elysium confirmar pagamento de verdade — conferi buscando meu
teste no Attio por telefone/CPF/email, nada foi criado, porque o fluxo
servidor nunca passou do 202). É só a **tela** que mentia.

## O fix

Troca `res.ok` pela checagem exata do status de sucesso — `res.status ===
200`, mantendo `422` (recusa) como está:

```ts
if (active && (res.status === 200 || res.status === 422)) {
```

Confirmei que as duas rotas devolvem exatamente `200` (implícito, sem
`{ status }` explícito no `NextResponse.json`) no caminho de sucesso — o fix
não muda o caso que já funcionava, só remove o falso positivo do 202.

## Dados de teste — já removidos

- Transação Elysium `a45346b2-d986-499c-b308-0fe8162c0912`: **apagada**
  (confirmei o `status`/`amount` batendo antes de deletar, e confirmei
  `findUnique` retornando `null` depois).
- Attio: busquei por telefone (`+5511900000001`), CPF e email — **nenhum
  registro criado**, como esperado (ver seção acima).
- Nenhuma inscrição real foi criada na Cogna.

## Verificação

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — limpo, nenhum erro
- `npx next lint` nos dois arquivos — limpo

author: pcarleton
body:
Proposed -01 text, cut down to be only what's required for interop.

**Changed**

- `aud` is the authorization server's issuer identifier, a single value; the token endpoint URL is a MAY (supersedes D6). Deployed RFC 7523 grant handlers that require a single audience reject the two-value array, and ID-JAG makes the same choice.
- The Agent Identifier is an opaque string, unique within its Platform and never reassigned; the URI form is no longer recommended (withdraws D7).
- How an authorization server obtains a Platform's keys is the administrator's choice: entered directly, a JWK Set URL, or the `jwks_uri` in issuer metadata. What has to interoperate is which keys verify an assertion, not how they arrived. A Platform SHOULD publish keys at a URL so rotation needs no administrator.
- "Platform" is one customer's partition; "Platform registration" is the authorization server's record of one trusted Platform. Under a shared issuer identifier the registration names the claim that tells Platforms apart (`tenant` RECOMMENDED only for new shared issuers). Relates to #7; replaces the tenancy text explored in #10. 

**Small normative additions**

`resource` REQUIRED; optional `scope` claim as in ID-JAG; no refresh tokens and access tokens that do not outlive the assertion by much; no client registration per Agent (the Platform may be required to authenticate as a client); first-seen stated as "MUST NOT reject solely because the `sub` is unseen"; error responses say who must act, using existing error codes; `grant_types_supported` is a SHOULD.

**Cut without changing the decision**

AIMS correspondence table (the Overview and figure stay, shortened); Scope section (now in the abstract); retirement prose (now the lifetime rule); instantiation and IdP projection; the property vocabulary (points at the `roles`/`groups`/`entitlements` names already in use, defines none). Unused references removed.

**Added**

Open Issues (claim step by a non-administrator, proof of possession, explicit JWT type, `jti` single use, `aud`, shared-issuer claim, who may register a Platform), a first Security Considerations list, and the Note to Readers restored.

Security Considerations is a list for now; a fuller treatment is coming separately.

# Description

Using random delays and a temp file, this script prevents asynchronous workers from executing the same command.

This can be useful if for example you want to use a qui automation to initiate a **library scan** for services such as *Audiobookshelf\Plex\Navidrome\etc*. Such a scan is a **bulk** action that only needs a **single** execution, rather than **every** matched torrent of the automation initiating its own scan.

# Setup

1) Rename the `singleExection.sh` script to something more relevant to what you will be doing, such as `scanAudiobookshelf.sh`
2) Edit the `commandsToRun()` function so that it lists the command(s) you want to be run by only a single worker of a qui automation
3) Mount the script into your qui container and add the script as an **External Program**, so it can be used by your automations

author: hugocorreia90
body:
Closes #1892. A CTE named after a model invented a dependency on it — and two models with mutual local CTE names were refused at compile time as a cycle that does not exist.

```
$ rocky compile --models models
Error: circular dependency detected involving: ["alpha", "beta"]
```

Legal SQL. Neither model reads the other. `alpha` has a local CTE called `beta`, `beta` has one called `alpha`.

## The cause is one missing question

`extract_query_lineage` never looked at `query.with`, so the names a `WITH` clause binds were unknown. The main body was then walked by `extract_table_factor`, which sees `TableFactor::Table { name: "orders" }` and has no way to tell a CTE reference from a real table.

```
  WITH orders AS (…)        parsed, then discarded
  SELECT … FROM orders   -> TableFactor::Table { name: "orders" }
                         -> source_tables["orders"]
                         -> classify_table_ref -> ModelRef("orders")
                         -> edge  cte_reader -> orders          INVENTED
```

`resolve_dependencies` classified that name against `model_names`, matched, and added the edge. `topological_sort` then found the cycle.

## The fix names the two things apart

`TableReference` gains a `binding` field, and `TableBinding` is the enum that answers it:

```rust
pub enum TableBinding {
    #[default]
    Physical,
    Cte,
}
```

`extract_query_lineage` now builds a `CteScope` from `query.with` and passes it down. Dependency derivation and `referenced_tables` skip a `Cte` reference.

**This change only ever removes edges.** It cannot turn a compiling project into a refused one — the direction that would need a cycle guard.

## Three rules it has to get right, each with a test

**A CTE reference is always a single unqualified name.** So the check is on the whole spelling, not on the last part: `FROM v2.orders` is not shadowed by a CTE called `orders`. Without that, the fix would silently drop a real edge.

**Names fold case, as SQL identifiers do.** `WITH Orders AS (…) … FROM ORDERS` is one binding, not two names.

**Scope nests inward and never leaks up.** A CTE bound by the outer query is visible inside that query's derived tables, so the scope is threaded through the `Derived` arm. A CTE bound inside a subquery stays there.

The `bind_cte_names` doc records what a later change has to do differently. Binding the whole clause at once is right **only** while CTE bodies are not walked. When #1867 walks them, binding must become incremental — inside CTE *i* only CTEs 1..*i*-1 are visible, plus *i* itself when the clause is `RECURSIVE`. Otherwise this reads a real table reference in an earlier body as a reference to a later CTE and drops its edge:

```sql
WITH a AS (SELECT * FROM orders),   -- a real model read
     orders AS (SELECT 1)            -- the CTE, defined after
SELECT * FROM a
```

## Blast radius, measured rather than assumed

Every other consumer of `lineage.source_tables` is already fail-closed on CTEs, because `lineage_is_provably_complete` refuses any query carrying a `WITH`:

```
  rocky-cli/commands/skip_gate.rs:473    gated   already safe, unchanged
  rocky-cli/commands/backfill.rs:464     gated   already safe, unchanged
  rocky-cli/commands/run.rs:10137        gated   already safe, unchanged
  rocky-cli/commands/run.rs:11827        gated   already safe, unchanged
  rocky-compiler/src/resolve.rs:312      NOT gated   FIXED HERE
  rocky-compiler/src/semantic.rs:324     NOT gated   deliberately untouched
```

`lineage_is_provably_complete` is left exactly as strict. It is the skip gate's fail-safe, its whitelist is about *completeness*, and nothing here changes what the walk covers.

`semantic.rs`'s code is untouched, but its **behaviour changes**, and I had this wrong until I traced it. Correcting it here rather than shipping the claim:

`SELECT *` expansion is gated on `reader_depends_on_it` — #1631's fix, which binds the star to the DAG edge rather than to a name. Removing the invented edge removes exactly what that gate consults. So `SELECT * FROM orders` where `orders` is a CTE stops taking model `orders`'s columns and falls through to `source_schemas`, the same fall-through an external table of that name gets.

That replaces a **wrong** answer, not a right one: the CTE's own columns are what the query returns, and the model's columns were never that. Resolving the star to the CTE body is the further fix and needs `lineage.rs` to carry those columns — #1867's half.

Probed, because "falls through to nothing" is the kind of claim that turns into a new diagnostic:

```
  models/orders.sql     SELECT 1 AS model_col_a, 2 AS model_col_b
  models/cte_star.sql   WITH orders AS (SELECT 9 AS cte_col) SELECT * FROM orders
  models/downstream.sql SELECT model_col_a FROM cte_star

  rocky compile   has_errors: False    only I001 (SELECT * advisory)
```

No new error, no W006, no compile failure. `rocky lineage cte_star` now reports `columns: []` where it used to report the shadowed model's columns. `a_star_over_a_cte_no_longer_takes_the_shadowed_models_columns` pins it.

## Evidence

**Mutation-checked.** `scripts/mutation-check.sh` forcing every reference back to `Physical`:

```
thread 'resolve::tests::mutual_cte_names_do_not_close_a_cycle' panicked at
  model 'alpha' has an invented dependency: ["beta"]
mutation-check: OK — the test failed under mutation, so it is fix-sensitive.
```

**Twelve tests.** Eight in `lineage.rs` for the classification, the three rules above and two more `WITH` spellings, three in `resolve.rs` for the derived graph, one in `semantic.rs` for the star consequence. The third `resolve.rs` test is the one that keeps the fix honest: a query that binds a CTE **and** reads a real model must keep the real edge. Without it, suppressing the whole `FROM` clause would satisfy the other two.

I set out to write the spelling tests as a confidence gap and found one instead. `WITH orders (id) AS (…)` and `WITH RECURSIVE orders AS (…)` both bind correctly and are now pinned. `WITH orders AS MATERIALIZED (…)` does **not** parse under `DatabricksDialect` at all — so a model using it already fails lineage extraction outright, long before binding is asked about. That is pre-existing and unrelated to this change; it is recorded in the test's doc comment rather than left as an unknown.

**Probed with the built binary**, not only by unit test. `rocky compile --models …` on the same four fixtures, before and after:

```
                                                     before      after
  mutual CTE names                                   REFUSED   1 layer
  CTE named after a model            layers                2         1
  plain read of a model  (control)   layers                2         2
  subquery read          (#1867)     layers                1         1
```

The control is the one that matters most: an ordinary `SELECT id FROM orders` still derives its edge. The subquery row is unchanged on purpose — that is #1867's half, and this change does not touch it.

`cargo test -p rocky-sql` 296 passed, `-p rocky-compiler` 486 passed, `-p rocky-core` 2190 passed, `-p rocky-cli` 1965 passed, `-p rocky-engine` green — 0 failed anywhere. Clippy `--all-targets --all-features` clean on both edited crates, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

`LineageResult` is cached in memory only (`Project::lineage_cache`), derives no `JsonSchema`, and reaches no exported CLI output — so there is no schema bump and no codegen cascade. The new field carries `#[serde(default)]` regardless, matching the field beside it.

## What I am least confident about

Whether a model that today relies on the invented edge for its ordering will now run too early. The edge was false — the reader does not read the model — but a project can be accidentally correct: someone writes `WITH orders AS (…)` inside a model that genuinely needs `orders` built first, declares nothing, and the bug orders it anyway. Removing the edge makes that project race. There is no way to

author: joamag
body:
Makes the template engine substantially faster, and adds the unit test suite it was missing.

## Performance

Measured on a real MVC page (the `nanger` plugins view, a 9 file extends/include chain) and on a 100 row table, best of 5 batches:

| workload | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| full per request render | 1.835 ms | 0.463 ms | **3.97x** |
| render only (already parsed) | 0.284 ms | 0.132 ms | 2.15x |
| loop heavy page, parse and render | 7.927 ms | 3.270 ms | 2.42x |
| loop heavy page, render only | 7.667 ms | 3.227 ms | 2.38x |
| parse only, large template | 9.287 ms | 2.392 ms | 3.88x |

Every change was measured in isolation, and the ones that did not pay were dropped rather than kept on principle.

### Where the time went

**Parsing** (was 85% of a request, since every render re-read and re-parsed the whole template chain):

* Parsed templates are cached and a copy of the tree is handed out per use. Copying measured 4.4 to 5.7 times cheaper than parsing. The cache is keyed by path and encoding and validated against the modification time and size of the file on every lookup, so editing a template is picked up without a restart.
* Inheritance and inclusion no longer render the parent template into a buffer that is then thrown away. A cold render used to evaluate 58 output nodes to produce 21; it now evaluates exactly 21.
* Tokenizing is a single ordered scan instead of five separate passes plus two sorts of the match list.
* Block indexing is folded into the tree copy instead of being a second full traversal.

**Rendering:**

* The escaping of literal values and the parsing of the filter pipeline now happen once at parse time instead of on every render of every node.
* Plain `{{ value }}` nodes take a dedicated path. The general one performs around 20 map lookups and 12 helper calls per node, almost all of which return an invalid value for the common case.
* The visit dispatch is resolved once per class instead of walking the class hierarchy on every node, and the tag dispatch is cached instead of being resolved dynamically per node.
* Loop state is no longer rebuilt from a string on every iteration, and the value resolution avoids a redundant map allocation and repeated lookups.

## Bugs fixed

Writing the tests with a critical eye surfaced 16 genuine defects, all fixed here rather than encoded into the tests:

* The `else` branch of a condition was silently dropped whenever the tested value was undefined.
* `{% if x in items %}` compared the operands in reverse, raising `TypeError` for any list.
* The start index of an iteration never worked, raising `ValueError` or `TypeError` in every form.
* A nested loop overwrote the loop variables of the loop containing it.
* Templates whose file name had no extension failed to load, which also broke the plugin's own `parse_file` entry point.
* Loading a template without an explicit encoding failed under Python 3.
* Filter and method arguments containing characters outside a narrow set were silently discarded.
* A comma inside a quoted argument split it, so `|split(',')` could not work.
* Output was corrupted whenever a variable encoding was configured.
* Printing a value crashed under the evaluation based visitor.
* Malformed tags raised an internal error instead of a template error, and `assert_end` raised the builtin error rather than the module one.
* `_get_serializer` raised `TypeError` instead of the intended error.
* Nested lists were wrapped in quotes when printed.
* The `xml_quote` attribute read the wrong key and was unreachable. It now defaults to the auto escaping mode, so the current escaping behaviour is preserved rather than weakened.
* An always true condition in the accept validation.

## Tests

`template_engine` had no tests at all. This adds `test.py` and `mocks.py` alongside the module, registered through the `test` capability, following the structure used by the other plugins. Test cases mirror the declaration order of the code they exercise.

**260 tests, all passing** under `python setup.py test`. **Coverage of the new and changed code is 100%** (308 of 308 lines); the package as a whole is at 92%. Note that the repository has no coverage tooling configured, so this was measured with `coverage` run against the suite.

## Compatibility

This is **not** a drop-in behavioural no-op. Fixing the defects above necessarily changes what some templates render, so the following are worth checking against the existing template corpus before merging.

Most likely to be noticed:

* `{% if value %}...{% else %}...{% endif %}` where the value is **undefined** previously rendered nothing at all, and now renders the else branch. Any template that relied, knowingly or not, on the whole block disappearing will change.
* `{% if x in y %}` previously compared the operands in reverse. Templates that were written around the reversed behaviour will change.
* Loop variables no longer survive the loop. `{{ is_last }}` or `{{ loop.index }}` read **after** a `{% for %}` used to hold the values of the last iteration and now resolve to nothing, and an inner loop no longer overwrites the state of the loop containing it.
* A parent template is no longer rendered twice per request, so any method called from a parent template (through inheritance or inclusion) is now invoked once instead of twice. This only matters for calls with side effects.
* Filter and method arguments that were previously discarded (because they contained characters outside a narrow set) are now actually passed, so a call that silently fell back to its defaults now receives its arguments.
* Nested sequences print as `[1, ['a']]` rather than `[1, '['a']']`.
* An explicit `xml_quote` attribute now takes effect. The default is unchanged: it follows the auto escaping mode, so escaping is not weakened anywhere.

Changes to the module surface, relevant only to code embedding the engine:

* Malformed tags now raise the module `RuntimeError` instead of `TypeError`, and an invalid serializer raises `InvalidSerializer`. Code catching the previous types needs updating.
* `filters`, `builtins` and `node_method_map` on a visitor are now shared objects rather than per instance copies. Adding a filter through `add_filter()` is safe and copies on write, but assigning into `visitor.filters` directly would now leak process wide.
* Literal nodes hold the already escaped value, as the escaping moved to parse time.
* `parse_file_path()` no longer routes through `parse_file()`, so overriding the latter no longer affects the former.
* Parsed templates are cached process wide (bounded at 1024 entries), which is new state that did not exist before.

## Notes for the reviewer

* Cache invalidation uses modification time and size. A change that preserves both is not detected; this is documented at the declaration and matches what comparable engines do.
* The tree copy shares the value and attribute structures between copies. Those are only ever mutated idempotently during a render, which is what makes the sharing safe.
* The previously unused tokenizing regular expressions are kept, since they are part of the public surface of the module.

author: devrohit06
body:
> **Stacked on #2122** (`feat/studio-history-store`). Targets that branch, not `dev`, so the diff here is only the two commits on top. #2122 has to land first, and per the stacked-PR rule it wants `--rebase`, not `--squash` — squashing the base creates duplicate-content conflicts here.

## What this changes

The site-authoring agent can generate its own imagery. `generate_site_image` lands on the `/sites` surface, writes to the site's public asset rail, and returns a permanent URL the agent can put straight into markup.

Scope is the **integration seam only**. New generation capabilities (reference images, video) belong to whoever is working on media-gen; this is the wiring that lets a site use what Studio can already do.

## Why a new server rather than media.py on the allow-list

`surface_registry` has kept `MEDIA_TOOL_IDS` off `/sites` deliberately. Adding them would not have worked anyway — the studio media server differs from what a site needs in three ways:

| | `media.py` | `site_media.py` |
|---|---|---|
| Sink | private adapter → `/api/v1/media/<name>` | `sites.public_assets` → absolute public URL |
| Side effect | creates a ripple gallery pocket on the chat canvas | none |
| Provenance | gallery pocket | `/studio` history, tagged `source="sites"` + `pocket_id` |

That first row is the load-bearing one. A backend-relative URL resolves against the **published site's own domain** and 404s, so every generated image would be a broken box on the live page — and it would look fine in any test that only checks `ok`.

Generation itself is studio's own proxy call, unchanged: same per-tenant LiteLLM virtual key, same spend attribution. Because every image is recorded in the same history `/studio` reads, an asset made while building a site shows up beside the user's own work and can be fed into the Flow canvas with no extra plumbing.

## Wiring

Three points, and missing any one leaves the tool invisible:

1. `CloudSiteMediaMcpProvider` in `extensions.py`
2. the `site_media` entry-point in `ee/pyproject.toml`
3. `SITE_MEDIA_TOOL_IDS` in `sites_allow`

**Deploy note:** entry points come from installed metadata, so the provider only registers after `pocketpaw-ee` is reinstalled. Tests import directly and do not catch that.

## The prompt teaches a ladder, not a tool

Four rungs, in order: owner uploads → stock for ordinary photography (free and instant) → generation for what stock cannot supply → gradient as the floor. Generation is deliberately third because it costs money per image, and the instruction says so.

The ladder is written out in four places, and `_design_system_block` reads `pocketpaw-design-taste`'s SKILL.md **at request time** — so a skill that stops at stock silently overrides the preamble for that turn. All four now agree, and a test keeps them that way.

## What a self-review changed

The headline finding inverted a claim this PR originally made.

**The `/sites` allow-list is not a boundary.** `allow_mcp_tool_ids` defaults to
`None`, which means *no restriction*, and most surface specs set neither
`profile` nor `profile_resolver`. An ambient server is therefore reachable from
`/chat` and elsewhere. Listing the id under `sites_allow` makes the tool
reachable where it is wanted; it does nothing to confine it.

The test meant to catch that could not. It read
`if allow is not None: assert TOOL_ID not in allow` — and `allow` **is** `None`
for CHAT, so the assert never ran. Green, proving nothing, beside a docstring
claiming the opposite.

There is no surface ContextVar to check, and `mcp_servers_allow` is per-*agent*
rather than per-surface, so opt-in would break the "just works on /sites"
behaviour. The guard is intrinsic instead: **the pocket must belong to the
caller's workspace**. A made-up id or another tenant's id buys nothing.
Same-workspace use from another surface still generates, which is spend rather
than a tenancy hole, and metering remains unbuilt.

Also fixed:

- A storage failure that is not a `PublicAssetError` (`StorageFailure`, an S3
  client error) escaped the loop and took the handler with it, discarding images
  already generated, billed and stored in the same call.
- `int(args.get("count"))` was unguarded, so `{"count": "two"}` raised
  `ValueError` out of a handler that returns structured errors everywhere else.
  MCP input schemas are advisory for in-process tools.
- The `model` argument advertised "a catalog image-model id", but
  `service.generate` routes a curated fal id to fal's own endpoint while this
  handler dispatches through the proxy — so ids that work on `/studio` would
  400 here. Removed rather than half-supported; choosing the generator belongs
  with the generation work.
- `pocketpaw-edit-react-site` teaches the ladder and never got the generation
  rung, while the commit adding it claimed "everywhere the ladder is written".
  The drift guard could not see it because the guard carried a hand-written list
  of four files. It discovers them now — a guard against drift that needs manual
  updating drifts the way it exists to prevent.

## Testing

14 new tests, and **12 mutations, all caught**. The mutation plan earned its place twice:

- Dropping `SITE_MEDIA_TOOL_IDS` from `sites_allow` is caught. Registration and reachability are separate facts here — an absent id is filtered out silently and the tool simply never fires.
- The ladder drift guard **escaped its first version**. `design-taste` names the tool twice (ladder and pre-flight checklist), so a whole-file `in` check stayed green while the ladder itself lost its last rung. The guard now checks per paragraph, scoped to paragraphs naming both stock and the gradient fallback, since matching on stock alone also flags a changelog comment and a bare tool-reference list.

660 tests pass across `tests/ee/sites`, `tests/cloud/surface` and `tests/cloud/studio`. All 36 import-linter contracts kept.

**No atlas entry owed** — atlas capabilities are admin-surface operations, not per-MCP-tool (`search_stock_images` and `list_site_assets` are absent too), and no skill directory was added, so the compiled artifact is unchanged. Checked rather than assumed, since that rule is a hard one.

## Already red on dev, unrelated

`test_concierge_autoembed` (×2) and `test_domain_routing` fail on a Paw Bar embed and a custom-domain billing limit. Neither goes near generation, the allow-list or prompts.

## Not solved here

**Nothing meters this.** `StudioModel.credits` is decorative, no route debits a wallet, and `require_license` checks expiry rather than plan. Text→image at least runs on the workspace's own virtual key so the proxy budget and the spend sweep apply; fal ops bill the deployment key with no check before and no ledger row after.

This PR moves generation onto the **agent's** path, where a retry loop can spend with no human between the decision and the bill. The per-call ceiling (`_MAX_IMAGES_PER_CALL = 4`) bounds one call; it is not a meter. Worth deciding whether this ships behind a flag until metering exists.

author: ooshonline
body:
## What I built and why

The first **engine-hardening** cut (roadmap #2), now that the test corpus (#11) exists as a safety net. `analyseWord()` used to strip **any** trailing `s`/`es`/`ing`/`ed` as an inflection, guarded only by "the base is ≥2 letters". That greedy strip quietly **mis-scored a whole class of very common early-reading words** — it treated root-final letters as suffixes:

| word | old reading | problem |
|---|---|---|
| `his`, `bus`, `gas` | base + `-s` | the `s` is the root coda, not a plural |
| `miss`, `class`, `less` | base + `-s` | that's a **double-s**, not a plural |
| `this` | `thi` + `-s` | lost the `sh`… wait, `th`+`i`+`s` — flagged a spurious ending |
| `thing`, `bring`, `string` | base + `-ing` | that's `i` + `ng` (a digraph), one syllable |
| `sled`, `shed`, `bled` | base + `-ed` | that's `e` + `d`, one syllable |
| `notes`, `rides` | base + `-es` → lost the magic-e | should be `note`/`ride` + `-s` |

`his` is one of the most frequent words in any Reception text, so this was worth fixing before anything cosmetic. The engine is the product's credibility, and "restraint over volume" says a night spent hardening the core beats a new panel.

## What changed (words-only walkthrough)

Nothing moves on screen — this is a pure **accuracy** fix inside the scorer. The greedy regex is replaced with four per-suffix phonics guards:

- **`-ing`** strips only when the base carries **its own vowel** — so `jumping → jump`, but `thing`/`bring`/`string`/`king` stay whole (`i` + `ng`).
- **`-ed`** strips only when the base carries its own vowel — so `jumped → jump`, but `sled`/`shed`/`bled`/`fled` stay whole (`e` + `d`).
- **`-es`** strips only after a **sibilant** base (`s`/`x`/`z`/`ch`/`sh`) — the real rule for when English adds `-es`: `boxes → box`, `wishes → wish`, `glasses → glass`, `buses → bus`.
- **`-s`** strips after a **non-sibilant consonant** (`jumps`, `hands`, `cats`) or a **magic-e base** (`rides`, `notes`, `makes`); it never strips after a vowel (`bus`, `his`, `gas`) or after `s`/`x`/`z` (`miss`, `class`, `box`).

So a teacher checking *"The bus is his"* or *"a little sled"* now sees those words scored honestly instead of being told they lean on the *endings* skill.

## Phonics decisions & limitations

- **Sample passage unchanged:** still **92%** on UK Reception and **100%** with everything taught (none of its words are affected), verdict text unchanged.
- **Every prior corpus assertion preserved:** `jumps`, `jumped`, `hands`, `packed`, `kicking`, `wished` all still strip correctly and keep their exact skill sets.
- **Deliberately conservative on vowel-team + plain `-s`:** `sees`/`goes`/`toes` are left whole (scored `["team"]`, i.e. decodable but not additionally crediting *endings*) rather than risk a wrong split — the `-s` there is trivial to read, so this is a safe under-attribution, and it's noted in the corpus.
- **Two residues stay locked as limitations,** each blocked by a *different* engine gap: `hundred` (`hun+dred`) — the base `hundr` still contains a vowel, so the `-ed` guard can't reject it without a coda/syllable check; and `tennis` — the false `-s` strip is now fixed, but the medial `nn` is still read as a blend (the separate medial-double gap).

## Verification

- `npm test` → **PASS**, zero dependencies. Corpus grows **323 → 352 hard assertions**; known limitations **27 → 23** (bus/his/miss/class and the thing/sled families promoted to hard assertions and locked). The passage's 92%/100% headline is asserted and green.
- **Headless Chromium, light + dark:** live `analyseWord` returns the corrected values (`bus`/`his` → decodable CVC, `miss` → double, `class` → blend+double, `thing` → digraph, `sled` → blend, `notes`/`rides` → magic-e+endings; `jumps`/`hands` unchanged); the gauge reads **92%** in both themes; the Node test hook is still browser-inert (`typeof module === "undefined"`); no new console errors beyond the offline Google-Fonts `@import`.

## What I'd build next

The two remaining inflection residues point at the next hardening targets: **medial doubled consonants** (`rabbit`, `kitten`, `tennis`, and the `tt`/`pp` in `little`/`apple`) read as blends rather than doubles, and **`-le` endings** (`little`, `gentle`, `table`) — both named in roadmap #2 and both now backed by the corpus.

body:
Actions Semiconductor ATS2851 controllers can stall BR/EDR Secure
Simple Pairing when the host replies to an IO Capability Request with
Dedicated Bonding.

This was observed with an Actions controller at USB ID 10d7:b012,
revision 88.91, while pairing a Sony WF-C510. After the host sent
Dedicated Bonding, no peer IO Capability Response arrived and the local
host disconnected after approximately 30 seconds.

Sending General Bonding instead allowed the IO capability exchange to
continue, followed by successful Simple Pairing, link key notification
and encryption.

Add a quirk that substitutes General Bonding in the HCI IO Capability
Reply while preserving the MITM bit and the connection authentication
state. Enable it for ATS2851 based devices.

Signed-off-by: Li Daoxun <lidaoxun25@mails.ucas.ac.cn>

## Summary

Adds `--all-hosts` / `-a` to `camp list` and `camp sessions`. Both commands
now answer across every declared machine plus the local one, merging the
per-host answers into a single listing where every row identifies its
originating machine. Hosts are contacted concurrently; the exit status is
read from the local answer alone, so remote reachability never masks the
local command's own status.

## Changes

- Extracts a value-returning local answer and a non-exiting per-host answer
  for both `camp list` and `camp sessions`, decoupling the answer-producing
  logic from process exit.
- Contacts declared hosts concurrently and merges per-host answers into one
  ordered, machine-stamped result.
- Strips control sequences from relayed remote stderr before rendering.
- Isolates a malformed row in the merged renderer so one bad host doesn't
  take down the whole listing.
- Folds the per-row renderers and widening readers into shared helpers.
- Repairs the all-hosts merge's failure-recovery and refusal handling.
