body:
Closes #35

## O que foi feito

- **Backend `bdgd-light serve`** (`src/bdgd_light/console/api.py`, FastAPI + uvicorn): um processo com a `SessaoCOD`, o `Orquestrador` (thread em segundo plano, uma execução por vez) e a `FilaEventos`; serve o `console/dist` e a API `/api/estado`, `/api/estado.geojson`, `/api/eventos` (injetar/reiniciar), `/api/propostas`, `/api/propostas/{id}` (com alternativas e veredito do verificador), `/aprovar` (= executar), `/rejeitar`, `/api/auditoria`, `/api/agente`. Autorização por `BDGD_CONSOLE_TOKEN` ou `--sem-segredo` (demo local, só `X-Operador`).
- **Painel do COD no console** (`console/src/cod.ts`): estado do cluster/agente, botão injetar (ou "reiniciar e injetar"), cartão da proposta (manobras, clientes, score, alternativas, verificador), aprovar/rejeitar, auditoria com hash; mapa recolorido quando o hash da auditoria muda. `?api=` para apontar a outro backend; proxy `/api` no Vite.
- **HITL** (`mcp_server/humano.py`, pedidos da PR-12): `Autorizador` com segredo/operador, token de aprovação com validade, trilha de auditoria.
- **Motor OpenDSS confinado a uma thread** (`twin.powerflow.no_motor`): o DSS C-API mata o processo com `SIGILL` quando chamado de outra thread que não a que o importou (inclusive `NewContext()`); todas as chamadas (e o `import`) vão para um executor de uma thread. Guarda em `tests/conftest.py` para ninguém importar `opendssdirect` na coleta.
- **Robustez com LLM real**: `OpenAICompatClient.chat` repete a chamada quando o provedor devolve mensagem vazia (`MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` do Gemini); perfis reais com 3 tentativas por padrão.
- Smoke `SMOKE_FLUXO=1` (injetar → proposta → aprovar → mapa recolorido) e docs: `docs/console.md` (novo), README, `console/README.md`, diário `docs/review/NOITE-2.md` §8; revisões PR-13/PR-14 do mantenedor versionadas.

## Validação

```bash
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format . && uv run pytest        # 253 passed
cd console && npm run check && npm run build
BDGD_CONSOLE_TOKEN=demo uv run bdgd-light serve --cluster tijuca --provider fake --estado /tmp/serve-demo/estado --fila /tmp/serve-demo/eventos.jsonl
cd console && SMOKE_FLUXO=1 SMOKE_TOKEN=demo node scripts/smoke.mjs "http://127.0.0.1:8000/?cenario=tijuca"
```

Demo ponta a ponta local (Tijuca, Chrome headless): operador fake — proposta em 17,2 s, executada com mapa recolorido em **19,6 s** (467 → 72 trechos desenergizados); `--provider gemini` (gemini-2.5-flash) — 3 execuções, mesmo plano, 41–58 s, ~54 k tokens, 0 recusas do verificador. Detalhes em `docs/console.md`.

Para o mantenedor: `uv run bdgd-light serve --cluster tijuca --provider gemini --sem-segredo` e abrir http://127.0.0.1:8000/?cenario=tijuca.

author: surxe-dev
body:
## What & why

The server is on Valheim 1.0. **Jotunn 2.30.0** is now a 1.0 build, so I re-tested the three mods we'd disabled for 1.0 to see whether the Jotunn fix (their dependency) is enough to bring them back — **on their current versions**, since none of them has shipped a new release.

**Method:** snapshot VM 100, stage each mod as a server `plugin`, restart the container, and read `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` for the latest boot. Then restore and apply the final set via `guests/vm-apply-valheim.sh`.

## Results

| Mod | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **FarmGrid 1.0.0** | ✅ **re-enabled** (optional, client-side) | Loads clean under Jotunn 2.30.0 — no TypeLoad/Harmony/dependency errors. Jotunn was its only blocker. |
| **Huginn Map 1.0.5** | ⚠️ **stays disabled** | Now *loads* ("Huginn active"), but its own code calls 1.0-removed game APIs — `Method not found: Minimap.ReadExploredArray` (map-share) and `Field not found: ZoneSystem.m_activeArea` (boat tracking). Headline features broken; needs a real 1.0 rebuild. |
| **GlassPieces 1.2.5** | ❌ **stays disabled** | Still `TypeLoadException` (VTable setup of its `Collector`/`SliderSwitch`) on 1.0. Depends **only on BepInEx**, not Jotunn — the Jotunn update never applied to it. Needs a rebuild. |

## Applied & verified on VM 100

Ran `vm-apply-valheim.sh`; confirmed the server came up with **3 plugins** (ModSentry 1.0.17, Drop That 3.1.5, Jotunn 2.30.0), **`FarmGrid.dll` in `ModSentry_Optional/`**, no load errors, world loaded, session active. (Restart rotated the crossplay join code, as expected.)

## Also fixed: client-modpack drift

While here, corrected stale client-pack docs/tooling that no longer matched the server policy:
- `build-modpack.sh` bundled all 6 DLLs (incl. disabled GlassPieces/Huginn) → now the real 1.0 set (ModSentry, DropThat, Jotunn + FarmGrid optional).
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` had **pre-1.0** Jotunn/DropThat hashes → regenerated from `dll/`.
- `INSTALL.md`/`README.md` listed GlassPieces as active and DropThat 3.1.4 → corrected to the actual 1.0 set + versions.

## Caveat

FarmGrid's server-side load is fully clean, but it's a client-side build-placement **grid overlay** — that UI wasn't exercised on a real client from the headless server. It's optional and enforces no NetworkCompatibility, so a client-side issue would be local to that player and wouldn't affect the server or others.

author: ajccarlson
body:
A workflow that reports which shapes it can produce works out those shapes from its own limits. If that calculation ever produced a size the workflow would not accept, the whole answer was thrown away - and the width and height the workflow could always be asked for went with it, leaving it reporting that it cannot say anything about the size of its output.

That is a feature taking away something that predates it. The sizes are now settled first, on their own, exactly as they were before shapes were offered at all. The shapes are then worked out and added only if they hold up. A calculation that does not hold up now costs the shapes and nothing else.

Nothing changes for any workflow whose shapes are worked out correctly: the same ratios, the same pixels, the same limits.

author: hellofrequencylab
body:
## What

The root cause of both halves of *"I tried to RSVP with my @frequency account… it should have tried to charge me… this event should be included in the Royal Temple membership."*

**Ticket tiers are rows in `event_ticket_types`, not columns on `events`.** `generateOccurrencesForAnchor` copies `INHERITED_COLUMNS` — columns. So every materialised date of a priced series inherits `price_cents` (it *looks* priced) and has **zero tiers**. Verified in production before writing anything:

| row | price | join_mode | **tiers** | **members-only tiers** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| anchor `meld-community-coworking-royal-temple` | $22 | rsvp | **2** | **1** |
| the date that was RSVP'd to | $22 | rsvp | **0** | **0** |

One missing copy, two symptoms:

1. **No charge is ever attempted.** The paid branch needs `isPaidEvent && hasTiers`; with no tiers it renders the plain RSVP button. A member joins a $22 event for free.
2. **Membership coverage can never apply.** Space-membership inclusion *is* a members-only tier row (`space_members_only` / `space_tier_id`). No tier rows means nothing to be included by. This affected **every date of every recurring priced series**.

## How

- **`occurrenceTierRows(anchorTiers, occurrenceEventId)`** — pure, tested, in the style of `occurrenceRow`/`propagationPatch` beside it. Carries every catalog column: `name`, `description`, `pricing_mode`, `price_cents`, `min_cents`, `suggested_cents`, `quantity`, `member_only`, `space_members_only`, `space_tier_id`, `sort_order`, `active`.
- **Reset by omission**, so the column defaults own them, each named in a comment: `id` (a new row — `event_tickets.ticket_type_id` points at exactly one), **`sold`** (the Stripe-webhook-owned counter; a copied `sold` against a copied `quantity` marks a brand-new date sold out), `created_at`.
- **Scoped to the rows this run actually created.** The occurrence upsert now `.select('id')`s, and `ignoreDuplicates` makes it `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so the returned representation is exactly what was inserted. An occurrence whose tiers a host has since edited is never touched.
- **`setSpaceEventAccess`** now reaches a series anchor's **future** occurrences, so turning on member inclusion doesn't stop at the anchor.
- **A backfill script** for the series already out there (`scripts/backfill-occurrence-ticket-tiers.mts`) — a one-off under `scripts/`, not a migration, dry-run by default, `--apply` to write.

### The gate worth knowing about

`lib/event-recurrence.test.ts` reads the **real column set** of `event_ticket_types` out of `lib/database.types.ts` and asserts **every column is classified** — either carried or on the four-name reset list. A migration that adds a tier column fails CI until someone decides which it is. That is the honest version of this fix: the bug was a column list that could silently fall behind a table.

[ADR-1308](https://github.com/hellofrequencylab/frequency-web/blob/claude/occurrence-ticket-tiers/docs/DECISIONS.md). LIVE-283 opened and closed.

## ⚠️ Numbering, and the production patch already applied

- **Renumbered from ADR-1306/LIVE-281 to ADR-1308/LIVE-283.** This branch was cut from `main`, where the next free numbers *looked* free — but [#2526](https://github.com/hellofrequencylab/frequency-web/pull/2526) is open against the same base and already claims 1306, 1307, 281 and 282. Whichever merged second would have failed `check:adr` on a duplicate, or merged two decisions under one number. The rename was safe to apply file-wide because `main` carries neither, so every occurrence on this branch is this work referring to itself.
- **The Meld series was patched by hand in production today**, at the owner's request: the anchor's two tiers were copied onto its 13 dates with `sold` reset. So the backfill will find nothing to do for Meld. It is still needed for any other priced series, and the code fix is what stops the drift returning on the next minted date.

## How to review (owner)

1. Wait for CI to go green (that IS the code review).
2. After merge, on production: let the daily cron mint the next Meld date (or add one), and confirm it arrives carrying **Day pass** and **Royal Temple Member** rather than bare.
3. Open any Meld date as a **Social Member** — the rate should read **Included**. As anyone else, the $22 flow should appear instead of a free RSVP button.
4. Optionally run the backfill dry (no `--apply`) to see what other series are affected.

## Verification

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] eslint `--max-warnings=0` on all touched files
- [x] `pnpm test` — 1190 tests across `lib/event-recurrence`, `lib/events/`, `app/(main)/events/` after the renumber; the agent's fuller run was 10,980 across `lib/**`
- [x] `check:backlog` (640 entries, 475 probes agree), `check:adr` (1132 distinct, each declared once), `check:schema-contract`, `check:authz`, `check:rls`, `check:one-list`
- [x] Read the live tier configuration and the affected rows before writing
- [ ] Checked the Vercel preview

## Notes / follow-ups

- **No migration.** The drift is data; the repair prints before it writes and was not run from here.
- **A tier's inventory is now per-date.** Right for "seats in the room", wrong for "passes for the season". Nothing in the model distinguishes them and no host has asked; recorded in the ADR.
- **`setSpaceEventAccess` reaches the occurrences that exist when it runs.** Dates minted later get their tiers from the anchor via the mint — same shape, different moment. Also in the ADR.
- Two test files fail in the agent's sandbox for environment reasons and are untouched by this diff (`copy-maplibre-worker`, `check-docs-links`); both fail on `main` there too.

body: Follow-up to #485 (#482). ## What changed The `dev` script now passes `--disable-source-maps`: ```diff - "dev": "next dev --turbopack -p ${RTX_PORT:-${PORT:-3000}}", + "dev": "next dev --turbopack --disable-source-maps -p ${RTX_PORT:-${PORT:-3000}}", ``` `next dev` normally forks `next-server` with `NODE_OPTIONS=--enable-source-maps`, so Node parses and caches the source map of every server chunk it loads. Once 16.3 evicts Turbopack's native memory, that cache is the largest avoidable part of the dev server's V8 heap. With the flag, `next-server` starts with empty `NODE_OPTIONS`. ## Measurements Same harness and 13-route sequence as #485: warm cache, Next.js 16.3.4, 2 min idle. The two control runs bracket the flag runs. | Run | Ready | First visit, 13 routes | Revisit | Phys footprint ready / after 13 routes / idle | **V8 heap used, idle** | HMR client / server | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Control | 529 ms | 9.95 s | 8.32 s | 378 / 748 / 689 MB | **415 MB** | 721 / 320 ms | | Control (repeat) | 554 ms | 10.19 s | 8.89 s | 567 / 1,003 / 948 MB | **410 MB** | 827 / 213 ms | | `--disable-source-maps` | 431 ms | 9.41 s | 8.34 s | 320 / 581 / 517 MB | **272 MB** | 321 / 216 ms | | `--no-server-fast-refresh` (rejected) | 547 ms | 15.40 s | 9.10 s | 444 / 2,193 / 900 MB | 415 MB | 415 / 541 ms | - **The reliable win is about 140 MB of V8 heap (−34%).** Old space falls from 216 MB to 92 MB. Idle heap sat at 403–421 MB across every 16.3.4 run in #485, so 272 MB is well outside the noise. - **Physical footprint moves by the same amount only some of the time.** Turbopack's native eviction varies by about ±250 MB between otherwise identical runs, as the two controls show. Count on the heap figure, not a specific footprint number. - **Timing:** ready time, compile, revisit, and HMR are unchanged or faster. No run produced a non-200 response, an error overlay, or a full reload. - **Rejected:** `--no-server-fast-refresh` is worse across the board. ## What you give up (checked) Nothing observable here. I used a temporary probe route under both configs: | | With `--enable-source-maps` | With `--disable-source-maps` | |---|---|---| | Error thrown in a route handler (Next logs it) | `src/app/api/…/route.ts:2:9` | `src/app/api/…/route.ts:2:9` | | `console.error(err)` | `src/app/api/…/route.ts:2:10` | `src/app/api/…/route.ts:2:10` | | Raw `err.stack` string | `.next/dev/server/chunks/[root-of-the-server]__….js` | `.next/dev/server/chunks/[root-of-the-server]__….js` | Next source-maps the errors it prints itself, and its own `prepareStackTrace` means a raw `err.stack` was never mapped by Node in the first place. Browser devtools source maps are unaffected; this only concerns the Node process. ## Verification - **Local App invocation:** `RTX_PORT=3487 npm run dev` serves `/dashboard` and `/api/health` with 200, and `next-server`'s `NODE_OPTIONS` is empty. - **CI:** the flag only affects `next dev`, which the gate does not run. CI still runs `check:all` on the unchanged build path. ## Not in this PR The production build is the memory floor: `next build` + `next start` runs the same sequence at 180 / 228 / 193 MB with a 120 MB heap. That's what marketplace installs already run. Using it for the canonical dev Local App would trade HMR for about 70–80% less memory, and it is a workflow decision rather than a code change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_018TfFDnLij6BPLPqTD2LFmu --- ## Summary by cubic Adds `--disable-source-maps` to the `dev` script so `next dev` starts `next-server` without Node source maps. This cuts the idle V8 heap from ~415 MB to ~272 MB (−34%) with no observable behavior change. **Notes** - Node was parsing and caching the source map of every server chunk; that cache was the largest avoidable part of the heap after Turbopack's native memory eviction. - Error source maps are unaffected: Next source-maps errors it prints itself, and raw `err.stack` was never mapped by Node. - Ready time, first-visit compile, revisit, and HMR are unchanged or faster. - CI is unaffected because the flag only applies to `next dev`, not the build or start paths. Written for commit dd2c156a1b841a5d53878c6d38a1807983e9ffaa. Summary will update on new commits.

author: doogit
body:
## Why

The dashboard's document-local response cache could retain unbounded entries, cached network-only payloads it should never keep, and issued duplicate concurrent requests for the same data (measured: 2 duplicate eligible requests per Overview document). This PR ships the PERF3 browser-cache wave, plus the Settings restructure / idle-sessions removal and deferred-chart skeleton from the UI-review lane, exported together from the private mainline.

## What changed

- Bounded the UI response cache: 128-entry cap with TTL-based eviction (45 s), expired entries dropped on read.
- Network-only endpoints (`/api/live`, `/api/status`, `/api/burn-status`) bypass payload caching; freshness timestamps are tracked separately so sidebar/Overview freshness still renders.
- Request coalescing: concurrent reads for the same cache key share one in-flight fetch; per-caller abort detaches only that subscriber, last-abort cancels the transport, rejections are never cached.
- Successful mutations clear the cache generationally so an in-flight fetch started before the clear cannot repopulate stale data.
- Settings page restructured into 4 groups; the idle-sessions list and its end-session action are removed (product decision — never re-add a session list to Settings).
- Deferred charts render a skeleton placeholder instead of a ghost loader.
- D7 loop-analysis review fix (`dd45bff`, merged via #13) reconciled into the export baseline.

## Files changed overview

- `src/ui/api/client.ts` — bounded cache, network-only bypass, generation-counter invalidation, in-flight transport sharing.
- `src/ui/settings/SettingsPage.tsx` — 4-group restructure; idle-sessions panel removed.
- `src/ui/shell/DeferredChart.tsx` — skeleton placeholder for deferred chart loading.
- `src/ui/recommendations/RecCard.tsx` — native disclosure semantics for recommendation actions.
- `test/ui/api-cache.test.ts` — new: bounds, TTL, network-only bypass, invalidation, coalescing (11 tests).
- `test/ui/freshness-integration.test.tsx`, `test/ui/foreground-poll.test.tsx` — new route-navigation acceptance: cached remount issues no refetch; freshness survives non-retained payloads.
- `test/ui/settings.test.tsx`, `test/ui/rec-actions.test.tsx`, `test/ui/lazy-loading.test.tsx` — updated for the restructure/skeleton.
- `test/ui/idle-sessions-panel.test.tsx`, `test/ui/settings-fb6.test.tsx` — removed with the idle-sessions surface.

## Test evidence

Private union head (source of this export), all gates:

```
tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.node.json && tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.ui.json  (pass)
node suite:  Tests  1587 passed | 1 skipped (1588)
UI suite:    Tests  648 passed | 4 skipped (652)
```

This PR's CI: `ci` + package-smoke (ubuntu/macos/windows) + stranger-smoke — all green.

Before/after benchmark campaigns (3 matched runs each, frozen PERF0 budgets):

```
duplicate_eligible_requests (overview): 2 -> 0 (every run, every scale)
app query-cache retention: 6 -> 3 entries (~9.7 KB -> ~6.1 KB)
long tasks per navigation: 1 (68 ms max) -> 0
warm navigation worst: 45.1 ms -> 26.8 ms (budgets: <=45/50/50 ms at 1k/10k/100k — all pass)
```

## Success criteria

- Duplicate same-document requests eliminated — met (2 → 0, repeatable across 3 runs × 3 scales).
- Cache bounded with no freshness regression — met (retention down, route-navigation + freshness acceptance tests green).
- No daemon-side change — met (diff touches `src/ui/` + `test/ui/` only).
- Residual: cold-navigation and layout metrics each showed one isolated single-observation ambient spike per campaign (both directions, same shape before and after); medians and 2-of-3 runs sit inside every budget.

## Risk & rollback

If the coalescing or invalidation logic is wrong, stale or shared responses could render until the 45 s TTL expires; revert this PR (single export commit) to restore the previous unbounded-cache behavior.

author: atelypham
body:
## Description

The download-all pre-zip build opens one storage read per photo and hands each stream straight to archiver, which uses them one at a time. Every read past the one being written parks an S3 socket holding megabytes of unread data, and both early exits abandon all of them: archiver's `abort()` does not touch its source streams, and the error path only removes the temp directory. Nothing else reclaims those sockets, because the SDK arms its socket timeout on a 3s delay and clears it as soon as the response headers land, so a fast response never gets one at all.

On an S3 deployment running v3.45.15 that left 43 of the 50 pooled sockets ESTABLISHED with between 1.3MB and 4.9MB sitting unread in each receive queue, tx_queue empty, no kernel timer, byte identical across a resample seven days apart. In the same log, 48 `POST /api/admin/events/*/upload` starts against 11 completions, and `socket usage at capacity=50 and 261 additional requests are enqueued`. Uploads stopped completing and nothing surfaced an error. Recycling the process was the only way out.

The common trigger is an ordinary upload, not a client disconnect. `invalidate()` runs on every photo upload, delete and bulk edit, and it aborts an in-flight build.

Local filesystem installs are not affected. They take the `archive.file(filePath, ...)` branch and open no sockets, which is probably why this has gone unnoticed.

### What changed

- Track every storage read the build opens and destroy all of them on every exit path, including the invalidated one.
- Cancel an in-flight build from `invalidate()` rather than waiting for the loop to reach its next version check. Without this the loop can park waiting for a read slot that a stalled archive will never free.
- Cap reads in flight at 2. A 120 photo build peaked at 50 concurrent GETs, the whole agent pool, which starves uploads, thumbnailing and gallery reads for the duration of the build even when nothing fails.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

`backend/__tests__/services/downloadZipSocketLeak.test.js` covers a source stream dying mid build, an upload invalidating the build, and the cap on reads in flight. All three fail on `main`.

Separately, against a fake S3 endpoint and the SDK version this repo pins, with no PicPeak code in the picture: the build ends with `aborted` and 11 of 12 sockets are still ESTABLISHED 75 seconds later, past the configured 60 second `socketTimeout`. Destroying the appended streams is what closes them.

- [x] Unit tests pass (`npm test`)
- [x] Manual testing completed

**Test Configuration**:
* PicPeak Version: main, leak observed on v3.45.15
* Node.js Version: 24
* Database: SQLite for the tests, PostgreSQL on the affected deployment
* Browser: n/a

## Checklist:

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

author: sunnywang666
body:
## Confirmed bound-text deadlock and direct repair

The bound-text account selector held AccountService's non-reentrant lock while calling ModelCatalogService.route_for_model. The catalog calls AccountService.list_accounts and attempts the same lock. Any explicit model (including Production's gpt-5-6) can deadlock before an upstream text submission. The health handler synchronously reads get_stats on that lock and then stalls the event loop as well.

Move model lookup outside the account lock. Resolve the binding and validate current account status/type under the lock afterward; token refresh stays outside. Do not replace Lock with RLock, bypass model authority, or change account selection.

The regression uses the real AccountService and ModelCatalogService with a controlled outer catalog backend: three bound requests and health read. It failed on the old implementation before reaching the backend; after repair all three use their original binding, health remains responsive while model lookup waits, and only one catalog refresh occurs. Disabled and wrong-model accounts remain rejected. Model catalog, routing, continuation and image-task suites: 38 passed on local Python 3.12; exact release runtime preflight remains a separate deployment step.

Read-only Production evidence: original requests start 2026-09-10T16:44:01.497Z; last successful Provider health response 16:44:01.243Z, then health stalled. At 18:29 UTC Provider was unhealthy with 752 consecutive health failures, 0% CPU, main process waiting on futex, no restart/OOM; egress was healthy. The running Worker explicitly uses gpt-5-6. TAT reads inv-d8gwr5g49w, inv-d8gwrughqx, inv-d8gwt10j3t; no service restart or external write. Exact live Python stack was not dumped; deterministic source-path reproduction and runtime symptoms establish the deadlock diagnosis.

## Result recovery scope

Add authenticated read-only recovery of the original bound text result on the existing conversation-bindings/text resource. Validate bound account, conversation, original active-branch anchor, and completed final assistant text. Initial stream failure can read an already completed answer once; no new message or account failover is issued.

## Source and integration target

This candidate starts at f368c4daeaa223ae44dc3f14fa6c582a916025ce on codex/content-image-task-session-v2-20260825, the company Provider line used by Workbench. It does not rebase onto or import upstream main. Review only this bounded delta.

## Verification and limits

- Existing conversation-continuation and image-task suites: 22 tests passed.
- Tests exercise FastAPI GET through the service with only account/backend boundaries substituted; missing auth and mismatched account fail closed.
- Partial text, analysis messages, a later user turn and wrong conversation cannot become a successful original answer.
- Existing protocol documentation updated in place.
- No live Provider requests, Production changes or real generation were performed. Old attempts whose original cursor was lost are not reconstructed or automatically retried.

Deploy this Provider support before the paired Workbench Worker consumer. This is a draft source candidate, not a release or live incident resolution.

## Resumo

Fecha o lote hub-staleness (#7101 anthropic-claude, #7103 openai-chatgpt).

de uma vez" contava 2× em QUALQUER consumidor da camada unificada (hubs,
`corpus-index-coverage-report.ts`, `regenerate-entity-pages.ts`, etc.) —
visível ao vivo no dry-run do `hub-staleness-check.ts`, que listava a mesma

author: bagelbits
body:
## What does this do? - Moves the runtime to **Ruby 3.4.10** and **Rails 8.1.3.1**. Rails 8.1 declares `required_ruby_version >= 3.2.0`, so the Ruby bump is a precondition, not a nicety. - Replaces **webpacker** with **shakapacker 10**. Webpacker is retired and cannot run on Rails 8; this is the largest behavioural change in the PR and is detailed below. - Walks `config.load_defaults` from **6.0 to 8.1**, one version at a time. - Drops gems that have no Rails 8 story: `turbolinks`, `sass-rails` (unmaintained `sassc` backend, now `dartsass-sprockets`), `spring`/`spring-watcher-listen`, and `byebug` (now `debug`). - Rebuilds CI, which was pinned to a toolchain that no longer exists. **Product context** No Linear issue or Notion spec — this is maintenance work with no ticket. Flagging that rather than leaving the section blank. ## The webpacker to shakapacker migration Two shakapacker defaults differ from webpacker in ways that silently break react-rails server rendering. Both took a real fix, not a config toggle. 1. **Shakapacker fingerprints packs into a `js/` subdirectory.** react-rails' built-in `SeparateServerBundleContainer` does a raw `File.read` on `public_output_path.join(filename)`, which assumed webpacker's flat, unhashed layout. Server rendering now resolves the bundle through the manifest instead (`config/initializers/react_server_rendering.rb`). 2. **Shakapacker enables chunk splitting; webpacker did not.** Splitting scattered the `server_rendering` entry across five files, and react-rails only ever evaluates one — so `ReactRailsUJS` landed in a chunk the renderer never loaded. Splitting is disabled to keep each entry self-contained. ```mermaid flowchart TD Src["app/javascript/packs/*"] --> WP["shakapacker + webpack
(splitting disabled — THIS PR)"] WP --> Manifest["public/packs*/manifest.json
fingerprinted, under js/"] Manifest --> Browser["javascript_pack_tag
browser bundle"] Manifest --> Container["Manifest-based SSR container
(THIS PR)"] Container --> SSR["react-rails ExecJS
server-rendered HTML"] classDef pr fill:#DDF4FF,stroke:#0969DA,stroke-width:2px,color:#111827 classDef ext fill:#F6F8FA,stroke:#57606A,stroke-width:1px,color:#111827 class WP,Container pr class Src,Manifest,Browser,SSR ext ``` ## Breakage the new versions required fixing - `ActiveRecord::MigrationContext`'s second argument was **removed in Rails 7.2**. `config/application.rb` still passed it, which crashed boot outright. - `rspec-rails` 8 renamed `fixture_path` to `fixture_paths`. - `ActionController::ParameterMissing`'s message gained `"or invalid"` in Rails 8; ten spec assertions matched the exact string. - `cache_classes` → `enable_reloading`, and `action_dispatch.show_exceptions` takes `:none` rather than `false` since 7.1.
The json 3 trap — worth a look, since it would have landed in production, not CI Updating rubocop pulled **json 2 → 3**, which drops the `create_additions` keyword from `JSON.parse`. That silently broke two gems at their locked versions: - `execjs` 2.8.1 — failed on every server-rendered request. - `sprockets` 4.2.1 — failed in `Sprockets::Manifest#json_decode`. The sprockets failure only appears **once a manifest file exists to parse**, which means a clean test run stays green and the first production precompile is where it bites. A full `bundle update` picks up releases of both that account for json 3.
## `load_defaults` 6.0 → 8.1 Stepped one version at a time with the suite run in between. No application changes were needed at any step — the app serializes nothing through YAML columns, keeps no persistent cache (`:null_store`/`:memory_store` only), calls `to_time` nowhere, and already pinned the cookie serializer to `:json`. ## CI The existing workflow could not have passed on this branch. It requested an undefined `${{ env.RUBY_VERSION }}`, installed Node 14, and ran `yarn install --pure-lockfile` against a repo that carries only a `package-lock.json`. It now reads `.ruby-version` and `.nvmrc`, installs with `npm ci`, and talks to the MySQL service container rather than the runner's own daemon. ## How was it tested? All checks below were run from a **clean database, cleared caches, and a fresh `npm ci`**. - [x] RSpec — 68 examples, 0 failures - [x] RuboCop — 67 files, no offenses - [x] Production `assets:precompile` succeeds - [x] Manual dev-environment validation — homepage and `/admin` return 200, React content confirmed present in the server-rendered HTML - [ ] CI green on this branch — has not run yet; this push is the first time the new workflow executes
Command evidence ```bash bundle exec rspec # 68 examples, 0 failures bundle exec rubocop # 67 files inspected, no offenses detected SECRET_KEY_BASE_DUMMY=1 RAILS_ENV=production NODE_ENV=production \ bundle exec rails assets:precompile # [Shakapacker] Completed webpack build in 3.53s curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3124/ # 200 curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3124/admin # 200 ``` Local MySQL ran as an 8.0 container; CI uses the same major version.
## Deliberately not included - **113 autocorrectable RuboCop offences** are parked in a regenerated `.rubocop_todo.yml`. They are pre-existing debt surfaced by newer cops and the Ruby 3.4 target; autocorrecting would bury the upgrade in unrelated spec churn. - **7 npm advisories** remain, all reachable only through `webpack-dev-server` (`qs`, `uuid`, `sockjs`). `npm audit --omit=dev` is clean of anything the app ships. npm's proposed fix is installing `webpack-dev-server@1.16.5` — a four-major-version downgrade — so it was refused. - **eslint 8 is EOL.** Moving to 9 is a flat-config migration and belongs in its own PR. ## Two pre-existing issues noticed, not addressed Both predate this branch and are called out only because the upgrade work surfaced them: 1. `config/application.rb` runs migrations from `after_initialize` on every web boot. This is why the database must already exist before the app can boot at all — it is the reason `db:create` cannot work and CI has to create the schema by hand. 2. The layout loads **Bootstrap 4.4.1 from a CDN** while `package.json` carries `bootstrap ^5.3.3` and `react-bootstrap` 2.x, which targets Bootstrap 5. ## Was any impacted documentation updated? No committed docs changed. The repo has no README section covering setup versions or the asset pipeline, so nothing there went stale. ## A note for the reviewer `brew install mysql-client` was needed locally for the `mysql2` native extension to build against Ruby 3.4. ## Summary

Static, no-build website for Koka Group LLC (The Koka Group), an independent P&C insurance agency in Michigan. author: anishkajan
body:
Two additions to `publish.yml`, both on a published release, both skipped for a prerelease. Together they make a release the single event that updates every distribution channel: PyPI, the GitHub Release, the R2 mirror, and now the install script.

## `latest.txt`

The mirror job points `hydracuda/latest.txt` at the new tag, then reads it back and compares.

That object is what `curl … | sh` resolves when nobody pins a version, and it is the **only mutable key in the bucket** — everything under `hydracuda/<tag>/` is immutable and would 404 rather than serve the wrong bytes. A stale pointer is therefore the one thing in this pipeline that regresses silently: every new install quietly gets the previous version and nothing else notices. Hence the read back, rather than trusting the exit code of the write.

Not written for a prerelease: `latest` is what a first-time install gets, and that is never a release candidate. A prerelease stays installable with `HCUDA_VERSION=<tag>`.

## The dispatch

A terminal `redeploy-installer` job sends a `repository_dispatch` of type `hydracuda-release` to [Xtrinel-Group/hydracuda-install](https://github.com/Xtrinel-Group/hydracuda-install), which is where the Worker lives, with the tag in `client_payload`. This is the trigger you asked for; the Worker's own `push: main` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers stay as they are for iterating on its code.

The Worker resolves versions through `latest.txt`, so it does not strictly *need* a redeploy to serve a new release. What this buys is that a Worker running older code than its own `main` cannot survive a release unnoticed, and that the tag arriving in the payload lets the deploy check what it deployed against what was released instead of deploying blind.

## One thing you need to add

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to this repository, so it cannot dispatch to another one. This needs a secret **in HYDRACUDA**:

| Secret | What |
| --- | --- |
| `INSTALL_DISPATCH_TOKEN` | fine-grained PAT, Contents: write on `Xtrinel-Group/hydracuda-install`, nothing else |

Contents: write is what the `repository_dispatch` endpoint requires; there is no narrower permission for it.

**Until that secret exists, the next release will show one failed job** — `redeploy-installer`, with an error naming the missing secret. Everything before it (PyPI, release assets, mirror, `latest.txt`) will have already succeeded, and the Worker can be deployed by hand from its own repository. I chose failing over skipping deliberately: a redeploy that silently stops happening is indistinguishable from one that works. Say the word if you would rather it be a warning.

## Verification

- `pytest -q` — 468 pass. `tests/test_workflows.py` is 27 with 6 new assertions: the pointer is written from the tag and to the bucket root (not under the tag prefix, which would leave the default install unchanged), it is read back and compared, both the pointer step and the dispatch job are prerelease-gated, the dispatch names the event type the Worker subscribes to and carries the tag, the token is `INSTALL_DISPATCH_TOKEN` and not `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and a missing token exits 1 with an `::error::`.
- The R2 secrets test indexed the mirror job's **last** step by position. The new step would have moved that assertion onto `latest.txt` and left the artifact upload unchecked — it is now parameterized over both steps that talk to R2. Verified by reverting the fix and watching it pass with a gutted upload step.
- The event type is checked against the live Worker's own `deploy.yml`, which already subscribes to `repository_dispatch: types: [hydracuda-release]`.
- The Worker is deployed and reachable at `https://hydracuda-install.fancy-dust-86bb.workers.dev`; an end-to-end `HCUDA_VERSION=v0.5.0` install through it verified the checksum against the mirrored `SHA256SUMS` and ran `hcuda 0.5.0`. `/latest.txt` is a 404 today, which is exactly what this PR fixes — for the next release, since nothing here backfills 0.5.0.

Not verified: nothing in this diff has executed. It runs on the next published release. Both steps are `aws s3 cp` against a prefix the mirror job already writes to with the same credentials, and the dispatch is one `gh api` call.

## Backfilling 0.5.0

`latest.txt` will not exist until the next release. If you want `curl | sh` to work before then, the object can be written by hand — one `aws s3 cp` — or 0.5.1 will do it. Your call; I have not touched the bucket.

Closes #269. Part of #267.

**This is #265's content, unchanged, retargeted at `main`.** #265 was merged — but into `feat/loadgen-skeleton` (its stated base), and #264 had already merged that branch into `main` before it, so W1's content never actually reached `main`: `main` today has `loadgen/Main.scala` and nothing else under `loadgen/src`. #265 is closed and GitHub will not let a closed PR's base be changed, hence a new PR rather than an edit.

Same single commit, rebased onto the current `main` (`f12b530`). Verified after the rebase, together with the four Phase 1 tracks merged on top: **125 loadgen + 19 mockapi tests pass**.

## Housekeeping this implies

- **`feat/loadgen-skeleton` should be deleted after this merges.** It currently holds `W0 + the W1 merge` on top of the *old* `main`. If it were ever merged to `main` after this PR, W1's files would arrive a second time. I have not deleted it — it is not mine to remove — but it should not be merged.
- #269 will close on this merge; #268 (W0) closed with #264.

## What this adds (unchanged from #265)

- **`config/LoadgenConfig.scala`** — the full HOCON tree from dev spec §5, decoded via `zio-config-magnolia`, the same mechanism `CoreConfig`/`EdgeConfig` use. One deviation, called out in the file: the spec used `session.actions` and a top-level `actions` for two unrelated things (a NegBinomial count distribution vs. the ten business-action definitions), so the former is `session.action-count` here.
- **`LoadgenConfigSpec.scala`** — decodes a full example campaign config, plus a coordinator config that omits `shard`.
- **`protocol/{AuthClient,EdgeClient,AdminClient}.scala`** — the three client traits (§4). `AdminClient`'s payloads are `Json.Obj` placeholders: the point of the trait now is *which* admin operations a campaign needs, not their wire shape (track E replaces them).
- **`protocol/ProtocolError.scala`** — the error ADT, with `StepUpRequired`/`Forbidden`/`Unauthorized` kept out of the failure channel as documented outcomes. Track F (#290) now enforces that split structurally.
- **`protocol/{Acr,ConversationStep}.scala`** — ported from `e2e/.../support/` per §3.1, with the meta-tag regex hoisted to a top-level `val` instead of being recompiled per page.
- **`protocol/Types.scala`** — opaque wrappers so a CSRF token cannot be passed where a conversation cookie is expected, plus the small result types.
- **`model/{VirtualUser,DeviceSession}.scala`** — the driver-side shapes behind `vu_users`/`vu_sessions`.

## Review fixes already folded in

- `shard` is `Option[ShardConfig]` — it was required, which would have failed decode for every coordinator/seed/provision config before role dispatch could read `role`.
- `EdgeClient.call` takes one `EdgeCredential` (`Cookie` | `Bearer`) instead of two `Option`s documented as "exactly one" — edge prefers the bearer token when both arrive, so the looser signature let a caller measure the mobile path while believing it measured the web one.
- `ActionOutcome` carries `rotatedSession: Option[EdgeSession]`, so a driver can actually adopt edge's rotated cookie rather than dying mid-run with a stale one.
- Every default parameter value dropped, per #267.

## Known gaps the Phase 1 tracks found in these contracts

Not fixed here — they need decisions, and are itemised on #267:

- `VirtualUser`/`DeviceSession` are strict subsets of what track C must persist (missing credentials, expiries, `acr`, `state`), so #288 carries superset rows with projections.
- `CampaignPhaseConfig`'s three independent `Option`s permit both ambiguous and incomplete phases; #289 dispatches on field presence and rejects both, but a sealed variant here would make them unrepresentable.
- `StoreConfig` has no credentials, so nothing can build the emulator's own datasource from it (#288).
- `session.action-count.dispersion` names no convention (#289).
- `ProtocolError.scala` is not `scalafmt`-clean; CI does not gate formatting today.

author: shayann07
body:
The clones from the first competitive audit were never kept, so every later question about what someone else does had nothing to consult. All eight repositories are on disk now, in `liquidglass-competitors` next to this one, and this document carries the file and line for every claim.

### What it settles

- **The field is three lineages, not eight.** PrismalAGSL and liquify are Kyant0's shader, same algorithm and same constants. liquify says so in its header; Prismal does not, but the code settles it. Kyant0's family is one vote, not three.
- **Our sampling-direction claim is correct**, verified three ways. Kyant0 negates the amount at the host and *deletes* the padding outward sampling would need, so outward is structurally impossible there. QWEA0 defaults `refractDir` to −1. Cloudy subtracts an outward normal.
- **QWEA0's "pixel-measured iOS replica" does not survive the code.** Eyedropped colours and hand-typed point coordinates in a demo Activity. The test suite is two IDE templates and one suite covering blur energy conservation.
- **Blur-before-refraction is universal.** haze recovers a sharp rim by punching a hole and refilling from the unblurred capture, which is a real trade rather than a mistake.

### What is worth taking

Nineteen techniques ranked by value over cost. The top three are not optics:

1. Render the glass graph at ~0.7 scale, adaptively. haze measured a 39.7% cut in median frame time going from 0.75 to 0.5.
2. Draw the shadow **into** the backdrop so the glass refracts its own contact shadow.
3. Composite highlights in a perceptual space with a chroma term. Adding white, which is what we do, desaturates every highlight.

### A bug this found in ours

Our capture padding has no dispersion term, so a high `dispersion` with a high `refractionDepth` clips the fringe at the rim. No shipped preset is near the threshold. Not fixed here; it wants a rendered test at an exaggerated value.

### Hardware facts, checked not assumed

- The platform backdrop path is real and haze ships it flag-gated, needing Android 17.2. The Pixel 7 reports `sdk_full` 37.0 and the installed platform is `android-37.0` with no backdrop method, so that work is blocked on a build, not on hardware.
- The Huawei is a JKM-LX1 on API 28 with OpenGL ES 3.2. The sample installs and runs without a crash and the fallback measures as documented, a lit rim at 124 against a body at 81. Cloudy's AGSL-to-GLSL-ES translation is a much cheaper route to a real material there than QWEA0's native path.

### Source change

One line: an inline credit to Kyant0 on `gradRoundRect`, matching what `NOTICE` already records and how haze and QWEA0 are credited a few lines away. No behaviour change; `:liquidglass:allTests` green locally.

body:
A failed TUI save could report a conflict and then lose the local draft when a background reload arrived. Save failures now keep reloads paused, including results already in flight, until a save succeeds. The unsaved warning survives input cancellation, and further edits cannot trigger a merge against an undo snapshot containing unsaved work.

Reload eligibility is shared between scheduling and result handling, which also prevents an in-flight result from replacing data while typing or choosing a move destination. The UI and README explain that drafts remain session-only and are lost on exit; durable recovery and conflict resolution remain future work.

Validation: `go test -count=1 ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, and `go vet ./...` passed with isolated HOME directories. Added regression coverage for conflict reloads, input cancellation and validation, subsequent edits, ordinary save failures, successful retry, and reload results arriving during input or move selection.

author: szymonpajzert
body:
The gap between the columns of „Rozkład ocen: Dobre znalezisko" was about two thirds of a column wide, which is what „Co się działo w bazie" looked like before it went to 90% - the same complaint, a screen further down.

`barPlotOptions` said it capped a bar at 24px. It does not: `maxBarThickness` is Chart.js's option and ApexCharts reads nothing of the sort, so the cap was decoration and `columnWidth` was setting the geometry by itself - 60% shared, and 62% and 72% where the two vote charts narrowed it further. Five buckets in the ~465px plot a half-width card gives on a 1200px page is a 58px column with 35px of white either side of it.

So: one shared 85%, the dead option deleted from the theme and from the timeline's `MAX_COLUMN_PX`, and both overrides dropped. Nothing caps a column now because nothing ever did; what does it is the page, which is 1200px at most, and the comment says so - along with what a chart of fewer than five categories would need instead.

The timeline keeps its 90%. Thirty columns read as a shape rather than as scattered pins only that tight, and it is the same 5% either way at five.

## 📌 Description

Add SM120/SM121 NVFP4 support to the existing explicit `mm_fp4(..., backend="cute-dsl")` path. Hardware validation is on SM121 (DGX Spark/GB10); SM120 is still pending. This draft does not claim a performance improvement over tuned CUTLASS or an end-to-end speedup.

The SM12x runner accepts packed uint8 NVFP4 operands, BF16 output, 128x4 E4M3 scale storage, N divisible by 128, and K divisible by 256. Narrow kernels handle ragged M; full-tile kernels are admitted only when M is divisible by 128. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly.

The runner uses CuTe kernels for every admitted shape. It revalidates cached tactics against the actual shape, including M=5000 sharing the 8192-row tuning bucket, and uses separate compiler namespaces for its kernel families. SM12x launches remain stream ordered for either `enable_pdl` hint value. Automatic selection, the public `b12x` backend, and existing SM10x CuTe behavior stay unchanged.

Related: #3170 and #4223. The open #4071 ports a broader kernel collection into `flashinfer.experimental.sm12x`; this proposal integrates dense NVFP4 with the existing public `cute-dsl` backend and its autotuner, including actual-shape cache validation. Its kernel-family overlap is acknowledged. The existing b12x implementation from #4253 remains intact. #5093 separately changes CUTLASS scheduler tactics.

author: henrypinkard
body:
A test run that dies without its run-end cleanup leaves its whole `romp-tests-*` temp root behind; the kernel's boot reconcile now removes such roots when their owning pid is dead.

## Tier

Tier: fix

## Why

`tests/conftest.py` mints one private `romp-tests-*` root per run under the system temp dir and removes it at run end (PR #944 and follow-ups). A run that dies without reaching that removal (pytest-timeout's `os._exit`, a kernel restart cutting the tool shell, the cut-turn reaper's kill) leaves the root standing with every worker root and child scratch inside it. On the shared devbox those roots, together with sessions' scratch, piled into millions of small files, and the next boot's `/tmp` cleanup spent 39 minutes deleting them while ssh, Tailscale and the romp manager all waited behind it (2026-09-10).

## What

- `tests/conftest.py`: writes an owner marker (`romp-tests-owner.json`: the run's pid and start time) into the root and into the package state dir at mint time.
- `kernel/sdk_backend.py`: `sweep_dead_test_roots(tmpdir)` removes `romp-tests-*` directories whose marker names a dead pid. A live pid stays; a root with no marker or an unreadable one stays (refusing is the safe direction: the sweep cannot tell a foreign directory or a pre-marker root from a leak). `_boot_reconcile` calls it beside the orphan-CLI reap and the leftover-scope sweep and reports the count in its summary line. Under the suite the kernel's tmpdir is the run's own root (TMPDIR is redirected), so a test kernel never reaches the real system temp dir.

Not in scope: sessions' worktrees and scratch parked under `/tmp` by hand (a fleet-brief rule, not code) and the pr-watch skill's own scratch sweep (its skill file).

## Tests

`tests/test_test_root_sweep.py` (new, 9 tests): a dead-owner root goes and is counted; a live-owner root, an unmarked root, an unreadable marker, a marker without a pid, a foreign prefix and a symlink all stay; the running suite's own root carries a marker naming this process and survives a sweep of its parent; the marker name agrees between conftest and the kernel; `_boot_reconcile` calls the sweep. Everything is built under the test's own temp dir, never the real system temp dir.

Ran `python3 -m pytest tests/test_test_root_sweep.py tests/test_sdk_backend.py tests/test_cut_turn_tree_kill.py tests/test_tempdir_hygiene.py -q`: 274 passed, 37 skipped, 3 failed; the same 3 fail identically on untouched main on this macOS machine (BSD `mktemp` ignores `TMPDIR` without `-t`; a scope-count assertion), so they are pre-existing there and pass in CI's Ubuntu.

CUR 2.0 delivers resource tags as a JSON map whose keys carry `user_` and `aws_` prefixes. The CUR 2.0 path copied these keys verbatim, so user tags became labels like `user_owner`, while legacy CUR produces `owner`. 

## Related Issues
<!-- Link related issues using keywords: Fixes #123, Closes #456, Relates to #789 -->
N/A

## User Impact
<!-- Describe any user-facing changes. Is this a breaking change? Is there backwards compatibility? -->
- label-based Cloud Cost reports, filters, and aggregations keyed on tag names now work for CUR 2.0 users. 
- Label keys change from `user_<tag>` to `<tag>`. Previously ingested data keeps the old keys until re-queried. No impact to legacy CUR. 

## Testing
<!-- Describe how you tested your changes: unit tests, manual tests, integration tests, etc. -->
<!-- Integration tests: https://github.com/opencost/opencost-integration-tests -->
Unit tests fail on the previous code and passes with this fix. Verified against a live CUR 2.0 Athena table where `aggregate=label:name` was empty, but `label:user_name` was populated.

author: guilaile95
body:
# Factor Validation v0.1 — implementation evidence

任务：`PLANNING-PARITY-FACTOR-VALIDATION1`

本文件记录本轮 bounded implementation、source-to-sink contract 和本地验证证据。GitHub PR、exact-head CI、merge commit 与 post-merge CI 以 live GitHub 和 #203 最终 recovery coordinate 为准，不在此文件中预填未知坐标。

## Scope

- source 只使用现有 RDP Parquet / DuckDB 和 `query_full_market(as_of=T, latest=false)`。
- registry 只有现有透明 Full Market metrics：`return_5d`、`return_20d`、`return_60d`、`close_vs_ma20`、`close_vs_ma60`、`volume_ratio_20d`。
- 每次请求只运行一个 Factor；forward windows 固定为 5 / 20 条已存储观测。
- 结果是只读的 cross-sectional Spearman rank IC、average-rank tie 处理，以及 top 20% minus bottom 20% 的描述性 forward-return spread。
- `formal_state_write.performed = false`；没有新增 provider、数据依赖、账户/持仓/研究/交易写入或投资 authority。

明确不包含完整回测、成交/成本/滑点、PnL/NAV、grid calibration、Walk-Forward、factor weight、composite score、BUY/SELL、recommendation 或 Product Reality。

## Factor-value parity

Factor value 不在新模块中重新计算。对每个 factor date，代码通过现有 Full Market contract 取得同一 artifact、同一 security、同一 `source_metric`，并直接将该字段作为 factor value；response 的 parity mode 为 `DIRECT_SOURCE_METRIC_REUSE`。因此不会产生第二套 return / MA / volume-ratio 语义。

本地 parity test 对六个 registry factor 都用同一 fixture，将 Full Market 返回的 source metric 替换为有区别的 sentinel values，再检查 IC 输入收到的值逐项相同；这不是“两套算法碰巧算出同一个结果”的断言。

## Statistical and temporal contract

- IC 是日期 T 内不同证券之间的 Spearman rank correlation，不是单证券时间序列相关。
- Tie 使用 `AVERAGE_RANK`；pair 少于 2、factor 恒定、forward return 恒定或 rank variance 为零时 `rank_ic = null` 并给出 reason。
- 真实 `0.0` 保留为零；null 不转换为零。Bucket spread 同样区分真实 0 与 null。
- forward return 为 `future_close / current_close - 1`，窗口按 5 / 20 条已存储观测计，不称严格交易日历 T+5 / T+20。
- Factor value 使用 `query_full_market(as_of=T, latest=false)` 的 T 截止语义；未来行只用于 forward outcome。历史扫描最多读取 250 个 factor dates，并暴露 requested/effective range、artifact coverage、attempted/evaluated、immature、excluded 与 truncation。
- `RDP_OBSERVED_CROSS_SECTION` 是当前 artifact 在日期 T 的 observed cross-section，不是 point-in-time historical constituent 或 historical investable universe；`HISTORICAL_VALIDITY = NOT_PROVEN`。
- RDP `ADJUSTMENT = UNADJUSTED`，除权除息影响未被调整。High/Low 只代表描述性分桶统计，不代表交易策略或投资收益。

## Browser vertical

使用 61 个 security、90 个日期的 deterministic isolated RDP artifact（60 个完整序列，另有一个提前结束的序列），覆盖正 IC、负 IC、tie、factor null、immature forward window、正 spread、真实零 IC 和 null 展示。

路径为：`/signals` → `因子有效性` → 选择 factor / 日期范围 → `运行因子验证` → 5 / 20 observation → 展开历史横截面。验证链路是真实 FastAPI + production frontend build + fixture adapter，Factor 计算未 mock。Desktop 使用 1440×900，narrow 使用 390×844；检查了 parity、observed-universe / UNADJUSTED limitation、零与 null 展示、页面无 document-level overflow、无 pageerror / console error。浏览器专用插件当前不可用，使用仓库现有 Playwright regular fallback；截图保存在仓库外的临时 evidence 目录，不进入数据或 Git。

## Local validation

基线：`feature/research-system-v01@c7d306778e5e0417638ee1e5d77eec4b91959b11`。实现工作在 isolated worktree `luna/factor-validation-v01`；Owner checkout 未进入、未清理、未覆盖。

```text
backend factor tests: 6 passed
RDP / Historical Signal Validation / Pattern / Screener regressions: 60 passed
frontend focused + Signals / Pattern / Screener tests: 639 passed, 0 failed
production build: passed (tsc -b && vite build)
Factor browser E2E: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

主要命令：

```text
py -3 -m pytest tests/test_factor_validation.py -q                 # backend: 6 passed
py -3 -m pytest tests/test_research_data_plane_full_market.py tests/test_research_data_plane_patterns.py tests/test_historical_signal_validation.py tests/test_screener.py tests/test_screener_api.py -q  # 60 passed
npm test -- --test-name-pattern="factor validation|historical validation|Full Market|result grouping"  # 639 passed
npm run build
npm run test:e2e:factor-validation
git diff --check
```

## Independent Gate

```text
FACTOR_SOURCE = EXISTING_RDP_ONLY
FACTOR_REGISTRY = EXISTING_TRANSPARENT_METRICS_ONLY
FACTOR_VALUE_PARITY_WITH_FULL_MARKET = PROVEN
IC_METHOD = CROSS_SECTIONAL_SPEARMAN
TIE_RANKING = AVERAGE_RANK
FORWARD_WINDOWS = 5_AND_20_STORED_OBSERVATIONS
HIGH_LOW_BUCKET = TOP_20_PERCENT_MINUS_BOTTOM_20_PERCENT
HIGH_LOW_IS_TRADING_STRATEGY = NO
FUTURE_LEAKAGE = NO
HISTORICAL_UNIVERSE_AUTHORITY = NOT_AVAILABLE
RDP_ADJUSTMENT = UNADJUSTED
HISTORICAL_VALIDITY = NOT_PROVEN
PER_SECURITY_HTTP_N_PLUS_ONE = NO
NEW_PROVIDER = NO
NEW_DEPENDENCY = NO
FACTOR_WEIGHT_AUTO_UPDATE = NO
BLACK_BOX_SCORE = NO
BUY_SELL = NO
FORMAL_STATE_WRITES = ZERO
PRODUCT_REALITY_DAY_1 = NOT_STARTED
```

本地 evidence 支持 Gate = `ACCEPT`；Ready、ordinary merge 和 post-merge closure 仍以 exact-head / exact-stable live GitHub 证据为准。

body:
## De qué va

Dos cosas: el realm de Keycloak deja de llamarse `sgtm`, y **este repositorio se levanta en docker
compose por primera vez** — con las pruebas de extremo a extremo que faltaban para que el frontend y
los otros módulos puedan usar esta API.

Cierra la parte de este repositorio de [`infrastructure`#70](https://github.com/hneyra/infrastructure/issues/70).

### El realm

`despliegue/compose.yaml` apunta a `/realms/kamayuk` en `KAMAYUK_OIDC_EMISOR` y `KAMAYUK_OIDC_JWKS`;
las cinco pruebas que nombraban el realm o el cliente del backoffice pasan a `kamayuk-*`. El
descriptor **no cambia**: deriva de `e.plataforma.{emisor,jwks}` y no tiene ni un literal.

### Y este repositorio se levanta por primera vez

Las cinco filas del registro decían «el compose no se levantó ni la imagen se construyó: sin demonio
de Docker en esta máquina». Esa máquina existe, y de los cinco sistemas `identidad` era el único sin
una sola imagen. Medido:

- las dos imágenes se construyen (583 MB y 505 MB, exit 0);
- la cadena levanta con los dos `Job` en `Exited (0)` y el backend **healthy**;
- y **la predicción de la tabla se cumple exactamente**: 170 eventos —158 `PERMISO_FIJADO`, 2
  `GRUPO_DADO_DE_ALTA`, 5 `USUARIO_DADO_DE_ALTA`, 5 `MIEMBRO_AFILIADO`— y 5 cuentas, sin la de
  `identidad`, que no se consume a sí mismo.

### `despliegue/pruebas-e2e/`

Tres `.http` con las **23 operaciones** y sus cuerpos, y `ejercer.sh` con **55 casos que afirman** y
salen con código distinto de cero. **16 de los 55 son negativos**, porque un e2e de camino feliz no
distingue una API que valida de una que se traga cualquier cosa.

Se demostró que muerde: con la etiqueta de Traefik reclamando `/identidad-otro` y el contenedor
recreado, sale con **código 1 y 52 de 52 en rojo**. Y un caso estaba mal escrito:
`DELETE /seguridad/usuarios/{id}` da **404 y no 405**, y el backend tiene razón — esa ruta no tiene
manejador, así que no hay verbo admitido que anunciar.

Su README lleva los cuatro rodeos que hoy hacen falta para que un token sirva, **cada uno con su
issue** ([#72](https://github.com/hneyra/infrastructure/issues/72),
[#73](https://github.com/hneyra/infrastructure/issues/73),
[#74](https://github.com/hneyra/infrastructure/issues/74)), para que desaparezcan de ahí el día que
se cierren. Ninguno se arregla desde aquí.

### Dos afirmaciones corregidas

`infrastructure` **sí** compone este sistema desde `49ceb1a`, así que el «rojo ruidoso» que anuncia
la cabecera del compose está cerrado. `README.md` y `CLAUDE.md` decían lo contrario.

## Cómo se verificó

**582 pruebas, 0 fallos, 0 omitidas**, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3m 33s`; el descriptor **21 de 21**; la
autoprueba del registro en verde. Cinco roturas aplicadas **cada una sola** y restauradas por copia
comparada con `cmp`.

First PR of the Don Engine integration (Generation 14). The engine lands in later PRs, but its type surface, row shapes, and locked financial constants must exist first so subsequent work builds against them without churn. The shared server utilities (rate limit, HTTP errors) are merged additively so existing consumers — admin login, signup — keep their exact behavior.

## What
- **Copied verbatim** from the Gen 14 drops: `src/lib/don/types.ts`, `src/modules/don/records.ts`, `src/modules/don/constants.ts`, `src/modules/don/http.ts` (clientIdentity). No renaming, no reimplementation, no improvements.
- **Merged, never overwrote** `src/lib/server/rateLimit.ts`: added `DON_API_RATE_LIMIT` (30 req / 60s) + `donRateLimit(key)` helper; kept `checkRateLimit(key, config)`, `ADMIN_LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT`, and the repo's `REGISTER_RATE_LIMIT`.

Live consumers call the repo's per-key `checkRateLimit(key, config)`; adding a parallel rule registry would put two sources of truth for limits in one file. body:
## What

The first slice of the **D1b** tail (config-architecture C36): add **Gitea** as a third `Forge` impl, proving the C36 *"add a host = a new impl + a factory line, no core allow-list edit"* recipe end to end ([`04-forge-registry.md`](docs/design/config/04-forge-registry.md)).

## The impl

`GiteaForge` (`crates/agent-forge/src/gitea.rs`) speaks Gitea's GitHub-*shaped* `/api/v1`, and the divergences are exactly what the `Forge` seam absorbs:

| Aspect | GitHub | GitLab | **Gitea** |
|---|---|---|---|
| auth header | `Authorization: Bearer` | `PRIVATE-TOKEN` | **`Authorization: token`** |
| merged state | `merged_at` non-null | `state: merged` | **`merged: true` bool** |
| paging | `per_page`+`page` | `X-Next-Page` | **`limit`+`page`** (shared `Link`) |
| review event | `APPROVE` | (no object) | **`APPROVED`** |
| draft-on-create | `draft` flag | `Draft:` prefix | **`WIP:` prefix** |

## Wiring (one-card build path, unchanged)

- `kind.rs` — gitea in `known_kinds` / `default_base_url` (`https://gitea.com/api/v1`, the public instance) / `expected_encoding` (`OwnerName`) + build dispatch, so a `kind: "gitea"` card validates and builds with **no `agent-core` change**.
- `registry.rs` — the in-loop `[forge] backend = "gitea"` factory line.
- `fleet_review.rs` — gitea clone-URL + PR-ref arms so the fleet path clones + fetches PRs.

## Opt-in + gated

- `forge-gitea` is **NOT** in the default `forge` set → the standard github+gitlab build is byte-unchanged.
- New `nix/checks/forge-gitea.nix` runs the mapper matrix + card-build + a loopback e2e (token-auth + `merged`-bool) in the gate; clippy `--all-features` compiles the factory line.

## Gate

`nix flake check --max-jobs 8 --cores 4` green (the lone failure was the known `leak` memory-pressure flake on the untouched `agent-tools` crate — verified passing isolated via `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.leak`). Buf untouched (no proto change).

## Still open in D1b

The **bitbucket** host impl (next PR), then **card-by-id** (fleet/loop rows selecting a persisted forge card by id).

body:
## Purpose

Simplify the work-hour batch UI introduced in #26 so users can register one day or a recurring date range through the same form.

## Solution

Add 單日 / 多日 options inside 工作日期. Multi-day mode keeps the existing start-date controls and adds an end date in the same compact dropdown layout as 查詢工時, followed by weekdays labeled 僅登錄以下星期. Both modes use the existing work-time fields and 新增 button.

Remove the separate batch panel, extra-date input, time-slot editor, presets, and preview list. Users can submit another time period by changing the shared work-time fields. Keep native single-day submission, sequential Big5 batch transport, validation, stop handling, and the session duplicate guard. Wait for host initialization before copying date options, and fold the README batch section into Features.

## Verification

- `bun run check`: typecheck, lint, formatting, and 89 tests pass.

author: cremerfreddy
body:
Der Name erklärt sich auf der Seite selbst: Ein **Tukul** ist die runde Hütte Ostafrikas, in der sich Familie und Fremde ans selbe Feuer setzen. Daraus folgt das, was diese Küche unterscheidet — geteilt wird vom selben Teller. Im alten Entwurf war das eine Zeile in der Speisekarte.

## „Wie man von einer Injera isst"

Vier Sätze: Das Fladenbrot ist der Teller. Ein zweites, gerolltes Stück ist das Besteck. Gegessen wird mit der rechten Hand, von der eigenen Seite der Platte. Und *Gursha* heißt, jemandem einen Bissen zu reichen.

Wer zum ersten Mal vor einer Sharing-Platte sitzt, sucht nach der Gabel — und bestellt sie deshalb oft gar nicht erst. Das ist der Punkt, an dem eine Website tatsächlich etwas ausrichtet.

## Die Karte nach Herkunft geteilt

Statt einer vermischten Liste: **Ostafrika geschmort** (Doro Wat, Injera-Platte, Berbere) gegen **Westafrika gegrillt** (Suya, Jollof, Puff Puff). Zwei Küchen, die sich in Technik und Würzung deutlich unterscheiden.

Die **Bar** hat einen eigenen Abschnitt mit dem, was Hibiskus, Baobab und Tej überhaupt sind — drei Zutaten, die auf keiner anderen Karte in Freiburg stehen.

## Eine offene Frage, offen gestellt

Das Haus ist als „Bar & besondere Gastronomie" geführt, schließt aber um 19 Uhr — obwohl drei Cocktails auf der Karte stehen. Statt das zu kaschieren, benennt der Abschnitt „Bis 19 Uhr — noch" die naheliegende Entwicklung: Aus einer Küche mit Bar könnte abends eine Bar mit Küche werden. Die Getränke stehen schon da.

## Entfernt

Die Galerie mit sechs Kacheln ohne Bilder („Gewürze & Aromen", „Feuer & Grill", „Lounge-Klänge") und das Kontaktformular, das als „Entwurf, nicht aktiv" gekennzeichnet war.

## Gestaltung

Der Kreis als Leitmotiv: die Sharing-Platte von oben im Hero, Dachringe als Bandtrenner, runde Kanten durchgehend. Lehm, Ocker, Hibiskus und Indigo auf Sand. Gabarito und Lexend.

## Fakten

Sedanstraße 12, @tukulafrofood, alle Zeiten und die gesamte Beispielkarte samt Preisen sind übernommen, mit sämtlichen Vorbehalten.

author: balusc
body:
Both `required` declarations name a duty of the page author and say nothing about what happens when it is violated. That is why one is enforced only under `Development` and the other is not enforced at all, and neither behavior is documented anywhere. Each now states what the implementation must do.

| omitted where the tag is used | `Development` | `Production` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<required>true</required>` in a `*.taglib.xml` | renders, both implementations | renders, both implementations |
| `cc:attribute required="true"` | `TagException`, both implementations | renders, both implementations |
| a JSP tag file's `required="true"` | translation error | translation error |

For a tag declared in a tag library descriptor this is new behavior on both sides. JSP tag files, which Facelets tag files inherit the concept and much of this wording from, reject the same omission at translation time, so reading the element as being there for tooling alone is not the historical reading. It is also the only declaration available to a tag file: the documented workaround of a `<handler-class>` calling `getRequiredAttribute` cannot be applied there, `handler-class` and `source` being alternatives in the same `xsd:choice`.

For a composite component attribute the change is the project stage. Both implementations already throw, both only under `Development`, and nothing says they may stop in `Production` — the sentence they implement was never conditional.

Note for the TCK: a test written only against `Development` lets a stage guarding implementation pass whatever the text says, which is how the present situation survived unconditional wording for so long. This wants exercising in `Production` as well.

Measurements behind the table, across both implementations and against JSP, are in #1904. Implementation on the Mojarra side is in progress, under `Development` first.

Closes #1904

author: cmbant
body:
Formalizes the real Hermitian trace-pairing layer used immediately downstream of coherent-copy separation in QI-A.

Persistent changes:
- add `FormalResearch/QIA/HermitianInnerPairing.lean`;
- import it from `FormalResearch.lean`.

The module works directly on mathlib's real self-adjoint submodule `selfAdjoint.submodule ℝ (Matrix n n ℂ)` with bilinear form `(A,X) ↦ Re (Tr (A X))`. It proves nondegeneracy algebraically by testing a Hermitian direction against itself, using positivity of `Aᴴ A`, reality/nonnegativity of its trace, and `Matrix.trace_conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_zero_iff`. It then derives surjectivity to the algebraic dual and the concrete span theorem `hermitianMatrix_span_eq_top_of_trace_separation`.

Validation: GitHub Actions run `34518502750` at tested head `851d6de4acf2a2ed1a5295703d7ca479b315381d` passed placeholder rejection, `lake build FormalResearch.QIA.HermitianInnerPairing`, and full `lake build FormalResearch`. The temporary branch-only workflow was removed afterward; cleanup head is `282fee3bbc09b6230e0b7ed99046c2c0ce374fa5`.

Exact tested blobs: Hermitian module `5a2b21e469e174195a4bb7b1d68a8e52c00e8c6b`; aggregate `12c8a8262b11a4fe4daf25300863b16e4e1d7b08`.

Base pin before this PR: `formal-research-lean` at `4d4e7a81bbf0bf165047d41d92db02a61c764163`.

Scope boundary: this does **not** prove coherent-power polarization/separation, construct the concrete symmetry-reduction/CPTP channel, or prove the full pure-copy spanning theorem end-to-end. It removes the real-Hermitian finite-dimensional trace-pairing/duality premise, leaving coherent-power separation as the source-specific load-bearing hypothesis.

author: miikka-niemela
body:
## Linked issue
Closes #247

## Spec
`specs/027-team-search.md`

## Decision record
`decisions/027-team-search.md`

## Summary

A field in the site header, offered only to a signed-in reader, matching team names as a case-insensitive substring with Finnish `ä ö å` folded **in both directions** — `jarvenpaa` finds `Järvenpää`, `HÄRMÄ` finds `Härmä`.

## Two steps, deliberately

This module finds the ids whose **any** recorded name matches; `resolveTeamNames` says what each team is called **now**.

Collapsing them into one query would show a club's *old* name whenever an old name is what matched — the opposite of useful for someone searching a club they remember under a former name. There is an integration test for exactly that: a club stored under two names is found by the older one and rendered under the newer.

## Folding without an extension

```sql
translate(lower(name), 'äöåÄÖÅ', 'aoaAOA')
```

`unaccent` is available but **not installed**, so it would need a `CREATE EXTENSION` migration and the privilege to run it on Railway — and it is not `IMMUTABLE`, so it could not carry an index at all. `translate` is (`pg_proc.provolatile = 'i'`, checked), and migration `0014` adds four expression indexes over it.

## Two things the probes found that the spec did not anticipate

Both would have shipped looking entirely plausible, and neither would have failed a test I had written first.

**1. TASO's `competition_id` is a season bucket, not a competition.**

| column | holds |
|---|---|
| `competition_id` | `spljp19`, `maajp18` — a **season bucket** |
| `category_id` | `VL`, `WCQ`, `UNL` — the **competition** |

`resolveTeamNames` was reading the first. The very first probe rendered `FC Honka [spljp19 · 2019]`; it now reads `FC Honka [Veikkausliiga · 2019]`.

**2. A TASO national side has no team page at all.**

`/maajoukkueet/joukkue/[id]` is **football-data's** page — `CompetitionTeamPage` reading the `matches` table — and TASO ids are a separate id space. `/kotimaa/joukkue/[id]` is scoped to `{ kind: "taso", bucket: "domestic" }` and cannot find one either.

`regionFor` was returning `"kotimaa"` for every TASO team, so those results would have been links to a page that cannot find them — or, if a number collided, to a **different team**. They render unlinked now.

Searching for a national side still works where it should: `EC` and `WC` are in the `national-teams` region, so a football-data Spain resolves to `/maajoukkueet/joukkue/<id>` correctly. Finland is the one TASO case that deserves a link, and is filed as **#325**.

Both fixes are in `favourites.ts`, so `/suosikit` gets them too.

## Security

- The action **re-checks the session** — a server action is a public endpoint whether or not anything renders a control for it — and checks it *before* the term, so a short term cannot probe the endpoint's behaviour.
- The term is a bound parameter throughout; no `sql.raw` anywhere in the feature.
- `\`, `%` and `_` are escaped, backslash first. Unescaped, one `%` matches every team stored.

## How to verify

- [x] `npm run test:unit` — 2114 passing, 100% on all four metrics
- [x] `npm run test:integration` — 111 passing, 17 of them new and against real rows
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` — 215 passing, `--workers=1`
- [x] `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `/`, `/domestic`, `/foreign`, `/national-teams` still build as `○` static — the header is on every page, so this was the risk (#182)
- [x] The unit suite passes with `DATABASE_URL` and `REDIS_URL` pointed at a dead port, so nothing in it touches either
- [x] Thirteen mutations, all caught

## About those mutations

Eleven die in the unit suite. **Two survive it** — folding one side instead of both, and not escaping `%` — and die in the integration suite instead (3 and 1 failures).

That split is the point rather than a gap: both are SQL semantics, and the unit suite mocks the database. It deliberately does **not** assert on the `where` clause, because that is a drizzle SQL object whose internals would break on a version bump while proving less than running the query does. I removed a recorder that captured the clause and asserted nothing on it, since it implied coverage that was not there.

## What is deliberately unproven

**The substring query has not been measured at production scale, and the spec required it.** The local database holds 449 TASO rows and zero football-data rows, so any timing from here would describe nothing. A leading-wildcard `LIKE` cannot use the new B-trees either.

The decision record says this plainly rather than implying otherwise, and names the threshold (~200 ms) and the two candidates (`pg_trgm` with GIN, or a materialised team table). Worth watching once this is on staging with real data.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable signed-in readers to find teams by name from the site header while presenting accurate, current team information and safe navigation.

New Features:
- Add a signed-in header search for teams by case-insensitive Finnish-folded name substring across both data providers.
- Display matching teams with current names, competition and season context, linking only to valid team pages.

Bug Fixes:
- Correct TASO competition and season resolution and prevent national-team results from linking to invalid pages.
- Ensure renamed teams are shown under their latest recorded name while remaining searchable by former names.

Enhancements:
- Add server-side authorization, input validation, wildcard escaping, bounded recency-based result ordering, and protection against stale concurrent searches.
- Add folded-name database indexes and record performance and data-model decisions for the search.

Documentation:
- Document the team-search specification and implementation decisions, including matching behavior, performance constraints, and edge cases.

Tests:
- Add unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage for search matching, authorization, Finnish folding, provider separation, ranking, rendering states, and prerendering compatibility.

author: namedgraph
body:
## Problem

`http-tests/imports/import-internal-url-400.sh` has been failing since it was added in #377, printing only:

```
./imports/import-internal-url-400.sh   failed
```

Bare `grep -q` pipes gave no way to tell whether the harness broke, which assertion got a non-400, or what the server actually returned.

## Diagnosis

The first commit instruments the test — capturing `create-item.sh`'s stdout/stderr/exit status, and each import POST's status and body, with `Expected`/`Got` per assertion. CI then said it outright:

```
DEBUG: created import target item = [https://localhost:4443/67cb1c3b-.../]
curl: option --data-binary: error encountered when reading a file
DEBUG: [link-local ldh:file] file=http://169.254.1.1/data.ttl  Expected: 400  Got:
```

The harness was fine. The RDFImport body starts with `@prefix`, and **curl reads a leading `@` in `--data-binary "<arg>"` as a filename to slurp** — so curl aborted before sending anything, the status came back empty, and the request never reached the server.

This footgun was in the test as originally written, which means **the SSRF validation it guards has never actually been exercised**.

## Fix

Send the Turtle body via stdin instead:

```bash
printf '%s' "$body" | curl ... --data-binary @-
```

The server side was correct all along and needed no change: `ImportExecutor.start` runs `URLValidator.validate` on the request thread *before* the async `CompletableFuture`, and `InternalURLException` maps to 400 — so link-local/RFC-1918 `ldh:file` and an internal `spin:query` now get the expected `400`.

Sole instance of the pattern: every other `--data-binary "$var"` in `http-tests` is a SPARQL update/query (never a leading `@`).
