author: deblasis
body:
## What

- `WINTTY_TEST_CONFIG` arms an app-side guard: when set, Wintty refuses to run against any config root or resolved config path outside the temp directory. The refusal sits in `Program.MainImpl` ahead of the first `InitGhostty` (so before libghostty can read, create or template any config file), exits with code 4, and prints both paths to stderr. Belt checks also sit on `ConfigService`'s resolved path, on the `SeedConfigIfEmpty` write (outside its recovery `try`), and on `ConfigFileEditor.WriteAtomic`, the one choke point every Settings page, profile toggle, opacity drag and raw-editor save funnels through. `TestConfigGuardWiringTests` pins that wiring to the syntax tree.
- `--no-config` no longer constructs the real `ConfigFileEditor`: such a run gets `NoConfigFileEditor`, whose writes are refused loudly (and logged by the write scheduler and the startup migrator, which also skips its config appends under the flag). Previously every Settings-UI write on a `--no-config` run landed in the real config file.
- Every harness that launches the app now stages a per-run random temp `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and arms the guard. The previously unisolated launchers moved onto a shared helper, `windows/scripts/lib/test-config.ps1`: `search-fuzz.ps1` (isolation unconditional; the `-RealConfig` hatch was removed later in this PR, see item B), `mouse-fuzz-probe/remain/dialogs.ps1`, `release-smoke.ps1`. The already-isolated launchers (esctest, latency-probe, vttest, mouse-smoke, tab-colors, jumplist, shader-notice, splash-race, frame-style-fuzz, the seam probes) arm beside their existing XDG staging, and `seam-client.ps1` arms for every seam harness.
- A source-scan test, `HarnessConfigIsolationScanTests`, fails naming file and line for any app launch under `windows/scripts` or the justfile that neither arms `WINTTY_TEST_CONFIG` nor goes through the helper. The script allowlist is `crash-canary`/`crash-matrix` (`+crash` is intercepted before `InitGhostty` and never reaches config) plus the user launcher `run-win-launch.ps1` (founder rule, see below); the justfile pass has no allowlist since the run-win recipes route through that launcher.

## run-win amendment (founder direction)

`just run-win` / `just run-win-release` are the USER launcher, not a test, so they keep the user's real config by default, unchanged. Both recipes now route through `windows/scripts/run-win-launch.ps1`, which resolves the mode from the environment, in this precedence:

1. `REAL_CONFIG=1`: run against the real config, overriding everything, announced with a loud red banner (a decision that visible).
2. `ISOLATED_CONFIG=1`: explicit opt-in to a fresh random temp XDG root with `WINTTY_TEST_CONFIG=1` armed.
3. `CLAUDECODE=1` (set by Claude Code in every process it spawns; verified absent from the User and Machine environments, so a human terminal never carries it): isolated by default. The April taint was an agent manual test pass through a dev build, which is exactly the path this closes.
4. Otherwise (a human terminal): the real config, unchanged.

Pinned by tests: `Run_Win_Recipes_Route_Through_The_User_Launcher_Script` and `Run_Win_Launcher_Pins_The_Founder_Rule_For_The_User_Launcher` (markers, precedence order inside `Get-RunWinMode`, the loud announcement, and no `Exit-WinttyTestConfig` after launch, since the window outlives the recipe). The justfile source scan is now strict with no allowlist: any bare `Wintty.exe` exec line in a recipe fails it, because that would bypass the agent-session default. Red first (3 failures on the pre-change tree: bare exec lines, no launcher, no routing), green after (33/33).

Live verification: with only `CLAUDECODE=1` set, the launcher staged `wintty-testcfg-<128-bit-hex>`, armed the guard, launched the app, and the 495 files under `%APPDATA%\Ghostty` hash-identical before and after; the mode matrix (7 env permutations, including `REAL_CONFIG` beating `CLAUDECODE`) passes via the probe harness.

## Items A and B: random staging everywhere, no real-config escape

(A) The fixed-name and clock-keyed staging roots moved onto randomly named roots. frame-style-fuzz and shader-notice-fuzz stage through `Enter-WinttyTestConfig` (their HHmmss-keyed `%TEMP%` stage is gone; shader fixtures live beside the config inside the helper's root, invisible to config resolution); mouse-fuzz-jumplist's `New-IsolatedConfig` uses the helper; the vttest pair (fixed `vttest-run` / `vttest-section`) and the esctest pair (fixed `esctest-run` / `latency-probe-run`) use the helper for the config root (the esctest results dir keeps its own random guid name so the report outlives the app); splash-single-instance-race's `$PID`-keyed scratch became a guid. The source scan grew `Every_Staged_Config_Root_Is_Randomly_Named`: every `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` assignment is followed through its definition chain (variables, parameter defaults, in-file functions) and fails naming file, line, and the offending definition unless the chain reaches `[guid]::NewGuid` / `New-Guid` / `GetRandomFileName` / `RandomNumberGenerator` / one of the helpers, or is a save/restore. Red first: 10 violations across 8 scripts (all of the above, pre-migration). Green after: 0.

(B) `search-fuzz.ps1` lost `-RealConfig` entirely: isolation is unconditional, staged through the helper. A test harness must not be able to point the app at the real config. If the historical 0xc000027b under an isolated root returns, that is a product bug (possibly the x:Load-overlay family, wintty-release #806), to be captured with cdb on the window-owner PID (break on `av` and `40080201` first chance) and fixed, never routed around; the param comment says exactly this. Pinned by `Search_Fuzz_Has_No_Real_Config_Escape` (no `RealConfig` code line; `Enter-WinttyTestConfig` present). Verified live: `just search-fuzz '-Seed 7 -Iterations 8'` ran the isolated default clean (22 checks, 0 findings, no startup failure), with all 495 files under `%APPDATA%\Ghostty` hash-identical before and after.

## Fix round 1 (adversarial review: 4 Mediums + Lows)

- M1: the guard's temp anchor is now the known-folder temp (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp` via the known-folder API, which the process environment cannot move), never `Path.GetTempPath()`; and an armed run refuses outright when TEMP or TMP points outside that anchor. Unit tests cover the redirect-to-APPDATA and drive-root shapes; the app-level probe reran the review's exact case (exit 4 now, where the pre-fix build ran).
- M2: reads are enforced. A managed pre-pass before the CLI branch (so `+show-config` is covered too) refuses exit 4 for any `--config-file` value and any `config-file =` include chain reachable from the root's default files that resolves outside temp, expanding relative includes against the including file's directory exactly as Config.zig does. Include, flag, and chained include all refuse at app level.
- M3: the scan now judges each LAUNCH SITE (an arming line inside an if/else/switch blesses nothing, and only arms before the launch count), sees every launch form the review proved invisible (`[Process]::Start($psi)` with the target set by property, call operator, Invoke-Item, literal-path Start-Process, `cmd /c start`, explorer.exe, `dotnet run`, unresolved variables fail closed), and excludes resolved tooling targets (pwsh, cdb, the repo's BackdropStage/WindowCapture helpers), fixing the `$cdbExe` false-positive class. A synthetic fixture corpus (`ScanFixtures/`, 11 violations + 3 cleans) bakes the per-form RED into the suite. `fuzz-suite.ps1` arms every leg it launches. `run-win-launch.ps1` is allowlisted with the founder-rule reason.
- M4: the boundary compare runs on final paths: the longest existing ancestor is resolved through GetFinalPathNameByHandle (junctions and symlinks included), the anchor too, and an unresolvable existing path refuses. Real junction test refuses; symlink test skips with a reason where the host lacks the privilege. The review's write-through-the-junction case now ex

body:
Follow-on from card 263 (#88), which deleted the `generate-insight` function
that was this table's only reader and writer. With that gone,
`public.insight_cache` was referenced by nothing at all.

**Already applied to production** on 2026-09-10. This PR records it in the
migration history.

## Checked before writing, not after

| | |
|---|---|
| rows | **0** |
| distinct users | 0 |
| newest row | none |
| constraints POINTING at it | none |
| views / rules depending on it | none |
| triggers | none |

So there was no data to lose and nothing to break.

## The caution was misplaced, and that is worth recording

This was flagged as the riskier half of card 263 because migration
`20260810000000` exists precisely to stop its foreign key blocking account
deletion — which broke Delete Account in build 7 and made the table look
load-bearing.

It was not. It was an **empty table wearing a cascade rule to protect an
operation against rows that never existed**. Dropping it removes that failure
mode permanently instead of maintaining a guard around nothing.

## Safety

`restrict` rather than `cascade`, so that if the dependency check had been wrong
the migration would have failed loudly instead of quietly taking a dependant
with it.

Verified afterwards with a separate `select` rather than the results pane:
`to_regclass('public.insight_cache')` is null, and the **plural**
`public.insights_cache` is untouched and still holding its row.

That distinction is the whole hazard here, and it is one character. The plural
table is what `generate-insights` reads and writes, and it stays.

body:
## Intent

URGENT hotfix (second one on staging today): LargeIngestionGate failed AGAIN right after merging #374 (which fixed the plain-hypertable version of this exact class of bug), now on a different assertion: logs_severity_rollup_present == false. Root cause is the SAME architectural gap #374 already fixed, just for continuous aggregates instead of plain hypertables -- pg_dump --schema-only does not capture TimescaleDB's continuous-aggregate catalog registration either. #374's baseline regeneration moved included_through past 20260812140000_ensure_logs_severity_stats_5m_cagg.exs (and, unnoticed until now, past every other ensure/repair migration for all 21 continuous aggregates that exist today), so none of them re-run on a fresh bootstrap and their effect was never captured by the schema-only dump. Extended scripts/db/generate-platform-baseline.sh the same way #374 fixed hypertables: recreate every current cagg from its own view_definition in dependency order (discovered flow_traffic_1d is built on flow_traffic_1h's own materialization hypertable, so a naive single pass breaks -- used a recursive CTE ordered by dependency depth); drop the orphaned artifacts pg_dump already captured for each cagg first (its outer view, _direct_view_NN, _partial_view_NN, and the materialization table -- all pg_dump captures as plain schema, just without the special registration) -- discovered empirically that skipping this, or interleaving drop+create per cagg instead of all-drops-then-all-creates, both fail, because TimescaleDB assigns each new materialization table's internal id fresh in creation order (not matching the source database's numbering), so a not-yet-dropped later-cagg orphan can collide with an earlier cagg's freshly assigned id; omit IF NOT EXISTS on the recreated CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW (confirmed empirically TimescaleDB's cagg DDL hook doesn't handle it and silently creates a plain unregistered view instead -- not needed anyway since this only runs once into a fresh empty database); restore each cagg's refresh policy from timescaledb_information.jobs; run this whole block under an explicit SET search_path since view_definition's table references come back unqualified. Retention/compression policies have the same gap but are explicitly out of scope for this fix -- nothing in the currently-gating test suite depends on them, and closing that needs its own verification pass, not folding into an already-large urgent fix. Regenerated the baseline with the fixed script (included_through unchanged). Verified against a real srql-fixtures scratch database: loading the new baseline directly registers all 30 hypertables and all 21 continuous aggregates with no errors; a full StartupMigrations bootstrap from empty now reports logs_severity_rollup_present=true with the exact expected column list, logs_hypertable_present=true, 30 hypertables, 21 continuous aggregates, no errors/warnings in the bootstrap log; confirmed idempotent on a second bootstrap run; schema_baseline_freshness_test.py's 4 assertions still pass. This must land on staging as fast as safely possible -- staging is currently broken for anyone bootstrapping fresh, for the second time today.

## What Changed

- Extended `scripts/db/generate-platform-baseline.sh` to recreate every continuous aggregate from its `view_definition` in dependency order (via a recursive CTE, since some caggs are built on other caggs' materialization hypertables), so TimescaleDB's cagg catalog registration is captured — `pg_dump --schema-only` alone omits it.
- Before recreating each cagg, the script drops the orphaned plain-schema artifacts `pg_dump` already captured (outer view, `_direct_view_NN`, `_partial_view_NN`, materialization table) for all caggs first, then creates all caggs — interleaving drop+create breaks because TimescaleDB assigns materialization table ids in creation order.
- Recreated `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` statements omit `IF NOT EXISTS` (TimescaleDB's cagg DDL hook doesn't handle it correctly) and each cagg's refresh policy is restored from `timescaledb_information.jobs`, with the block run under an explicit `search_path` since `view_definition` table references come back unqualified.
- Regenerated `elixir/serviceradar_core/priv/repo/baseline/platform_schema.sql` and `metadata.json` with the fixed script so a fresh bootstrap registers all 21 continuous aggregates (in addition to the 30 hypertables already fixed).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change modifies the shared platform_schema.sql baseline that every fresh bootstrap depends on, using a non-trivial recursive dependency-ordered DROP/CREATE sequence for continuous aggregates; the logic (drop-orphans-before-any-create, dependency-depth CTE, search_path handling, refresh-policy restoration) is correct on inspection and matches the described empirical verification against a real scratch database (30 hypertables, 21 caggs, idempotent second bootstrap), with retention/compression explicitly and reasonably scoped out, so residual risk is limited to conditions not exercised by that verification (e.g. a future cagg with different registration edge cases) rather than a defect visible in this diff.

## Testing

Live-loaded the regenerated baseline schema into a real TimescaleDB+AGE Postgres instance twice from empty; both runs completed with zero SQL errors, registered exactly 30 hypertables and 21 continuous aggregates (including logs_severity_stats_5m and the dependency-ordered flow_traffic_1h/1d pair), and schema_baseline_freshness_test.py's 4 assertions pass. author: jaetill
body:
## What

Guests can pick games (and claim a side dish) straight from the invite email, with no sign-in. The public `GET /rsvp` route grows from three one-click RSVP buttons into a small picker page, authenticated only by the same HMAC token the email already carries.

## Why

The one-click RSVP landed a guest on a page that said "pick a game in the app" — and the app needs a Cognito login most guests never complete. Separately, the invite email rendered `description` but silently dropped `food` (the "Food plan" field), so dinner notes only reached people who signed in.

## How

**`lambda/rsvpLink.js`**

- `choice=games` → picker page, no write. Games with Join / Leave / Interested, who's playing, food plan, side form (when `allowSides`).
- `choice=join|leave|interested|uninterested&game=<id>` → one game. Join enforces `maxPlayers` and upgrades the RSVP to `playing` (the app's join rule). Idempotent. Stale links (game removed, seat filled) render a warning and **do not write** — no `lastModified` bump, no host push.
- `choice=side&desc=…` / `unside` → side dish claim (trimmed, capped at 120 chars, one per guest).
- `playing` / `if_needed` now land on the picker. `declined` still gets the static page and additionally withdraws the guest from games / interest / side, matching the app's cancel path.
- Token still pins `{nightId, invitee, exp}`; a token for night A can't touch night B (tested). `gameId` is looked up with `hasOwnProperty` so prototype keys can't resolve.
- Every host/guest string on the page is escaped (public route → stored-XSS surface). Tested with a payload in every field.
- Caller-attribution logging from #346 preserved; `game_id` added to the fields.

**`lambda/nudge.js`**

- `night.food` in all four builders (invite/nudge × text/HTML) plus the "bring your own meal" note; side sign-up line when `allowSides`, pointing at the picker link.
- `rsvpLinks.games` minted alongside yes / ifNeeded / no.

## Tests

- `tests/rsvpLink.test.js` (32): pure mutations (capacity, idempotency, RSVP upgrade, decline cascade, sides), render escaping + link encoding, and handler end-to-end via `_setForTest` (If-Match write, no-op → no write, wrong-night token → 404).
- `tests/nudgeFood.test.js` (25): food block in all four builders, sidesOpen gating, null-links fallback, escaping.
- Full suite: 27 files / 336 tests green.

## Deploy

Not in the GitHub workflow — `rsvpLink` and `nudgeNonResponders` get redeployed with the `build/zip.py` flow after merge. No IAM, env, or API Gateway changes needed (same route, same S3 keys, same secrets).

body:
Version bump and the release entry for 0.6.55. No code changes.

The SQL side of this release closes S2 of #304, which is the stage that turns a parse tree into something with SQL meaning. Every box on #307 is ticked. Window specifications read, `PIVOT` and `UNPIVOT` read in both of the spellings DuckDB takes for each, the jump table the transformer dispatches through can no longer be built with a hole in it, the corpus differential can say which refusal each of the 39,028 refused statements landed on, and the parse budget in the specification has a number in it that anybody can reproduce with a command.

Alongside it, the categorical work that came in from the other direction. A category column survives being filtered, taken, stacked and filled, which it did not before: eight kernels were producing a column whose type said category and whose category list was empty, and had been since dictionary columns were added. Comparison works. The Mojo `Series` can reach the same surface the Python `cat` namespace could. An imported dictionary column can be read at all.

There is also a join that builds on the shorter side rather than the one the caller named second, and four error messages that described our internals instead of the user's mistake.

Patch rather than minor, since the milestone the SQL work belongs to is not finished. S2 is.

Four files, the three version copies and the changelog.

author: freepeace13
body:
## What does this change

`plugins/doc-to-markdown` now owns its JavaScript instead of relying on a hand-downloaded `markdown-it.min.js` committed to `resources/dist/vendor/`. Nothing recorded which version that file was, where it came from, or how to reproduce it.

**The build**
- The plugin gains its own `package.json` (`markdown-it` as a real dependency, pinned by a committed `package-lock.json`) and a Vite library-mode config that bundles it into one browser-ready IIFE.
- Authored JS moves to `resources/js/doc-to-markdown.js`; `resources/dist/` becomes generated output and is gitignored.
- `host/`'s Vite build is untouched and still knows nothing about this tool.

**The delivery**
- `DocToMarkdownServiceProvider` publishes the bundle to `public/vendor/doc-to-markdown` under the `doc-to-markdown-assets` tag; the view loads it with `asset()`.
- The two routes that streamed assets off disk through PHP are gone.
- The script URL is fingerprinted with a hash of the published file's contents. The published path is stable and unhashed, unlike `host/`'s Vite output, so without this a browser would keep serving the previous bundle after every rebuild.

**Two fixes found while verifying**
- **CI built only `host/`'s frontend**, so it never built or published this plugin's bundle. The suite stayed green while `/doc-to-markdown` served a `<script>` pointing at a 404 — `asset()` only builds a URL, and no host test fetches it. CI now mirrors `make install`.
- **The rendered Markdown had no styling for headings or links.** Tailwind's preflight resets headings to `font-size: inherit` and links to `color: inherit`; the preview's stylesheet restored weight and margins but never declared a `font-size` and had no `a` rule, so converted documents rendered as undifferentiated plain text. markdown-it ships no CSS of its own, so that block is the whole stylesheet for a rendered document. The preview also no longer sits in a fixed 16rem box with its own scrollbar.

**Backward compatibility:** the `doc-to-markdown.assets.markdown-it` and `doc-to-markdown.assets.script` routes are removed. Nothing outside the plugin's own view referenced them (verified by grep across `plugins/` and `host/`).

**Note for reviewers:** this trades away the old "works right after `composer install` with no npm step". `make install` and CI now run the plugin's npm install, build, and `vendor:publish --tag=doc-to-markdown-assets --force` — `--force` matters, since `vendor:publish` silently skips existing files. The new `plugins/doc-to-markdown/README.md` documents the sequence.

## Checklist

- [x] Tool-specific logic stays inside `plugins/<name>/` — nothing tool-specific was added to `host/`.
- [x] No plugin reaches into another plugin's `src/` directly (only `ServiceProvider` and `ToolContract` are used as public surface).
- [x] New tools register via `ToolRegistry::register()` inside their own `ServiceProvider::boot()`. *(No new tool; existing registration untouched.)*
- [x] Branding/UI uses `plugins/ui`'s `<x-brand::...>` components rather than duplicated markup/styles. *(The preview stylesheet is scoped to `.markdown-render` and consumes theme tokens rather than hardcoding brand values.)*
- [x] Tests were added/updated in the correct location (`plugins/<name>/tests` for plugin behavior, `host/tests` for host-level seams).
- [x] `make test` passes locally.
- [x] `cd host && ./vendor/bin/pint` passes locally (or was run with no changes needed).

Verified from a wiped state (`rm -rf` the plugin's `node_modules`/`resources/dist` and `host/public/vendor`, then `make install`): Pint clean, host 4/4, plugin PHP 18/18, plugin JS 4/4.

author: pierrecabriere
body:
Closes #1347

## Root cause

`@better-auth/core` carries `jose` as a **real peer**, so the version skew between `apps/api` (`jose: ^6.2.12`, `apps/api/package.json:47`, set by #1289) and better-auth's own transitive pin (6.2.7, `bun.lock`) made bun materialise two peer instances of `@better-auth/core@1.7.3`. Which copy a consumer links is decided by the peer graph, not by any line of our code — and `oauth2/verify.mjs` marks insufficient-scope errors in a **module-level WeakSet**, private to a copy. That is the bug #1295 fixed, one import site at a time (`apps/api/src/modules/mcp/router.ts:39-54`), leaving the invariant itself unguarded and one direct import still live at `apps/api/src/modules/oidc/services/enduser-token.ts:21`.

Reproduced in a clean worktree off `main`: `node_modules/.bun/` held `@better-auth+core@1.7.3+0ac89928…` (jose 6.2.12, linked by `apps/api`) and `+53b163a2…` (jose 6.2.7, linked by `better-auth` and `@better-auth/oauth-provider`).

## Fix

Three layers, smallest first:

1. **Collapse the duplicate** — pin `jose` in the root `overrides`, next to `zod`. zod is pinned there already, which is precisely why both core copies linked an identical zod and `instanceof APIError` kept working. After the change: exactly one `@better-auth/core` and one `jose`, with `apps/api`, `better-auth` and `@better-auth/oauth-provider` on the same copy. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` is green on the committed lock.
2. **Route the live imports through the façade** — `verifyJwsAccessToken` (`enduser-token.ts`) and `encodeBasicCredentials` (two oidc integration tests) now come from `better-auth/oauth2`, which re-exports `@better-auth/core/oauth2` from the copy better-auth itself links.
3. **Guard it** — an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` ban on `@better-auth/core/*` across `apps/api/**`, plus a unit test asserting the resolution is single.

Two judgement calls worth flagging:

- **`@better-auth/core/utils/host` is carved out of the ban**, in the rule rather than with a disable at the import site. better-auth re-exports no host classifier (its own `utils/url.mjs` deliberately keeps the zod-carrying one out of the client bundle — verified against the installed dist), and `isLoopbackHost` is a pure predicate with no module state to get wrong. `oidc/services/redirect-uri.ts` needs the very predicate DCR applies; re-implementing it is the drift #1012 is about. Deep subpaths under `utils/host` stay banned. This also means `@better-auth/core` must remain a direct dependency of `apps/api` — the issue's "drop the direct dependency" option is not available.
- **The Pi SDK ban is restated, not duplicated by accident.** ESLint flat config *replaces* a rule across blocks rather than merging it (the config file says so itself, at the web seam exemption), so a new block covering `apps/api/**` would have silently dropped the Pi guard for `apps/api/src/**`. `PI_SDK_BAN` is now a shared constant carried by both blocks. Verified by positive control.

## Tests

New: `apps/api/test/unit/better-auth-single-instance.test.ts` (2 tests) — asserts `@better-auth/core/oauth2` resolves to one path from `apps/api`, from `better-auth` and from `@better-auth/oauth-provider`, and that one `jose` sits under it. The behavioural half was already covered by `apps/api/src/modules/mcp/test/integration/mcp.test.ts` (the `insufficient_scope` step-up challenge); what was unguarded is the resolution, which can split again on the next bump with our code unchanged.

**Negative control**: restored the pre-fix `package.json` + `bun.lock`, wiped `node_modules`, reinstalled → 2 core copies, and the new test fails on the exact split (`+0ac89928…` vs `+53b163a2…`). Restored, reinstalled → 2 pass.

```
TEST_TIER=0 bun test apps/api/test/unit/better-auth-single-instance.test.ts        → 2 pass 0 fail
TEST_TIER=0 bun test .../oidc/test/integration/{routes/realm-isolation,services/oauth-flows}.test.ts → 20 pass 0 fail
TEST_TIER=0 bun test .../mcp/test/integration/mcp.test.ts                          → 20 pass 0 fail
TEST_TIER=0 bun test .../oidc/test/{unit/enduser-token-verify,integration/middleware/enduser-token-auth}.test.ts → 34 pass 0 fail
TEST_TIER=0 bun test apps/api/test/unit/redirect-uri.test.ts                       → 14 pass 0 fail (with realm-isolation)
bunx tsc --noEmit -p apps/api | -p packages/db | -p packages/core                   → clean
bunx eslint <touched files>                                                        → clean
```

ESLint positive controls (probe files, deleted after): `@better-auth/core/oauth2` in `src/` → error; the same in `test/` → error; `@better-auth/core/utils/host/deep` → error; `@better-auth/core/utils/host` → allowed. Pi SDK ban still fires in both `apps/api/src/` and `packages/runner-pi/src/`.

## Notes for the orchestrator

- **`bun.lock` changed** and must ride with `package.json`. The override also lifts `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`'s `jose` from 6.2.4 to 6.2.12 (its range `^6.1.3` is satisfied); the MCP integration suite is green. Expect a lockfile conflict with any sibling that also touches deps — re-resolve by re-running `bun install`, not by hand-merging the lock.
- No migration, no env var, no OpenAPI change. Nothing to sequence at deploy.
- **Overlap with siblings**: none. #1348 (better-auth FK indexes) and #1349 (schema check reads the Drizzle object) touch `packages/db`; this PR touches `apps/api`, the root `package.json`/lock and `eslint.config.mjs`. If a sibling adds a `no-restricted-imports` block for `apps/api/**`, it must carry `PI_SDK_BAN` and `BETTER_AUTH_CORE_BAN` — the replace-not-merge trap is documented at both blocks.

author: kirillzyusko
body: ## 📜 Description Added support for `NestedScrollView` for `KeyboardAwareScrollView`. ## 💡 Motivation and Context When users enable `useNestedScrollViewAndroid` feature flag, then `ReactNestedScrollView` is used: ```kt if (ReactNativeFeatureFlags.useNestedScrollViewAndroid()) ReactNestedScrollViewManager() else ReactScrollViewManager(), ``` As a result our condition returns `false` (casting of `parentView` to `ReactScrollView` is failing): ```kt if (parentView is ReactScrollView && parentView.scrollEnabled) { ``` So we never recognize the `ReactNestedScrollView` as a `ScrollView` and because of that condition is evaluated as `true`: ```ts // input belongs to ScrollView if (layout.value?.parentScrollViewTarget !== scrollViewTarget.value) { return 0; } ``` So scrolling never works. In this PR I created small extension called `View.isEnabledReactScrollView()` that checks both cases: `ReactScrollView` and `ReactNestedScrollView`. This implementation had technical difficulties, because `ReactNestedScrollView` is not available in earlier RN versions (was introduced only in RN 0.85+) so I had to use reflection, because we can not use direct class references as it may be not available in all framework versions. Closes https://github.com/kirillzyusko/react-native-keyboard-controller/pull/1537 ## 📢 Changelog ### Android - added `View.isEnabledReactScrollView()` extension that checks both `ReactScrollView`/`ReactNestedScrollView` cases; - use `isEnabledReactScrollView()` condition instead of previous check; ## 🤔 How Has This Been Tested? Tested via CI (e2e tests). ## 📸 Screenshots (if appropriate): ## 📝 Checklist - [x] CI successfully passed - [x] I added new mocks and corresponding unit-tests if library API was changed

author: pcbz
body:
## What

Add a `workflow_dispatch` **`mcp_endpoint` input** to the MCP Registry publish workflow, so "Run workflow" shows a box to type the endpoint. Falls back to the `MCP_ENDPOINT` repo variable when the input is blank.

## Why

The publish workflow only read `vars.MCP_ENDPOINT`, which is set automatically **only on the GCP terraform path**. We deploy via **Azure**, which never sets it — so every `v1.0.0` tag run hit the guard (`MCP_ENDPOINT is empty … Skipping`) and no-op'd (green, but nothing published; `server.json` still has the placeholder URL). There was no way to publish without that variable.

## Change

- `on.workflow_dispatch.inputs.mcp_endpoint` — optional string, described for the UI.
- "Resolve endpoint" step: `endpoint = inputs.mcp_endpoint || vars.MCP_ENDPOINT`; skips only if both are empty; exposes the resolved value as a step output.
- Sync step reads that resolved endpoint (via `env:`, not inline, so no shell-injection from the input).
- Header comment updated to describe both sources.

## How to use (after merge)

Actions → **Publish to MCP Registry** → **Run workflow** → paste `https://<app>.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp` → Run. It syncs `server.json` (url [+ version on a tag]), commits to `main`, authenticates via GitHub OIDC, and publishes.

## Reviewer notes

- Tag-triggered runs still work if `MCP_ENDPOINT` is set; the input just overrides/enables manual publishing.
- The dispatch button + input box only appear once this is on `main` (GitHub reads dispatch inputs from the default branch).
- `registry-publish.yml` YAML parses.

author: robertschneiderdevoba
body:
Closes #141

## Readability

`render-markdown.nvim` was already installed but ran with `opts = {}`, which means `file_types = { 'markdown' }`. The chat buffer has the filetype `codecompanion`, so it never got rendered — that is why prompts and answers ran together as raw `##` headers and backticks. Adding the filetype is the whole fix; markdown files are untouched, and the plugin's load behaviour stays as it was.

## Context usage

`display.chat.token_count` now reports the share of the context window instead of a bare number:

```
 (1.2k/8k · 15%)      →  Ollama, window known
 (1234 tokens)        →  no window available, falls back
```

For that to mean anything the window has to be known, and Ollama's `num_ctx` defaults to `nil`. It is now pinned to 8192, which serves two purposes: the percentage has a denominator, and the window stays small enough that CPU inference does not suffer — a large context is expensive to process there.

**Where this will be empty:** the `claude_code` ACP adapter carries no token or usage handling at all (nothing in its source references either), so on the Mac the counter has nothing to show. Over ACP the agent reports no usage back to CodeCompanion. The fallback keeps that case from breaking, but it will not produce Claude-CLI-style numbers there.

## Verification

- The counter is a plain function, so it is tested directly: 1234/8192 → `(1.2k/8k · 15%)`, 7900 → `96%`, 0 → `0%`, and both an adapter without a schema and a `nil` adapter fall back instead of erroring
- `stylua --check` clean on both files
- **Not verified visually:** whether the rendered chat actually looks the way you want. That needs a real UI, and it is a matter of taste anyway — if the concealed markdown bothers you while editing, the alternative is CodeCompanion's own `show_header_separator = true` instead of the renderer.

body:
## Summary

Addresses #510 (unit 510-A, planned in #510's Execution Plan Index). Adds deterministic pre-persistence pointer-cardinality/kind validation for thin-control-state parser-sensitive fields, so the live #499 corruption shape — a canonical `Stage 2` field whose own value embeds a second parseable pointer as parenthetical prose (`Stage 2: #508 ... correction dispatched as PR #509`) — is refused before it can become durable state.

## Changes

- **`tools/orchestration/control-field-validator.mjs`** (new, additive — not an extraction): field-local pointer cardinality/kind validator. Reuses `ready-dispatch-gate.mjs`'s existing `parseControlBullet`/`parseExecutionPointer`/`findNearDuplicateBulletLabels`/`isNoneSentinel`/`readExecutionBulletField`/`describeExecutionConflict` verbatim. Default field specs: `Execution`/`Execution issue` (issue-kind), `PR` (pull-kind), `Stage 2` (issue-kind).
- **`tools/orchestration/write-control-snapshot.mjs`** (new): write-before-validate helper (`node tools/orchestration/write-control-snapshot.mjs --control-issue <N> --body-file <path|->`) for the manual thin-control-body edit path identified in #510's Shared Contract as previously unmediated by any script. Refuses an invalid proposed body before ever calling `gh issue edit`.
- **`tools/review-watch/lifecycle-gate.mjs`**: adds `validateAuditVerdictRewrite`, a defense-in-depth guard wired into `checkRecordVerdict` immediately before the `gh issue edit` write, proving a Verdict-only rewrite leaves the adjacent `Work issue`/`Merged PR` pointer fields byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: one paragraph under § Parent snapshots directing sessions to persist thin-control bold-bullet field edits through `write-control-snapshot.mjs` instead of a direct `gh issue edit`.
- **`ready-dispatch-gate.mjs` / `next-review-transition-gate.mjs`**: unmodified. Existing fail-closed read-time behavior (near-duplicate labels, `AMBIGUOUS`/`NOT_READY`) is preserved unchanged.

## Verification

All 8 of #510's `## Verification` cases are exercised as automated regression tests:

1. #499 regression (exact corrupted `Stage 2` shape rejected) — `control-field-validator.test.mjs`, `write-control-snapshot.test.mjs`
2. Corrected #499 shape accepted — `control-field-validator.test.mjs`
3. Cross-field control (`PR` + `Stage 2` both valid together) — `control-field-validator.test.mjs`, `write-control-snapshot.test.mjs`
4. Historical prose elsewhere in the body does not contaminate canonical fields — `control-field-validator.test.mjs`
5. Missing/multiple/wrong-kind pointer negatives — `control-field-validator.test.mjs`
6. Near-duplicate regression (#493/#495 protections intact) — `control-field-validator.test.mjs`
7. Write-before-validate ordering (invalid proposal never reaches `gh issue edit`) — `write-control-snapshot.test.mjs`
8. Full test suite + control-plane checks run below; Stage 1 requested on this PR, fresh Stage 2 to follow post-merge

Local verification performed on this PR's frozen head (`48b99aa`, rebased onto `origin/main`):

- `node --test tools/review-watch/*.test.mjs tools/orchestration/*.test.mjs` → **1007/1007 pass, 0 failures** (includes 28 new tests in `control-field-validator.test.mjs`/`write-control-snapshot.test.mjs`, 3 new tests in `lifecycle-gate.test.mjs`, and every pre-existing `ready-dispatch-gate.test.mjs`/`next-review-transition-gate.test.mjs`/`lifecycle-gate.test.mjs` case — including #493/#495 near-duplicate coverage — unmodified and still passing)
- `node tools/check-control-plane-paths.mjs` → OK
- `node tools/check-startup-budget.mjs` → OK (AGENTS.md addition stays within budget)

## Scope note

This PR touches control-plane paths (`AGENTS.md`, `tools/orchestration/**`, `tools/review-watch/**`) per `docs/bounded-review-cycle.md`'s Entry check — full Stage 1 + fresh Stage 2 audit required, no exemption.

## Non-goals preserved

No change to Stage 1/Stage 2 lifecycle policy, no redesign of the thin-control schema, no generalized Issue-editing framework, no reopening of #493/#495's near-duplicate-label work, no semantic/LLM classification — deterministic structural validation only, reusing existing parser authority.

Closes #107. Closes #113.

## Why

`docs/contract-watch.md` item 4 has been OPEN since 2026-09-07, asking of each of this repo's checks not *"does it pass"* but **"has each one ever been observed to fail?"** Five of the eight gates had never been. Two of them were also carrying a known evasion, deferred at the time under a stated decision rule rather than rushed onto a release branch.

The shape this addresses: a gate that scans, greps or compares a generated artifact **can pass while looking at nothing**, and no mutation of the code under test reveals it — because the code under test is a regex or a string comparison. A dead matcher and a clean tree produce identical output.

## Red first

Both `#113` holes reproduced against the unfixed tree before anything changed, by driving the module's own matcher:

```
HOLE 1  write nested in $( ) inside echo:
   flagged=False  echo "$(cp "$STAMPED" "$NOTES_REL")"
   flagged=False  printf %s "$(tee "$NOTES_REL" < "$STAMPED")"
HOLE 2  quoted mention counts as a publish rename:
   findall count on decoy = 1
```

## What changed, per gate

| Gate | Vacuity | Control |
|---|---|---|
| `check_publish_atomic.py` | **added** — empty script, or zero segments examined, now dies | 14: every evasion rounds 3/5/6 walked past, plus both #113 holes, plus 4 MUST_PASS shapes |
| `check_scratch_prefix.py` | already guarded | 3 fixtures, one per minting shape |
| `check_footprints.py` | **looked, already guarded** (`len(arms) != 6`, `not seen`, `not ro`, 0 labels, missing cold entry) | 4 groups over 3 extracted parsers + the verdict arithmetic |
| `check_archive_members.sh` | already guarded (incl. the word-split `--require "   "` case) | 4 over synthetic member lists |
| `check_composing_mode.py` | **looked, already guarded** — ~18 dies, the best-defended of the five | 4 groups over `BRACE`, `INVOKE`, `GUARD`, `doc_arms` |

"Looked, already guarded" is recorded deliberately so nobody re-audits it.

### Two real fixes

- **#113 hole 1** — command substitutions are now descended into (`command_substitutions()` + `deep_segments()`). This is the round-5 family, *"an allowed prefix launders a write"*, one level down.
- **#113 hole 2** — required renames counted by **fullmatch over segments** instead of `findall` over the raw line. That count is the gate's positive half; a single `echo '...'` defeated it.
- **#107** — `EXPECTED_SITES` keyed on **variable names**, not per-file counts. A count is restorable by a decoy; a name is not.

## The A/B that matters

`#107`'s decoy attack applied verbatim to the real `build_release.sh` (disguise `OUT_TMP` into an unseen shape, add a swept-looking `DECOY_TMP`), with **both** scanners run against the **same mutated tree**:

```
OLD exit=0  "check_scratch_prefix: 6 minting site(s), all swept"
NEW exit=1  "build_release.sh: expected scratch-minting site(s) bound to
             OUT_TMP; the scan found DECOY_TMP, NOTES_TMP"
```

Same mutation, opposite verdicts — the name-keying is what does the work.

## Every control driven red

Each with the mutation asserted present first, and every tracked file restored **from a copy taken first**, never `git checkout`:

- catch-all added to `ALLOWED` → `POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: the scanner did not flag echo "$(cp ...)"`
- `parse_labels` regex broken → `POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: parse_labels returned []`
- `if rs < 0` → `if False` → `POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: declaring 100 bytes while measuring 200 did not flag RESIDENT UNDER-DECLARED`
- `grep -qxF` → `grep -qx` → `POSITIVE CONTROL: 'lib_version.o' matched 'lib_versionXo'`
- `BRACE` narrowed → `POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED: BRACE parsed [('', 'long,short,compact')]`
- `GUARD` widened → `NEGATIVE CONTROL FAILED: GUARD matched .ifdef LIB_POLYVAL_NO_AES`

**Two of these previously produced a green run.**

## Two self-inflicted traps, recorded because they nearly shipped as evidence

1. **A fixture that polluted the thing it tested.** `check_scratch_prefix`'s fixtures, written literally in a file under `tools/`, were read by the real scan as genuine minting sites — measured: `check_scratch_prefix.py:133 <unbound> mints unswept-selftest.* NOT SWEPT`. They are now assembled at runtime, with assertions that fail loudly if a split stops reconstructing them.
2. **An A/B leg that never ran.** The first `#107` comparison ran the old scanner from the session scratchpad, where `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` resolved outside the repo; it died on a missing Makefile and the pipeline still reported `exit 0` — that was `tail`'s status. This is the trap CLAUDE.md's working standard already documents. Re-run with the old scanner placed inside `tools/`, where its own path assumptions hold. A third leg (`GUARD`) fired correctly while its mutation-present assertion printed 0 from a bad grep, and was re-run with the mutation confirmed by `diff`.

Green lines now report the control count, so the evidence is in the run rather than a transcript nobody rereads.

`make verify` 14/14 throughout. No library source touched; measured footprint rows unchanged by the `check_footprints` refactor.

## Review focus

Suggested claims to falsify: *"every control fires for the reason its message states"*, *"no control can pass while its gate is dead"*, and *"the check_footprints refactor did not change any measurement"*.

Independent of #119, which touches different files.

author: mgilbir
body:
CSS Fonts 4 §6.9: which national standard's forms a run's ideographs take, whether its characters are set on the ideographic advance or their own, and whether its kana are the small ones an annotation is set in. Nine keywords, all of them a request for a feature the face declares, and none of them read until now.

A set like the figures beside it — and the first group is **six alternatives rather than a pair**: JIS78, JIS83, JIS90 and JIS04 were four revisions of one standard and `simplified`/`traditional` are two forms of one character, so all six answer the same question and a value naming two of them asks for one ideograph in two shapes.

## The widths reach Latin, and that is what the narrowing is for

The six national forms and `ruby` act on East Asian characters, so a run of Latin is set identically with them and without — and a document that sets §6.9 on its `body` has Latin runs in a Latin face throughout. Reporting every one of them would hold a correct page out of the clean count for ever.

The width pair is not like that. A Japanese font draws the ASCII letters twice, once proportionally and once on the em, and `full-width` asks for the second drawing: two letters at full width are **two ems** where the same two proportionally are barely one.

So the narrowing is three classes, not one — `fwid` needs a character that *has* a full-width form, `pwid` one that *is* one. Both read from the table `text-transform: full-width` is applied from, so the two statements of which characters have a width twin cannot drift apart. That needed two predicates out of `paragraph`; they are there rather than written as ranges beside the caller because a hand-written twin of a generated table is right on the day it is written and wrong at the next Unicode revision.

## The fixture is a font, because no font has all nine

Noto Sans JP declares six — `jp78`, `jp83`, `jp90`, `fwid`, `pwid`, `ruby` — and none of `jp04`, `smpl` or `trad`, which is what a good CJK face looks like. A test written against it would report that three of the nine do nothing, and could not tell that from their doing nothing because the engine forgot to ask.

So the per-feature assertions run against a built font declaring all nine over one character of each class, and HarfBuzz's numbers over the real face pin what the tags mean: 辻 is a different ideograph under `jp83` and `jp90` and its own under `jp78`, and "A1" is `34 17461` proportionally and `15356 15340` on the em.

The **report** needed a font too. The fallback library has six of these, so a fixture set in it would be reporting on a face that can do the job; what the report is about is the ordinary East Asian face that draws the characters and declares no feature over them.

## Verification

Nine planted defects, each watched failing: the set never reaching the run, `adds()` dropping the tags, no report at all, the narrowing collapsed to one class, the narrowing dropped, the six national forms treated as separate groups, `fwid` and `pwid` swapped, the shorthand not resetting the longhand, and the reverse width index reading the table forwards.

`make test-corpora` green. **The suite cannot verify any of it** — the one corpus document naming §6.9 selects its variant with a script — so the reftest number is a regression check: 5982 clean, 80 tainted, 191 failed, no document changed side.

### Description

Fixes #1747

Replaces the local `NVEsmPreTrainedModel.get_extended_attention_mask` added in #1746 (a re-implementation of the deprecated `ModuleUtilsMixin` method) with `transformers.modeling_attn_mask_utils.AttentionMaskConverter`.

In `NVEsmModel.forward`:

```python
- extended_attention_mask = self.get_extended_attention_mask(attention_mask, input_shape)
+ extended_attention_mask = AttentionMaskConverter(is_causal=False).to_4d(
+     attention_mask, query_length=1, dtype=self.dtype
+ )
  extended_attention_mask = extended_attention_mask < -1  # TE boolean mask, True = masked
```

`to_4d` with `query_length=1` yields the same `[batch, 1, 1, seq_len]` additive mask (0 / `dtype.min`) the old helper produced, so the boolean mask handed to TE's `padding` attention is unchanged in shape and values. author: maxvint
body:
## Capability and contract

Native desktop notifications now consume the existing Workbench SSE stream
after Runtime readiness, including while the window is hidden to the tray.
The tray gains a persistent, default-on Notifications toggle next to Start
at Login. This is the G4 consumer implementation of
`docs/plans/desktop-notifications-sse.md`; the implementation and acceptance
notes are in `docs/plans/desktop-notifications-implementation.md`.

**Dependency: requires #1982 merged first.** This branch is based directly
on `desktop`, not stacked on the producer branch. The existing run detail
endpoint already supports the one-shot timestamp fallback.

### Boundaries and behavior

- `runtime-host` remains Tauri-free: bounded SSE decoding, an exact two-event
  allow-list, durable completion-minus-start duration, one bounded timestamp
  refetch, separate 512-key/24-hour approval and run dedup sets, and bounded
  reconnect backoff independent of `/ready`.
- Only `scheduled` and `watch` bypass the 30-second duration threshold;
  `agent_run` and future kinds follow duration. Missing/invalid timestamps fail
  closed. Suppressed events are consumed, never queued for later delivery.
- The shell owns one connection per adopted origin, keeps it through window
  closure, and cancels on confirmed readiness loss, Stop, Uninstall, or Quit.
  Generation checks also reject stale main-thread notification deliveries.
- Focused+visible or disabled notifications suppress delivery. Notification
  title/body are fixed native catalog copy in both locales; no untrusted
  Runtime title, output, or error is interpolated.
- The notification plugin is Rust-only. No Python, HTTP route, authentication,
  IPC command, capability, deep-link implementation, or window-state change.
  The explicitly approved dependencies are `tauri-plugin-notification = "2"`
  and existing locked chrono 0.4.45 with std-only features; Cargo generated
  the lockfile without updating existing package versions.

## Evidence layers

- Unit/contract: virtual-clock fake SSE tests assert allow-list filtering,
  dedup reset/capacity/TTL, durable duration independent of attachment or
  delayed receipt, refetch-once/fail-closed, precision/offsets, focus/preference
  suppression without replay, and reconnect/backoff/timeout behavior.
- HTTP boundary: an isolated loopback fake server exercises the real reqwest
  adapter, production framing, absent replay/auth headers, redirect refusal,
  response bounds, matching run identity, and single-segment URL encoding.
- Native/privilege contract: persistence uses test-owned temporary paths;
  tests assert native catalog intentions and shell lifecycle/capability
  wiring without sending any OS notification.
- Local validation passed: desktop `npm ci`, `npm run build`,
  `npm run test:i18n`; UI `npm ci` and `npm run build`;
  `cargo fmt --all -- --check`;
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`;
  `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (188 tests including the doc-test).
- Scenario IDs: G4's frozen **Tests (invariants)** section is the scenario
  contract; no separate desktop scenario catalog exists.
- No user Runtime was restarted or real OS notification emitted. The
  unchanged npm lockfiles report audit warnings; UI dependency/chunk warnings
  and Cargo's local cache-cleanup permission warning are outside this change.

## Known-by-design

1. **Real OS acceptance remains integration work.** Notification permission,
   visible native delivery, hidden-to-tray behavior, and tray-toggle UX need
   packaged macOS/Windows acceptance; green Rust tests do not claim it.
2. **v1 uses OS-default activation, not an explicit click callback.** The
   orchestrator amended the contract because the desktop notification plugin
   drops its native handle and exposes no desktop action callback. macOS
   normally activates the sending app; Windows behavior is backend/OS
   dependent and may only dismiss. Explicit cross-platform
   show+unminimize+focus is **v2 with native activation adapter (macOS
   UNUserNotificationCenter delegate + Windows toast activation)**. No fake
   click wiring or explicit-click claim is included.
3. **Notification-specific deep-link targets remain a G5 follow-up.** No
   session navigation or deep-link code is changed here.
4. **SSE has no replay.** Missed events stay missed; pending Vault state is
   recoverable in Workbench. Retained keys are bounded, so an evicted/expired
   pending request or run may notify again by design.

5. **Windows replacement is already implemented; intentionally unchanged.**
   Review thread `PRRT_kwDOPbFPYs6hN4-s` claimed that `std::fs::rename`
   cannot replace an existing Windows destination. The Rust standard library
   explicitly uses `MoveFileExW(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` for this
   operation ([pinned source](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.90.0/library/std/src/sys/fs/windows.rs#L1244-L1245)).
   More importantly, the exact PR head's
   [Windows CI job](https://github.com/avibe-bot/avibe/actions/runs/34520276319/job/103015765171)
   passed the existing consuming test
   `notifications::tests::preference_defaults_on_and_persists_the_tray_choice_across_restarts`:
   default on -> toggle off -> reconstruct state -> toggle on -> reconstruct
   state again. This exercises replacing the existing preference file, not
   just its initial creation. Keep the current replacement path rather than
   adding a delete-before-rename gap or an unnecessary platform adapter.

Do not merge from this lane. Await exact-head Codex review, zero unresolved
threads, passing desktop-shell/lint CI, and orchestrator integration approval.

## Summary & Motivation

Follow-up to #1517. The merge of that PR triggered a Dependabot rescan of `main`, which surfaced advisories published on 2026-09-08 for four packages. This PR takes the patches. The two `next` advisories are critical, unauthenticated RCE in the Image Optimization API via AVIF and unauthenticated RCE on Windows-hosted servers. `next` is a direct dependency of `@turnkey/sdk-react`, so this also bumps that package and adds a patch changeset.

| Package | Before | After | Alerts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `next` | 15.5.21 | 15.5.24 | #1653, #1654 (sdk-react), #1655, #1658 (lockfile) |
| `js-yaml` | 3.15.1, 4.3.1 | 3.15.2, 4.3.2 | #1659, #1660 |
| `sharp` | 0.35.3 | 0.35.4 | #1661 |
| `svgo` | 2.8.3 | 2.8.4 | #1656, #1657 |

Advisories:

- `next`: GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 (RCE via AVIF in Image Optimization), GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 / CVE-2026-75604 (RCE on Windows hosts). sdk-react does not run the image optimizer or a Windows server itself, but downstream apps that use sdk-react resolve `next` through it, so the direct bump matters.
- `js-yaml`: GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh / CVE-2026-84375, `maxTotalMergeKeys` does not bound CPU for empty merge sources. Dev tooling only, same reachability as in #1496.
- `sharp`: GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c, bundled libheif vulnerabilities. Transitive via `next`.
- `svgo`: GHSA-4vpr-x523-8j87 and GHSA-w27v-7q3p-w38r, the same `removeScripts` bypasses fixed for 3.x in #1517. The advisory range now also covers 2.x, so this adds a scoped override for the 2.x line pulled in by `rollup-plugin-postcss`.

The 83 new alerts on manifests under `examples/` (76 `next`, 5 `js-yaml`, 2 `baseline-browser-mapping`) are dismissed as `not_used` with the standing comment. I dismissed them today. After this PR merges, the 5 alerts listed as intentionally open in #1517 are the only ones left on the root lockfile.

author: lczh
body:
Tier: fix

## What was wrong
Verified on `main`: the end and interrupt route, when the session lived on an attached remote, forwarded the request to that machine's kernel, dropped the reply, and answered ok regardless. The CLI prints "romp end: ok" on any ok, so from a hub, ending a runaway on a box whose tunnel had just dropped printed success and exited 0 while the runaway kept running. And the "when idle" deferral never crossed the wire, so ending a remote session at its next idle killed it mid-turn instead. The send route, forwarded to the same machine, already answered honestly in both respects.

## What changes
The remote arm mirrors the send arm. The forwarded body carries the idle deferral when the request asked for it. When the far kernel does not answer, the route answers ok false and names the host, so the CLI reports "kernel refused" with that text and exits 1. Otherwise the far kernel's reply comes back verbatim: a far refusal arrives as itself, and an ok that carries the deferred flag rides through so the caller can read it. The working-status route is left alone, since the bus posts its own local id there.

## Deliberately left out
This covers requests that address the session by its id, the shape the CLI sends for one and what the forward carries. A remote session addressed by name still resolves locally, because name resolution reads the local names registry, live sessions and threads and never the polled remote names; that is the hub's pre-existing addressing model, shared by the send and compact routes, and a separate defect. An older far kernel that ignores the deferral gets no special answer; its reply simply lacks the flag, which the caller can read.

## Tests
A new module drives the real request handler over loopback with only the host lookup and the forward stubbed, the forward as a recorder: ending at idle over a dead tunnel forwards the deferral and answers ok false naming the host; interrupting over a dead tunnel answers ok false; a far refusal comes back verbatim; the far deferred flag comes back. On `main` all four fail: the forwarded body lacks the deferral, and the reply is ok true in every case. The module passes 4, and the neighbouring headless-ops, tunnel-truth, end-on-idle and perf-stats modules pass unchanged.

erichare
body:
## Summary

Cutting the first RC of a patch release picks up the RC number of the *previous* minor cycle: the first 1.12.2 RC comes out as `1.12.2rc5` (the number 1.12.0's next RC would have used) instead of `1.12.2rc0`.

### Root cause

`determine-rc-number` takes the max of `langflow_pre_release_tag.py --print-rc-number` across every package the run publishes. `next_rc_number()` returns `max(rcN) + 1` for a base version **even when that exact final is already published**. `langflow-sdk` isn't bumped for patch releases (it's still `0.4.0` on release-1.12.2), and PyPI still has `0.4.0rc0`…`0.4.0rc4` from the 1.12.0 cycle, so the SDK contributes `5` and wins:

```
PyPI langflow: next rc number for 1.12.2 is 0
PyPI langflow-base: next rc number for 1.12.2 is 0
PyPI lfx: next rc number for 1.12.2 is 0
PyPI langflow-sdk: next rc number for 0.4.0 is 5
Shared pre-release rc number: 5
```

Bundles already had a guard for exactly this case (`final … is already published; excluding its historical RCs`). The SDK path didn't.

### Fix

- **`determine-rc-number`**: move the bundle guard into a `consider_unreleased_versions` helper and use it for `langflow-sdk` too. langflow / langflow-base / lfx still count their RC history on purpose: a pre-release run always publishes them, so their RC numbers have to stay collision-free.
- **`determine-sdk-version`**: in pre-release mode, reuse an already-published SDK final (`skipped=true`) instead of minting an RC. This change is required. Once the SDK stops raising the shared number, the RC would be `0.4.0rc0`, which already exists on PyPI, so `publish-sdk` would fail. It also matches the stable path, which already skips an unchanged SDK. `build-lfx`, `test-cross-platform`, `release-inventory` and `publish-lfx` already handle `build-sdk` being skipped, and lfx's `langflow-sdk>=0.4.0` resolves to the published final.
- That PyPI lookup retries and **fails the step** on a network or parse error instead of falling through to "not published". Falling through would silently bring the collision back.
- `ci-scripts-test.yml` now also triggers on `release.yml`, so edits to these steps run the tests that cover them.

## Tests

New `scripts/ci/test_release_rc_number.py` pulls the real `run:` scripts out of `release.yml` and runs them under `bash -e` with `curl`/`uv` stubbed against fixture PyPI data. The fixture matches PyPI as of 1.12.1. The existing tests only check the workflow's text, so they couldn't catch a wrong computed number.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First 1.12.2 RC, SDK unchanged | `rc5` | `rc0` |
| langflow already has `1.12.2rc0`, `rc1` | `rc5` | `rc2` |
| SDK bumped to `0.4.1` with `0.4.1rc0`, `rc1` on PyPI | `rc2` | `rc2` (still coordinates) |
| SDK step, `0.4.0` final published | `0.4.0rc0`, `skipped=false` | `0.4.0`, `skipped=true` |
| SDK step, PyPI unreachable mid-step | exit 0, mints `0.4.0rc0` | step fails |

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest scripts/ci/`: 157 passed
- [x] Patched `determine-rc-number` step with real `curl` against live PyPI and Docker Hub on this branch → `rc_number=0` (SDK and 22 published bundles excluded)
- [x] Patched `determine-sdk-version` step against live PyPI → `version=0.4.0`, `skipped=true`
- [ ] Dry-run `release.yml` as a pre-release on `release-1.12.2`: `Determine Shared RC Number` logs `Shared pre-release rc number: 0` and `Determine SDK Version` logs `SDK 0.4.0 is already published; reusing it for this pre-release.`


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

  * Published SDK versions are reused when appropriate instead of generating unnecessary new release candidates.
  * Release workflow validation now better handles unavailable package registry responses.

* **Tests**

author: gallowbell
body:
## Summary
This PR implements two major combat mechanics (armor and splash damage), overhauls the tower upgrade system to prevent runaway power scaling, and fixes several bugs in the game loop and UI.

## Key Changes

### Combat Mechanics
- **Armor system**: Enemies now have an `armor` stat that reduces incoming damage by a flat amount per hit, with a minimum of 1 damage guaranteed. Armor is applied after crit multipliers so high-damage towers still punch through.
- **Splash damage**: Towers can now have a `splashRadius` property. When set, they damage all enemies within that radius of the primary target, with armor applied per victim. Splash kills award their own gold rewards.
- Updated `DamageSystem.applyHit()` to accept an optional enemy list and return splash hit/kill information via `DamageResult`.

### Upgrade System Overhaul
- **Fixed compounding growth**: The old system multiplied already-upgraded stats by a growing factor each level, causing quadratic DPS scaling. Now every level's stats are derived from the immutable `baseDefinition`, preventing runaway power.
- **New upgrade formula**: Cost is `baseCost * 0.4 * currentLevel` (reduced from 0.6); damage grows 35% per level, fire rate 20%, and range 8% per level.
- **Level cap**: Added `maxTowerLevel: 4` to prevent infinite scaling. Towers now track `baseDefinition` (level-1 stats) and `investedGold` (cumulative cost).
- `TowerUpgradeSystem` now validates max level and returns `boolean` from `applyUpgrade()` to indicate success.

### Game Loop & Rendering
- **Fixed-timestep simulation**: Replaced variable delta-time with fixed 1/60s steps accumulated per frame, capping at 8 steps to prevent spiral on long frames. This makes tower fire rate independent of frame rate and speed multiplier.
- **Render phase separation**: Moved range indicator drawing to a dedicated `drawScene()` method called after simulation, preventing flicker from the render layer being cleared mid-frame.
- **Scene reset**: Added explicit per-run state reset in `create()` to prevent stale state leaking across `scene.restart()` calls.

### Bug Fixes
- **Gold spending**: `spendGold()` now returns `boolean` and refuses unaffordable or negative amounts, preventing silent clamping and double-charging bugs.
- **Sell refunds**: Changed from `tower.definition.cost` to `tower.investedGold` so refunds reflect actual investment, not base cost.
- **Upgrade pricing**: Fixed double-charging by reading the cost BEFORE upgrading, matching the price shown to the player.
- **Leak handling**: Extracted leak logic to `handleLeak()` to avoid duplicate processing.
- **Test stability**: Mocked `Math.random()` in damage tests to prevent flaky crit-chance assertions.

### Type System
- Added `TowerDefinition` and `LeveledStats` types for better type safety.
- Updated `TowerState` to include `baseDefinition` and `investedGold` fields.
- Added `armor` field to `EnemyDefinition` and `EnemyState`.
- Added `splashRadius` to tower definitions and `splashHits`/`splashKills` to combat events.

### Testing
- Added comprehensive test suite for armor mechanics (subtracts from damage, minimum 1, applies after crit).
- Added splash damage tests covering radius, victim selection, reward payout, and armor interaction.
- Added full `TowerUpgradeSystem` test suite validating the new non-compounding curve, level cap, and cost tracking.
- Updated existing tests to use new tower/enemy factory signatures.

### Config & Build
- Removed committed `vite.config.js`, `vitest.config.js` and `.d.ts` files to prevent them shadowing TypeScript sources.
- Updated `.gitignore` and `tsconfig.node.json` to prevent tsc output from interfering with Vite config resolution.

author: farhadeidi
body:
## Summary

`npx bookmarks-but-better` becomes the **Daemon Manager** — the one place a person installs, checks on, and configures the daemon — and the daemon binary stops asking questions. Records the decision as [ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-manage-the-daemon-from-an-npm-tool-and-keep-management-out-of-its-api.md) and prepares the 4.1.0 release.

- **Daemon Manager** (`packages/bookmarks-but-better`): `status`, `install`, `uninstall`, `vault list|add|remove`. With no command it installs when nothing is installed and otherwise shows the status and a `@clack/prompts` menu of what can be done about it — each problem's fix first. Every command asks for what it was not given; `--yes` takes the defaults. It reads no bookmarks and by default installs its own version of the daemon, so it joins the one-version rule (checked by the release `validate` job).
- **Daemon binary**: `setup` removed; `service status --json` added; `/health` carries `clients` (open event streams) so `status` can say whether a browser is connected. `service install` restarts a running service on every platform, since it is how a new binary, port or vault set is applied. No management endpoint on the HTTP API — the daemon stays fully separate from any UI.
- **Installers**: `--skip-setup`/`-SkipSetup` gone; `--vault <dir>`/`-Vault <dir>` do the whole first run without a terminal; without it they install the binary and print the next steps. An install over a configured machine reinstalls the service on the new binary; a 4.0.0 service's vaults are adopted into the registry first.
- **Vault Registry** (ADR-0005) and multi-vault `service install`, cherry-picked from the earlier branch. The shell, menu and TUI work from that branch was withdrawn (see ADR-0006, considered options).
- **Settings** opens on Sources, which is now the first tab.
- Docs, website, settings-panel install guide, CHANGELOG (`4.1.0` section) updated.

## How it was verified

- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`; `bun run lint/typecheck/format:check/test`, website typecheck and build; `node --test` for the package; `npm pack --dry-run`; `shellcheck`; `tests/install/smoke-test.sh`.
- `bun run test:e2e:manager` (new): builds the daemon, serves it as a fake release under the manager's own version in a throwaway HOME, and drives install → status → vault add → vault remove → uninstall against a real LaunchAgent, with assertions. `bun run try:manager` opens the same setup in a shell for poking at by hand.
- Reviewed by two sub-agents (standards and spec); the defects they found are fixed in the last commit.

## Not verified here

- `install.ps1` is syntax-checked and reviewed only; no Windows machine. CI runs it for real.
- Publishing to npm is manual and happens **after** the stable `v4.1.0` GitHub release exists (docs/RELEASING.md); the package is not published yet.

## Release order after merge

1. `git push origin v4.1.0-beta.2` and try the manager against the real prerelease.
2. RELEASING.md checklist, then `git push origin v4.1.0`.
3. `npm publish` from `packages/bookmarks-but-better`.

author: tomyhara
body:
## What this changes

Re-running the release workflow now replaces what the draft release holds
instead of trying to add to it, so the draft is always exactly one build. It
also fails if what ended up attached does not match what was built.

This is the fix for run #2 of the v0.0.1 release, which built both platforms
successfully and then failed to attach the macOS disk image with
`ReleaseAsset.name already exists`.

### Two defects, one hiding the other

**GitHub compares release asset names case insensitively.** The earlier
CLI-only build attached `mochi-0.0.1-macos-universal.dmg`; this one produces
`Mochi-0.0.1-macos-universal.dmg`. `gh ... --clobber` compares names exactly,
so it saw nothing to replace and uploaded a name GitHub considered taken. Of
the six files, that is the only pair differing only in case — and it is the
only one that failed.

**Underneath that, `--clobber` was doing nothing at all here.** A draft release
has no git tag until someone publishes it, and gh's lookup by name does not
populate the asset list, so there was never anything for it to find. Run #1's
own log is the evidence: `gh release view` lists no assets seconds after
uploading five. The name collision was only the trigger; re-runs had never been
able to replace anything.

So the update path resolves the release through the API, deletes every asset it
holds, then uploads. That also clears assets named by conventions the workflow
no longer uses, which is what the earlier CLI-only naming had left behind.

### A partial upload was silent

`gh release upload` uploads concurrently, and a failure part way through leaves
a release whose files do not match its own `SHA256SUMS.txt` — worse than a
failed build, because nothing looks wrong. Since these builds are unsigned, the
checksum file is the only thing a person can verify against, so it has to cover
every attached file. The step now compares the attached names against `dist/`
and fails, naming the difference.

## Requirements covered

FR-10.1, NFR-4b.7. No requirement text changed.

## How it was tested

Only `.github/workflows/release.yml` changed; no Rust or TypeScript is touched,
so the suites that guard those would pass or fail identically to main, which is
green. What needed proving was the shell, and this step had already failed once
in CI, so it was not re-run on a guess.

The script was extracted from the workflow and run against a stub `gh` that
models the two GitHub behaviours above — case-insensitive asset names, and a
draft whose asset list comes back empty:

- [x] **the stub reproduces the real failure**: the old script against run #1's
      five assets fails on the same asset with the same message as run #2
- [x] the new script succeeds from no release at all (create path)
- [x] the new script succeeds over run #1's five assets, ending with exactly
      the six built files
- [x] the new script succeeds over run #2's partial state, ending the same way
- [x] **the new check fails** with the missing file named, when the stub is
      made to drop one upload
- [x] `bash -n` and a YAML parse of the whole workflow
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

`cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy` were not re-run: no code they cover
is in this diff.

## Checklist

- [x] No change writes to the original session files (FR-2.5, NFR-3.5)
- [x] No new outbound network call or telemetry (NFR-3.1, NFR-4b.8) — the
      change is CI-only and ships in no binary
- [x] External processes are still launched from an argument array, never a
      shell string (NFR-3.6)
- [x] Any new golden file is free of credentials and personal paths (NFR-4b.4)
      — no golden file added
- [x] New source files carry the Apache-2.0 header (NFR-4b.1b) — no new source
      files

## Review notes

The whole change is one step in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The deletion
loop is the part worth a second look: it removes every asset on the draft
before uploading, which is deliberate and was confirmed with the repository
owner, since assets from an older run cannot be regenerated once the naming
they used is gone from main.

After merging, re-running the release workflow for `v0.0.1` produces a draft
holding the three installers, the two command line archives, and a
`SHA256SUMS.txt` covering all five.

author: patskiller
body:
## A regression I introduced, caught on the first organic wake after it deployed

#960 made durable memory findable. The very next scheduled slot (23:00Z, served SHA `f17c0e759`) produced this:

```
23:00:01Z STALE    f17c0e759 | facts: 1 | research: 1 | effect: None
23:00:01Z SETTLED  f17c0e759 | facts: 0 | research: 1 | effect: changed_question
23:00:01Z SETTLED  f17c0e759 | facts: 0 | research: 1 | effect: changed_question
```

The one wake that **succeeded in loading a memory fact** is the one that produced no decision.

## Root cause: a control that had never once executed

`refuse_stale_memory` at `persistent_agent_wake.py:477` aborts the wake when the snapshot is stale. `stale` is derived from the newest **loaded** fact:

```python
stale = False
if newest is not None and (now - newest) > timedelta(hours=self.stale_hours):
    stale = True
```

Every wake loaded zero facts, so `newest` was always `None` and `stale` was always `False`. **The branch was dead from the day it was written.** #960 armed it, and its first act was to abort a wake.

This is the §7 shape inverted: not a control whose name exceeds its code, but a control that was never reachable, so nobody learned what it does.

## Why refusing is the wrong response

Before memory was loadable, these subjects proceeded with no facts. After, one 18-day-old fact ends the decision entirely. **The desk does strictly less the more memory it can find** — and a refused wake produces no decision at all, which is the same terminal slot loss as this morning's `MEMORY_MALFORMED` regression, in a new costume.

Measured when found `[VERIFIED]`:

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| subjects with loadable memory | 71 |
| past the 168h window | **65** |
| median newest-fact age | **432h** |
| wake subjects that would refuse | 2 of 25 |
| wake subjects proceeding **with** memory | **0** |

Producer: `stale_memory_blast_radius.py` in the closure audit directory, positive-controlled.

## The change

A stale snapshot is replaced with an empty one and the wake continues:

- **The intent is preserved** — the wake still never reasons from stale facts. It proceeds without them, exactly where it stood yesterday.
- `stale_memory_degraded_to_empty` is recorded in `policy_decisions`, so a degraded wake is never confused with a normal one.
- `snapshot.stale` is left untouched, so the signal survives for anything that wants to report it.
- **Malformed memory still refuses.** A store we cannot parse is a different condition from one that is merely old, and a test pins that boundary so this change cannot widen.

## An existing test is updated, deliberately

`test_stale_memory_refuses` pinned `ok is False` / `state == "STALE"`. It pinned behaviour that had never run in production and is now known wrong. It is renamed to `test_stale_memory_degrades_and_does_not_refuse` with the reason recorded in its docstring.

Calling this out explicitly because AGENTS.md §5 forbids updating test literals to make a red test green. **The policy is corrected; the literals follow.** The old assertion was an adjudication, not a floor.

## Tests

8 in `tests/test_wake_stale_memory_degrades.py`, registered in the CI allowlist. The wake-level tests drive `run_scheduled_wake` end to end rather than asserting on a helper — the first draft made exactly that mistake and asserted on a transformation the test performed itself.

**Mutation-tested:**

```
restore the refusal                     -> 3 failed
degrade swallows fresh memory too       -> 12 failed
```

A source-level guard asserts `refuse_stale_memory` is absent from the string constants, walking the AST rather than grepping, so a comment quoting the old name cannot satisfy it.

31 related memory/wake tests pass. `ruff` clean. Digests regenerated.

## Authority

`MBI_BEHAVIOR=0`. Cognition only: this changes whether a wake reaches a decision, never a size, weight, order or stop.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: mojeeq
body:
## The setting did nothing

Setting `R_SCRIPTS_ENABLED=true` in `.env` had no effect on a Docker deployment. The container never reads `.env` itself - Compose uses that file for `${...}` substitution only, and the image copies `app/`, `requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml`, nothing else. The four R settings were absent from the shared `x-backend-env` block, so the value went nowhere however carefully it was written.

R is already in the image (`r-base-core` is installed in the Dockerfile precisely so this would be one setting rather than a rebuild), so the feature was one line of YAML away from working and gave no clue why it wasn't.

`R_SCRIPTS_ENABLED`, `R_BINARY`, `R_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `R_MEMORY_MB` are now forwarded to `api`, `worker` and `beat`, each keeping the default the application already had.

I checked the rest of the surface while here: every other setting offered in `.env.example` does reach the container. These four were the whole gap.

The user guide still had a "The command box" section documenting Stata `gen`/`replace`/`egen`, and a "Running R over a dataset" section - both removed when R moved to the project. Rewritten:

- **`docs/user-guide.md`** - one "Running R in a project" section covering the R tab, `read_dataset` / `write_dataset` / `datasets`, the working directory that survives between runs, saved scripts and the after-each-import replay. It says plainly how to turn it on, and what to check if the tab still reports R as switched off after a restart.
- **`docs/architecture.md`** - describes `rproject.py` and the workspace model, rather than the deleted `stata.py` and `stata_expr.py`.
- **`docs/api.md`** - lists the project script routes in place of the deleted `/datasets/{id}/command` ones.
- **`README.md`** - the feature bullet and the security bullet now match what the platform does.
- **`.env.example`** - the comment beside the setting describes projects rather than the command box, and names the command that applies it.
