author: e107help[bot]
body:
### Why

Two menu configuration screens told an administrator their preferences were saved whether or not the save had happened. Both called the preference handler's `save()` with the third argument `false`, which tells the handler to display nothing, and then announced `LAN_SAVED` without looking at what came back.

- [`e107_plugins/login_menu/config.php` lines 97 to 99](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/65bc3ed38d710e4d4010898f64998eec40048bed/e107_plugins/login_menu/config.php#L97-L99)
- [`e107_plugins/online/config.php` lines 40 to 49](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/65bc3ed38d710e4d4010898f64998eec40048bed/e107_plugins/online/config.php#L40-L49)

`save()` answers `true` for a write, `0` for nothing to do and `false` for an error, [as its own docblock says](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/65bc3ed38d710e4d4010898f64998eec40048bed/e107_handlers/pref_class.php#L558-L565). An error is a MySQL failure on the `core` row, or the optimistic retry giving up because another writer kept changing that row underneath it, and [the handler already knows which](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/65bc3ed38d710e4d4010898f64998eec40048bed/e107_handlers/pref_class.php#L606-L621). With its display suppressed none of that reached the page, and the green "Saved" went out anyway.

Fixes #6196

### What Changed

- Both screens drop the third argument, so the handler reports the outcome it has already worked out, and each screen's own `LAN_SAVED` goes with it. One message per save rather than two.
- Each screen's admin log entry now depends on the save. The login menu screen's `MISC_03` moves behind a `=== true` return. The online screen's `MISC_02` was written by the very call that decided whether to save at all, so it now follows the save rather than leading it.
- That call was also the online screen's no-change gate, and the gate goes with it. The save is forced, so the handler reaches storage on every post and [answers `0` when storage already holds what was posted](https://github.com/e107inc/e107/blob/65bc3ed38d710e4d4010898f64998eec40048bed/e107_handlers/pref_class.php#L629-L648), saying so in the same words the screen used to say itself.

The guard is `=== true` rather than a truth test because the handler's other two answers are both falsy and mean opposite things.

### How It Was Tested

`e107_tests/tests/unit/menuConfigSaveMessagesTest.php` posts each screen's own save button inside a booted CLI subprocess and counts the success boxes on the page that comes back. Each screen's save is refused with a validation error, which is the one refusal that can be provoked without breaking the database. The screens cannot tell one refusal from another, since neither looks at why the handler said no, and a refused save reaches neither storage nor the admin log, so the two cases leave the shared menu preferences as they found them.

Both cases were run against the unfixed sources as well, and both fail there, so they are not passing by accident. The whole unit suite was run over the branch.

The failed save an administrator actually meets is a MySQL error on the `core` row, and I have not driven one of those on a live site. That path is traced, not reproduced.

### Backwards Compatibility

No rendered HTML changes. The markup of every message box and of both forms is untouched, and the difference is only in which boxes appear. Three things an administrator sees do change:

- A successful save says "Your settings have been saved" (`LAN_SETSAVED`, from the handler) where it said "Saved" (`LAN_SAVED`). Nothing in the tree keys on either wording on these two screens.
- A save that changes nothing says so on the login menu screen, which used to say "Saved". The online screen said it already, from its own branch.
- A failed save reports the MySQL error number and text, or the conflict behind it, instead of claiming success.

### AI Model

Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5), as e107help.

### Checklist

- [x] One issue per PR: the diff is scoped to this change only
- [x] Commit messages explain *why*, not just *what*
- [x] New or changed behavior has test coverage (or explain why not)
- [x] No unrelated reformatting, renames, or import reordering

author: vafaei-ar
body:
## What this adds

- local multi-user voice profiles keyed by immutable numeric Telegram user ID
- explicit voice ownership/permission confirmation before enrollment
- local voice-profile listing, default selection, and deletion
- FFmpeg normalization of Telegram voice/audio recordings to 24 kHz mono WAV
- Telegram long-polling bot with `/start`, `/setupvoice`, `/voices`, `/defaultvoice`, `/deletevoice`, `/settings`, and `/health`
- `presentation-narration.md` upload and deterministic validation
- direct plain-text read-aloud from ordinary Telegram messages
- generation confirmation for narration files plus immediate generation for plain text
- Chatterbox as the production/default backend, with CUDA as the bot's default device
- warm backend reuse plus serialized GPU rendering
- 96 kbps mono MP3 delivery

## Managed background service

Normal operation is a terminal-independent **user-level systemd service**. No sudo and no permanently open terminal are required.

User commands:

```bash
lectra configure
lectra start
lectra status
lectra restart
lectra stop
lectra logs
lectra logs --follow
lectra enable
lectra disable
```

`lectra start` installs/refreshes the user service unit, starts the local FastAPI service and Telegram bot, checks the voice-service API, then exits. Closing the terminal does not stop Lectra. `lectra enable` enables autostart at user login.

The Telegram token is entered through a hidden prompt and persisted only in a private local config file (0600). The systemd unit points to that environment file and does not embed the token.

## Plain-text read-aloud

Any ordinary non-command Telegram text message is synthesized immediately with the user's default voice profile. Commands such as `/health` are excluded. If `/setupvoice` is waiting for an enrollment recording, typed text does not trigger TTS.

Plain text uses a first-class `/v1/text/jobs` endpoint and shares the same GPU queue, Chatterbox backend, progress state, MP3 encoding, and error reporting as presentation narration. Telegram's 4,096-character text limit is enforced, and long messages are split at sentence/word boundaries into roughly 420-character speech chunks for stable TTS.

## Progress-aware generation

During generation the Telegram status message reports:

- waiting for GPU
- loading the model
- speech synthesis progress as completed/total segments or text chunks
- percentage and progress bar
- elapsed time
- MP3 encoding
- completion/upload

Generation failures are shown directly in Telegram with sanitized error text. A global Telegram error handler reports real application errors, while transient Telegram `NetworkError` failures are logged as concise warnings because the polling library retries them automatically.

## Bugs found by real testing and fixed

1. `ChatAction.UPLOAD_AUDIO` no longer exists in python-telegram-bot 22.8. The bot no longer uses that action.
2. The first token-redaction regex failed for tokens embedded directly after `/bot` in Telegram API URLs. The regex is corrected and routine httpx/httpcore INFO request logs are suppressed.
3. The progress bot called `/v1/jobs/...` while the service exposed `/v1/render/jobs/...`, producing the observed `HTTP 404: Not Found`. The service now supports the bot path and the canonical render-job path during the v0.3 transition.
4. `/health` used `render_job_progress` while the bot checked `progress_reporting`. The service now advertises both during the transition.
5. The systemd launcher originally dereferenced the venv Python symlink and then quoted `EnvironmentFile`; both caused managed startup failures on the target machine. The unit now preserves the venv interpreter path and writes an unquoted absolute EnvironmentFile path.
6. Transient Telegram `502 Bad Gateway`/`NetworkError` polling failures previously produced full traceback floods. They are now treated as recoverable transport warnings.

## Version

Voice service is now **0.3.2** for direct plain-text TTS on top of the 0.3.1 managed-service/API fixes.

## Validation

- target-machine managed-service work previously reached **33/33 tests passed** before the final systemd and Telegram-network fixes
- regression coverage now includes systemd unit generation, private configuration permissions, stale/incompatible service rejection, render-job route aliases, health capability keys, per-segment progress, render-job completion/failure, progress formatting, token redaction, transient Telegram network errors, plain-text chunking, the `/v1/text/jobs` contract, and plain-text render-job completion

## Real end-to-end re-test required before merge

1. pull the latest branch and reinstall editable dependencies;
2. run the full pytest suite;
3. run `lectra restart` and confirm `lectra status` reports voice service 0.3.2 and plain-text capability;
4. send one ordinary text message and confirm immediate progress + MP3 return;
5. upload a real narration file and confirm live generation progress;
6. verify any Chatterbox/service error is visible in Telegram;
7. close the terminal and verify the bot remains responsive.

Do not merge until those flows succeed.

body:
## Summary

Answers "who is using model X?" from the LLM provider details page, so a team still on a deprecated model can be found and contacted without leaving the admin UI.

**Provider details page**
- "Cost per Model" becomes **Models in use**: adds Requests, Apps and Last used columns; every header sorts; default order is most recently used first. Model names link to the new detail view; the model-price link moves to a row icon plus a "Manage model prices" button.

**New model detail page** (`/admin/llms/:id/models?model=…`)
- Token and cost charts for that model alone, date range picker, summary chips.
- **Apps using this model** table: app (linked to the app page), owner email as a `mailto:` link, requests, tokens, cost, first used, last used. Sortable. Deleted apps stay listed but greyed out and unlinked.
- The model goes in the query string because vendor model IDs can contain colons and slashes (Bedrock, OpenRouter).

**Backend**
- `GetTotalCostPerVendorAndModel` also returns `requestCount`, `appCount` and `lastUsed` (additive JSON).
- New `GET /api/v1/analytics/apps-for-model?llm_id&model_name&start_date&end_date` backed by `analytics.GetAppsForModel`, which joins `apps` and `users`. Scoped to the LLM entry: the same model name can sit under two entries for one vendor, and the question is asked from one provider's page.
- `GET /api/v1/analytics/usage` accepts an optional `model_name` filter so the detail page reuses the existing multi-axis chart data.
- `analytics.ScanTime` scans `MAX/MIN(time_stamp)`: aggregate columns have no declared type, so the SQLite driver returns raw text where Postgres returns a timestamp.

**No schema or data-plane change.** `llm_chat_records` already carries model name, `llm_id`, `app_id` and timestamp from both the embedded gateway (`proxy/analyze_utils.go`, `translator.go`, `bedrock_translator.go`) and the edge analytics pulse (`grpc/control_server.go`), so edge-routed traffic is included.

**Also fixed on the way:** the cost chart spread the API dataset straight into Chart.js, and the dataset's `yAxisID: "y1"` created an empty second y axis beside the configured "Cost ($)" one. Both pages now share `usageCharts.js`, which copies only label and data.

**Docs:** `dashboard.md`, a new "Finding who uses a model" section in `llm-management.md`, `features/LLM.md`. Swagger regenerated with plain `swag init -g api/api.go -o docs/swagger`; the committed output was already stale, so the diff also picks up governed-metadata endpoints from earlier PRs.

- [x] `go test ./analytics/ ./api/` green. New tests: `TestScanTime`, `TestGetAppsForModel` (ordering by last used, deleted and hard-deleted apps, owner email, interaction-type filter, LLM scoping, empty result), extended `TestGetTotalCostPerVendorAndModel` (asserts the three new fields with seeded rows so the aggregate scan runs on SQLite), `TestGetUsage` model filter, handler test for the new route (400s and happy path).
- [x] The three queries run as raw SQL against the dev stack's Postgres and return real rows.
- [x] Frontend: 20 new Jest tests (`modelUsage.test.js`, `LLMModelDetails.test.js`); full suite green (158 suites, 1401 tests). ESLint clean on changed files.
- [x] Clicked through on the Docker dev stack: table, sort, link-through, detail page, app link, single cost axis.

## Resumen

Implementa configuración por tenant del segundo factor de administración (MFA), permitiendo ambientes de demo/QA desechables que no dependan de un buzón real:

- Script `seed_demo_qa.py` para crear tenants así sin tocar código

Ausentes ambas claves, el comportamiento no cambia: MFA sigue exigido y el código sigue siendo aleatorio (defecto seguro).

body:
### What

Adds `--log-sample-completions N` (default `0`). When set, `log_rollout_data` in `miles/ray/rollout/metrics.py` logs the first N prompt/response pairs of every rollout step as a `rollout/completions` table with reward, status and response length, right after the step's scalar metrics. Rows are taken round-robin across prompt groups (`group_index`), so a small table shows different prompts rather than one prompt's n responses; chat prompts render as `role: content` lines, prompt and response text are capped at 2048 and 4096 characters, and every cell is a string or an int so no table column mixes types (wandb rejects mixed columns by default). Tables travel through a new `log_table` method on `TrackingBackend` in `miles/utils/tracking_utils/base.py`: the base implementation is a no-op, `WandbBackend` logs a `wandb.Table`, and `TrackingManager` plus a `tracking.log_table` facade fan it out. mlflow, tensorboard, prometheus and the dashboard are untouched. The monitoring guide gets a paragraph.

### Test

`tests/fast/utils/tracking_utils/test_log_table.py` injects a fake `wandb` module and checks the table payload (name, columns, rows), that a backend without tables ignores the call, and that the manager fans out only to enabled backends. `tests/fast/ray/rollout/test_sample_completion_rows.py` checks the round-robin order over the flat sample list the executor passes, the limit, the rendering of chat prompts, dict and missing rewards, status and length, the empty step, and that `log_rollout_data` calls `tracking.log_table` once when the flag is on and never when it is 0. The rollout test fixture gains the new field with its default.

### Verification

- The seven new tests pass; `tests/fast/ray/rollout`, `tests/fast/utils/tracking_utils`, `tests/fast/dashboard` and `tests/fast/utils/test_arguments.py`: 966 passed, 4 skipped.
- Disabling the call site in `log_rollout_data` makes the `log_rollout_data` test fail.
- The flag parses through the miles argument provider.
- ruff, black and isort at the pre-commit pins are clean on the changed files.

### Scope

- The rollout executor logs from a secondary shared-mode wandb writer (`x_primary=False`); scalar metrics already travel that way, but this is the first `wandb.Table` in the codebase and I could not confirm on a live wandb project that shared mode uploads the table. Worth one real run before relying on it.
- wandb is the only backend with a table type today. A trackio implementation is a one-method follow-up once #3201 lands (`trackio.Table` has the same columns/data shape).
- Eval rollouts are not covered; `log_eval_rollout_data` can reuse `sample_completion_rows` if wanted.
- No GPU run; the change is confined to CPU-side logging.

author: anujayavijayakumar
body:
This PR is the union of the two previous implementations:

  * NNGenPrompt.py            (production)  -> "wide" selection mode
  * NNGenPromptcurriculum.py  (curriculum)  -> "tall" selection mode

Selection is per config key via the `selection_mode` field, which DEFAULTS TO
"wide". Every config that exists today omits that field, therefore every config
that exists today takes the exact code path it took before this merge:
same lemur.data() kwargs, same JoinConf shape, same max_rows, same output
columns. Nothing about the legacy pipeline changes unless a config opts in.

MODE SUMMARY
-------------------------
wide : one LEMUR row -> one training sample. Supports the full production
       feature set: on-disk corpus (data_dir), prun_data, classification
       patch/enrich, delta mode, formula evaluation, system prompts,
       shrink_nn_code / nn_code_max_chars.

tall : k LEMUR rows -> one training sample. Rows are grouped by `anchor_nn`,
       sorted by jaccard, chunked into blocks of k, and flattened into
       acc_i / hp_i / tr_i / nn_i / name_i / jaccard_i keys by _pack_k_models.
       Requires similarity_mode="anchor_band_db_minhash" (see note below).

BOTH modes share one emit tail (_emit_row), so tall mode now inherits the
production features it previously lacked: formula evaluation, system prompts
and delta mode. Conversely wide mode gains `is_generation`.

NOTES ON THE UNDERLYING QUERY LAYER (ab/nn/util/db/Query.py)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1. join_nn_query() dispatches three ways. Only similarity_mode=
   "anchor_band_db_minhash" produces the `anchor_nn` / `anchor_jaccard`
   columns tall mode needs. A tall config with similarity_mode="none" would
   fall into join_nn_query_sql_Var_num and return k rows with no anchor
   column. _build_sql_conf() rejects that combination up front rather than
   letting it fail deep in the tall loop.

2. join_nn_query_anchor_otf() accepts `limit_clause` and never uses it, so
   `max_rows` has no effect in the anchor path. Row count there is
   num_joint_nns * JoinConf.overfetch_factor (default 10) for a SINGLE
   resolved anchor. Tall mode therefore passes max_rows=None instead of the
   old `n_training_prompts * k * 10` expression, which was both inert and a
   TypeError when n_training_prompts was None. To change tall row volume,
   set `overfetch_factor` in the config.

body:
Closes Bug 2 in `BUG.md`: the gate's submit handler awaited `api('/auth')` unguarded, so a
`fetch` that never reached the server rejected into nothing — the form sat unchanged with the
passphrase still typed, which a reader cannot tell from a dead button. The gate is the one
screen there is no routing away from, so that silence is the costliest one in the client.

## Summary

- **The gate answers a passphrase it could not send** (`041eca2`) — the handler now tells the
  three outcomes apart: accepted, refused, never-arrived. The last two share `#gate-error` and
  leave the gate standing, because the form is the way forward from both; only a refusal calls
  `passphrase.select()`, because only a refusal implicates the passphrase. This closes the last
  of this file's four unguarded server calls — Bug 1 closed the other three.
- **Bug 2 gets the test that fails without its fix** (`10132bd`) — three tests hang off
  `signIn()`, which had only ever been driven down the success path: accepted, refused, and
  never-sent. The third fails on the unfixed tree for exactly Bug 2's reason; the other two are
  coverage this handler never had.
- **The gate's two refusals are told apart by test, not by hope** (`77ba26e`) — the fence the
  review asked for. `passphrase.select()` was the whole behavioral difference between the two
  error outcomes and nothing asserted it; asserting the field's `value` cannot, since `select()`
  does not change it. A prototype spy asserts it instead — called once in the refusal test,
  never in the unreachable one — proven by deleting the production line and watching exactly
  that test go red. `vi.restoreAllMocks()` is load-bearing, not tidiness: `vi.spyOn` on an
  already-spied method returns the existing spy with its history.
- **Docs and queue** (`f9c89bb`, `6ea03e7`, `2b652db`, `145c490`, `fa50b50`) — Bug 2's queue
  line checked off; three items logged for later without widening this branch: that nothing
  verifies a PR (this repo has no workflows), the ECONNREFUSED noise a green test run prints,
  and Bug 3 — `route()`'s catch rendering `error.message` verbatim, so an offline click reads
  "Failed to fetch". The last commit corrects Bug 3's own remedy, which classified only
  `TypeError` and so would have closed the bug with its `SyntaxError` half (the unguarded
  `response.json()`) still live; both exception types were verified by running them.

## Test plan

- [x] `./run-build.sh` — 0 errors (typecheck worker + client, client bundle, `ratify-log`
      bundle check)
- [x] `./run-tests.sh` — 160/160 passed, 10 files, both projects (workers on real workerd,
      client on happy-dom)
- [x] Regression proven twice by removal: stashing `src/client/main.ts` turns exactly one test
      red for Bug 2's reason; deleting `passphrase.select()` turns exactly one test red for the
      new fence's reason
- [x] `/qa-review`: READY WITH CAVEATS (0 CRITICAL, 1 HIGH, all 10 claims HOLD, HIGH
      confidence, security clean) → `/qa-fix` (test-only, no production change) → fix-check
      **READY WITH CAVEATS**, the HIGH **CLOSED**
- [ ] CI — none to run: this repo has no `.github/workflows`, which is itself a queued item
      (`f9c89bb`). The wrapper runs above are the only gate.

## Caveats carried forward

- **One WATCH, deliberately not fixed here:** the `generation` comment at `main.ts:37-47`
  claims "Every path that decides what is on screen advances this", and `showGateError` now
  changes what is on screen without advancing it. Harmless today — every path that makes the
  gate visible bumps the generation first — but the overclaim is against this project's grain
  and is worth a clause when this merges.
- **Bug 3 is logged, not fixed.** Pre-existing, its own branch and its own test.

body:
The two surfaces `check:contrast` deliberately held out — `.ui-legend-swatch` and `.ui-progress-segment` — plus the meter fill that shares their tokens. All three painted the FILL tier as standalone graphics.

## The palette decision, with numbers

**The 3:1 floor of SC 1.4.11 applies.** Nothing is written on a progress fill, so *where the colour stops* is the entire datum; a slice of a partition carries its share of the whole with no words on it. That is precisely a "graphical object required to understand the content". The wa-iro hue loses.

Legend and Progress moved **together** because a swatch is a SAMPLE of the bar beside it — a key that is not the colour it is a key to is not a key. A unit assertion now pins the two to the same token per tone so they cannot drift apart again.

Measured in Chromium, before → after:

| surface | tone | ground | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.ui-legend-swatch` | warning | light card | **1.74** | **5.90** |
| `.ui-legend-swatch` | success | light card | **2.18** | **6.84** |
| `.ui-legend-swatch` | destructive | dark card | **2.95** | **5.52** |
| `.ui-progress-segment` | warning | light track | **1.60** | **5.41** |
| `.ui-progress-segment` | success | light track | **2.00** | **6.28** |
| `.ui-progress-segment` | destructive | dark track | **2.42** | **4.52** |

Worst case anywhere on the two routes after the move: **4.52:1**.

## Re-adding the routes fixed nothing on its own

`check:contrast` has two non-text passes: one wants ≤24px on **both** axes (a dot), the other a border on exactly **one** side (a rail). A progress fill is neither — 8px (meter) or 22px (slice) tall by whatever width its share makes it, drawn as a background, no border, no text. So the route could be added and the sweep still printed `✓ AA clean` over a bar at 1.60:1. That was measured, not assumed.

Hence a **thin fill** pass that generalises the other two instead of matching a class name: childless, textless, an opaque fill of its own, short axis in `[3px, 24px]`. The 3px floor is the rail pass's own, and it is what keeps `Separator` out — 1.4.11 does not reach a divider.

## Two things the new pass then found

- **Loading placeholders are not 1.4.11 graphics** (1.09:1 light / 1.33:1 dark, deliberately — a skeleton is the shape of content that has *not arrived*, the SC's own pure-decoration exception). Exempted across all three non-text passes by an ARIA fact, `[aria-busy="true"]`, never a class name. Every placeholder this library draws already sits inside one.
- **`docs/showcase/acme-portal` drew its bars on a near-black track.** That theme repoints `--secondary` at a navy *button* colour and `--progress-track-background` defaults to it: 2.50 (success) / 2.90 (warning). Naming the track is the fix — 6.49 / 5.59 — not dragging the tier back. Any theme that repurposes `--secondary` owes that line.

## Mutation-tested three ways

- `--mark-warning: var(--warning)` → unit ratios red **and** browser sweep red (1.74 swatch / 1.60 segment).
- Repointing one CSS rule at the fill tier → the alias assertions and the "same token per tone" assertion go red.
- Deleting the thin-fill pass → the progress route returns to a silent "AA clean".

`check:contrast` now holds all 28 routes with nothing held out; `pnpm verify:ci:static` and `pnpm test` (4797) green locally.

author: phattailed
body:
docs: record the heartbeat loop as §47, which two code comments already cited

The heartbeat fix left dangling references: comments in wsclient.go and heartbeat_loop_test.go point at
doc/interop §47, and the document stopped at §46. Written now, because the finding earns a section on its
own merits.

Three things worth keeping:

The specification requires answering a heartbeat with a heartbeat and warns against an endless loop one
sentence later. Answering unconditionally satisfies the first clause and violates the second, so the
document cannot be followed literally on both counts.

Passive mode had concealed it. The loop needs a long-lived connection on which both ends heartbeat, and a
passive lane sends keepAlive only -- so a passive-only client had no exchange to loop. Adding the request
lane created one and the loop began immediately. A feature that removes the only thing suppressing a
latent fault will look like it caused the fault.

And the instrument was blind by construction. The frame rate had been measured through the capture
directory and reported as normal, but capture deliberately excludes keepAlive and heartbeat -- an
exclusion added hours earlier in the same session. The count was of everything except the messages in
question. The lesson is not "measure more": a filter added for one purpose silently invalidates later
measurements that pass through it, and it is invisible at the point of measuring. What settled this was
counting from the other end of the wire.

author: dynosuprovo
body:
## Summary

Fixes #327

When tasks or tags contain backslashes (such as Windows file paths like `C:\Users\...`, regex syntax like `\1`, `\g<0>`, or trailing backslashes), `topydo ls` previously crashed with:
```
Error while parsing format string (list_format config option or -F)
```

### Cause
In `ListFormatParser.parse()`, `re.sub(r'(?<!\\)%({ph}|\[{ph}\])'.format(ph=placeholder), repl, substr)` passed `repl` as a string argument. Python's `re.sub` parses string replacements for regex escape sequences and group backreferences. When encountering invalid group numbers (`\2`, `\9`), unknown escapes, or trailing backslashes, `re.error` was raised and caught as `ListFormatError`. Even valid backreferences (such as `\1`) were inadvertently substituted with matched groups from the pattern instead of preserving the literal text.

A similar issue existed in `_truncate()`, where `re.sub(re.escape(p_repl), p_repl[:text_lim] + '...', p_str)` passed the replacement string directly.

### Solution
1. Use a callable replacement `lambda _: repl` in `re.sub()`. Per Python's `re` specification, passing a function bypasses template escape/backreference processing and replaces matches with the literal string.
2. Use `lambda _: p_repl[:text_lim] + '...'` in `_truncate()` to prevent escape processing during truncation.
3. Added unit tests in `test/test_list_format.py` verifying backslashes in task text, tags, and during truncation.

## Verification
- Unit tests added in `test/test_list_format.py` pass (`test_list_format_backslash` and `test_list_format_backslash_truncate`).
- Existing test suites in `test.test_todo`, `test.test_filter`, and `test.test_sorter` (98 tests) pass.
- `git diff --check` passes with 0 whitespace errors.

author: dastratakos
body:
## What

The store writer, `apps/web/server/hosted/store/writer.ts`: the one path by which a `messages`, `turns`, or `events` row is written. It consumes the A3 run event stream (`BrainRunEvent`, every turn kind) for a conversation the caller names by row id and account, and keeps the record `plan/storage-plan.md` describes:

- **turns**: queued (`enqueueTurn`, written ahead of the stream, or at `TURN_STARTED` where nothing queued it) → running → settled / cancelled / failed, with the origin it was queued under, usage split four ways, `response_ids` where the runtime has them (empty otherwise), and the failure word.
- **messages**: each user message the turn opened with lands as its own row by the message's id. The turn's answer is one assistant row keyed by the turn id as `client_id`; while the turn runs that row is its journal — a tool call is written in `input-available` **before** execution and moved to `output-available` / `output-error` as the result lands, a reasoning summary is written as it completes — and the turn's completed message replaces the journal's parts whole and sets `finished_at` once. After that the row is immutable: a late, never-seen event for it is refused as `finished`; a redelivered known one reads as `repeated`.
- A turn that ends with a call still unanswered settles the call as `output-error` (nothing will answer it now; an unknown action is never retried) and closes the row. A writer that dies between the call and its result leaves the part in `input-available`, which is what a resume reads.
- **compaction**: `recordCompaction` writes the assistant row through A6's `compactionSummaryMessage`, naming `first_kept_message_id` and, only where the owner counted them, `tokens_before` (absent otherwise, never zero — A6's finding). The stream's `COMPACTION_COMPLETED` carries neither the first kept message nor, under eve, the summary text, so it is consumed as `ignored` and the compaction's owner hands the row over.
- **events**: `recordEvent` is the one path to the `events` table, numbered by the conversation's event sequence. C5 wires `announce → speech.offered` through it; this PR wires no kind.

## How the invariant holds

"No code path writes messages except this writer" is stated over the import graph, not intended: `tests/store-writer-boundary.test.ts` walks `apps/web/server` and `apps/web/api` and asserts that the set of modules importing `messages`, `turns`, or `events` from the schema by name is exactly `{ server/hosted/store/writer.ts }`. A reader that lands later joins that list by name.

## Idempotency and sequences

- A message by `(conversation_id, client_id)`, a turn by its id, a tool part by its call id, a reasoning part by its item id. The same event delivered twice writes one row; a whole turn replayed changes nothing (`repeated` on every event, counters unmoved) — tested.
- Every write runs under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the conversation row, which serializes the conversation's writers, so a check made before an insert holds when the insert runs (this is what makes select-then-insert idempotency race-free). Sequences come from the row's counters, and each allocation lands on the first position no row holds (`greatest(counter, max(seq)+1)`), so a position taken outside the counter costs a skip and nothing else. The unique `(conversation_id, seq)` constraint stays the backstop: under the lock and this allocation the B1-convention "retry signal" cannot fire, so there is no retry loop — a violation that still occurs is a writer outside the lock and surfaces loudly. Tested by taking the counter's next position out from under it. A second `speech.claimed` on one message is answered `already_claimed` under the same lock rather than thrown as a driver error.
- A conversation Clear has stamped (`deleted_at`) is written by nothing: `no_conversation`, like one that never was.

## Validation on write

Every message is held to the vocabulary before it lands through `readStoredUIMessages` — the same reader with the registry pre-check A1 built, never the SDK's `validateUIMessages` directly — over the row's JSON shape, so no row can carry a tool the catalog does not register, an input its schema refuses, or metadata outside `@sidecar/wire`'s set. A refusal comes back as the reader's own word and path (`message_refused` + `not-registered` / `malformed`). The `ai` pin stays `7.0.97` and `zod` `4.5.4`, matching A1; the writer needs neither cast because it goes through A1's wrapper.

## eve conditions (S0 Q3)

The consumer is shaped so eve's adapter can feed it: the completed message is the authoritative ordered projection that replaces in-flight parts (order by `stepIndex` is the adapter's, not arrival order in the row); a null `message.completed` simply never completes the journal and `TURN_ENDED` closes it; cancelled parts are settled at `TURN_ENDED`; a retried step's stale in-flight parts are replaced by the projection; `turns.response_ids` is written where present and left `[]` otherwise.

## Findings for the orchestrator (also sent by message)

1. **`turns.origin` vocabulary gap.** A3's `BrainTurnOrigin` names `observation` and `child_completion`; the plan's `TURN_ORIGIN` (B1, D1) names neither. The writer maps `observation → roster_diff` (true in the hosted tier, which opens observation turns from roster diffs alone) and `child_completion → child` (the schema comment already reads `child` as "a child's completion"; the conversation's kind tells a child's own task turn from the parent's completion turn). A queued row's origin (C2's decision) always wins over the mapping.
2. **Refused vs unknown is not on the row.** The SDK's `output-error` part has `output?: never`, and A3's completed projection carries `errorText` alone for an error part, so the action envelope's `status` (`refused` vs `unknown`) does not survive on an `output-error` part. D1 currently draws every `output-error` as refused. The writer matches A3's shape exactly (it must, for the projection to replace the journal without churn). If the distinction must be stored, the slot is `resultProviderMetadata` on the part, in both A3's builder and here — a contract decision, not made in this PR.
3. **Compaction rows are built by A6's `compactionSummaryMessage`** (A6 merged as edc5bad1), so an uncounted compaction is written with `tokens_before` absent — never zero, never refused — and a summary with no words is refused as the builder says.

## CLAUDE.md sentences this contradicts (for G5)

- "the journal that records an action before its effect and its result before the next inference" and "the action journal that pairs each action with its outcome" — the journal is now the in-flight assistant message's tool-part state, no separate journal.
- "What the brain keeps is one generation per conversation, in one database under one writer … one SQLite file per agent" and the generation / checkpoint / cursor / envelope description — replaced by `messages` / `turns` rows in Postgres.
- "The envelope holds the Responses input from the latest compaction onward — the API's encrypted compaction item included" — compaction is a summary message.

## Verify

```sh
./scripts/check.sh
pnpm --filter @luke/web test:store
pnpm --filter @luke/web exec tsx --test tests/store-writer-boundary.test.ts
```

No macOS or UI code is touched; `verify.sh` does not apply.

## Reviews run

Neither skill is installed here; both were located online and applied as written.

- **Cursor `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review`** (cursor/plugins, `cursor-team-kit/skills/…/SKILL.md`; "thermonuclear code review" resolves to this and to its security sibling, so both were run). Quality pass: REQUEST CHANGES with four blockers, all taken — (1) the ~90-line unique-violation retry apparatus (driver-error schema, constraint-name coupling, retry loop, two realign statements) deleted in favour of the self-healing allocation above; (2) the `speech.claimed` race made a typed `already_claimed` refusal instead of a thrown dr

author: t-crypt
body:
Adds a native Flow tab to Command Center and a resource-popout summary for AI, Gaming, Security and Dev. The map shows real claims, capacity contention, workload priority and profile state. Negotiation controls retain the existing engine behavior and reject actions when the queue changes during a press.

The view reuses shared telemetry and releases its monitoring watches when hidden. Animation is finite and the graph is bounded. No workload detectors, scheduler changes or action-receipt backend are added.

## Planes carry their own profile

Each plane reads its own domain rather than a shared phase string. AI reads resident model claims and the VRAM they hold, Gaming reads the session trigger, Security reads the engagement, Dev reads the project session. Plane state is gated on the install layers: a layer this system does not carry reads "not installed" instead of an idle plane that will never wake, and an installed layer with no registrant names the registrant that is missing. Planes are selectable, so the claim lens inspects them alongside reservoirs and workloads.

No plugin id appears in any core file. Planes key off ProfileEngine owners and InstallProfile layers, so the gaming profile plugin registers under the owner the engine already knows.

## Performance

- The model publishes a signature. The map repaints and replays the pulse only when claims, plane phases or contention move, so a 1 Hz metric tick no longer redraws a settled map.
- The metric rail keeps its delegates across a value tick instead of rebuilding all seven every second.
- Sparks are instantiated only while motion is on.
- The resources popout uses a summarize() path that skips the node and edge layout it never draws.
- Watches stay inside the visibility-gated loader, so nothing periodic runs while Flow is hidden.

Validation: 41 model assertions, 14 QtTest checks, 3 singleton reachability tests, the profile substrate test and FlowScene qmllint pass. An offscreen live-service smoke test confirmed monitoring stops when hidden. Desktop frame-time and RSS profiling on real hardware remains outstanding.

![Illustrative Flow fixture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/T-Crypt/aphotic-hypr/feature/aphotic-flow/assets/screenshots/aphotic-flow-preview.png)

The screenshot uses labeled fixture data. Ready for UI and architecture review; no automatic merge is requested.

## Version

Ships as 2.0.5. VERSION carries the bump, RELEASE_NOTES.md carries the one-line blurb `aphotic whatsnew` reads, and the README feature list and site status page name the Flow map.

author: stanca88
body:
Fixes the Shop tab (and recipe detail Ingredients list) rendering raw JSON blobs like `{"name":"butter","amount":2,"unit":"tablespoons","category":"Dairy & eggs"}` instead of clean ingredient text.

**Root cause**: ingredients are stored in a Supabase `text[]` column, so saving an ingredient as a JS object causes Postgres to coerce each array element to its JSON string form. `normalizeIngredient()` already had logic to parse a plain object, but nothing detected/decoded a JSON *string* — and `loadSharedRecipes()` bypassed `normalizeIngredient()` entirely, running these JSON strings through the plain-text line parser instead, which doesn't understand JSON and falls back to using the whole blob as the ingredient name.

**Fix**:
- `normalizeIngredient()` now detects a `{...}`-shaped string, `JSON.parse`s it, and re-normalizes the result.
- `loadSharedRecipes()` now routes every ingredient through `normalizeIngredient()` instead of calling the plain-text parser directly.

This also resolves the Shop cards looking broken/overflowing on mobile, since the long raw JSON text no longer needs to fit in the card layout.

Verified with `npm run build`.

body:
## Description

Suite à la revue P1 sur #765 (https://github.com/ironlam/poligraph/pull/765#discussion_r3870161871) : le `--force` ajouté à l'étape "Analyse presse IA" de `scripts/sync-daily.ts` contournait le seul garde-fou qui empêchait ce workflow et la fonction Inngest `sync-daily` d'analyser les mêmes articles de presse en même temps. Les deux tournaient sur le même cron `0 5,11,19` et partageaient le throttle de 6h (`syncMetadata`), qui ne réserve pas les articles de façon atomique : ils pouvaient donc lister le même lot d'articles non analysés avant que l'un des deux ne les marque, payant deux fois l'analyse IA et dupliquant décisions de résolveur, rejets ou affaires.

Ce workflow porte déjà la cadence (via `--force`), donc l'étape `press-analysis` de `src/inngest/functions/sync-daily.ts` est retirée : il n'y a plus qu'un seul planificateur pour l'analyse presse, et `--force` n'a donc plus de second processus avec lequel entrer en conflit.

- `scripts/sync-daily.ts` : reprend le `--force` de #765, avec un commentaire expliquant pourquoi c'est désormais sûr.
- `src/inngest/functions/sync-daily.ts` : suppression de l'étape `press-analysis` dupliquée.
- `src/__tests__/consistency.test.ts` : test de non-régression de #765 (`--force` présent) + nouveau test garantissant que l'étape Inngest ne revient pas.

author: michael-wynne-wsu
body:
Fixes #2164.

## Two defects, one of them silent

A circle drawn on the map is stored as a **128 sided polygon** carrying
`circle_center` and `circle_radius`, because GeoJSON has no circle type. So the
accessible lat/long editor rendered **128 latitude/longitude rows** for one,
labelled as an ordinary polygon.

Worse, editing those rows achieved nothing. `massageFormValues()` rewrote the
geometry but carried the original properties through untouched, and
`mukurtu-leaflet-widget.js` rebuilds the circle from `circle_center` and
`circle_radius`, discarding the edited geometry.

A keyboard user's changes were accepted and then thrown away. That is the half
that undercuts an ATAG Part B claim: the accessible alternative accepted input
it could not keep.

## What it does now

A circle presents as a **centre and a radius**. The centre reuses the existing
point machinery, so place search and the coordinate hints behave exactly as
they do for any other single point. Saving rewrites the metadata and the
geometry together.

An ordinary polygon is untouched and still renders as a vertex list, which is
asserted.

## The geometry

`CircleGeometry` does the conversion server side, walking a fixed distance
along each of 128 bearings from the centre, rather than projecting to screen
pixels the way Leaflet-Geoman does in the browser.

The two agree closely at the scales a coverage map uses. Exactness is not
required: the polygon is a fallback for consumers that cannot draw a circle,
and the map always rebuilds the true circle from the metadata.

## Verification

**Mutation, not just a green run.** Reinstating the old behaviour (rewrite
geometry, leave metadata stale) fails the round-trip test with:

> circle_center latitude was not updated, so the map would rebuild the original
> circle and discard this edit.

The geometry tests assert the property that actually makes it a circle rather
than just a ring of the right length: every one of the 128 points is within a
metre of the requested radius, and circles widen in longitude towards the
poles, which a naive degree offset would fail.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `CircleGeometryTest` | 12 tests, 667 assertions |
| `AccessibleCircleEditingTest` | 4 tests, 46 assertions |
| Existing widget tests, run together | 32 tests, 769 assertions |
| Full unit suite | 267 tests, 5419 assertions |

## No update hook, no JS change

Existing stored circles are read correctly as they are, so nothing needs
migrating. And the map already rebuilds from `circle_center`/`circle_radius`,
so now those are written correctly an edit made in the accessible editor shows
up correctly on the map without touching the front end.

## Pre-merge checklist:

- [x] I have checked for and if required, created update hooks. (None needed: code only, existing data reads correctly.)
- [x] I have run an accessibility check, and resolved any issues. (This PR *is* the accessibility fix; it came out of the review on #2161.)
- [x] I have recompiled SCSS if required. (Not required.)
- [x] I have updated or created CI/CD tests, if required.
- [x] I have updated from `main` and resolved any merge conflicts.
- [x] If this PR's base branch is not `main`... (Base is `main`.)
- [ ] I have verified that all expected checks pass.
- [x] I have run the pr-expert-review skill and resolved all relevant issues.
- [x] If I added a content entity bundle... (Not applicable.)

author: tmaeder
body:
`batch_approve_safe_news` and `unbatch_approve_safe_news` are an asymmetric pair, and the asymmetry destroys data.

`batch_approve` overwrites **three** fields — `quality_status`, `seo_indexable`, and `auto_publish_blocked_reasons` (cleared to `'{}'`) — but stamps only **two** of them into `enrichment_status.batch_approve`. `unbatch` restores those two and then **deletes its own trace** (`enrichment_status - 'batch_approve'`).

So a round trip leaves the row with no blocked reasons *and* no record that anything happened. The reason a human or a later sweep would need is gone, and the evidence it ever existed is gone with it — the same erases-its-own-evidence shape as the auto-pause incident in CLAUDE.md.

**Measured on prod 2026-09-10: 10,808 live articles currently carry the `batch_approve` stamp.** Running `unbatch` today would clear the blocked reasons on every one.

## Scope — stated, not implied

This does **not** explain the separate cohort of **2,524** articles that are `quality_status='passed'` and `seo_indexable=false` with an empty reasons array. **Zero of those carry a `batch_approve` stamp**, so they did not come through this path and their cause is still unidentified.

This stops a leak; it does not diagnose that cohort. Those 2,524 stay deindexed pending a real answer rather than being published on the assumption the block was a mistake.

## Not recoverable, and deliberately not faked

The 10,808 rows already stamped have no `prev_blocked_reasons` — the value was never saved. `unbatch` leaves their column untouched.

The `CASE` keys on `jsonb_typeof(...) = 'array'`, **not** on a NULL check, because writing `'{}'` for a missing key would be indistinguishable from a recorded *"there were no reasons"* — which is exactly the confusion this pair created in the first place.

## Verified against prod before committing

| expression | result |
|---|---|
| restore round trip | `['image_unusable','truncated_body']` exactly |
| post-migration stamp | `typeof = 'array'` → restore branch |
| pre-migration stamp | `typeof = NULL` → leave-alone branch |

The migration ends in a `DO` block asserting both branches; it was run standalone against prod and passed. `check-migration-versions` OK (1,627 files, 1,627 unique). Version leaves headroom above both the applied max (`20400214091533`) and a sibling session's in-flight `20410601100000`.

author: frankischilling
body:
Adds drifting blocky clouds, refines the day sky and celestial glow, and aligns local chat panels. The final performance pass removes repeated atmosphere, mesh, and hidden HUD work while preserving the rendered result.

Clouds form connected patches with thickness, shaded sides, slow world-space drift, and day/night lighting. Their first visible surface respects terrain depth. The repeating shape is now computed once and uploaded as a 512-byte occupancy bitset. Clouds pause with gameplay; /time changes lighting without repositioning them. This remains a decorative layer without weather, collision, or cloud shadows.

Day retains the supplied colors and 24-degree spacing, with anchors at -30, -6, 18, 42, and 66 degrees to narrow the pale horizon. Night and twilight keep their existing heights. Sun and moon use pixel-stepped square halos, a soft bloom skirt, and broader forward glare. The updated sun art is copied unchanged. Chat uses a full-width translucent input strip and a shared history panel capped at 640 pixels, with shadowed text and history above the hotbar.

Performance changes:
- Cache cloud occupancy; skip inactive sky palettes and celestial calculations outside the existing glow extent.
- Cache chunk solidity and borders, skip empty face slices, and return early for empty chunks. Preserve greedy ordering and geometry. Inline the existing block predicates without changing invalid-ID handling.
- Stop formatting hidden F3 diagnostics and sampling their biome noise.
- Extend the benchmark to include the actual sky/cloud/terrain/selection/HUD frame, nighttime, and flight through the cloud layer. Add a standalone CPU mesh profile.

On Intel UHD Graphics at 1280x720, three alternating paired trials measured daytime moving-sky frames at 0.960 to 0.626 ms, cloud-layer flight at 1.084 to 0.714 ms, two-chunk edit rebuilds at 1.205 to 0.810 ms, and startup mesh/build/upload at 153.546 to 94.637 ms. Geometry and upload counts match. Two initially slower nighttime results did not reproduce in five-pair follow-ups; both sets are retained. Small changes and noisy tails are not claimed as reliable gains.

Full code review coverage, limits, reproduction instructions, and raw trial summaries: [performance report](https://github.com/frankischilling/kernelcraft/blob/graphics/sky-position-glow/docs/pr60-performance.md).

Validation:
- Native Windows `./build.cmd -Test` and `./build.cmd -Configuration Debug -Test` pass, including CPU, application, persistence, HUD, and real OpenGL checks.
- All nine final visual captures are byte-identical to the cloud baseline. A framebuffer fingerprint checks all 4,096 cached cloud cells against the original GPU pattern.
- Independent mesh face coverage, seam edits, materials, shader halos, sky palettes, chat, input isolation, GL state, and save checks pass. A detached-chunk regression fails on the baseline and passes with the corrected interior neighbor handling.
- Complete-frame day/night benchmarks, F3, targeted repeat trials, and generated/empty/sparse/solid/checkerboard CPU mesh profiles pass their invariants. No hands-on keyboard/mouse playtest or discrete-GPU performance claim.
- Formatting and staged diff checks pass. Linux GCC/Clang Release/Debug builds with -Werror, CPU tests, sanitizers, Mesa application/rendering checks, and GCC build regressions passed for performance commit dcf1185: https://github.com/frankischilling/kernelcraft/actions/runs/34548762126.

Closes #59. Closes #61. Closes #62. Closes #63.

Leave this PR unmerged for review.

author: syedahmad0786
body:
Google Chat project-space support needs explicit employee identity, provider-granted scope evidence, and a private read-only Space observation before any future shared turn can be considered.

This draft adds:

- immutable, one-way-revocable employee Google identity records and a server-only accessor for an owned Google Workspace credential; OAuth tokens are never returned through HTTP;
- recorded provider-granted OAuth scope evidence: legacy and manual replacements remain unknown, an omitted refresh scope retains prior evidence, and an explicit refresh scope replaces it;
- a signed `google_chat_read` opt-in that requests only `chat.spaces.readonly` and `chat.memberships.readonly`. Completion requires active HRMNY staff, the exact verified `hrmny.co` account, and both scopes actually granted;
- bounded private Google Chat Space and membership validation plus a Work-permission observation. It stays observation-only (`bindingReady: false`): this PR adds no Space binding, shared turn, send path, caller-supplied token route, or activation.

Validation:

- Exact predecessor `a579ec2`: Verify and Database CI checks passed; the hosted PostgreSQL identity proof passed.
- E2E exposed a test-fixture defect: the Google card was read from an HTTP batch, while the fixture mocked a single-operation response. `fa0c93c` patches the real batch response at `connections.list` and preserves its other results. The exact-head E2E rerun is pending.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec eslint --no-ignore e2e/connections-google-workspace-oauth.spec.ts` and `git diff --check` pass for the fixture correction.
- No Google provider call, consent completion, migration apply, deployment, or Space activation occurred.

Release ordering: migration 0083 must follow PR313's 0082 after its journal reconciliation. Recompose from that merged main, verify the combined migration chain and hosted PostgreSQL proofs, then use the separately approved migration release procedure.

author: xrl
body:
Closes ledger rows **L12-2 / L6-12** (no log event for decisions), **L12-3** (no audit record carries the W3C trace id), **L4-8** (`auditPath` required), and **L6-1** (`FileAuditLog` durability machinery — the whole sink goes, `sequence` with it).

## Summary

Audit is one structured log record per broker decision, inside the caller's trace: `broker.decision` or `broker.execution` on the `dekopon_broker::audit` target, on stdout as JSON always and as an OTLP log record when `telemetry` names a receiver. **There is no on-disk audit sink.** Losing the exporter loses audit.

This amends the constitution. `docs/design.md#non-goals` said the JSONL file "becomes an opt-in sink, off by default"; it now says there is no on-disk audit sink. The rpi-homelab, the one running install, already ships OTLP.

**Breaking configuration change.** `auditPath` and `serverLimits.auditMaxLineBytes` are unknown fields now. `broker.yaml` is `deny_unknown_fields`, so a config that still names either refuses startup naming the field — the same as `checkpointPath`, `checkpointLockPath` and `auditMaxRecords` already on `main`. `docs/upgrading.md` has the migration. The old `audit.jsonl` is inert.

## What changed

**Emission.** `Broker::record_audit` emits each `AuditEvent` as a log event, then offers it to the `AuditLog` sink. Four sites each produce exactly one record: a denial, an allow, a failure after authorization but before the provider ran, and the terminal outcome. The event fires inside `broker.authorize` or `broker.execute`, which descend from the `broker.invocation` span that adopted the client's `traceParent`, so `CorrelatedJson` and the OTel log bridge stamp the live ids without `dekopon-broker` linking a telemetry SDK. `dekopon-brokerd` installs the log bridge from the same `telemetry` block through `dekopon_telemetry::optional_logger_provider`.

**Offline correlation.** With no `telemetry` there is no OpenTelemetry context, and neither `trace_id` nor `span_id` is fabricated. The stdout line still names the caller's trace: the JSON formatter renders the enclosing `broker.invocation` span, and after #211 its `trace` field *is* the client's W3C trace id. The `trace.id` span field this PR used to add is gone — it was the #211 collapse.

**Deleted, `dekopon-broker`** (semver break): `FileAuditLog`, `FileAuditState`, `count_audit_lines`, `FileAuditError`, `DEFAULT_MAX_AUDIT_LINE_BYTES`, `AuditRecord` and its `sequence` ordinal, and `AuditError::{Poisoned, RecordTooLarge, SequenceOverflow, Serialize, Io}`. `libc` leaves the crate. `sequence` never reached a record anyone reads, because emission precedes `append`. Without it `AuditRecord` only wrapped `AuditEvent`, so `append` now returns `()` and `InMemoryAuditLog::records()` returns events in append order. `AuditError` keeps `Full`. `TraceOnlyAuditLog` is a unit struct.

**Deleted, `dekopon-brokerd`:** `src/audit.rs` (`BrokerdAuditLog`), `BrokerdError::Audit`, sink selection, the private-parent check on the audit path, `audit_path` and `audit_max_line_bytes` in config, and the audit-path storage-collision check. `run` serves `TraceOnlyAuditLog`. The shared `socket::validate_*` helpers stay, because the compile cache, ChatGPT `authFile`, and providers use them.

**The `AuditLog` trait stays.** `dekopon-brokerd`'s sink can no longer fail, so `broker_audit_append_failed` and `BrokerError::{DecisionAudit, AuthorizedFailureAudit, OutcomeAudit}` are reachable only from an embedding. `outcome-unaudited` also survives for terminal evidence that fails to hash. Collapsing the audit variants touches ~110 `InMemoryAuditLog` test uses and `Broker<A>`'s generic, so it is a follow-up.

## One record

From `crates/dekopon-brokerd/tests/audit_stdout.rs`: the real binary with no `telemetry`.

```json
{
  "level": "INFO",
  "message": "broker decision",
  "audit.event": "broker.decision",
  "invocation.id": "invoke-stdout",
  "capability.id": "echo.echo",
  "decision.id": "allow-invoke-stdout",
  "decision.allowed": true,
  "principal": "caller",
  "actor.kind": "agent",
  "actor.id": "brokerd-test",
  "provider": "echo",
  "authorized.by": "broker-test",
  "policy.revision": "policy-test",
  "policy.ids": "caller-echo",
  "policy.digest": "sha256:2d0bcc0950f2…",
  "target": "dekopon_broker::audit",
  "spans": [
    {"name": "broker.invocation", "invocation": "invoke-stdout", "capability": "echo.echo",
     "trace": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"},
    {"name": "broker.execute", "provider": "echo"}
  ]
}
```

`broker.execution` adds `effect`, `risk`, `idempotency`, `credential` (symbolic name only), `outcome`, `duration_ms`, `error`, `output.digest`, and `http.calls`. The fields are documented under [the broker audit record](docs/observability.md#the-broker-audit-record), and the `ci.yml` audit-event doc gate enforces that.

## Chart (0.5.0)

The chart drops `auditPath` and `auditMaxLineBytes` from both broker configs. The broker container no longer mounts the state claim's `broker/` subPath: it reaches the claim only through its own ChatGPT credential subdirectory, the same shape the gateway already has. `broker-chatgpt/` is a sibling subPath of the claim, so it never needed `broker/` created. The init container no longer creates `broker/`, no longer refuses a root-level `audit.jsonl`, and no longer reserves `broker` as a ChatGPT `subdir`. Tier C/D keep `$cfg` and provider storage. **The state PVC stays** for both seed-once ChatGPT credentials. `replicas: 1` / `Recreate` are now justified by the rotating refresh token alone.

`ci/verify-init-permissions.sh` now asserts that neither daemon mounts the claim root. It drops the audit-parent tier, the unmigrated-layout refusal, and the reserved-subdir renders. `check-ipc-layout.py` proves broker-private state against provider storage.

## Tests

- `dekopon-broker/tests/audit_log_events.rs`: one record per decision, against a sink that writes nothing, each in its own span. The credentialed HTTP fixture checks that the record names `fetch-token` and that neither the secret nor `Bearer` appears in any captured span or event. - `dekopon-brokerd/tests/audit_trace.rs`: with a real OTel layer, every record from `Invoke` **and** from the storage-routed `RecordDeliveredTurn` carries the client's trace id inside `broker.invocation`.
- `dekopon-brokerd/tests/audit_stdout.rs`: the real binary with no `telemetry`. Both records reach stdout, no native ids are fabricated, and every record's `broker.invocation` span carries `trace` equal to the parent the client sent.

No credential, capability, or authority change. Audit records stay metadata-only: `secret` and `credential` are symbolic names, and HTTP evidence has no path, query, header, or body. The audit file and its private-parent check were never a containment boundary for anything else. Removing them remo

Look for a case your code skipped"* — `output_invalid`, `infrastructure=False`. The platform handed the sandbox a shorter list, then charged the student an official attempt for it. - **Official** was quieter and worse. Both sides decode the same payload, so counts agreed; with no retrieval rungs, `rewritten` is empty at `metrics.py:356-365` and `retrieval_mrr` silently keeps the verbatim value — the memorization probe `retrieval-v4` exists to keep out of the score. No local run can show either: locally both sides use the same tier. ## The change - `decode_payload` rebuilds the retrieval rungs and emits the same kinds, rungs and order as `materialize_cases`. - `attach_gold` gives a retrieval rung `gold_rows` and a search rung `gold_image_ids`. `dataclasses.replace` raises on a missing field, so the old single branch would have failed outright once retrieval rungs existed. - Search gets its own copy of the descriptor pool, as `materialize_cases` does. Sharing one array let an in-place `prepare_database` change what the retrieval rungs were ranked against; a reviewer measured all three rewritten retrieval outputs differing from the local run. Sharing within each component still holds, so the index is still built once. - Result cap 8 MiB → 64 MiB. The old figure was sized against the six-case shape. Measured on the real tier with random float32: **16,214,347 bytes** at the demo submission's 200-d embedding, **41,318,368 bytes** at 512-d. A correct run was being refused as the student's fault. ## Validation Hosted, on the real public repository at its exact commit, runner v31: ``` smoke_modal.py --benchmark language-search \ --repo LashikaKapoor28/Language_Module_Capstone \ --sha 8789361ad7dec86fa724431873f674e03b449951 9 predictions for 9 cases PASSED in 842s overall 0.4126 (primary) text_mrr 0.7829 retrieval_mrr 0.2281 search_mrr 0.2267 retrieval_mrr_verbatim 0.2747 _keywords 0.2848 _truncated 0.1746 _typo 0.2249 student python 3.8.20 ``` `retrieval_mrr` 0.2281 is the mean of the three rewritten rungs, not `retrieval_mrr_verbatim` 0.2747. That is the defect this fixes, visible in the numbers. Audio re-checked on the same image: `identification_score 0.5375`, 282/282, unchanged from v30. `scripts/run_python_tests.py` on CPython 3.11.15: every suite passed. ## Tests The `RungCasesSurviveTheBoundary` fixture hand-built the same wrong shape, so seven passing rung tests agreed with the bug. It now mirrors `materialize_cases`, including the search copy and the shared id list. Four tests added or widened, each verified to fail without its matching fix: decoded shape vs the controller's, per-kind gold, the copy, and a mutating prepare. `run_week3_local_parity.py` now expects `retrieval_mrr_`, which would have caught this with no hosted run at all. ## Known follow-ups, both outside this PR - `metrics.py:494` now emits `retrieval_mrr_keywords/_truncated/_typo`. `plugins.py:89-93` declares `retrieval_mrr_verbatim` and the three `search_mrr_` but not these, and they are absent from `metric_help`, `metric_roles` and `sample_metric_keys`, so a run page would show "Retrieval Mrr Keywords" with a default arrow. That is a `benchmarks/week3` submodule commit and should land before any student-visible Language run. - The grid is still assembled in two places. Extracting the assembly half of `materialize_cases` into a shared constructor would end the drift and remove the fixture as a third copy. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix Week 3 sandbox to run the same cases the controller scores > - Aligned `decode_payload` with the controller's case layout: adds a verbatim search case, places rewritten retrieval cases before rewritten search cases, and gives search cases a separate descriptor array so search mutations cannot corrupt the retrieval pool > - Fixed `attach_gold` so rewritten retrieval rungs receive pool-row gold and rewritten search rungs receive image-ID gold, matching the controller's scoring expectations > - Raised the serialized prediction size guard in `modal_app.py` from 8 MiB to 64 MiB to accommodate larger result sets > - Expanded local parity validation in [run_week3_local_parity.py](https://github.com/SamGu-NRX/CogPortal/pull/13/files#diff-722702c4b285d0f89399b78e936db89fa9ef5fb3e566c1b6dd67ec0bf38eba43) to require retrieval MRR metrics for each non-verbatim rung > - Risk: search and retrieval descriptor arrays are now distinct objects in `week3_payload.py`; any code that assumed shared descriptor identity between the two pools will break > > > > Macroscope summarized c811ade. > >

author: vpulim
body:
Closes **TASK-325**.

## The defect

The agent-workspace UI shipped in the image on 2026-08-24 and **no operator could turn it on**. `presets/k8s/src/index.ts:1395` gates route registration on `AX_AGENT_WORKSPACE_PREVIEW`, and the chart had no value for it — so `helm show values` never mentioned it, and enabling it took a hand-written `host.env` block in a gitignored overlay that only we had.

Sharper than the card knew: **the durable user-files browser from #504 is behind the same flag**, so it too is unreachable on a fresh install. Two features shipped invisible, not one.

## The change

`channelWeb.agentWorkspace` (default `false`) renders the env var.

Default OFF is the truth rather than caution: with the flag absent the preset never registers `/api/workspace/*` at all, so the surface **does not exist on the wire** rather than being hidden. That is a real capability boundary, and an unmounted route is the cheapest capability minimization there is (invariant #5). The template stamps nothing when off rather than `"0"` — an absent var is the honest shape for a capability nobody granted.

## Why nothing caught it

Worth keeping, because it is a class and not an incident. The `env-shape` guard has two gates:

1. every **REQUIRED** var is stamped by the chart, and
2. every **stamped** var is read by the preset.

This var is read as a bare `process.env` lookup and is **optional**, so it falls between both — read by the code, stamped by nobody, invisible to the check. That third direction ("read, optional, never stampable") is a genuine gap. I tried to size it and **failed**: a first pass said 23 vars, but that conflated "never stampable" with "not stamped in *this* configuration"; a second pass with every feature toggled on returned 48, which was garbage because the render had errored and produced an empty file. Sizing it honestly needs rendering across feature combinations, which makes it its own task — filed separately rather than bolted on here half-measured.

## Tests

Three, and the **default-off one is load-bearing**: a flag that silently defaults ON is a capability nobody granted. RED-proven — flipping the values default to `true` fails it. The third pins independence from `channelWeb.enabled`, since serving the SPA and mounting the workspace routes are two different grants.

Chart suite 110/110 (was 107).

## Migration

`gke-values.local.yaml` is gitignored so it is not in this diff, but it has been migrated off its `host.env` block to `channelWeb.agentWorkspace: true`. Verified the live overlay still renders the env var **exactly once** — an operator carrying both mid-migration gets two entries with the same name, which is legal YAML whose winner depends on template order. The values comment says so out loud.

## Note on provenance

author: john-dennehy
body:
### Summary
Addresses #12 by enabling the voice assistant to proactively speak brief TTS summaries when agent tasks complete, in addition to the existing earcon chime and desktop notification.

### How It Works
When an interactive coding agent (`agy`, `claude`, `opencode`, etc.) finishes a turn:
1. The existing `Stop` lifecycle hook fires `omarchy-voice-agent-notify`
2. The script plays a chime and sends a desktop notification (existing behavior from #13)
3. **NEW:** If the voice assistant is currently active (listening/speaking), the script writes a `notify` command to the daemon's IPC file
4. The daemon receives the notify command and injects a brief TTS prompt into the Gemini Live session
5. The assistant speaks a concise 1-sentence announcement (e.g. *'Agy has finished and is waiting for your input.'*)

### Changes

**`daemon.py`:**
- Refactored `control_reader_loop` into a unified `handle_command()` async dispatcher (eliminating duplicated command parsing between stdin and cmd_file)
- Added `speak <text>` command: injects raw text into the live websocket session for TTS
- Added `notify <msg>` command: wraps the message in a brief-announcement prompt and sends it to the model, plus logs it to the transcript

**`bin/omarchy-voice-agent-notify`:**
- Added step 3: checks `status.json` for active voice state, and if active, writes a `notify` IPC command to the daemon

**`bin/omarchy-voice`:**
- Added `speak` and `notify` subcommands for direct CLI usage

**`README.md`:**
- Documented new CLI commands and proactive voice announcements feature

Closes #12

author: realkarych
body:
Equivalent type and table recreation changes PostgreSQL OIDs, causing false schema differences for enum arrays, domains, composites and ranges. Compare qualified declared type identities and structural type modifiers, preserve true array element identities, and include the collation namespace.

Closes #120

Validation:
- A real failing-before enum-array recreation changed its raw OID and produced only a type_oid snapshot diff; equivalent domain/composite/range cases reproduced the same defect.
- All 11 recreation cases, six actual type changes, array/interval modifiers and qualified collation regressions pass on PostgreSQL 13, 17 and 18.
- Full PostgreSQL 17 integration race suite, Go tests, lint, Markdown and diff checks passed.
- Review found a further generated-array-name collision case; the new regression preserves identical user definitions in reversed creation order and now passes. Scoped re-review confirms the finding is addressed; all 16 CI jobs passed on the fix, including PostgreSQL 13–18 and native Windows/macOS/Linux.

This PR builds on #133. TypeOID and physical UDTName remain Go diagnostic fields but leave serialized equality; JSON gains type_identity, type_modifier and collation_schema. README documents that referenced type identity is covered while standalone domain/composite/range and extension definitions remain outside comprehensive coverage.

author: leonardoazeredo
body:
`main` is now protected — pull requests required, force-pushes and deletions refused, and `enforce_admins` so it applies to admins too. Two things in this repo still pushed `main` directly, and the remote rejects both:

- **The auto-deploy workflow's fallback** merged a dispatched branch locally and ran `git push origin main`. That step runs *after* services have been recreated on the NAS, so the rejection would leave the host deployed from a commit `main` never reaches — the worst version of the failure. The workflow now refuses the run up front, before anything touches the NAS, when the branch has no open PR; the merge step has no direct-push path left.
- **`scripts/post-merge`** pushed after a local merge. It still tries — correct for a clone whose `main` is unprotected — but when the remote answers "protected branch" it now names the cause, the recovery (`git reset --hard origin/main`) and the PR commands, instead of "fix the push".

`CLAUDE.md`'s deploy step 4 is rewritten around the PR flow, since the local-merge route it used to offer is closed.

New guard: `tests/deploy-workflow.bats` asserts as text that nothing in the workflow pushes `main`, that the merge goes through `gh pr merge`, and that the missing-PR preflight precedes the first step that changes the host. Two corpus entries prove those assertions can fail — `killed 2/2` on pi1.

Verification: local `18 ok / 0 not ok` across `nas-sync.bats`, `hooks-installed.bats` and the new file; pre-commit (secrets, YAML, doc links) passes; full NAS suite green apart from the seven pre-existing git-dependent failures.

author: justinduverge-design
body:
Three fixes from founder + external-beta reports on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-10.

## 1. The six-digit code could not be typed in (Freddy, external beta)

iOS `OmenOtpCodeField` centred an invisible `TextField` inside `.frame(height: 60)`. A frame does not grow what touch can reach, so the live region stayed the field's natural ~25pt line height while the boxes drawn under it are 60pt — taps on the top and bottom thirds hit nothing. Confirmed by temporarily rendering the field opaque. Fixed with `.contentShape(Rectangle())` after the frame plus a tap-catcher on the ZStack.

Android had no hit-area bug. Both platforms now open the code screen focused.

**Founder confirmed typing works on a physical iPhone and on Android.**

## 2. Command Center clipping and dead space

- The league carousel's pager was pinned to a hard 270. A paged pager does not size to content and a constant cannot grow, so the page header overflowed and the Sleeper badge was sliced in half. Both platforms now measure pages and take the tallest.
- `OmenMatchupHero` wrapped its content in a greedy `GeometryReader`, which claims all offered height and has no intrinsic height, so the card could never be shorter than its 220pt floor. Width now comes from a `.background`, which measures without participating in layout.
- Waiver page reduced to its deadline line and link; the full briefing is unchanged in the sheet.
- Tighter rhythm, and scrolling switched off **only when the content fits** — a flat disable would strand the bottom of the screen at large Dynamic Type.

## 3. Material components ignored Omen tokens

`OmenTheme` wrapped `MaterialTheme` but passed no arguments, so Material used its own light default in both themes. `ModalBottomSheet` defaults to `surfaceContainerLow`, so dark-mode detail sheets came up near-white under dark content. `omenMaterialColorScheme` maps existing tokens onto Material roles — no new hexes, registry stays source of truth.

## Verification, stated plainly

- iOS: builds clean, 461 tests. The only 4 failures are `KeychainSessionStoreTests` (`errSecMissingEntitlement` under `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) and fail identically on a clean tree.
- Android: builds clean, all unit tests pass.
- Theme bridge verified on emulator in **both** themes with the earlier per-sheet overrides deleted, so the bridge carries it alone.
- **Not machine-verified:** everything on the `carousel != null` path. No screenshot scenario exercises it on either platform — the demo fixtures all run the legacy stacked branch. That layout is verified only by the founder on device. A multi-league scenario is worth adding so this stops being untestable.

Known wart: commit 2a446a9's message says "OmenTheme never wraps MaterialTheme". It wraps it and passes nothing; cb9c12f states the mechanism correctly.

body:
## Summary

Workstream D of the deploy-downtime plan (PR #398): everyone signed in to LawHand — portal clients included — now sees a short, kindly worded banner while a release is in flight, instead of hitting a bare connection failure with no warning.

- `deploy_prod.sh` writes `release-window.json` into the host-status directory (the read-only mount the backend already uses for disk status) after preflight passes and before the databases come up, maximizing lead time. A dedicated EXIT trap removes it on every exit path — folded into the scheduler cutover trap mid-script and re-armed for the post-cutover gates — so the banner can never outlive the deploy. A failed write only warns; an advisory can never block a deploy.
- New public `GET /api/release-window` (alongside `/api/version`) serves only `active`/`window_id`/`message` from a strict, fail-closed reader: missing, malformed, symlinked, or stale markers mean "no active window", the message is length-capped, and no host or build detail reaches the browser. A 2-hour auto-expiry backstops a hard-killed deploy that cannot run its trap.
- New `ReleaseWindowBanner` frontend component: slim, non-modal, dismissible per user per window id, polled every 30s, rendered for every signed-in role — deliberately not client-skipped like `ReleaseAnnouncement`.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/test_release_window.py tests/test_release_window_deploy.py tests/test_route_auth_coverage.py tests/test_release_notes.py`: 30 passed, 1 skipped (symlink pin needs privilege on Windows; runs in Linux CI).
- Full backend suite vs `origin/main` in a detached worktree: failure sets byte-identical (72 pre-existing environment failures on both), zero regressions.
- Frontend: `eslint` clean on touched files; full `vitest` suite 158 files / 974 tests passed; `npm run build` succeeds.
- `bash -n scripts/deploy_prod.sh`; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check`; `python scripts/generate_release_notes.py --check`.
- Manually traced every `deploy_prod.sh` exit path (preflight, backup, cutover, health gates, success) to confirm the marker trap covers each.
