author: dreamcreateweb
body:
Ledger item **R1·S1** from [DREAMCRM-24].

## The hole

`lib/services/insurance-ocr.ts` filtered its `imageUrls` on `/^https?:\/\//` and nothing else, so the public insurance-card scanner would fetch and bill **any URL on the internet**. The two call sites each had a different opinion about what "our storage" means:

| Call site | Gate before |
|---|---|
| `lib/services/insurance-ocr.ts` | `/^https?:\/\//` only |
| `app/site/[slug]/intake/[formSlug]/actions.ts` | `u.host.includes(S3_BUCKET)` (substring — `mybucket.attacker.example` passes) **or** `u.host.endsWith('.amazonaws.com')` (every public S3 bucket on the internet) |
| `app/(portal)/patient/intake/actions.ts` | none |

Cost of the hole: a clinic's `MONTHLY_CAP = 400` scans spent on someone else's images, plus our servers fetching an attacker-chosen URL.

## The fix

Adopt `isAllowedAttachmentUrl` (`lib/attachment-hosts.ts`) — the same boundary message attachments already use, matching the exact hosts `lib/blob-s3.ts` `publicBase()` mints (`S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, `${bucket}.s3.${region}.amazonaws.com`, the `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` per-store subdomain, and `ATTACHMENT_HOST_ALLOWLIST`).

The gate lives in the **service**, so a future call site is covered by construction rather than by remembering to filter. Both actions adopt it too, and the hand-rolled `isOwnUploadUrl` is deleted.

## Tests

Seven new cases in `tests/intake-forms/insurance-ocr.test.ts`: foreign host, bucket-name lookalike, somebody else's S3 bucket, a mixed list (drops the foreign one, still reads the real card), the Vercel Blob subdomain, and a CloudFront origin from `ATTACHMENT_HOST_ALLOWLIST`. The pre-existing fixtures moved to realistic bucket URLs.

New adoption guard `tests/intake-forms/insurance-ocr-host-adoption.test.ts`: fails if any file outside `lib/attachment-hosts.ts` re-implements a storage-host check, if an OCR entry point stops importing the shared gate, or if the service's filter reverts to a protocol test.

### Red run (conventions §2)

Reintroduced **both** bugs in the tree — the protocol-only filter in the service and the old `isOwnUploadUrl` in the site action — and watched **6 tests fail**, naming both sites:

```
× refuses an image url on a host we do not serve (no vision call, no spend)
× refuses a bucket-name lookalike host (the old substring match let this through)
× refuses somebody else's S3 bucket (the old amazonaws.com fallback let this through)
× drops only the foreign url and still reads the real card
× no file re-implements the storage-host check outside the shared module
× the OCR service itself gates on the allowlist, not on a bare protocol test
```

That red run also caught a weakness in the guard itself: the "every entry point filters through the shared allowlist" check *passed* while the hand-rolled filter was live, because the doc comment above it happened to name `isAllowedAttachmentUrl`. It now strips comments and requires the real `import … from '@/lib/attachment-hosts'`; re-broken, it fails.

## Risk notes

- **Not a money path**, no migration, no tenant-scoping or auth change.
- **Behaviour change on a patient-facing surface:** a card image on a host outside the allowlist is now refused with the existing "please type your details" copy instead of being scanned. Verified the allowlist derives from the same env `lib/blob-s3.ts` builds upload URLs from, so real uploads match. A CloudFront/custom origin already has the `ATTACHMENT_HOST_ALLOWLIST` escape hatch.

Full suite green: 7,438 passed / 7 skipped, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` clean.

author: stvad
body:
Fixes #931.

## The gap

`ensureSystemPages` reports a failing `ensure` and carries on, so a system page can be absent for the rest of the session. Every other system page is re-ensured at its point of use — Properties/Types through the seed materializer's `ensureParent`, Journal through `getOrCreateDailyNote`, Locations through `createOrFindPlace`. Recents was the exception: both consumers navigated straight to `recentsPageBlockId(workspaceId)`, so a page skipped at bootstrap stayed a dead link until the next workspace open.

I checked the other direction too — every remaining `openBlock` / `navigateFromGlobalCommand` call site targets a block it has already resolved (`block.id`, a search hit, a user-chosen shortcut). Recents was the only one navigating to a *derived* id.

## The shape

A lazily-created target is described by one value: the block id, and how to materialize its row.

```ts
// recentsNavigationTarget(repo) — id, workspace and materializer from ONE read
openBlock(event, target)                       // header button
await navigateFromGlobalCommand(repo, target)  // global command
```

`ensure` lives on `OpenBlockContext` and `GlobalCommandNavigateInput`, so it travels with the id it belongs to, and one plugin-side helper derives the whole triple — the id is derived from the workspace and the materializer is bound to it, so all three must name the same one. That helper is also the single home for the pin-versus-hash decision below. Both gesture surfaces then run one ordering (`navigateEnsuringTarget`): **navigate, then materialize what it landed on.**

```ts
const landed = await navigate(repo, input)
if (!landed || landed.blockId !== blockId || landed.workspaceId !== workspaceId) return landed
try { await ensure() } catch (error) { /* logged */ }
```

Materializing *after* is the whole design, and it took two review rounds to get there. There are **two** seams that can veto or retarget a navigation — `navigationIntentVerb` resolves the gesture, `navigationVerb` executes it — and I first put the ensure between them, so whichever seam ran later always got the last word after the write had already committed. `NavigationResult` is the only value that has heard from both, and the module already documents it as the source of truth over the request. Comparing against it means a vetoed gesture (`null`) and a retargeted one (some other block) both write nothing, with no reasoning about which seam is where.

Landing first also keeps `navigate` on the handler's own turn, so two rapid gestures reach the serialized `repo.tx` in click order — a deferred navigation could otherwise drop an old destination on top of a newer one.

The cost is that the panel opens a moment before the row does. That is confined to the case this exists for: with the page present the ensure is a cache-hit read and nothing is visibly late, and with it missing an empty panel that fills itself in beats a permanently dead link. `preventDefault` and the passthrough branch are untouched — the click surface behaves exactly as it did before this PR.

The command resolves its workspace through `activeWorkspaceIdPreferringHash`: during a workspace switch the hash already names the workspace the user is looking at while `repo.activeWorkspaceId` still names the previous one, and the command would otherwise open — and now materialize — the one they just left. The header button stays on the pin, like every other click surface; making Recents the one exception would be a local inconsistency in a shared path rather than a fix.

`getOrCreateRecentsPage` also passes `skipUndo: true` now. Opening Recents is a navigation; cmd-Z after it should undo the user's last edit, not un-create the page. `UndoManager.record` clears the redo branch on every push, so the unattended create was discarding a pending redo — the rule `getOrCreateKernelPage` documents and `getOrCreateMigrationsPage` already follows.

### Shapes I built and threw away

- **`use()` + a memoized ensure**, mirroring `usePluginPrefsBlock`. Keeps the click synchronous, but the memo is per-Repo-instance and the bootstrap ensure does not populate it, so the button's first call always suspends — a Suspense fallback plus React's 300ms throttle means the Recents icon appears late on **every** app open. `useUIStateBlock.suspend.test.tsx` also documents that a genuine `use()` suspension never resumes in this harness, so the path would have been untestable.
- **Deferring the navigation until the ensure resolves** (rounds 1–2). Correct-looking, and wrong at three seams and one race, all of which the flipped ordering removes rather than guards.
- **A generation counter to cancel stale ensured navigations.** Real machinery in core navigation for a case the ordering makes impossible.

## Adjacent, deliberately not fixed here

- `open_today` and `open_preferences` materialize before `navigateFromGlobalCommand` consults the policy, so a vetoed command still writes — the same ordering Recents had. Not mechanical to convert: both use the *result* of the ensure as the blockId, where Recents derives its id up front. Filed.
- A failed ensure now leaves the panel open on a block that never arrives. Better than a click that silently does nothing, but still unexplained; surfacing it means deciding where a failed navigation target reports, which is a design call worth making deliberately. Filed.
- Properties/Types/Locations still use the default `skipUndo: false`. Their only caller is `ensureSystemPages`, which runs before there is a stack to clear.
- Navigating to a **tombstoned** page points the panel at the tombstone while the restore runs, and `PanelContentRecovery` bounces the pane after `RECOVERY_DEBOUNCE_MS` (120ms). I verified the shape rather than assuming it — the watchdog recovers only on a confirmed tombstone, so the ordinary "never created" case never trips it. Not introduced here (the same click hit the same tombstone before, with nothing restoring it afterwards), and the fix belongs in the watchdog: the alternatives are special-casing tombstones into the navigation path, or raising a constant the code deliberately keeps below human-perceptible latency, which would slow every real deletion. Filed.

## Verification

`pnpm run check` green (693 files / 9058 tests).

Mutation-tested by deletion, per clause and per position. Every guard fails a distinct named test:

| mutation | fails |
|---|---|
| drop `ensure` from the header button | `the header button creates the page, then navigates to it` |
| drop `ensure` from the global command | `the global command creates the page…`, `a second open reuses the page…` |
| `useOpenBlock` rebuilds its context field by field | `carries \`ensure\` through to the navigation` |
| materialize before navigating | 5 tests, incl. both retarget cases and the execution-seam veto |
| drop the landed-`null` check | `an EXECUTION-seam veto leaves it unrun` |
| drop the workspace half of the comparison | `a WORKSPACE-only rewrite leaves it unrun` |
| run `ensure` on a native passthrough (position) | `a native passthrough leaves it unrun` |
| call `ensure()` outside the try | `a SYNCHRONOUS throw is caught too, not just a rejection` |
| drop the try/catch | the rejection *and* the synchronous-throw tests |
| drop `skipUndo` | `creating the page lazily does not discard a pending redo` |
| read the pin instead of the hash (command) | `the command follows the hash, not a pin the workspace switch has not caught up to` |

Seven negative assertions across the rounds initially passed for the wrong reason — they ran before the thing that would make them fail had happened. Each now fences on a write that *does* land (both navigations queue through the same serialized `repo.tx`, so absence is a fact about the queue), and each mutation fails on its assertion in tens of milliseconds instead of timing out. The `useOpenBlock` regression needed a render-level test to catch at all, since a dropped callback is a missing behaviour rather t
